summary: On Mac only, printing a form containing a PDF or PICT picture placed as a static object, using [Print form](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-form) together with the Page Setup dialog, could crash the application inside [PAGE BREAK](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/page-break) processing. The crash stemmed from an Apple-side bug in PDF image handling rather than QuickDraw, occurred whether printing via the command or a direct PDF print, and the picture itself did not render in the output.

When appending a child node to an XML document whose root element defined a namespace, [DOM Append XML child node](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dom-append-xml-child-node) incorrectly added an extra, empty `xmlns` attribute to the newly created element.

On Mac, quitting 4D Server 64-bit via AppleScript did shut the server down successfully, but AppleScript still reported error -128 back to the caller, an unwarranted error given that the termination had actually completed.

When the current selection contained deleted records, [SELECTION TO ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/selection-to-array) filled the resulting array with 0 for those records instead of the expected -1, making it impossible to tell a deleted record apart from record number 0.

This entry appears to be an internal test/placeholder record ('Preprod: test without modification, mail z') rather than a documented user-facing bug; no technical detail is available from the release notes.

On Windows, when the taskbar was docked at the top of the screen, the scroll buttons of an oversized pop-up menu (one containing more items than fit on screen) could not be operated, blocking access to items below the visible area; the same menu scrolled normally when the taskbar was positioned at the bottom.

In 4D Write Pro, importing text that contained an ` ` HTML entity via [WP New](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-new) failed, raising an unexpected error #106 instead of completing the import.

Dragging the sort editor window's border to widen it and then narrowing it again caused the actual resize amount to drift out of sync with the distance the mouse moved, leaving the window wider or narrower than the drag gesture indicated.
Searching Design mode for unused local variables incorrectly listed local variables that were actually referenced inside SQL code blocks, reporting them as unused when they were not.

In the 64-bit version, Control- (or Command-) clicking the header of a property group in the form object property list — as opposed to clicking its disclosure icon — no longer expanded or collapsed the group, breaking that keyboard-modifier shortcut for toggling property sections.

After a client session was promoted from the default user to Designer in order to call [OPEN ADMINISTRATION WINDOW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-administration-window), immediately reverting the promotion with [CHANGE CURRENT USER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/change-current-user) prevented the administration window from appearing at all. The fix ensures the OK system variable is now correctly set to 1 whenever CHANGE CURRENT USER successfully restores the current user; by design, the administration window (an asynchronous dialog) still will not display once the session has already been demoted back to a regular user.

In the 64-bit version, opening a saved label definition file (.4LB) after the fields or tables it referenced had been renamed caused the Label editor to fail to open the file, because field references in the file were stored as plain names rather than in tokenized form.

When client-server communication was encrypted over SSL, a session could not resume its postponed connection after the machine woke from sleep. Sleep detection for encrypted client-server communication was not supported prior to v16; this fix restores proper session resumption for encrypted connections.

In the Method Editor, choosing 'rename in all references' from the method-rename dialog collapsed backslash-continued multi-line commands down into a single line; renaming via 'replace content' from the Design-mode search results window, or renaming a method currently open in its own editor, was unaffected.
In the 64-bit version, dismissing the form editor's 'Clear custom templates' dialog — whether by Cancel or OK — unexpectedly reset the displayed state of the object entry-order (tab order) view.

Passing a picture-type variable to [ORDER BY FORMULA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/order-by-formula) could crash the application; the 4D SVG component's `SVG_Export_to_picture` method could trigger a similar crash.

In 64-bit mode, choosing a target file path in the data export dialog reset the previously selected export fields, silently re-selecting every field instead of preserving the subset the user had chosen.
In the 64-bit version, help tips set on a list box's header or footer area were not saved when the form was saved.

When SVG_SET_OPTIONS had automatic ID generation enabled, the auto-generated id took precedence over an explicit id attribute passed to the SVG_New_group component method, contrary to the documented behavior that automatic IDs should only be assigned to elements that don't already have one; SVG_SET_ID could be used to override the id as a workaround.
In 4D Server's license-renewal dialog, manually typing in a valid license number left the warning icon and its tooltip visible even after the complete, valid number had been entered.

On Mac, enabling the system preference for moving keyboard focus between controls with Tab did not allow users to Tab into pop-up menus or drop-down lists, making them unreachable via keyboard-only navigation.

Pop-up/drop-down list objects failed to correctly resolve XLIFF references in their displayed item titles, unlike lists built with the Toolbox List editor. The issue affects only 'value' mode pop-ups (numeric data source) drawing from a referenced list whose item titles use the `:xliff:` prefix; the documentation never claimed pop-up titles are auto-processed for XLIFF, and 'reference' mode (string data source) titles still require explicit conversion via [Localized string](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/localized-string).

In the Toolbox's Formats and Filters page, changing the test area's data type away from 'Numeric' caused the combo box to immediately snap back to 'Numeric' and clear the entered test value, making it impossible to test a filter against any other data type.

In the 64-bit version, launching a built/merged application produced with 4D Volume Desktop briefly flashed the full Design-mode menu bar (4D, File, Edit, Run, Records, Tools, Window, Help) at startup. The 32-bit version showed a similarly brief flash, but with only two menus, making it far less noticeable; in both cases the menu bar was disabled, so there was no risk of it being usable.

On Windows, in engine-deployed applications (standalone or client/server), a custom application icon configured at build time failed to appear on several secondary windows — including the startup options window (opened by holding Alt/Option at launch), the server selection window (opened by holding Alt/Option when starting a client), user authentication, client auto-update, and the application/server quit dialogs — which showed the default 4D icon instead.

[SET DRAG ICON](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-drag-icon) did not accept a picture passed through direct object-notation reference (for example `Form.image`); the picture first had to be copied into an intermediate local picture variable before it could be used.
When a subform object had its 'Automatic Width' property enabled, it could no longer be resized vertically using either the keyboard or the mouse.
In a list box with both 'Display Footers' and 'Column Auto-resizing' enabled, resizing a column horizontally caused the list box's vertical scrollbar to disappear.

[COLLECTION TO ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/collection-to-array) failed to convert ISO 8601 date strings stored in a collection into Date values, even when the `Dates inside objects` database parameter was set to `String type without time zone`; [OB GET ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-get-array) converted the same values correctly under the same setting.
Calling [HTTP Get](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-get) against certain APIs — such as the Google Maps geocoding API — could unexpectedly return a 403 Forbidden status.

Reordering the fields already selected in the Quick Report field-selection list via drag-and-drop caused every moved field to end up displayed as the same field; validating the selection and reopening the Quick Report editor before reordering worked around the issue.
On Windows, right-clicking inside a very small 4D Write Pro area could crash the application.

On Mac 64-bit only, in a client/server application, an output form containing 300 or more list box columns became extremely slow and unresponsive whenever a user simply selected a record. List-form redraw was optimized as part of the fix, but performance with extremely high object counts remains inherently limited by the Cocoa framework.

When a plug-in (such as API Pack) prevented focus from leaving an object on a detail form displayed via [MODIFY RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/modify-record), clicking the standard 'Next record' or 'Previous record' action unexpectedly closed the form and set the OK system variable to 1. The fix disables [NEXT RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/next-record) and Previous record whenever the current entry cannot be validated, leaving only Validate or Cancel available — by design, to prevent invalid data from being left uncommitted; forms that must allow advancing regardless need to be redesigned.

On Windows, running [New process](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/new-process) in a loop from a client running on the same machine as the server could intermittently return error 10035 or 10002 on the client side.
In the Import dialog, changing the "Import from line" field (which sets the starting import row) unexpectedly reset all the other import settings that had already been configured.

When the web server's character encoding was set to Shift-JIS and a web form's submitted variables were retrieved with [WEB GET VARIABLES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-get-variables), the Japanese text values assigned to the variables came out garbled (mojibake). The issue affected v13 and later.
French-localized version only: in the Form Editor, Alt-clicking a break to add a new one always numbered the new break "0" instead of assigning the correct sequential break number.

When styled text (using an inline "text-align" property on a span) was printed to PDF via a print command, the alignment style was not applied to the rendered output, even though this had already been fixed for on-screen display under ACI0095913 — the fix did not extend to the print/PDF rendering path.

Inside a 4DLOOP block containing a full 4DIF/4DELSE/4DELSEIF/4DENDIF construct repeated three times, [PROCESS 4D TAGS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/process-4d-tags) raised a "missing 4DENDIF" error on the loop's second pass, misinterpreting the nested tag structure. Wrapping the whole three-part block in an outer 4DIF True/4DELSEIF avoided the problem.

On macOS (specifically Big Sur), typing a diacritic combined with a base letter — e.g. pressing "^" then "a" to compose "â" — no longer composed the accented character and instead entered the two characters separately. On Mac generally, holding a key to bring up the accent-picker popup for composing accented characters also stopped working; this appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0102536.

In the Structure Editor's Inspector window, pasting/typing a relation name (for a one-to-many or many-to-one relation) into the relation area was not saved if the Inspector window was closed before the field lost focus.
On the 64-bit Mac version, displaying a sheet-style window suppressed the On Activate and On Deactivate form events entirely, so form code relying on those events never ran for sheet windows.

Setting an object property to a numeric value of infinity with [OB SET](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-set) no longer converted that value to Null as it should; an object holding such an INF value then triggered a runtime error when parsed with [JSON Parse](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/json-parse), making it unusable. Per ECMAScript and RFC 4627, Infinity and NaN values are supposed to be converted to null.

[QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query-by-attribute) and equivalent ORDA queries support "linked" queries against attributes nested inside object fields, but this did not work correctly for attributes of type Date (e.g. `locations[a].creation_date`), while string-type attributes queried fine. This was a side effect of v17 adding support for storing dates inside object fields; using the string-without-time-zone representation avoided the bug.

After double-clicking from a list box or list form into a detail form and then using a standard navigation action button to move from a locked record to an unlocked one, [Locked](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/locked) incorrectly continued to report the record as locked.

When sending a long email body in ISO-2022-JP mail mode, the resulting MIME source was emitted as one very long unwrapped line instead of being folded into properly self-contained ISO-2022 lines as required by the MIME format.

When an email body encoded in ISO-2022-JP mode contained a character that could not be represented in that charset, the mail transporter failed to automatically promote the message to UTF-8 encoding as it should.
When `headerCharset` was set to ISO-2022-JP mode for an outgoing email, the attached file's name was encoded incorrectly.

In the client/server architecture, a relation configured via [SET FIELD RELATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-field-relation) (referred to in the Japanese notes as an automatic relation setting) was not honored by [RELATE ONE SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/relate-one-selection), which failed to use the relation parameter that had been passed to it; ORDA relation attributes were unaffected.

After repeatedly reusing the Query Editor to run several queries in a row, its interface could unexpectedly go blank — the search-condition rows and the row of action buttons disappeared, leaving little more than the partially rendered edges of the dialog.

In a 4D web area using the CEF-based (or Windows) embedded rendering engine, pages from sites like Google did not display in the system's configured language (e.g. Italian) even though the OS language was correctly set.

With the method editor preference to auto-insert a closing parenthesis enabled, autocompletion for [BEEP](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/beep) suggested an incorrect syntax, inserting `BEEP()` even though BEEP's real (undocumented) syntax is `BEEP : 48 : X | L`; passing a negative value silenced the beep, an unofficial behavior that this fix removed.

For commands that take only optional parameters — such as [BEEP](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/beep), [Application version](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/application-version), [Current method name](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/current-method-name), and [START TRANSACTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/start-transaction) — pressing Tab to autocomplete the command name in the method editor automatically appended a pair of parentheses, which could then cause an error when the code was run or compiled.

On Windows, calling [GET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-print-option) to retrieve the double-sided/binding option while omitting its optional third parameter raised a runtime error instead of falling back to the default value, even though that parameter is documented as optional.

While editing text, pressing Home moved the caret to the beginning of the current paragraph rather than the beginning of the current line, and End behaved the same way for line/paragraph ends; this change aligned the behavior with Microsoft Word's conventions.
The runtime error #314, raised when a Null collection is passed as the first parameter of the For each syntax, was shipped with no descriptive error text.
In client/server mode, calling the collection method `.sort()` on attributes of type time (or date) inside a transaction produced incorrect results.

On 64-bit Windows, if an application's Quit menu item was wired to a project method instead of the standard "Quit" action, closing the 4D MDI application window did not execute that method, leaving the application unable to quit via the window close control.
For a 3D button showing both a picture and a title, when the picture was right-aligned, the title text rendered one pixel higher than it should; left-aligned pictures were unaffected.

In a current-selection list box, pressing the down arrow highlighted the first row; after then running a query that changed the record order and pressing down arrow again, the row selected was the one below the previously highlighted row rather than the expected first row — the highlight should have reset when the query ran.

In a current-selection list box, selecting a row, then clicking a column header to sort, then navigating with the up/down arrow keys selected the wrong row instead of correctly tracking from the current selection.

With word wrap enabled, clicking in the trailing whitespace at the end of a line in a text area, Write Pro area, or list box placed the caret at the start of the next line instead of after the clicked word — expected only when a word itself was too long to fit and had to break, but not for a normal trailing space after a complete word.

In the method editor, pressing Cmd+L (macOS) or Ctrl+L (Windows) no longer opened the "Go to line" dialog, because that same default shortcut was also bound to another action (jump to Explorer/Form) — a duplication dating back to ACI0070697 (v12) that only surfaced as a conflict once the method editor moved to 64-bit. The default shortcut for "Go to line" was changed to Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+L to resolve it.

While drawing or moving an object in the Form Editor by dragging with the mouse, pressing Escape crashed the application on Mac, or closed the Form Editor window on Windows — instead of simply canceling the drag operation as expected.

In the Structure Editor's Inspector window, after typing a Japanese table or field name (confirming the IME input, then the text entry, then tabbing to the next object), clicking the Structure Editor window and then clicking back into the Inspector to type another Japanese name disabled Japanese (IME) input entirely; closing and reopening the Inspector window restored it. The bug occurred specifically when a focusable, tab-enabled checkbox retained focus while another window began accepting text input without the checkbox's window being closed.

On 32-bit Windows, repeatedly opening and closing windows on the client side could eventually crash the application; the issue appeared related to menu bar management in applications containing several menus.
Pressing Page Up or Page Down in a single-line text input form object did not trigger the On After Keystroke form event, unlike other navigation/editing keystrokes.

If a form had an object placed on page 0, focus was lost from form objects every time a standard record-navigation action (such as [NEXT RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/next-record)) was executed, even when that page-0 object itself was not focusable. The expected behavior is for focus to remain on the first tab-enabled, focusable object.

In client/server mode, calling ORDA's `entitySelection.query()` on a relation attribute inside a loop returned stale results after the first iteration; excessive network optimization in ORDA appeared to prevent related entities from being reloaded on subsequent passes through the loop.

When an array-type listbox's control arrays (row height, row control, etc.) were not explicitly declared, 4D inferred the row height array as a text variable and the row control array as undefined, since the compiler cannot infer whether a control array should be boolean or long integer. Running the compiled application then made the form extremely sluggish, affecting the listbox and other text-entry areas on the same form. The fix makes the row height array automatically declared as a long integer array; declaring process variables explicitly for control arrays is still recommended.

In client-server mode on Windows, attempting to trace/debug a trigger did not work: an empty debugger window appeared instead of stepping into the trigger code. This was related to 4D Server's move to a new threading model, which could be disabled by placing a file named "noThreadedFibers.prm" next to 4D Server.exe.

In client-server mode, when an entity's related attribute was modified and saved with entity.save(), the attribute's value became undefined, and calling entity.reload() afterward failed to restore the correct related-attribute value.

In client-server mode, if an entity was loaded and its corresponding record was subsequently updated through the classic (procedural) language, calling entity.reload() did not refresh the entity with the latest values.

Printing a label form via [`PRINT LABEL`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-label) without displaying the editor could raise a "Division by zero" error when the label width exceeded the paper width, on the 64-bit version. This occurred because the 64-bit label editor computes label width from the paper width, whereas the 32-bit editor derives it from horizontal tabs.

In 4D Write Pro, deleting a table with the Backspace or Delete key required the table to be selected on its own, but a table located at the very end of the document could not be selected that way, so it could not be deleted. The fix aligns behavior with Microsoft Word: Backspace deletes a fully selected cell, row, or table, while Delete removes characters within a cell but only removes a table if it is included as part of a larger selection.

When a listbox combined the "Column auto-resizing" option with one or more locked (non-scrolling) columns, resizing the listbox window or dragging a header separator produced erratic, unnatural column-width adjustments.
In a standalone application built with the 64-bit Windows version, the Quick Report editor had no default HTML template available as a report output destination.
Importing data into Microsoft Access via the 4D ODBC driver failed whenever a 4D table name contained an underscore character.

In the 64-bit Quick Report editor, resizing a column's width caused the column's underlying formula (e.g. String([Table_1]Field_1)) to be overwritten with a generic reference like C1, losing the original expression.

Executing [`RELATE MANY SELECTION`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/relate-many-selection) inside an "On Startup" database method caused the structure file to be opened read-only on the next restart. The structure file itself was not actually locked, and restarting the application again resolved the issue.

In 4D Write Pro, applying an underline or strikethrough to text rendered in Small Caps mode (capital letters at lowercase height) drew the line inconsistently, positioned slightly too low relative to the capital letters.
When a Quick Report's master table contained a deleted field, the report inserted the wrong field and displayed an invalid field number instead of handling the gap in the field list correctly.
Restoring the database settings' backup schedule to factory/default settings did not actually reset the backup values.

For a form object (such as a text variable) with both a choice list and a required-value list assigned, newly added list items appeared correctly in the displayed choice list, but selecting one of those new items triggered a "value is not allowed" error instead of being accepted.
Semaphores created by a component were not released when the process that created them terminated, leaking the semaphore. Semaphores created by the host application were unaffected.
For a Quick Report embedded in a form, selecting the report's output destination from the contextual menu raised error 9850.

On the 64-bit Windows version, printing in landscape orientation using the legacy GDI print layer did not work in print preview: the paper orientation setting was ignored and output could not be produced in landscape.

After dynamically duplicating columns in an array-type listbox whose "lk auto row height" property was set to "lk yes", deleting one of the duplicated columns with [`LISTBOX DELETE COLUMN`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-delete-column) crashed the 4D client. The crash did not occur when automatic row height was disabled.
On Mac, in the 64-bit version only, dragging and dropping text between two text areas copied the text instead of moving it; copying should only occur when Option is held during the drag.

When a related one-to-one record had already been deleted, retrieving its [record number](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/record-number) via [`SELECTION TO ARRAY`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/selection-to-array) returned 0 instead of -1. Since 0 is itself a valid record number, this made it impossible to distinguish a deleted related record from a real record at position 0.

Converting a 4D Write document to 4D Write Pro caused anchored image field references to be displayed incorrectly: the referenced image itself was shown in place of the reference placeholder. New documents created directly in Write Pro were not affected.

With single-click edit mode enabled on a listbox, holding Control or Shift and clicking a non-enterable column failed to extend the multi-row selection as expected; clicking an enterable column worked correctly.
When sending mail in quoted-printable mode, the MAIL command wrote the text body's line breaks using CR only instead of the correct CRLF sequence.

In 4D Write Pro, running [`ST FREEZE EXPRESSIONS`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/st-freeze-expressions) caused page-number expressions inserted in the footer (e.g. "page x of total pages") to be evaluated incorrectly, such as always showing "page 1 of 0". This is expected in principle since freezing header/footer expressions evaluates them only once — total page count remains accurate but the page number itself is fixed at 1 — so page-specific values should be avoided in frozen header/footer expressions.
When updating or inserting data into a MySQL 8 database through the Unicode ODBC driver from 4D, the last character of a string value was dropped and not recorded.

In 4D Write Pro, after setting document text to bold, calling [`WP GET ATTRIBUTES`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-attributes) inside the On Data Change event that immediately follows returned an incorrect value for the wk font attribute instead of reflecting the current formatting.
Calling [`OPEN SETTINGS WINDOW`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-settings-window) on a client to display the "User settings for data" data-file selector page crashed 4D Remote.

Duplicating a form object that had a placeholder set, using [`OBJECT DUPLICATE`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-duplicate) on a variable, caused the application to crash as soon as the form was closed.

Double-clicking the edge of a listbox column header auto-resizes the column to fit its content, but if the visible rows included hidden rows, the column was instead resized down to its minimum width rather than fitting the actual content.
On Mac, trying to create a new database on a network drive, a mounted disk image, or an otherwise connected volume raised an error instead of succeeding.

On the 64-bit version, printed labels used a different layout than the 32-bit version: for example, a label form set up for 3 columns by 14 rows in 32-bit printed as 4 columns by 11 rows in 64-bit, even with identical form, page, and print settings.

Passing an empty string as the first parameter of [`EXPORT DATA`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/export-data) was supposed to open a "Save As" dialog for choosing the export file name, but it opened the "Export" dialog instead, and the project's export settings were not applied to the resulting export.

In client-server mode, calling dataClass.query() or entitySelection.query() with an [`ORDER BY`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/order-by) clause placed anywhere other than at the very end of the query string returned an unexpectedly empty entity selection instead of the correctly ordered results.

On the 64-bit version, some old label definition files (.4LB), including ones created back in v15, could fail to load. These files had been produced with a bug present in older versions of the label editor; the fix allows such malformed files to be loaded correctly.
The English-language resource files 4DClientEN.xlf and DataToolLogEN.xlf contained a spelling error, with "occured" used instead of "occurred" in an error message.

On macOS, if a system dialog was displayed via a command such as [Create document](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-document) after a sheet (spreadsheet-style) window had already been opened, 4D could freeze entirely.

In the Form Editor, moving a 4D Web area or a 4D View Pro area from one view to another did not persist: after closing and reopening the form, the area reverted to its previously assigned view. Write Pro areas were unaffected.

On 64-bit Mac, [SET FILE TO PASTEBOARD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-file-to-pasteboard) only placed the first of several supplied file paths onto the pasteboard, silently dropping the rest instead of copying all of them.

In the Form Editor (development mode), changing a list box header/footer/column style sheet to bold did not immediately refresh the editor's on-screen rendering, so the header appeared not to update even though the property list setting had changed.

After creating an entity selection with [USE ENTITY SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/use-entity-selection) and then calling [DUPLICATE RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/duplicate-record) followed by [SAVE RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/save-record), the entity selection was updated incorrectly: it ended up containing the newly duplicated record instead of the original current record.

A PDF file attached via [MAIL New attachment](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-new-attachment) (using the SMTP transporter) sometimes failed to appear in the iOS Mail app when the message also included an image attachment alongside the PDF. Sending the PDF alone worked fine, and Android devices were unaffected.

When a parameter passed to a command such as [Execute on server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/execute-on-server) was not given an explicit type declaration, compilation failed instead of the parameter defaulting to a Variant, as expected for automatic variant typing.

When a 4D Write Pro document was exported to HTML, empty lines incorrectly picked up whitespace styled with the formatting (e.g. underline) of the preceding text, which could distort line and paragraph layout.

When importing a UTF-8 encoded CSV file (or an Excel .xlsx file) through the "Import data from file" dialog, associated with [IMPORT DATA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/import-data), Arabic characters were not decoded correctly and displayed incorrectly in the import preview area.

When a button had both a standard action and an object method configured, the object method ran before the standard action instead of after. This ordering had never been formally specified; the fix standardizes it so the object method now generally runs before the standard action, except for the "Delete record" standard action, tied to [DELETE RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/delete-record), which still shows its confirmation dialog first because of the automatic prompt it displays.

Calling [RELATE ONE SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/relate-one-selection) during a transaction that had used [SET QUERY AND LOCK](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-query-and-lock) incorrectly raised a "record is locked" error, even though SET QUERY AND LOCK is only documented to affect specific query-type commands, not relation-selection commands.
The DatePicker Display Dialog widget method ignored the initial date value passed via its defaultDate parameter, so the widget did not display the requested default date on open.
On macOS Mojave and later, the vertical alignment of items in pop-up menu lists was rendered slightly higher than in prior 4D versions, producing a visually inconsistent menu appearance.

On 64-bit Mac, setting the spooler document name option via [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option) had no effect on the default file name proposed by the "Save as PDF" or "Save as PostScript" print dialog options.
The 4D Server crashed when a remote 4D Client inserted a BLOB array into an external data file.

Converting a 4D Write document containing tables (built from tabs and framing lines) into 4D Write Pro could produce inaccurate results: vertical tab-based lines could change from black to white, the spacing between paragraph text and framing lines could shrink, and horizontal lines could disappear. The color regression has been fixed, but layout differences from 4D Write's tab/line-based pseudo-tables remain expected; complex tables are recommended to be rebuilt as HTML tables after conversion.

On Mac, if the mobile-project table list was already displayed, the file-selection dialog for opening or creating a 4D for iOS mobile project could not be opened from the toolbar or menu, leaving 4D unresponsive.

On Windows, in a built SDI (single-window) application, canceling the login screen left a hidden background task running instead of exiting; the application could then not be launched again until that orphaned task was manually terminated in Task Manager.

A 4D Write Pro document exported to .docx format via [WP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-export-document) could sometimes trigger an error when the resulting file was opened in Microsoft Word.
When converting a 4D View document to 4D View Pro, numeric formats using a comma as the decimal separator were incorrectly converted to use a period instead.

The spell-check dictionaries for certain languages, such as French and Norwegian, were assigned the same numeric identifier, causing them to be confused. On Mac, the fix changes the system spell checker to use locale identifiers (like fr-FR or en-US) instead of numeric IDs; the Hunspell-based spell checker still relies on IDs issued directly by its library.

Using the standard action image/width?value= on an anchored image in a 4D Write Pro document, triggered from a button's click event, deselected the image and prevented its width from being changed; inline images were unaffected. The fix preserves the image selection across focus loss when the "Always show selection" property is enabled.

The standard action spell/suggestion?index= produced no suggestions when triggered from a custom contextual menu item, apparently because the spell-check library had not been initialized; running the spell checker once from 4D's built-in contextual menu first worked around the issue.

Converting a 4D View document to 4D View Pro could lose line-break information within a cell, causing multi-line cell text to collapse onto a single line. This occurred because converted spreadsheets did not enable the wordwrap option by default; since View Pro only honors multiline formatting when wordwrap is also enabled (unlike 4D View, where multiline was always on independent of wordwrap), users converting documents where 4D View had wordwrap disabled must now enable wordwrap manually afterward to restore line wrapping.

On Mac, in Project mode only, applying [OBJECT SET RGB COLORS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-rgb-colors) to a rectangle object with a line width of 0 or 1 caused the top and right borders to render incorrectly at runtime. The fix also adds consistent support for "transparent" and empty-string values for both foreground and background colors.

On Windows, when the computer was offline and a browser accessed 4D's built-in web server using the hostname localhost, a runtime error claiming that "some port numbers are already in use" was returned instead of a successful connection.

[Drop position](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/drop-position) failed to return -1 when an item was dropped onto an empty row area of a list box, unless the row height was set to automatic sizing.

In a 4D View Pro area, changing a cell's value programmatically with [VP SET TEXT VALUE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-set-text-value) did not refresh the formula bar to reflect the new value; clicking away and back, or double-clicking the cell, was needed to force the update.

After locating a list box column via "Search in Design" and jumping to the Form Editor, deleting that column from the contextual menu instead removed the column immediately to its left. Jumping to the form from the Explorer did not exhibit the problem.

On 64-bit Windows, in application (SDI) mode, clicking the window's top-right close button failed to quit the built application, whereas quitting via the Quit menu item or the Control+Q shortcut worked correctly. Closing via the title-bar button requires the "Quit" standard action to be assigned to a menu item.

In a 4D View Pro spreadsheet, deleting rows that contained cell references and then dragging to force recalculation of the remaining references could leave some cell values incorrect. The fix updates the underlying SpreadJS library to version 13.0.6.

ORDA computed relation attributes based only on the field's own value rather than the actual primary key when a relation's source field was not itself the primary key, which could cause entity links to be lost.

After converting a 4D View document to 4D View Pro, cells containing time values did not display correctly: the underlying value was preserved, but its time format was not applied, leaving the cell appearing blank or malformed.

On macOS 10.15 (Catalina), 4D or 4D Server could crash immediately after launch if a browser-downloaded disk image's installation folder (e.g. "4D v17.3") was dragged as a whole onto the hard disk and 4D was launched from within it, rather than dragging the individual application. This happened because Gatekeeper could not verify the app and launched it in a translocated (quarantined) state, identifiable in crash logs by a "Translocated Process" path under /private/var/folders/. The fix prevents translocation when the folder is drag-installed, though un-notarized v17.x/17R6 builds may still require launching with the Control key held down the first time after upgrading to Catalina.
In a 4D View Pro area, the Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z undo shortcut did not work. On macOS this only failed while editing a cell, whereas on Windows undo was broken at all times in the area.
Opening a label definition file (.4lbp) that contained a rectangle with rounded corners in the Label Editor produced an unexpected error message instead of opening the file.

When an ORDA query used the IN operator with a collection of strings, a trailing wildcard character (@) on the last string in the collection was ignored, causing the query to return incorrect results.
Using ORDA to query an object field for [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) values returned incorrect results instead of correctly matching entities whose object field was null.

On macOS only, clicking a 3D push button no taller than 22 pixels with its font color set to "Automatic" failed to switch the text color from black to white while pressed in light mode (the correct behavior); the text incorrectly stayed black. Dark mode was unaffected since black text is expected there.
On Windows, clicking "Preview" in a Quick Report when XPS was not installed on the machine raised a syntax error instead of gracefully handling the missing component.

Calling the [SOAP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/soap-request) command from within a component method always returned False, making it impossible to execute a web service (SOAP) request from component code.

On macOS 10.15 (Catalina), executing [DOCUMENT LIST](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/document-list) against a folder located on the same disk as the system volume was roughly 10 times slower than in 4D v17; folders on a separate volume were unaffected. The fix optimizes handling of the combined Mac HD - Data volume layout introduced in Catalina.

In Project mode only, a listbox using a "current selection" or "named selection" data source was missing the "Coordinates and Sizing / Row Height" property in its property list, a setting that was correctly shown in binary (non-project) mode.
In 4D Write Pro, pasting externally copied data into the top-left cell of a table inserted the pasted content outside the table boundaries instead of into the cell itself.

In Client/Server mode, an entity added to a selection via `$selection.add()` (entitySelection.add()) was not included in the current selection created by [USE ENTITY SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/use-entity-selection), so the command failed to return the correct record for that entity.

HTTPS connections could not be established using cert.pem and key.pem certificates issued by Comodo. The root cause was that these certificate files were delimited with "-----BEGINCERTIFICATE-----" (missing a space) instead of the standard "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----"; the fix makes 4D internally tolerate and correct this malformed delimiter.

On Windows, switching to Compiled mode from the Run menu, then displaying an [ALERT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/alert) dialog from the On Startup database method and closing it, left the Run menu missing afterward, making it impossible to switch back from Compiled to Interpreted mode.

Converting a corrupted 4D View document to 4D View Pro could freeze or crash the application. The document could appear to work correctly beforehand, giving no indication of the underlying damage prior to conversion.

Emails sent through the SMTP transporter had their subject line encoded incorrectly; the resulting quoted-printable text could show up literally (unencoded) in the iOS Mail app instead of being decoded to the intended subject text.

When "Encrypt Client-Server Communications" was enabled, a client that disconnected could remain listed indefinitely on the server as a ghost user, even after the normal client/server connection timeout had elapsed.

On macOS, in a database converted from an earlier 4D version with the compatibility option "Save methods as Unicode" left disabled, closing and reopening a method that contained a block comment (/* */) converted it back into legacy line comments (//); for inline commands this had the side effect of turning all subsequent code on the line into a comment. The fix instead prevents block comments from being entered at all in databases where this compatibility option is off.

File names of attachments added via [MAIL New attachment](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-new-attachment) were not properly MIME-encoded in the generated header, resulting in badly encoded, non-ASCII attachment file names.
In Project mode only, a variable name bound to an object such as a button could not be removed from the property list, preventing the binding from being cleared through the interface.
On macOS only, passing a 4D Write BLOB to [WP New](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-new) in order to convert it to a 4D Write Pro document could crash the application.
In Project mode only, rectangle object borders were not drawn cleanly at runtime, producing a badly rendered outline instead of a crisp border.

In a project database, the "Line Color" (stroke) attribute could not be removed from the Property List for rectangle, oval, and line objects using Control+click to reset it, unlike in binary databases.

After exporting a binary database to Project mode, grid (matrix) objects on forms were not converted correctly: their border color was rendered black instead of grey. This happened because the binary database's grid objects had a border style of "None", so no stroke color was recorded for them; the fix ensures a stroke color is set when converting grid objects to SVG.

At runtime in Project mode only, a picture variable placed on a form displayed incorrectly because its height did not match the height used in binary mode, caused by an internal automatic resize being applied to the picture.

Typing a word followed by a period inside a new-style block comment incorrectly triggered the object-notation autocomplete popup, showing a list of candidate property names as if the text were object code rather than plain comment text.

In Project mode only, at runtime a button's icon could be drawn outside the button's rectangle. This occurred because a line break within the button title caused the object's height to be auto-corrected; the fix ensures that height adjustment no longer happens for non-standard buttons.
When sending mail via the transporter with the "mail mode UTF8" constant, the '?' character in the message subject was not encoded correctly.
In Project mode only, grouping a set of objects that included a line object failed to include that line object in the resulting group, so it was not drawn as part of the group.
Converting a 4D View document containing a specific formula to 4D View Pro could trigger error #20, "4D View Document is corrupted", preventing the conversion from completing.

On macOS (64-bit) only, after using [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option) to set a custom spooler document name and then calling [PRINT SETTINGS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-settings), the configured name was not reflected in the file name shown by the "Save as PDF" button in the lower-left corner of the print dialog.

On Windows only, calling [HIDE TOOL BAR](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/hide-tool-bar) while the application was running in the background incorrectly triggered the "On application foreground move" database event, so simply toggling the toolbar's visibility when another application came to the foreground made the application unable to move from the foreground at the wrong time.
When a form's platform property was set to "print", checkboxes on that form were rendered with a badly designed, crooked-looking vector image.
Calling [VP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-export-document) before the 4D View Pro area's document had fully finished loading caused the application to crash.

When a standalone application session connected to a server via [Open datastore](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-datastore) was quit, non-secured sessions on 4D Server were properly closed, but the corresponding TLS (secured) sessions remained open instead of being terminated.

In 4D Write Pro, when [ST FREEZE EXPRESSIONS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/st-freeze-expressions) froze an expression whose evaluated result was an empty string (""), the command inserted a single space (" ") into the document text instead of leaving it empty.

On macOS only, in the [On REST Authentication database method](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/on-rest-authentication-database-method), the 4th parameter ($4), which returns the client's IP address, incorrectly prefixed IPv4 addresses with "::ffff:" instead of returning them in plain form.

On Windows only, printing a form with [PRINT SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-selection) had been slower since v15/v17.x depending on the printing margins used, with no workaround other than enabling the "Legacy printing layer" option in [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option) to fall back to the older GDI print layer, or avoiding changes to the print margins. The root cause was that the Direct2D print layer sent three separate driver commands per print job, each beginning with the same control sequence ("CT~~CD,~CC^~CT~"); some printer drivers (e.g. Zebra GK420d label printers) reset their paper settings on every occurrence of that sequence, adding unnecessary delay. The fix sends that initial sequence only once so paper settings are not repeatedly reset, restoring the faster GDI-era print speed.

After opening a session with [Open datastore](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-datastore), the [Process activity](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/process-activity) command's returned object should report "windows" or "mac" in the "hostType" attribute for that session, but it incorrectly returned "browser" instead.

In the method editor, using "Search references..." from the contextual menu to find calls to a command incorrectly matched all textual occurrences of the command name, including those inside comments, rather than limiting results to actual (uncommented) code lines using the command; constants and plugin commands were affected the same way.

Launching 4D Server as a Windows service with a remote data file (.4DD) on a mapped network drive failed to open the database. The fix requires the service to run under the same user account that mounted the network drive; otherwise 4D Server still cannot resolve the network path.
On Windows, importing certain CSV files unexpectedly raised error 215 instead of completing the import, with the failure tied to specific file content rather than the CSV import feature in general.

In 4D Write Pro documents, when the "show invisible characters" display option was turned on, space characters stopped being shown at all, even though a visible dot/marker should appear at each space position like it does for other non-printing characters.

After sending mail with [SMTP New transporter](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/smtp-new-transporter), if the method then called [ALERT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/alert) and the dialog was left on screen for five minutes or more before being dismissed, resuming execution triggered an SSL read failure instead of returning cleanly.

On 4D Server (client/server only), executing a formula that recursively referenced itself crashed the application; since such recursive object references cannot legitimately be passed over the network, the fix instead makes 4D return a generic network error ("Attempt to read beyond end of stream") rather than crashing.
Right-clicking the context menu of a Quick Report editor embedded as a custom form object triggered a runtime error (error 9852) instead of showing the menu normally.

In Project mode, when a form object's size was anchored relative to an object group rather than to a plain object, converting the database to project mode computed the resulting form size incorrectly, since anchors cannot legitimately reference a group (only objects). The fix clarifies the conversion logic: if another object's bottom-right coordinates coincide with the group's, that object becomes the anchor; otherwise the form size anchor is reset to "automatic" and a warning is written to the conversion log.

In Project mode client/server, even though the structure file was opened as read-only, 4D Server still allowed adding tables and methods via the file menu (though such changes could not actually be saved); the disabled/protected menu items should have been unusable in this case.

In some cases, running [BACKUP](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/backup) and then switching to a different data file with [OPEN DATA FILE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-data-file) unexpectedly crashed the 4D Server application instead of completing the file switch.
A built standalone application failed to launch in MSC (Maintenance and Security Center) mode even when the Alt key was held down during startup, so the recovery/maintenance interface never appeared.
In Project mode only, after converting a database to a project, help tips displayed their internal tip name instead of the actual tip content/text.

When using an SMTP_Attachment or Transporter object on a system whose locale was not set to Japanese, attaching a file with a Japanese file name to an outgoing email returned error -43 (invalid path) instead of sending correctly, and the resulting attachment could end up corrupted.
Converting a 4D View document to 4D View Pro did not correctly carry over the font size applied to cells, so text appeared in the wrong size after conversion.

Converting a 4D View document to 4D View Pro could fail to correctly translate certain conditional number formats (for example multi-section formats combining euro currency, negative-in-parentheses, and a blue color for positive/zero values), causing cells whose value was zero to be shown with a blue background/text instead of the expected white/default appearance.

On macOS Catalina (10.15), 4D Server's application menus became unresponsive after launch and could only be re-enabled by sending the application to the background and then bringing it back to the foreground. The fix revisits the activation policy of the launched application: when the "--headless" command-line parameter is passed, the policy changes after startup, causing the Dock icon to flash briefly and then disappear; setting `LSUIElement` to `YES` in Info.plist now gives normal user-experience behavior priority over headless mode.

Converting a 4D View document to 4D View Pro did not preserve the "[h]:mm" custom time format used for summed time values, so a total that should read as "26:30" (over 24 hours) was instead displayed as "02:00"; the fix ensures the "[h]" format is retained after conversion for interoperability.
In ORDA, running a query with the 'in' operator against an indexed object (Object) field could crash the application.

After configuring print settings such as paper size, orientation, black-and-white, or duplex with [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option), subsequently calling [SET CURRENT PRINTER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-current-printer) unexpectedly reset those print parameters instead of leaving them intact.

In the Database Settings dialog's "Memory" section, unchecking "Calculation of adaptive cache" should reveal an "Apply" button for entering a manual cache size, but the button was missing, a regression dating back to v17 R5.

In ORDA, querying an indexed object (Object) field using the 'in' operator together with a wildcard ('@') string did not return a record that had just been added while inside a transaction, producing an incomplete/incorrect result set.

On Windows only, in a 4D Write Pro document, combining [ST INSERT EXPRESSION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/st-insert-expression) and [WP SET TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-set-text) to insert text containing a line break (\n) caused characters to overlap/be drawn on top of each other at the break position instead of wrapping onto a new line correctly.
4D failed to start up entirely when the operating system's region/language format was set to Thai, preventing any use of the application under that locale.
On the Mac version of 4D for iOS, attempting to display the "Action" section of a mobile project triggered a syntax error dialog (#-10716) instead of opening the section.

On Windows 64-bit applications only, a menu item's keyboard shortcut stopped working (and the shortcut indicator could fail to display) when another menu item nearby had a style option such as Italic or Underline applied.

In Project mode, calling [FORM GET OBJECTS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-get-objects) did not return the data source (variable) name for web area objects, even though this data source name was expected to still be exported so that WA commands could keep executing against the variable name as before.

When tracing a method that contained block comments ("/*" ... "*/"), the debugger's [TRACE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/trace) window could highlight the wrong line, placing the cursor on a line that was not actually the one being executed because the comment lines threw off the line-number offset.
Calling the `.lastIndexOf` collection method on an empty collection crashed the application instead of returning a not-found result.
Canceling an export operation that was started from a 4D View Pro area's File menu caused the View Pro area to hang; the only way to recover was to close the form.

When converting a 4D View document to 4D View Pro, a cell-specific alignment setting that differed from the alignment applied to its entire column was not carried over correctly, so the converted document lost that per-cell alignment override.

On the Mac version of 4D for iOS, dragging a row up or down within the listbox of the mobile project's "Action" section to reorder actions crashed the application. The underlying issue affected any collection-type listbox whose current-item reference used an expression like `object.property`.

In 4D Write Pro, resizing a picture using the palette widget had no effect on the picture's size. Only inline pictures can be resized via the widget tool; anchored pictures still require a manual mouse-drag resize.
In 4D Write Pro, using the top toolbar widget to change the border color or border width of a section, paragraph, or picture unintentionally also reset the border style to a solid line.

In 4D Write Pro, trying to remove the border of a selected section or picture via the top toolbar failed to clear that border; instead, the paragraph's border was removed while the section/picture border remained, whereas the standard action `section/borderStyle?value=none` was expected to run.

In a 4D Write Pro document, changing only the vertical text alignment and then exporting and reimporting the document caused the new alignment value to be lost, since it was never actually saved into the document.

Passing text enclosed in "<" and ">" characters to the `SVG_New_textArea` and `SVG_SET_TEXTAREA_TEXT` commands produced invalid XML output, so the text could not be displayed; escaping the characters as `<` and `>` did not work around the problem either.

Dragging and dropping a line from a listbox onto a button caused [GET PASTEBOARD DATA TYPE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-pasteboard-data-type) to return no value the second time it was called from the `On Drop` event, effectively resetting the command's parameters mid-drop.

In Project mode, clicking a checkbox or button with the Form Editor's "Text" tool to edit its title displayed the text-editing zone in the wrong position, appearing centered and shifted upward instead of aligning with the object.

In Project mode, a text input object that had been disabled via [OBJECT SET ENABLED](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-enabled) still triggered an `On Getting Focus` event when clicked, even though a disabled object should not be able to receive focus.

Converting a 4D View document containing the "Century Gothic" font to 4D View Pro did not preserve that font correctly, substituting Times New Roman on Windows or Arial on Mac instead. The problem was specific to font names containing a space; the fix changes the conversion format so the font list is written as `'Century Gothic,Arial'` rather than the malformed `'Century Gothic',Arial`.
In Project mode only, a table form's Design-mode window title and its entry in the Window menu did not include the owning table's name as a prefix, unlike the expected naming convention.
In the Form Editor's property list, property names failed to display at all when the interface language was set to Spanish or Portuguese, leaving the panel effectively blank for those localizations.

On Windows, after setting the current printer to the Generic PDF driver with [SET CURRENT PRINTER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-current-printer), configuring output-to-file with [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option), printing via [PRINT SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-selection), and then reopening the print settings dialog with [PRINT SETTINGS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-settings), the "Print To File" checkbox remained checked even though printing had already completed.

When a MAIL object's bodyStructure.type was set to 'multipart/related', the SMTP transporter ignored it and always used 'multipart/mixed' instead. For example, converting a 4D Write Pro document to MIME with [MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) and sending it caused Mac mail clients to display the inline attachment a second time, after the message body.
In Project mode only, executing [EXPORT DIF](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/export-dif) caused the application to crash.
In Project mode, the File menu's Print command could not be executed while the Form Editor was in use, leaving the print option effectively disabled for JSON-based forms.

In 4D Write Pro, changing the page margins using the widget tool had no effect on the document. The fix ensures margin and padding changes apply to the currently selected section rather than being expected to affect (or silently fail to affect) the whole document.

Input fields displaying 4D Write Pro document properties did not automatically refresh to reflect changes made in the Write Pro area, unlike input fields bound to ordinary object properties, which stay in sync with the underlying object.

On Mac, printing a document containing paragraphs with background color to PDF and viewing it in the Preview app showed a thin white border line between paragraphs (Google Chrome and Windows were unaffected). Previously, a `crispEdges` rendering setting was applied to shape edges to avoid this artifact, but not all PDF viewers support `crispEdges` consistently; the fix now pre-analyzes paragraph background colors so consecutive paragraphs with the same background are rendered as a single shape, giving clean fills on screen and in print regardless of `crispEdges` support.

On Mac, text output via the [MESSAGE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/message) command displayed with garbled/oversized characters once the text no longer fit within the window height and needed to scroll. The overlay bitmap accounted for the window's scale factor (resolution), but that information was apparently not passed to the drawing API, which uses logical coordinates.
On a list form, a button object configured with the standard "Accept" or "Cancel" action could not be disabled using [OBJECT SET ENABLED](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-enabled).

Launching a built standalone (desktop) application while holding the Alt key displayed the startup options screen as expected, but choosing "Restore from backup" closed the application instead of launching the MSC (Maintenance and Security Center) tool.

When the `<hardlink>` tag was set in buildApp.4DSettings, the resulting build failed to create the lastDataPath.xml file. The fix ensures the hardlink tag is no longer applied/used for single-user application builds.
In 4D Write Pro, changing a document's measurement unit (wk layout unit) mid-way caused right-aligned text to switch to left alignment.
When a mail object's header field contained an umlaut character or an underscore, the SMTP transporter encoded the value incorrectly.

When a mail object's "to" or "from" header field contained a double-quote character, the SMTP transporter encoded the value incorrectly. The fix encodes an address like `Hans "Otte" Meier <xxx@4d.com>` using `=?UTF-8?Q?=22?=` for the quote; this displays correctly in Thunderbird and Outlook, though Apple Mail appears to drop the quotes.

Clicking a cell in a 4D View Pro area and clearing its content with the Delete key did not trigger the form's On After Edit event, so code depending on that event to react to cell deletions was never called.
Documents printed with QR PRINT had extra margins added on all four sides, matching the printer's non-printable ("dead") margin area, in addition to the margins actually specified.
On Windows, printing a report without preview via QR PRINT produced an XPS preview with incorrect margins, adding extra top/left/bottom/right spacing equal to the printer's non-printable dead margin.
In Project mode, a JSON form's text input object with its dataSourceTypeHint property set to "undefined" (equivalent to "None" in the property list) was incorrectly treated as type "text".

Issuing a POST request to a non-local (remote) URL with [HTTP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) could sometimes return an empty response body even though the httpStatus was correctly reported as 200.
On Mac OS, the underline font attribute was not applied to the titles of certain objects, specifically buttons, check boxes, and radio buttons.

In 4D View Pro, the spellchecking option was missing from the cell's contextual menu while editing, even though that menu must first be enabled via [WA SET PREFERENCE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wa-set-preference). This left users unable to invoke spellcheck from the right-click menu during inline cell editing.

The command [DISTINCT ATTRIBUTE VALUES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/distinct-attribute-values) returned an empty array instead of the expected unique values when applied to a set of records that included duplicates.

Moving a column in a quick report displayed inside a subform did not refresh the on-screen column order, even though the underlying report data was actually reordered correctly. This made the subform's displayed layout appear stale relative to the real report content.

On the Spanish localization only, calling [SET ABOUT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-about) at application startup (from a built double-clickable application) caused the app to crash immediately after launch.

On Windows, calling [OBJECT SET FONT SIZE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-font-size) immediately followed by two calls to [OBJECT SET FONT STYLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-font-style) crashed the application.

Compiling a host structure raised a compiler error for any component method that was called with a Variant-typed parameter, blocking compilation of otherwise valid code that used Variant parameters across a component boundary.

On macOS, displaying text set in a barcode font added a stray trailing space character at the end of the text, which corrupted the encoded data and made the resulting barcode unreadable. The issue did not reproduce on macOS 10.15 Catalina.

For structures created in very old versions of 4D, design windows left open when the database was closed were not restored to their previous position and size after restarting. This occurred because such legacy structures could have the "do not restore Design mode windows" setting enabled, an option no longer exposed in the current version's Database Settings, leaving affected users unable to turn it off themselves.

The mail transporter produced incorrect quoted-printable encoding when sending messages, corrupting the message body. As a result, Apple Mail displayed only the plain-text part and omitted the HTML part entirely (Gmail displayed both parts), apparently because the MIME content contained extraneous line breaks.
Applying the SVG_ROTATION_CENTERED component method to an ellipse object failed to rotate it around the specified center coordinates, leaving the ellipse in its original orientation.

On Mac in binary (non-project) mode, using the MSC "Encryption" page to save an encryption key froze the application whenever the default save location happened to be inside the application package itself, since that location is write-protected.

Calling [SET DATABASE PARAMETER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-parameter) with the `SMTP log` selector from the client side in Client/Server mode unexpectedly returned an "Invalid parameter" error instead of succeeding.

In 4D Write Pro, after printing a document while the Header area had keyboard focus, focus did not return to the Header area once printing finished; switching to another application and back restored the ability to focus the header again.

In Client/Server mode, executing a SQL statement (via EXECUTE IMMEDIATE) containing a very long WHERE...IN clause (roughly 11,930 values) triggered a stack overflow error instead of running the query.

A crash could occur in [PROCESS 4D TAGS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/process-4d-tags) when a method invoked from a `#4DEVAL` tag attempted to load a picture, indicating the tag-processing engine did not safely handle picture loading triggered from evaluated expressions.

In Project mode, when a database was exported as a project, style sheets containing font names with characters outside a-z were not properly escaped during conversion to CSS, causing a CSS parsing error at startup.

When converting a 4D View document to 4D View Pro, cells whose value was 0 and whose number format was `###,##0;(###,##0)` lost their correct text color after conversion, so the zero value no longer displayed with the color defined by the original format.

Converting a 4D View document containing cells formatted with a "00"-style pattern (e.g. `...;[#FF0000]-00;...`) to 4D View Pro produced incorrect displayed values in those cells, showing the wrong number rather than the properly zero-padded original value.

When converting a database structure to v18, methods that were very old and had not been modified in a long time could have their comments unexpectedly stripped out during conversion. Updating such methods in v17 before upgrading avoided the issue.
In a 4D Write Pro area, repeatedly opening the contextual menu when it contained several nested submenu levels could crash the application.

Exporting a large 4D View Pro document (30 MB or more) could fail with a JavaScript error reporting excessive memory use. The fix introduces a 5-minute export timeout; actual export duration still depends on the machine's hardware specs.

In a 4D View Pro area, a time value exceeding 24 hours returned by a method was displayed as a clock time instead of an elapsed duration, ignoring the cell's format setting. To correctly display values over 24 hours, the cell format must be set to `[hh]:mm:ss`.

Calling the `checkConnection()` method on an [SMTP New transporter](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/smtp-new-transporter) object against certain mail servers returned errors 42, 43, and 49 even when the connection actually succeeded (Google's SMTP server and the legacy Internet Commands were unaffected). The fix corrects a case where `success` was wrongly returned as `True`; note that when connecting to servers not supporting TLS 1.1+, an error response is expected behavior, and for servers limited to TLS 1.2 or below you must lower the security baseline with [SET DATABASE PARAMETER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-parameter)(Min TLS version; TLSv1_0) — this applies to all transporters (SMTP, POP3, IMAP).

On macOS, running [FOLDER LIST](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/folder-list) or [DOCUMENT LIST](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/document-list) against a folder created by the Box desktop app (installed from box.com) returned an empty array instead of the folder's actual contents.

On a machine where 4D Server had never been installed, or where the `ProgramData/4D Server/VSS` file had been deleted, the VSS service failed to start even when 4D Server was launched with administrator privileges. Running the `installService.cmd` script found in the `Resources/VSS` folder works around the issue.

When a SOAP web service method returned a text array, retrieving it on the client side with [WEB SERVICE GET RESULT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-service-get-result) crashed the application, because the XML returned by the server was malformed. The issue could be reproduced with a method built via [ARRAY TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/array-text) and [SOAP DECLARATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/soap-declaration) declaring a text array output.

On macOS, the highly sensitive tracking of an Apple Magic Mouse 2 could easily trigger spurious drag-and-drop events in the Method editor's Methods page: even when the form object's *On Drag Over* event set `$0` to `-1` to reject the drop, the mouse pointer still changed to the "drop allowed" cursor icon.

Emails sent via a transporter object and viewed in the iOS or macOS Mail app showed inline images as regular attachments instead of embedding them in the message body; Outlook was not affected. This appears to be a regression of a problem previously fixed under ACI0100297.

In Project mode, dragging-and-dropping or copying/pasting a form object whose picture property referenced a picture file that no longer existed on disk triggered a runtime error instead of handling the missing reference gracefully.

Converting a 3D button that had no picture pathname set into a JSON-based form produced an invalid `icon` property value (the literal string `"/RESOURCES/"`) rather than omitting or correctly nulling the property.

When an incoming HTTP request body began with the byte 0x000D (carriage return), the 4D Web Server failed to process the request correctly on first receipt: beyond taking longer to receive, the BLOB size read via `GET HTTP BODY` did not match the `Content-Length` announced in the request header.

On Windows, calling [OBJECT GET BEST SIZE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-best-size) on a list box column returned a different "best width" in v18 than it did in v14 (also reproducible by double-clicking a list box header column separator). The discrepancy occurs because list boxes created before v14 are still drawn with the legacy GDI rendering mode (which can also be forced via database parameter 107 set to 2), whereas newer ones use DirectWrite; differing widths between rendering modes are expected, but the fix addresses cases where text was actually getting clipped.

On Windows, executing the [TRACE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/trace) command on 4D Server while the Server Administration window was maximized, causing the debugger to open server-side, crashed the application.

Converting a 4D View Pro document to SVG with [VP Convert to picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-to-picture) did not preserve the correct cell heights and widths in the resulting image.

On macOS, vertically resizing a list-type subform caused incomplete redrawing, leaving a gray area on screen; clicking into the subform forced it to redraw correctly. As of v18, an `On Resize` event is now triggered whenever a subform is resized (via splitter drag, splitter value assignment, [SET WINDOW RECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-window-rect), [OBJECT SET COORDINATES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-coordinates), [OBJECT MOVE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-move), or a parent form resize/move), letting a method run once the resize completes; note that `On Timer` is no longer fired during a subform resize, whereas previously it fired regardless of the configured interval.
4D View Pro commands lacked tooltips in the Method editor, and the syntax shown in the editor's status bar for these commands was incomplete.

Using [OBJECT SET RGB COLORS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-rgb-colors) to set the foreground color of an object whose border style was set to "none" caused a border to appear anyway; this spurious border could not be removed afterward even by calling [OBJECT SET BORDER STYLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-border-style).

In compiled mode, calling [OB SET](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-set) on a two-dimensional array returned a runtime error. Applications compiled under v17 could reproduce this after being upgraded and recompiled.
On macOS, printing a group box omitted its bottom border line from the printed output.

Using [METHOD SET CODE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/method-set-code) to create a new method returned an error in Project mode, while in binary mode it created the method but left it empty. In Project mode, restarting the structure revealed that the method had actually been created despite the reported error, and re-running the command against the now-existing method successfully set its code.

In the method editor, the "Find references" feature returned incorrect results when searching for parameters, methods, or project forms: string literals inside comments were being wrongly included in the matches, even though only real code references (commands, plugins, constants) should have been eligible.

In 4D Mobile (4D for iOS), moving focus to the filter/search field in the Data section sometimes left the down-arrow indicator improperly rendered, apparently because the required font was not installed on the Mac.

On Mac, when a button was disabled with [OBJECT SET ENABLED](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-enabled), its background dimmed correctly but the title text stayed black instead of graying out, so the disabled state was not visually communicated.
In compiled mode only, self-assigning a picture variable to itself (e.g. `vPict:=vPict`) destroyed the picture's contents instead of leaving it unchanged.

On Windows, upgrading a 4D Server application from v17 to v18 with administrator privileges did not automatically upgrade the previously installed v17 VSS (Volume Shadow Copy) service; the service was stopped but never updated to the new version.

In the Toolbox's menu editor, selecting an image from the picture library to use as the splash screen's background image did not actually apply it. The issue is fixed, but using the picture library for this purpose is still discouraged in general.

On Windows, while typing Japanese (IME) text in the Form Editor's property list, the underline guide showing the conversion range was not visible, because the line height was insufficient relative to the font height; this was linked to the property list's rendering having moved from GDI to DirectWrite.

In Project mode only, the name of a numeric filter/format was displayed incorrectly in the property list: the leading pipe character (`|`) that should prefix the name was missing. Applying the fix requires re-selecting a different filter and then reverting, to force the JSON file to refresh.
In the Quick Report editor, standard variables (page number, creation time, creation date, etc.) inserted into the right-side header or footer were placed on the left side instead of the right.

In the Quick Report editor, inserting standard variables such as page number, creation time, or creation date into the left-aligned or centered header/footer triggered an error instead of inserting the value.
