After converting a binary database with nested object groups (e.g. grouped groups containing radio buttons) to Project mode, the group ownership hierarchy was lost, so grouped radio buttons no longer behaved as a group. The fix now folds all objects into the outermost enclosing group to reproduce binary-mode behavior.

The POP3 Transporter object did not support USER/PASS authentication even when its `acceptUnsecureConnection` property was set to True: the transporter could not log in to a server using a plain username and password. A new `POP3 authentication user` constant (value `"USER"`) was added to force this login method.

On 64-bit Windows, sending keystroke events to third-party applications from 4D via [POST KEY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/post-key) did not work, so simulated hotkeys had no effect outside the 4D application.

On Windows, moving a list box via a splitter did not force its contents to redraw, leaving stale rendering inside the list box until [REDRAW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/redraw) was called explicitly. The problem did not occur when the list box's border style was set to "Standard".
On Windows, adding an object to a form that inherited from another form referencing a subform containing a list box caused the application to freeze while editing.
In the Japanese localization of 4D, newly created 4D View Pro objects were given the default name "Stepper" instead of "4D View Pro".

Calling `collection.clear()` on a shared collection did not go through the internal `Use`/`End use` locking mechanism, allowing a collection to be cleared even while another process held a lock on it.

In the Structure Editor's Inspector palette, for a text field the "Auto UUID" checkbox remained enabled even after the "UUID Format" checkbox was disabled, when it should have been disabled along with it.

In 4D Write Pro, if a document's text contained a NULL ASCII character (`Char(0)`), calling [WP SET TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-set-text) stopped updating the document from that character onward, effectively truncating the text update at the embedded null byte.

In a built (merged) client/server application, the `--user-param` command-line argument passed on Windows was not retrievable through [Get database parameter](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-database-parameter) or `User param value`, so custom startup parameters were effectively lost in that configuration.

When a 4D Write Pro document was exported via MIME (e.g. for sending by email), text set at font size 12 rendered smaller than text at size 11 in the recipient's mail client, because size 12 (Write Pro's default) was omitted from the export output and the mail client's own default happened to differ. `WP EXPORT DOCUMENT` and `WP EXPORT VARIABLE` HTML/MIME export were both fixed.

When an underscore character (`_`) appeared in a mail's subject or attachment filename, converting the mail with `MAIL Convert to MIME` wrongly replaced it with the string `=5F` (its quoted-printable ASCII escape) instead of leaving it as a literal underscore.
On Windows, structurally modifying a list box (e.g. hiding a column) while one of its cells was actively being edited crashed the application.

When a syntax error in an SQL statement triggered the error-handling method inside a transaction, the transaction level was rolled back unexpectedly. Ordinary errors returned during `UPDATE`/`INSERT` execution do not trigger this, but errors raised while parsing an `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` request also rolled back the transaction.

On 64-bit builds, passing `0` as the itemKey to `SET MENU ITEM SHORTCUT` was meant to clear the menu item's shortcut, but instead left an invalid shortcut label (like a bare "Ctrl+") displayed in the menu, even though the shortcut assignment itself was cleared internally.
Against certain mail servers (e.g. hMailServer), the POP3 Transporter's `getMail()` method returned Null for the second message retrieved instead of the message content.

On Windows, the euro sign (`€`) could not be typed into a text input field inside a CEF-based web area; a "tofu" placeholder glyph appeared instead. The 32-bit build was unaffected, pasting the character worked fine, and the issue applied more broadly to special characters entered via the `Alt` key.

If a comment block contained a nested single-line comment or wrapped code, closing and reopening the method caused the single-line comment marker (`//`) inside the block to multiply, altering the block's content unexpectedly.

In Project mode only, running [SCAN INDEX](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/scan-index) on a client/server database failed to build a current selection, so it behaved as if it returned zero records.

In a 4D Write Pro form where a widget sat above the Write Pro area, and an object receiving initial focus sat above the widget on page 2, navigating to that page triggered multiple spurious syntax errors (two on the first visit, five thereafter) about incorrect parameters.
Running an ORDA query on a collection-type attribute using a formula (i.e. a method) as the query condition could crash the application.
Calling `dataStore.cancelTransaction()` did not release the locks held on entities that had been deleted during the transaction, leaving them locked after the rollback.

In compiled mode, saving a collection-type object property inside an object field via ORDA (`$entity.save()`) appeared to succeed but the change was not actually persisted unless the field itself was explicitly re-assigned to force the update.

The HTML output produced by Quick Report was malformed, containing an excessive number of unexpected `
` tags, roughly proportional to the number of columns and records in the report.

When a font lacked either a bold or an italic style variant (e.g. "Elephant"), the SVG rendering engine and 4D Write Pro areas silently fell back to a default font (e.g. Times New Roman) instead of rendering the requested font, unlike browsers and web areas which display the intended font regardless.
POP3 Transporter methods could freeze when connecting to Exchange or Dovecot mail servers; Gmail was unaffected.

4D View Pro performance degraded severely (cell edits taking up to 10 seconds) when the datastore used a virtual structure containing a large number of tables and fields. A dedicated `VP SET ALLOWED FIELDS` command was added so the fields actually needed inside the View Pro area can be distinguished from an unrelated, larger virtual structure.

In a list box with the "Single-Click Edit" property enabled, editing a cell caused the [FORM Event](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-event) "On Before Data Entry" to fire twice unexpectedly — once for the list box and once for the column — instead of once.

When building a server application, the project's `ArrayExcludedComponentName` setting was ignored: components explicitly excluded were nonetheless always installed if they were among those pre-bundled with 4D Server.
Repeatedly stopping and starting the web server caused the same certificate to be added multiple times to the OpenSSL TLS certificate chain.

List boxes did not correctly display selection lists based on XLIFF enumerations. The fix note clarifies that to show an XLIFF list as a popup menu in a list box column, the column's "Associate with" property must be set to "List item reference" (rather than the default "List item value") together with a specified list, since that property is only visible once a selection list is assigned to the object.

On Mac, using [OBJECT SET FONT STYLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-font-style) to set a list box column to a bold system font caused progressively slower window redraws, worsening with the number of fonts installed on the system: 4D was re-scanning and rebuilding the system's bold-font cache every time the style was applied, instead of reusing the cache after the first lookup.
When a component ran in compiled mode, the parameters of its compiled methods were not recorded in the debug log (log modes 2 or 6).

In the Explorer, selecting a table from the Home page left the preview area blank instead of showing the table's field information; on Windows this also affected previews of forms, folders, and methods. The regression dates back to 17 R6.

In a dynamic (JSON) form, [EXPORT TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/export-text) created the output file but wrote no data into it. The fix extends beyond JSON forms so `EXPORT TEXT` works correctly across Project mode generally.

After converting a binary database to Project mode, methods that previously had an Owner group or Access group had those settings exported as method attributes, which were then still enforced to restrict web-server access (e.g. via `4DACTION/` calls) — even though Users & Groups permissions should not apply in Project mode at all. The fix excludes these group settings from the export and ignores them at runtime if present; no re-conversion is required.

The `Form` object was available in a project form's execution context but not in a table form's, an inconsistency between the two form types. The fix also adds a `Form.parentForm` property so a detail form reached from a list form can access the list form's `Form` object.

Since 4D v18.0 Hotfix 1, calling [Command name](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/command-name) with the number of an old/deprecated command (internally prefixed with `_o_`) returned an empty string instead of the command's name.

On Windows, when the MSC engine rebuilt its index at startup while running in SDI/engined mode, no icon appeared in the system taskbar during the (potentially lengthy) operation, because the progress bar used a palette window; if that window moved behind other windows, bringing the app back to the foreground became difficult.

A document converted from 4D Write to 4D Write Pro could contain hidden special characters (visible as a dot) on certain lines; pressing Return (not Enter) on such a line inserted the hidden character again instead of a line break. This is a rendering-only issue that does not affect normal-mode display or the document's actual content.

Sending an HTML email exported from 4D Write Pro via `WP EXPORT VARIABLE`'s MIME export could display incorrectly in the recipient's mail client when routed through a Kerio SMTP server: the Unicode byte-order mark preceded the raw HTML source (e.g. `ï»¿<html xmlns=...`) instead of being interpreted. Exchange servers were unaffected. The fix removes the BOM from Write Pro's MIME export.
Disabling the context menu property of a 4D Write Pro area also unexpectedly disabled the context menu of its ruler.

Calling [ZIP Create archive](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/zip-create-archive) with the `ZIP Without enclosing folder` option reported `success` as True even though no archive file was actually created.
An ORDA query combining `NOT` with `IN` against an empty collection (e.g. `NOT IN :1` with an empty parameter) returned zero records instead of the expected result of all records.

When a 4D Write Pro document was exported to MIME, inline images did not have their `Content-Disposition` set to `inline`, so the exported message lost the information distinguishing inline images from regular attachments.
On Windows, 4D Server could crash due to a design flaw in the "Application monitor" page of the 4D Server administration window; closing or minimizing the admin window avoided the problem.
In Project mode, the Database Settings still displayed the "Automatic comments" option, even though this setting has no meaning in Project mode and should be hidden there.

In client/server, calling `dataClass.get()` with an empty string as the primary key behaved inconsistently across configurations: standalone mode correctly returned Null, but client/server returned an entity object whose individual attributes were each set to Null instead of the entity reference itself being Null.

Converting a 4D Write document to 4D Write Pro could distort tab-based table layouts due to a rounding error when converting sizes from twips to cm/mm (the plugin rounds to 1mm precision). For example, `26.7cm` should convert to `756.8504pt`, but the converted document placed the tab at `758pt`, overflowing the width of a landscape A4 page and causing extra line breaks in Write Pro. The fix correctly reconverts absolute tab-offset values (default tab offsets were already fine); as a side effect, documents converted before the fix may show tab positions differing by up to 1mm.
The callback formula specified in the options of [ZIP Create archive](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/zip-create-archive) was never invoked during the archive creation process.
In the transporter log for a sent email, spaces in the subject line were left as literal spaces instead of being encoded as `_` characters as expected.
Inserting an expression into a 4D Write Pro area did not trigger the `On Data Change` form event, even though the document's content had effectively changed.
Zooming a 4D Write Pro area triggered the `On Data Change` form event on every zoom step, even though zooming does not change the document's data.

On Mac, when a dialog was displayed on top of a list-mode subform, the subform's unselected rows disappeared from view behind the dialog, leaving only the selected row visible. The issue affected list forms with "List editable" mode generally.
In the 4D Client (client/server) menu bar, the Settings icon was shifted to the left compared to its expected position.

On a client publishing its own web server, URLs beginning with `http://host/rest` but not exactly matching the reserved `/rest/` path (e.g. `/restaurant`) were rejected with a 403 error instead of being handled as ordinary URLs, since the match was only checking a prefix rather than the full path component.

In Project mode, after exporting a binary database to a project, the "Alternate Background Color" property of a list box column was not carried over into the design-mode display; even without conversion, this alternate background color property failed to reflect in Design mode.

Converting a database to a dynamic (JSON) form or to Project mode gave focus capability to objects that were explicitly marked non-focusable and non-tabbable. The fix also corrects ruler conversion to JSON so its focusable property and additional label positions (beyond "top" and "left") are supported.

On 64-bit Mac, the plugin SDK entry point `PA_GetKey` failed to return precomposed accented characters typed using dead keys: with a U.S. keyboard layout, holding `option` while pressing keys like `u`, `e`, or `i` normally produces a combining accent, but `PA_GetKey` returned `0` for that keystroke and then returned the unaccented character code for the following keystroke instead of the combined accented character.

In compiled mode, converting an `ARRAY LONGINT` to a BLOB with [VARIABLE TO BLOB](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/variable-to-blob) and then restoring it into an `ARRAY REAL` with [BLOB TO VARIABLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/blob-to-variable) only partially converted the array, unlike interpreted mode. Although the documentation states that BLOB source/destination types must match exactly, the fix makes compatible types convert automatically, so `BLOB TO VARIABLE` now handles integer/real conversions the same way interpreted mode does.
In Project mode only, a list box column's "Truncate with ellipsis" property never took effect, because the "Word wrap" property defaulted to "Automatic", which took precedence.
4D crashed at launch when the system's primary language was set to Hungarian, due to an issue in the spell checker.

On Mac, in Project mode, switching to another application and back while the Menu tab of the Toolbox dialog was open corrupted the display of the menu bar content shown on the right side of the Toolbox.
The `On Web Connection` database method was not triggered for an HTTP `PATCH` request sent to the web server; the server immediately returned a 501 error instead of invoking the method.

Resizing a table inside a 4D Write Pro document could crash the application, because the resize operation generated excessive undo/redo history that consumed large amounts of memory. The fix also improves undo/redo performance for large tables and fixes a related crash when a table's width was shrunk to its minimum, triggering automatic page-break and border recalculation.

When a list box column was bound to an empty choice list, pressing the down-arrow key while editing a cell in that column crashed the application; with a non-empty list, the popup menu displayed correctly and arrow keys could be used to navigate its items.

On Mac, if the backup's target folder contained a broken symbolic link, the backup was aborted with error 1409 instead of performing a partial backup; the symbolic-link file itself should still be backed up as-is even if its target does not exist.

In the mail transporter, when both `htmlBody` and `textBody` were set with `textBody` assigned first, the recipient's mail client displayed the plain-text body instead of the HTML body; setting the properties in the reverse order avoided the issue.
In Project mode, the Explorer's "Batch Settings of Attributes" dialog for methods did not work: the dialog displayed and could be confirmed, but the changes were never actually applied.
Moving a window with a field being edited from a Retina display to a non-Retina display (or vice versa) could cause the form's background colors to disappear.
Under certain conditions, an SQL `LEFT OUTER JOIN` query returned one duplicate extra record instead of the expected single row.
In 4D View Pro, inserting a date via a command without an explicit format always used the U.S. date format (`mm/dd/yyyy`) instead of respecting the current locale.

Emails sent from 4D did not follow RFC 2822 recommendations for the `Message-ID` header when using [SMTP New transporter](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/smtp-new-transporter), which could cause them to be flagged as spam by filters like SpamAssassin. RFC 2822 recommends a unique identifier followed by `@` and a domain name; 4D generated a unique UUID but omitted the domain part.

On Mac, in a table published via 4D for iOS, pressing `Cmd+A` in the Data section's filter text-entry area and then selecting a field in "Fields" crashed the application. The root cause was that an object without the expected property was passed to `Substring`, and the fix was made in `Substring` rather than in the 4D for iOS code itself.

During a transaction, attempting to drop (delete) a previously saved ORDA entity failed with a "Stamp has changed" error, whether the transaction was started with the classic `START TRANSACTION` command or ORDA's `ds.startTransaction()`.

On Windows, the `uptime` property returned by `Get system info` reset unexpectedly to 0 roughly every 49 days, since it was effectively just `Tickcount/60` and reset whenever the 32-bit tick count reached a multiple of `MAXLONG/512` (4194304). The fix now computes `uptime` using platform-appropriate 64-bit APIs (`GetTickCount64` on Windows, `sysctl`/`KERN_BOOTTIME` on Mac, `clock_gettime`/`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux) instead of the wrapping 32-bit tick counter.

On Windows, when the Japanese IME's text-conversion candidate window was drawn upward from the bottom of the screen (to remain fully visible), it covered the text being typed, since the popup was anchored to the bottom rather than the top edge of the input area.

On macOS 10.14 only, clicking a 3D checkbox's disclosure (expand/collapse) button did not update its icon, because [Form event code](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-event-code) did not return the correct event; macOS 10.15 was unaffected.

Converting a 4D Write plugin document to 4D Write Pro lost accented characters (`Ä`, `Ö`, `Ü`, `ß`) and underscore characters from style-sheet names. The fix preserves accented characters, but underscores remain intentionally converted to spaces, since they act as placeholders for whitespace in HTML-safe style-sheet names; commands referencing a style sheet name containing an underscore will therefore see the space-converted form.

In the method editor's type-ahead (auto-complete), constants were meant to appear first among suggested parameter values, but methods and 4D commands were unexpectedly listed ahead of them, with constants pushed to the end. This regressed after ACI0099525 (build 236865, between 17 R5 and 17 R6) added commands and methods as parameter suggestions to better support object-oriented syntax such as [File](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/file) and [Folder](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/folder). The fix restores constants to the top of the suggestion list.
Compiling code that used the picture operator `*|` produced a syntax error instead of compiling successfully.

Converting a 4D Write document to 4D Write Pro could lose certain expressions entirely; the issue occurred specifically with formulas containing a literal double-quote (`"`) escaped with a backslash (`\`).

On Windows, automatic updates failed for a server running as a service, because the updater used an incorrect service name, hard-coded as `"4DS "` plus the structure name — which does not necessarily match the actual service name.
Using one-to-many ORDA entity relations caused several memory leaks, affecting both standalone and client/server modes, with the leak being more pronounced on the server side.

Passing a constant such as `Build application log file` to [File](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/file) raised a "-9851 Invalid parameter number 1" error whenever the referenced file did not yet exist, even though the parameter itself was valid — the file simply hadn't been created yet. The fix also makes `Get 4D file` return the theoretical file path instead of erroring when the file is absent, except for `Backup log file` and `Last backup file`, whose paths remain undetermined (returning Null) until a backup has actually run.
In a large 4D Write Pro document containing page numbers, scrolling down through the pages became progressively slower; the problem became noticeable in documents around 500 pages.

When the SMTP transporter sent an email, the sequence `\r\n` (CRLF) was quoted-printable encoded as `=0D=0D` instead of the expected form; most mail clients tolerated this, but Outlook and Outlook Express rendered the message body with a corrupted layout.

On the new network layer, if a client's connection dropped abruptly while a new user process had a dialog open, the corresponding server-side application process was cleaned up after about a minute, but its user process lingered (disposed of only after roughly two hours). If the client reconnected during that window, the stale session/process was not removed, causing an extra client connection license to be consumed. Reconnecting after the orphaned process reached a "deferred" state avoided the problem.

After converting a structure from v16.x to a later version, a checkbox's standard action could be set to [ACCEPT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/accept) in the Form Editor's property list, which should not be a valid standard action for that object type.

The table list shown by the entity-selection list box builder was incorrect: it only listed tables with "Expose as REST resource" set to True, whereas it should show every table accessible via the `ds` command — i.e. any table valid for ORDA use, regardless of REST exposure. (Related: with ACI0100657, instantiating and starting a WEB Server object made `Folder(fk web root folder).platformPath` return the database folder instead of the correct web root folder path.)
Exporting a 4D Write Pro document to `.docx` merged separate bordered paragraphs into a single paragraph instead of preserving them as distinct paragraphs.
In a class, declaring a function before the constructor (instead of after) caused a runtime error when the class was instantiated and the function called.

On Windows, when the system language was set to English, the backup setting "Retry after n seconds" was not saved: the value was correctly written to the `.4DSettings` file, but the settings dialog displayed `0` instead of the saved value.
Exporting a 4D Write Pro document to HTML did not correctly render subscript/superscript styles applied to an entire paragraph, nor background color applied to specific words within a paragraph.
In Project mode only, restoring a database from a backup crashed the application when user settings were stored alongside the data file (i.e. when the structure and data reside in separate folders).
A 4D for iOS mobile application crashed if a custom data formatter installed in the `Resources` folder had a folder name that did not match the name declared in `manifest.json`.

Setting selector 34 to its default value of `0` via [SET DATABASE PARAMETER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-parameter) did not properly update the value subsequently returned by [Get database parameter](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-database-parameter) for that same selector.

In client/server, creating an entity selection from ORDA code running inside a component on the client side raised an unexpected error (-10716) — actually returning Null — while the same code worked fine in standalone mode or when run server-side.
Calling `OB Is empty` on an object that held a non-empty formula (method) property incorrectly returned True instead of False.

In a 4D Write Pro document containing a large number of bookmarks or custom properties (around 2000), typing text near the beginning of the document showed a noticeable lag between keystrokes and their on-screen display; typing near the end of the document was unaffected. The fix optimizes bookmark updates and undo-history management.

In 4D View Pro, the first keystroke made directly after selecting a cell (without double-clicking to enter edit mode or using the formula bar) did not trigger the `On After Edit` event — it only fired starting from the second keystroke. On Mac the issue cleared after restarting the app; on Windows, typing a number as the first character avoided it; using the formula bar or double-clicking a cell to start editing also avoided it.

In the backup database properties, the default value for "Retry after X second(s)/minute(s)/hour(s)" was wrong and inconsistent across platforms: `0000-00-00T00:00:00.561` on Mac versus `0000-00-00T00:00:00.000` on Windows, whereas v16 defaulted to 60 seconds. The fix corrects the bundled *Backup.4DSettings* resource file.

In a 4D Write Pro widget, evaluating a method/formula that used [WP Insert table](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-insert-table) as an expression could crash the application. The fix resolves the crash, though inserting a formula that updates the same Write Pro document it is embedded in is still discouraged.

On Windows, displaying an image file inside an integrated CEF web area caused keyboard focus to shift away from an adjacent list box to the web area, breaking arrow-key navigation over file paths shown in the list box; the system web area was unaffected.

In Project mode only, the `Administrator` user could not delete other users, whereas in binary mode this worked correctly; only users deleted by `Designer` should remain protected from deletion by `Administrator`.
If table encryption was enabled while a table had zero [records in it](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/records-in-table), no records could subsequently be added to that table.

Calling [QUIT 4D](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/quit-4d) while remote datastore sessions were still open could hang the server: with 2 open sessions there was no issue, with 3 a hang occurred rarely, and with 6 concurrent sessions the hang occurred reliably.

In Project mode, opening the data file of a server application built as an OEM license (with the `IsOEM` key set to True) produced an error; binary mode, standalone applications, and standard (non-OEM) licenses were all unaffected.

Depending on the crop parameters used, calling [TRANSFORM PICTURE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/transform-picture) with the `Crop` constant could crash the application on certain images, when an internal coordinate calculation produced a negative value.
An ORDA query on a one-to-many related attribute combining `AND` and `OR` conditions did not return the correct set of results.

The embedded CEF web area could not load an HTTPS page whose certificate was not trusted (e.g. self-signed), showing nothing instead of the page. The fix now displays a message indicating the certificate is untrusted rather than silently failing to load.

Calling [DOM Find XML element](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dom-find-xml-element) with an XPath expression naming an element containing a hyphen (e.g. `trans-unit`) failed to find the element, because the hyphen was being interpreted as a minus/subtraction operator. Converted applications can toggle the new XPath engine via the Compatibility tab in Database Settings; applications created in 18 R3 always use the new engine, which requires XPath expressions rooted at the document root to start with `/`.

When an HTTP `PATCH` request was sent to the web server, the `X-METHOD` HTTP header array was not populated with a value. `PATCH`, in use since around 2010 as a complement to `PUT`, is meant for partially updating a resource (e.g. specific JSON attributes) rather than replacing it entirely.

In a picture object's method, running `Select document` during the `On Clicked` event cycle, then switching focus to another window and back, could cause the `On Clicked` event to fire again unexpectedly on the original form; picture-style buttons were not affected. The fix resolves the issue, though using a picture object as a substitute for a button is still not a recommended technique.

4D Write Pro tables with very thick borders rendered with thin gaps of visible whitespace, or let the background color show through the border. This is largely a side effect of anti-aliasing when the default background clipping box is set to "paragraph"; switching the clipping box to `padding-box` avoids the visual overflow.

In client/server, when the IP address allow/deny filtering table combined a client's "deny" entry with an "allow all" (`*`) rule, deleting the first entry (the server's own local IP) shifted the client's deny rule into the first position, and connections from that now-first denied address were unexpectedly allowed through. By design, a deny entry listed before "allow all" should remain an exception, but the fix ensures the server's own local IP address is not incorrectly matched against the allow/deny list at all, which was the actual root cause.

In Project mode, opening a project rewrote the `catalog.4DCatalog` file on every open even when nothing had changed, because an extra tab character was being added inside `<comment>` elements whenever the XML contained CDATA — which made Git treat the project as modified even without any real changes.

Sending a REST request (URLs starting with `/REST/`) to 4D Server returned an "unable to connect to the Web Server" HTML error page, an apparent side effect of the fix for ACI0100637. A Web Services Expansion license is not actually required for 4D Server to process REST requests.
After exporting a structure to a project, a boolean field placed on an output form was not converted correctly.
An SQL query using an `IN` clause on an indexed field returned incorrect results unless the values in the `IN` list were sorted in descending order.

Against a Kerio mail server, the POP3 Transporter's `getMail()` method appeared to freeze for about five minutes before eventually reporting a download error; this was linked to a mismatch between the byte count reported by `getMailInfoList()` and the actual size of the downloaded BLOB data.
When a 4D Write Pro area with its top toolbar was placed on the form's second page, the toolbar's style-sheet selector did not reflect the current style sheet of the selected text.

After exporting and re-importing a 4D Write Pro document, the first-page number configured per section via `wk page first number` was not correctly restored, so each section no longer started at its intended page 1.
Exporting a 4D Write Pro document to `.docx` could produce incorrect character-level style attributes (color, underline, etc.) in the resulting document.

On Mac, an application unzipped with [ZIP Read archive](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/zip-read-archive) could fail to launch, because internal symbolic links inside the archive were being extracted before the original items they pointed to, breaking the bundle's structure.

On Windows, in MDI mode, if a process showing a maximized window opened a new window from another process, that new (non-maximized) window could crash the application when the user tried to resize it with the mouse.

If a mail object's `messageId` property was explicitly set to an empty string before sending, the transporter output a malformed `Message-ID` header (`<>`) instead of generating one automatically, risking the message being flagged as spam; leaving `messageId` undefined avoided the problem since a value is then generated automatically.

On Windows, with the region and language set to English (Singapore), the abbreviated system date format (`System Date abbreviated`) displayed incorrectly as `MM/DD/YY` instead of the locale-correct `DD/MM/YY`.

On the 64-bit version, calling [SET CURRENT PRINTER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-current-printer) with an empty string failed to reset the current printer back to the system default printer.

In client/server with a Windows server, calling `dataClass.fromCollection()` on a table that is the "many" side of a one-to-many relation raised an error; standalone mode was unaffected. The problem depended on the order attributes appeared in the collection, occurring specifically when the relation attribute came last.

In [DOM Create XML element](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dom-create-xml-element), adding several XML elements with the same name inserted each new element before the existing one rather than after it, producing elements in reverse order. The bug only occurred when the "Use standard XPath" compatibility option was enabled.
The `folder.getIcon()` method could return an unexpected error #-10729 ("Unknown member method").

Opening a label settings file whose field font was set to the "3 of 9" barcode font (3of9.TTF) raised an unexpected import error. The error no longer appears after the fix, but since this 1993-era barcode font uses technology unsupported on current systems, it still does not render on screen or in print.
In Client/Server mode only, calling `entity.toObject()` with an attribute path that included a related entity attribute could omit that relatedEntities attribute from the returned object.

Passing an object's picture-type property as the first parameter to [PICTURE PROPERTIES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/picture-properties) raised an unexpected error #-20003 in compiled mode; using a picture-type local variable instead avoided the problem. The application must be recompiled to pick up the fix, which only affects the PICTURE PROPERTIES command itself.

Exporting a binary database to a project could produce a project that failed to reopen, because the exported XML was invalid. This happened when structure comments contained control characters that had been introduced by an old comment-import bug; the fix now ignores characters not supported by XML 1.0 when writing the file.

On Windows, in an SDI application displaying the 4D Write Pro interface on an external (second) monitor, creating a new style sheet opened the save dialog on the main screen instead of the monitor where the Write Pro window actually was.

Running the [SPELL CHECKING](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/spell-checking) command on a text-entry area that already had automatic spell checking enabled caused the spell-check dialog to close immediately instead of performing a normal check. After the fix, the button that triggers the check should not be set as focusable, since spell checking operates on the currently focused object.

Converting a 4D Write document (.4W7) to 4D Write Pro could mistranslate the [Year of](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/year-of) reference "Year of([Courriers]DateCreation):Système date court" into "String(Year of([Courriers]DateCreation);1)", which is a syntax error that then triggered error 8 when the references were displayed. Affected documents need to be reconverted after applying the fix.
In Client/Server mode, accessing a picture-type attribute through ORDA returned the wrong picture size.

Calling a non-existent project method from inside a class function did not raise the expected "project method does not exist" runtime error. Instead, the process-variable token was silently ignored and the method's arguments were assigned directly to the left operand. The fix now correctly returns the runtime error.

Loading a label file that had been created in the old 32-bit format into the Label Editor triggered unexpected error #-9930 ("there is no attribute with this name for this element") inside the Editor_ON_DATA_CHANGE method. This appeared to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0096880.

In Project mode only, the Form Editor failed to reset a form's geometry stamp when the form was modified; running the form, moving or resizing its window, and closing it therefore did not preserve the new placement on the next run because the `geometryStamp` property had not been updated.
With the "custom user settings in external files" option enabled, it was not possible to drop a client from the server-side Administration window.

Sending an email with a very long subject line through the SMTP transporter inserted an unexpected extra space character into the subject; this occurred with the `mail mode UTF8 in base64` header encoding.

Loading a field containing a NULL value into a text array via [SQL LOAD RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-load-record) caused the application to quit unexpectedly, for example when reading data from a MySQL database over ODBC.

After a stored procedure had been running for several weeks, accessing the last element of a local array it had created could unexpectedly raise range-check error -20001, causing local variables to appear to lose their value.
Writing a valid block comment nested inside another valid block comment triggered an unnecessary "missing opening (or closing) delimiter" warning in the method editor.
The [VP Convert from 4D View](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-from-4d-view) command (4D View Pro) was not thread-safe, so it could not be run from preemptive processes.

If [LISTBOX SELECT ROW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-select-row) was used during the `On Load` event to pre-select a row, pressing the Up arrow key afterward selected the last row and pressing Down selected the first row, instead of moving to the adjacent row. Array-based list boxes were unaffected; the bug reproduced only in selection- and collection-based list boxes, apparently as a side effect of the fix for ACI0099586.

Displaying scrollbars on a picture object with [OBJECT SET SCROLLBAR](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-scrollbar) worked initially, but switching form pages and returning made the scrollbars disappear again.

In a list box column bound to an entity selection, choosing a value from an associated choice list did not assign that value to the current item's property; the same setup worked correctly for a collection-based list box.
The first time an application moved to the background, the `On Application background move` system event was not generated.
Enabling the new standard XPath syntax option made [DOM Create XML element](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dom-create-xml-element) run considerably slower than before.

Copying text style with the 4D Write Pro widget's style-copy tool did not copy the font family along with the other attributes — for example, copying "Optima Extra Black" and pasting the style applied "Optima Bold" instead.

In 4D Write Pro, tab stops on the horizontal ruler can be dragged and normally snap to graduation marks; holding a modifier key (Alt or Control) while dragging was supposed to allow finer positioning, as it did in the old 4D Write plugin, but had no effect. The fix restores modifier-key support across ruler operations, including tab positioning.

On Windows only, clicking the cancel button of an in-progress progress bar and invoking the callback set via 'Progress SET ON STOP METHOD' could return unexpected error #-9996 ("Stack is full"), apparently because the local process's stack size was insufficient.
In Project mode only, changing only an object's "Class" property in the Form Editor did not update the JSON form's geometry/placement stamp.

When a method name contained uppercase letters, anchor links embedded in the method's markdown documentation (.md) did not work correctly — clicking them shifted focus to Finder on Mac and did nothing on Windows. The fix corrects the behavior for invalid anchors, but anchor names must match the header's case exactly to jump correctly; for class member method anchors, always write both the anchor name and the header title in all lowercase, e.g. a link to `#getvalues` pointing to a `## getvalues` header.
In Quick Report, applying a format to a single cell unexpectedly also applied that format to the row's header label.
In the Quick Report cell format list, "<None>" could appear selected even though a specific format was actually assigned to the cell.

In v18, a button with a custom title font color did not gray out its title text when the button was disabled; this only happened when the title's font color was set to something other than "Automatic".

Updating an object-type field with [OB SET](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-set) or [OB SET ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-set-array) and then saving with [SAVE RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/save-record) caused [Modified record](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/modified-record) to return [True](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/true) even though nothing else had changed; assigning directly to the field itself instead made it return [False](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/false) as expected.

In Project mode only, moving or resizing an object belonging to a Form Editor group did not update the group's overall selection boundaries, leaving the group's visual outline at its old position/size.
In 4D Write Pro, placing the caret right after an inserted formula and pressing Backspace did not remove the whole formula; deleting worked correctly only if the formula was first selected.
In 4D Quick Report, a custom expression assigned to a column was lost if that column was hidden and then shown again.

After converting a database from binary to Project mode, a form displaying a boolean field as a checkbox could no longer be used to import data into that field; changing the object type from checkbox to a plain input object was required to work around it.
In the Quick Report editor, the [Min](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/min) ("< Min") summary function did not compute the correct minimum for a column of date values.
On a tab control that displayed an icon, clicking directly below the tab's text label did not register as a click on the tab.
Exporting a document that had been converted from 4D View to 4D View Pro out to .xlsx format could produce a spreadsheet that Microsoft Excel reported an error opening.

List box vertical auto-scrollbars were drawn incorrectly, showing a white (Mac) or gray (Windows) rectangle at the top (and bottom) of the scrollbar track; this affected only the "automatic" display mode — the always-visible mode was fine. The scrollbar track area should be filled with the same color as the header/footer.
In 4D for iOS, custom data formatters selected for a linked (many-to-one relation) field were not applied.

In Project mode, using [OBJECT DUPLICATE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-duplicate) during the `On Load` event to duplicate a hidden list box could crash the application as soon as the form was closed.

In Client/Server mode, when per-process debug logging was enabled, encountering a shared object or shared collection locked by another process could block the log and cause client/server communication to become unresponsive. The fix now logs `<<Busy>>` in this situation, matching the debugger's own behavior.

4D View Pro's current culture settings did not apply a custom date separator character. For example, on a French system (default `YY/MM/DD`) with the date format set to `DD.MM.YY`, View Pro continued to recognize dates using the `YY/MM/DD` separator instead of the configured one.

The [MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) command sometimes returned an empty `body` for the resulting mail object; specific plain-text emails were affected, while multipart emails worked correctly.

In Project mode only, [OBJECT SET CORNER RADIUS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-corner-radius) had no effect unless the shape object's "Corner radius" property had already been set to a non-zero value in the editor.
The `getMail()` method of the POP3 Transporter component could return [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) when retrieving mail from an hMailServer server.
In 4D Write Pro, if a formula placed directly before a line break returned only a line-break character itself, evaluating a `This.pageCount` expression in the footer crashed the application.

Iterating over the formulas inserted in a 4D Write Pro document with `ST Get expressions` and `ST get content type` could make the application become unresponsive. Since 18 R2, the more optimized [WP Get formulas](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-formulas) command should be used instead when only formula processing is needed.
In the Quick Report list-report editor's field list, adding a related-table field could display the wrong related table name.
On macOS only, exporting a 4D Write Pro document containing a pasted picture to .docx or .pdf displayed a placeholder icon instead of the actual image.
Creating a new table while simultaneously loading records in the Import dialog raised error 9935.

With two tables linked by a many-to-one relation and a SQL statement joining them on the foreign/primary key (`INNER JOIN T2 ON T2.foreign_key = T1.primary_key`) combined with `GROUP BY`, executing the query inside a [Begin SQL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/begin-sql) block returned error 1002 (SQLS).

In Client/Server mode, an ORDA query using the `IN` operator could return an incorrect (empty) result set when the queried field was not indexed. This reproduced specifically when the database language was Japanese with text comparison for string matching enabled.
In Project mode, switching focus back to a running 4D application in the background was slow, because the design environment re-checked all of the project's configuration files each time.

When a field with a Japanese name was placed on a form and its object method contained an error, the compiler's error message used the wrong text encoding, producing garbled characters for the affected path.
In the Server Administration window's Processes tab, when multiple rows were selected, it was not possible to click-and-drag the scrollbar to scroll the list.

On macOS only, a 4D Write Pro document exported as MIME via [WP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-export-document) would not open in a browser (e.g. Google Chrome) and, when sent by email, displayed as raw HTML source in the recipient's mail client instead of rendered content.

On macOS only, using the toolbar's PDF export from a 4D View Pro area suggested the system temporary folder — instead of a sensible default location — as the export destination, requiring the user to navigate a deeply nested path.
Using the Explorer's "Rename Method" command (with the "rename in all references" mode) did not update the method name referenced inside a form object's "Expression" property.
Placing both a 4D Write Pro area and its sidebar widget inside a subform caused an error whenever a bookmark or URL was set through the sidebar.
Converting a 4D View document to 4D View Pro produced cells missing their bottom border and, on the first column, their right border.

In the Japanese-localized product, a search query combining "is" (である) and "or" (または) conditions in the Query Editor was not loaded back correctly. Because queries combining several "or" conditions are internally converted to a "matches any value in the list" formula (to save display space), the reload logic failed to reconstruct the original query; the fix restores the previous internal query execution behavior.

In a Web Area, calling [WA SET PAGE CONTENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wa-set-page-content) a second time (e.g. after reloading a page) could leave the `$4d` object unable to call 4D project methods, on Windows with the CEF-based web area. This was caused by CEF removing APIs like `CefProcessHandler`/`setContent`, which prevented the bridge from being reactivated after a reload; WA SET PAGE CONTENT was reimplemented around a resource-load interception mechanism. When no base URL is given, the URL now defaults to `file:///` (a URL cannot be omitted), and setting the URL to `about:blank` causes the page content to be ignored.

On Mac binary-mode applications only, a button placed in the footer area of an output form (displayed via [MODIFY SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/modify-selection)) sometimes did not respond to clicks.
In Client/Server mode, calling `entitySelection.orderByFormula()` from a member method of a datastore class raised an error.

In the Method Editor, autocompletion of constants did not insert entries correctly. This was a side effect of adding support for named (keyword) arguments; the fix keeps the suggestion window appearing correctly, but constants are now listed at lower priority.

When several break levels were defined on a form, the Form Editor's ruler labeled them B3, B2, B1, B0 from top to bottom, while the property list instead numbered them "Form break", "Form break 1", "Form break 2" — an inconsistent naming scheme between the two views.

In Project mode, editing `folders.json` with an external editor to move (cut-and-paste) a method or form into a subfolder — a change visible in the Explorer — duplicated the item at the top level instead of moving it.
On Mac only, changing a 4D Write Pro area's text font from "Times New Roman" to "Times" made the text render in bold.
In the JSON (Project mode) Form Editor, it was not possible to set the title font color of Progress indicator labels.
On Windows only, some characters — such as "@" and "€" — could not be typed into a form's text area using Alt+numeric-code combinations; the same input worked fine in the Method Editor.

Converting a large 4D Write document (roughly A4, 1000+ pages, ~50,000 lines) to 4D Write Pro made it very slow to display initially. Improvements reduced the load time from 1 minute 32 seconds to 25 seconds (about 10 seconds if the content is loaded off-screen without displaying it in a form object, meaning roughly 15 seconds is spent on layout/rendering). 4D Write Pro is not designed to instantly open documents with tens of thousands of lines or thousands of pages — since it stores each line as an XHTML/HTML node, the document becomes a very large tree; even Microsoft Word takes about 10 seconds to open the equivalent XHTML file directly, so this load time is considered reasonable.

In the "Export data" dialog, applying a numeric format to a Real-type field made the preview area display the value with a doubled decimal point; this was a preview-only display glitch (the exported file itself was correct) and occurred specifically with formats like `###,###,##0.00`.

When creating a new list box in Project mode, the "movableRows" property was missing from the object's definition in the form.4DForm file (list boxes converted from Binary mode were unaffected); without this property, rows could not be dragged to reorder them.
The [CONFIRM](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/confirm) dialog window did not have quite enough vertical height for its content.

In the [BUILD APPLICATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/build-application) window, if only the "Build component" option was checked, the "BUILD" button remained disabled and could not be clicked.

Passing MIME data without a CRLF sequence to [MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) caused the application to hang; an empty string parameter was handled fine.

[MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) could return the wrong sent date/time for a converted mail object because the time zone offset was calculated incorrectly — for example, a header value of `Mon, 3 Aug 2020 09:27:52 +0200` was converted to `2020-08-03T09:27:52.000Z` instead of correctly shifting for the +0200 offset.

In a 4D View Pro spreadsheet, clearing a cell's content directly with the Delete key was not detected as a document modification (`designer.actions.isFileModified` did not become [True](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/true)); entering edit mode on the cell and then deleting the value worked correctly.

When a cell's range name had been created with the `vk workbook` scope, it could not be accessed by name using [VP Get value](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-get-value) or [VP SET VALUES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-set-values); range names scoped to the current worksheet worked fine.

In 4D Write Pro, inserting a formula such as `Char(13)` created in the Formula Editor, then switching the display from value to reference and back to value, crashed the application; a formula like [Current date](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/current-date) did not trigger the issue.

In 64-bit 4D, calling [RECEIVE PACKET](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/receive-packet) with a stop character was around 75 times slower than in 32-bit 4D. Specifying a byte size instead, or using [RECEIVE BUFFER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/receive-buffer), was unaffected; the slowdown reproduced regardless of the serial/USB adapter, platform, or connected device.
In the form property list's "Geometry" tab, it was not possible to edit a form's vertical margin; changing it via the "All" tab worked correctly.
In the Method Editor, with a folded `Case of` code block displayed, deleting a line from the unfolded code just below that block could crash the application.
On macOS only, when a combo box was too narrow, its items were not displayed in full alongside the dropdown arrow.
English version only: importing a large volume of data with the "create table" option enabled displayed a progress dialog containing a typo — "Concerting toText" instead of "Converting to Text".

In Project mode, a list box whose data source was a named selection created with [USE NAMED SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/use-named-selection) did not display data if that selection had actually been built via [CUT NAMED SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/cut-named-selection) or [COPY NAMED SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/copy-named-selection).

In Client/Server mode, inside a member method of a class derived from an entity selection, [This](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/this).length always returned 0; entity selections created on the client side were unaffected.

Using [READ PICTURE FILE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/read-picture-file) in a loop to load a large number of pictures into a picture array caused a memory leak; on Windows the application could crash or freeze, and on Mac it ran significantly slower. Versions 17.x and 18.x (prior to R4) were not affected.
Storing an SVG image smaller than 500 bytes into a picture field configured to store data outside the [Data file](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/data-file) crashed the application.
If a Project-mode component's name contained Japanese characters, starting a host in compiled mode with that component raised an error.

In 4D Write Pro, setting the left padding (margin) of a paragraph containing lines with tabs did not save that left-margin value to the document; the right margin was unaffected. This specifically occurred when the left margin was positive while the text indent was negative.

Copying and pasting a line of text in a document converted from 4D Write to 4D Write Pro duplicated the paragraph style sheet, so the paragraph and the pasted text ended up with two separate style sheets instead of sharing one. The root cause was a discrepancy between "implicit (default)" and "left-aligned" text alignment in the HTML produced during conversion; the fix makes the HTML output always specify alignment explicitly, which does not affect already-converted documents but may change the HTML produced by future conversions.

Passing a picture-type object property directly to [SET PICTURE TO PASTEBOARD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-picture-to-pasteboard) — e.g. `SET PICTURE TO PASTEBOARD($pictObj.myPict)` — failed with error #59.

In Project mode, the "Prompt If Related One Does Not Exist" field option had no effect. In Project mode there is generally no distinction between a form object bound to a "field" versus a "variable" — both are treated as text-entry objects; the fix restores field-specific behavior whenever an object's bound variable/expression actually corresponds to a field.
Clicking the header of a Quick Report area embedded in a form, when the report type was set to "cross report" (crosstab), could raise unexpected errors 9852/9853.

In 4D Mono (standalone) only, locking an entity inside a transaction and then calling `entity.lock(dk reload if stamp changed)` after [VALIDATE TRANSACTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/validate-transaction) left the entity lockable by a different process even though it was supposed to remain locked; Client/Server mode was not affected.
Passing an undefined (null) object to [WP Get formulas](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-formulas) crashed the application; the fix now returns a syntax error instead.

In 4D Write Pro, when a table was inserted at the very beginning of a document, it was not possible to insert a line of text above that table. The fix makes pressing Return with the caret at the start of a table located at the start of the body (or header/footer) insert a paragraph before the table — note this uses plain Return, unlike Microsoft Word's Shift+Return.

In Project mode, after converting a database from Binary to Project mode, combining [LISTBOX SET PROPERTY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-set-property) with the `lk named selection` property to configure a list box's named selection did not work.
[MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) failed to send an attachment whose file name contained German diacritical (accented) characters.

Inside a transaction, locking an entity and calling ORDA's `entity.drop(dk force drop if stamp changed)` reported `success` as [True](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/true) in the returned status object even though the entity had not actually been dropped.
In Project mode only, the Form Editor became very slow when a form contained a large number of objects (e.g. many buttons with icons set); Binary mode was not affected.

Grouping vertical or horizontal line objects produced a group selection outline that did not correctly enclose all the grouped objects — if a line's starting point was to the right of or below its end point, resizing the group could push objects outside its bounds, due to incorrect coordinate calculations for objects with negative height or width.

Converting a binary database to Project mode disabled the "relation auto-wildcard support" feature for relations — typing a value ending in a wildcard into a field and tabbing out no longer automatically displayed the list of matching candidate values.
On Windows only, using [Select document](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/select-document) to save a file into a folder whose name contained a period (dot) raised an error.
IMAP commands could not authenticate against an iCloud IMAP server (`imap.mail.me.com`) using PLAIN authentication with an app-specific password.
Right-clicking to open the contextual menu after selecting all the text of a very large imported 4D Write Pro document (1100+ A4 pages) froze the application.
In compiled mode, dereferencing a pointer to a table and passing it to [PRINT SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-selection) crashed the application.

The [File](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/file) and [Folder](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/folder) commands ignored the extra `*` (filesystem path) parameter option when given a filesystem-style path.
In Project mode, a plugin area's border line style was not drawn in the Form Editor's Design mode for a JSON form.
In a merged (built) application, the Command+Shift+F9 shortcut for the Runtime Explorer no longer worked.

Using an entity-selection-based list box inside a subform hid the "current item position" and "selected items" properties from the debugger; only the "current item" property was shown, unlike when the same list box was used directly on a form.

Converting an .eml file with a PDF attachment into a mail object (via MIME Convert to mail) and sending it could result in the attachment not appearing for the recipient. The source MIME file mixed `
`, `

`, and bare `
` line endings and did not conform to RFC 822; the improved MIME parser now sends the attachment correctly, but as a result the message may no longer display in Windows Mail (Thunderbird is unaffected).
[MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) could produce a mail object whose embedded (inline/ID) pictures did not display, due to an encoding issue.
In compiled mode only, if a form contained a tab control object bound to a non-numeric variable (an incorrectly declared form object), closing that form after opening it could crash the application.
Using the "Import data from file..." menu command and then switching to a table that had only a single field raised error 215 (xbox).

Importing data into certain tables via the Import dialog could silently skip fields that had actually been selected for import — the issue was not universal across all tables. It occurred when the field information in the generated `.4si` file did not include a table number; adding a `table_no` attribute to the settings file was a workaround, and the fix now automatically inserts the correct table number for fields selected via the header click in the import dialog.

On Windows only, running a build, syntax check, or compile against a very large structure could crash the application, due to a problem in the compiler's old memory manager; the fix switches the compiler to its new memory manager.
When a CSS class was applied at the whole list box object level, the CSS font set on the footer was not applied when the form ran, even though it displayed correctly in Design mode.
Exporting a 4D View Pro document containing pictures returned by 4D formulas to PDF did not render properly — the literal string `_pict_` was inserted in place of the picture.
Required-value and excluded-value lists applied to an input field stopped working (since v18.0 Hotfix 1), as a side effect of the fix for ACI0099771.

In 4D Write Pro, a hyperlink to a project method created with [WP SET LINK](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-set-link) did not respond to clicks in Application (runtime) mode; activating a different window and then reactivating the window containing the Write Pro area made the link clickable again.

Changing the client-side web server's HTTPS port (Client HTTPS port ID) via [SET DATABASE PARAMETER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-parameter) on the client side had no effect at Remote Client startup — the standalone application's port number was used instead of the configured one.

Resizing a form window while a 4D View Pro area was still being set up, just before it finished displaying, could freeze the application — apparently due to a JavaScript infinite loop that could occur right around the `On VP ready` event.
[FORM SCREENSHOT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-screenshot) of an output form omitted the [last record](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/last-record) from the captured image.

In the Method Editor, accepting an autocomplete suggestion right after typing "END S" (to complete "[End SQL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/end-sql)" following a [Begin SQL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/begin-sql) block) could crash the application.
Inserting a formula (resolved or not) into a 4D Write Pro document increased the height of the line(s) containing it.
It was not possible to set a form object's font to a user-installed font that was not present on the current platform.
In the Label Editor, concatenating field values in a label did not work correctly — only the first operand was shown in the preview.

On Mac only, building a client application without code signing made the resulting application crash immediately at launch; single-user and server applications were unaffected. The fix allows ad hoc code signing to be used when no Apple developer certificate is available, via a new boolean build setting, `/Preferences4D/BuildApp/SignApplication/AdHocSign`, in BuildApp.4DSettings.

Unplugging a serial device from the computer while its communication port was open crashed the application; the fix makes [RECEIVE BUFFER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/receive-buffer) return an error in this situation, the same way [RECEIVE PACKET](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/receive-packet) already did.
In compiled mode only, assigning a value to `$1` when that parameter does not actually exist could crash the application.

On Mac only, after switching to another application and then bringing 4D back to the foreground, "Search references" for a method (and syntax checking) became dramatically slower in Project mode — on large applications, completion could take roughly 10 seconds in Binary mode versus 10+ minutes in Project mode.
On Windows only, the [RESTORE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/restore) command could not restore the application when 4D Server was running registered as a Windows service (headless mode).

In binary mode only, deleting a form containing objects with object methods and emptying the trash left those object methods behind; running the MSC's application check afterward detected these unused `CC4D` resources as orphan methods.
A mail attachment object created with [MAIL New attachment](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-new-attachment) could not be shared with (passed to) another process.

While 4D Server was handling Web activity, remote 4D Remote clients using the legacy network layer showed high CPU usage; this did not occur if the structure file was read-only, suggesting the `.4DC` file was being updated on every Web request.
When a binary database was converted to a project, the "transparency" property set on a hierarchical list was lost — it was not exported to the converted project format.

Removing a field's uniqueness constraint and then switching to a different data file did not trigger the automatic index regeneration that should follow such a structural change, so adding a record could later fail with a duplicate-key error. Deleting the index file manually worked around the issue.

Selecting the full text of a large 4D Write Pro document (around 500,000 characters) and choosing "Copy" from the contextual menu could freeze the application, because Write Pro's copy operation must transcode multi-style text, HTML, RTF, and its internal format onto the clipboard simultaneously, putting heavy load on the underlying Xerces XML parser. The fix omits some data types from the clipboard payload when the amount of text is extreme.

In Client/Server mode, calling [SELECTION TO ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/selection-to-array) from the client side on a picture field whose storage option was set to "outside the data file" returned error -10533. Both the server and client builds needed updating to receive the fix.

Duplicating a form or project method stored inside an Explorer folder created the duplicate at the Explorer's top level instead of inside its original folder. The fix also makes duplication work correctly when several objects are selected in the Explorer's Home tab (previously only the first selected object was duplicated); in binary mode all duplicates land at the top level unless every selected object shares the same folder, while in project mode a new object is created in each source folder.

On Windows, clicking once on a link in the About dialog (legal information, copyright, or 4D worldwide) opened it twice in the Edge browser, because the page's HTML had the same script attached to both a `<div>` and a nested `<span>`.
In the French edition of 4D, the constant "mail disposition en pièce-jointe" for the French command equivalent to `MAIL Create attachment` was not recognized.
In Client/Server mode, the Server Administration window's menu became unusable — a side effect introduced by the fix for ACI0096662.
In Project mode, [OBJECT SET LIST BY NAME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-list-by-name) had no effect when applied to a text-entry object bound to a variable.

Converting a 4D View spreadsheet to 4D View Pro with [VP Convert from 4D View](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-from-4d-view) could drop most of the embedded formulas, particularly when a formula exceeded View Pro's supported length — for example when each parameter was wrapped in a casting function to force a string type, which made the converted formula even longer. The fix converts date literals to string literals and simplifies the [String](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/string) function call to a plain `TEXT` reference, since View Pro's standard functions work internally with variants and can accept dates passed as strings.

Loading a 4D View Pro document that had been converted from 4D View and contained long formulas — such as one summing 25 `AVERAGE` calculations — could take several minutes, a regression from v17. The fix improves asynchronous call performance in 4D and updates the underlying SpreadJS library to version 14.0.4.

Assigning the first element of a collection to a variable and then passing that same variable as both the current-element parameter and the collection parameter of a `For each` loop could cause a memory leak.

On Windows, the embedded CEF web area sometimes stopped responding to mouse-wheel scrolling and pointer-hover events — an apparent side effect of the fix for ACI0100774. Loading the HTML on an `On Timer` event triggered by [SET TIMER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-timer)(-1) instead of `On Load` worked around the problem.
In Client/Server mode, `dataClass.fromCollection()` did not return a shareable, non-modifiable entity selection as it should.
On a multi-core virtual machine, [Get system info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/system-info) reported the wrong number of processor cores.
[VP Convert to picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-to-picture) numbered sheets starting at 1 instead of 0.
Connecting to a remote datastore failed with a "cannot resolve relation" error whenever an exposed (REST-published) table had a relation to a table that was not itself exposed via REST.
When a spreadsheet cell contained multiple consecutive space characters, converting it to a picture with `VP Convert to picture` rendered them collapsed into what looked like the letter "i".

Using [OBJECT SET RGB COLORS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-rgb-colors) on a text-entry area that had a background color set caused an unexpected `On Data change` event to fire when the area lost focus. Objects whose background was set to transparent were unaffected.
On macOS 11 (Big Sur), quitting the application shortly after a form containing a CEF web area had been displayed — such as the Welcome screen — generated a crash report.

With a listbox's "automatic row height" option enabled, [OBJECT GET SCROLL POSITION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-scroll-position) returned row numbers starting at 0 instead of 1 as it does for a normal listbox. The fix preserves this behavioral distinction: for hierarchical lists, list forms, and listboxes without automatic row height, the command returns the first fully visible row; with automatic row height enabled, it returns the first row visible even partially.

[MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) sometimes failed to decode a message's subject correctly, occasionally leaving the raw escape sequences of a wrapped UTF-8 quoted-printable header in the result.

In interpreted mode only, passing an argument to the `Until` keyword of a collection's `For each` loop without wrapping it in parentheses caused the value to be silently ignored. The fix makes the parentheses optional.
Changing the Runtime Explorer's refresh interval in the Watch pane had no effect — the display always updated every second regardless of the configured setting.

On macOS in Project mode, running "Check syntax" a second time in a row took roughly ten times longer than the first run, due to macOS's `NewHandle()` memory allocator slowing down over time. The fix switches to `malloc()` for this allocation.
Using the `IN` comparator inside `entitySelection.query()` or `collection.query()` could leak the collection passed as the query condition.
In Client/Server mode, saving a 4D Write Pro document through ORDA and then accessing its entity attribute afterward returned an error instead of working normally.
Using the `@` wildcard together with the `IN` comparator in a query on an object property produced incorrect results — records whose value matched the search string exactly were excluded.
Exporting a 4D View Pro spreadsheet to SVG rendered word-wrapped cell text incorrectly.
In compiled mode, a runtime error in a method that used `#DECLARE` syntax reported the wrong line number in the error dialog.

Calling `min()`, `max()`, or `average()` on an empty entity selection returned "undefined" instead of [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null), inconsistent with the same operations on an empty collection, which correctly return Null.

[WEB Get server info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-get-server-info) always reported the default values for its `webInactiveProcessTimeout` and `webMaxConcurrentProcesses` properties instead of the values actually configured through the database settings or [WEB SET OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-set-option).
In compiled mode, passing [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) as an argument to a project method expecting a pointer parameter could crash the application.
In the French edition, the "Images" tab in 4D Write Pro's top toolbar was mislabeled, displaying "Import/Export" instead.
On macOS, applying a style sheet that used the "system font" with the bold attribute to an object did not actually render the title (e.g., a button's title) in bold.

In an ORDA query, using the `<=` or `>=` comparator together with a trailing wildcard (matching on a suffix) returned only records satisfying the strict `<` or `>` condition, omitting records that matched exactly (`=`).
Exporting a 4D Write Pro document to `.docx` format did not render numbered or bulleted list items correctly when opened in Microsoft Word.

On macOS Big Sur, installing 4D from a disk image (`.dmg`) and then displaying the Structure editor before quitting could crash the application on exit; installing from a `.zip` archive, or not opening the Structure editor, avoided the crash.
Declaring a variable with the `var` syntax across a line continuation (`\`), with a space character before or after the line break, crashed the application during method tokenization.
On Windows, during Japanese text input conversion, the cursor jumped to the start of the converted text block instead of staying at its expected position, usually the end of the block.

Running a built application from the Program Files folder with user settings enabled and a writable data folder crashed 4D when [OPEN SETTINGS WINDOW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-settings-window) tried to open the "User settings for data file" tab (the "Structure settings" tab opened fine). The fix now creates the Settings folder and its XML file alongside the [Data file](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/data-file) if they don't already exist.
On Windows, overwriting an existing label settings file (`*.4lbp`) did not replace it — instead a new file was created with the `.4lbp` extension duplicated in the filename.

Inserting a `span` element without an explicit font into a 4D Write Pro document via [ST SET TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/st-set-text) applied the default font to the inserted text instead of inheriting the document's font; a `p` element was unaffected.
Each call to [SHOW PROCESS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/show-process) toggled the process window's visibility off and back on, causing the screen to flicker.

When a MIME message's `From` header contained a comma (for example `DOE, John <john.doe@4d.com>`), [MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) failed to build a correct mail object, splitting the address into two separate senders (`DOE` and `John <john.doe@4d.com>`).

The first call to [DELAY PROCESS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/delay-process) made inside a worker process was silently ignored; it only took effect once a UI command such as [Open window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-window) or [ALERT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/alert), or a call to [TRACE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/trace), had been executed first.
Splitters placed on a list form could no longer be dragged — an apparent side effect of the fix for ACI0101035.

On macOS Big Sur, launching 4D after installing it (by opening the downloaded disk image and dragging the app into Applications) failed with "Cannot open '4D.app' because the developer cannot be verified"; Volume Desktop and 4D Server were unaffected.

[SET LIST ITEM PROPERTIES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-list-item-properties) required its icon parameter to be specified even when the caller only wanted to change the item's style, which was inconvenient since the icon can be set separately with [SET LIST ITEM ICON](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-list-item-icon).
