The fix makes the parameters following the icon optional (a color still cannot be set without also providing an icon).
Running [FORM Convert to dynamic](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-convert-to-dynamic) against a compiled structure file (`.4DC`) did not load the form's object methods.
In a 4D View Pro spreadsheet, entering a date such as October 26, 2020 into a cell was automatically shifted to October 25, 2020.

Placing a `Signal` object inside a shared object's properties to form an object group did not correctly update the `Signal` object's internal `__LockerID`; it was expected to flip from a negative to a positive value so that other shared objects in the same group could be used with `Use`.
4D View Pro's ribbon interface did not allow importing plain text files whose extension was not `.csv`.

On Windows, when [WRITE PICTURE FILE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/write-picture-file) was called with a default filename ending in `.gif`, the save dialog showed the wrong file extension (`.4pct`).

The "Import CSV file" interface in the 4D View Pro area's File menu only supported actual CSV data — specifying an alternate row or column delimiter such as `\t` or `\n` for other text formats was ignored. The export dialog received the same fix.
The Form editor did not save changes made to a form's HTML Help index (anchor/chapter number) property.

On Windows, using domain-based single sign-on for Client/Server authentication and enabling both request and debug logging could crash the server, because SSO closed the network connection that the logging process was still relying on.
In the Label editor, when a form was used for printing and the "Auto Resize" option was unchecked, the configured number of columns was ignored.

On Windows, when both the Japanese IME's conversion candidate menu and the Method editor's code-completion popup were displayed at the same time, the Japanese input was prematurely confirmed using the first conversion candidate. The fix mimics Visual Studio's behavior so both popups can coexist, though when typing near the bottom of the screen the code-completion popup may still appear behind the IME candidate window.
On macOS, [OBJECT SET FORMAT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-format) no longer worked for changing the resource picture file path of a 3D picture button.

When an object-type field held a collection, simply copying the entity with [OB Copy](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-copy) marked that field as "touched" even though nothing had actually changed.

The `HTTP timeout` option set via [HTTP SET OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-set-option) was not honored by [HTTP Get](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-get): if the server connection succeeded but the response was slow and the connection was never closed, the call would wait indefinitely instead of timing out.

Calling `GET BACKUP INFORMATION` from the client side in remote mode returned the structure's backup information instead of the user's, since the underlying [BACKUP](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/backup) info retrieval ([BACKUP INFO](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/backup-info)) did not distinguish the two contexts.

When processing a MIME message with [MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime), the `name` parameter of the `Content-Disposition` header was not parsed correctly; normally this `name` is carried in the `Content-Type` header, but mail clients such as Thunderbird can read it from either location.

On macOS, if a user enabled Preview in the system print dialog, that preview state persisted even after disabling it programmatically via [SET PRINT PREVIEW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-preview) — a subsequent [WP PRINT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-print) call still showed the preview. [Print form](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-form) was unaffected.
Clicking a listbox row while holding a modifier key to select it did not fire the `On Before Keystroke` event until the listbox regained focus separately.
Using a single tab of the 4D Write Pro widget panel (`WP_Palette_stylesheets`) as a standalone panel produced syntax errors; using the full widget avoided the problem.

Displaying a named selection created by [COPY NAMED SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/copy-named-selection) in a selection-type listbox, selecting multiple rows with Shift-click, and then pressing the Up or Down arrow key highlighted the wrong rows.
Passing an object property as a parameter to [Field name](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/field-name) triggered a compilation error ("Too many parameters has been passed to this method").

Selecting a row with [LISTBOX SELECT ROW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-select-row) and then extending the selection with Shift-click did not select the expected range: instead of extending from the row set by `LISTBOX SELECT ROW`, the selection ran from the first row down to the clicked row.
4D sent an incorrect `length` parameter to ODBC in its call to `SQLBindParameter` — an apparent side effect of the fix for ACI0099846, which itself had fixed a side effect of ACI0101084.

On macOS Big Sur, checkboxes and radio buttons shorter than 15 points were rendered incompletely, cut off on the left side; on Windows, a similar rendering issue affected objects 12 points tall or shorter, but only in the Form editor.
Typing a non-numeric keystroke in a date field's `On Before Keystroke` event erased the first character of the field's existing value unexpectedly.

The new `Is editing text` command did not distinguish between a listbox and its type-ahead field for entity-selection-based listboxes, always returning `False` in that context; selection-type listboxes worked correctly.
On Windows, the `%password` display font was ignored for a field shown in a list form when it wasn't in editing state — the masking only applied during actual data entry.

Converting a database to Project mode turned a minus sign (`-`) in a form object's "variable or expression" attribute into an underscore (`_`) — for example expressions like `This.length-1` or [Add to date](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/add-to-date)([Current date](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/current-date); 1; 0; -1) were corrupted by the conversion.
Converting a document with [VP Convert from 4D View](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-from-4d-view) could fail with error -10713.
On macOS Big Sur, the Cmd+Period keyboard shortcut (Cancel) could neither be assigned nor typed.
In compiled mode, a collection callback method declaring a variant-typed parameter received an undefined value for that parameter on every iteration after the first.

Repeatedly calling [WP Insert break](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-insert-break) inside a loop was noticeably slow, since inserting a break involves creating a new paragraph and is inherently heavier than inserting text into an existing one. The fix roughly doubles the performance of break insertion relative to plain text insertion, though the optimization applies only to off-screen document processing, not to documents currently displayed in a form; for heavy programmatic edits, copying the document to a variable with [OB Copy](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-copy) before processing off-screen is recommended.

Refreshing the current selection shown in a listbox with a new query, then immediately Shift-clicking a row, selected the wrong range — starting from the last previously clicked row rather than the first row — a side effect of the fix for ACI0101433.
Passing a Text-type field to [String](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/string) while no record was selected caused a runtime error.

A collection method's callback declared with `#DECLARE` received corrupted parameters starting from the second iteration — sometimes undefined values, sometimes an object intended for `$1` arriving in `$2` instead.

In Project mode, the listbox `resizingMode` CSS-equivalent attribute was not handled correctly: the Form editor's property list and the underlying JSON representation of the column auto-resizing option (enabled via `rightToLeft`, disabled via `legacy`) were out of sync.

The `@` wildcard for bulk-specifying method names in [SET ALLOWED METHODS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-allowed-methods) was not supported for a 4D View Pro area, even though it should be.

The Japanese IME stayed active when focus moved to an object that could receive focus but not text entry — such as a hierarchical list, ruler, stepper, or listbox — instead of being disabled automatically as it correctly was for buttons, radio buttons, and checkboxes.
On macOS Big Sur, a combo box's text-entry area visually overlapped its own rounded outline, because the custom-drawn focus ring didn't align with the rendered entry area.
On macOS Big Sur, the arrow button on the right side of a pop-up/drop-down menu was rendered with a couple of pixels missing.

On Windows, when PDF was set as the print destination and a print job was started with [OPEN PRINTING JOB](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-printing-job), calling [WP PRINT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-print) displayed the print dialog; even if that dialog was canceled, a file-save dialog still appeared, resulting in an empty PDF being created. Canceling the first dialog was expected to set the `OK` system variable to 0 and skip the second dialog entirely.
Certain fonts (for example "Uni Neue") could not be assigned to a document that had been converted from the legacy 4D Write format.

When duplicate keys inconsistent with the structure definition were detected in the data at startup, the resulting alert was displayed behind the Server administration window (or the 4D Explorer window for 4D standalone), because the alert appeared before the data-file check had finished and the administration window had come to the front.
In Client/Server mode, ORDA entity selections and their related attributes were not transferred correctly whenever an entity's value contained a comma.

Using an object-type parameter in a SOAP web service's input variables crashed the web service server. The fix makes [SOAP DECLARATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/soap-declaration) — which does not support `Is collection` or `Is object` types — return an error instead of crashing.
Entering [Form](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form) in the URL or Progress properties of a web area was not tokenized as a command call.

On macOS, pasting a previously copied or cut cell in a 4D View Pro spreadsheet with the usual Cmd+V shortcut stopped working — an apparent side effect of updating the embedded CEF web engine to version 86.

Nesting one `Use`/`End use` block inside another and, within the inner block, assigning a protected shared object to a property of an object protected by the outer block, produced error -10719 when the inner `End use` executed (because the assignment moved the inner object into the outer object's protection group).
In binary mode, setting a listbox header's image source property to "File" crashed the application immediately.
[WP Get text](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-text) returned an empty string instead of `\r` for a carriage return.

In the Structure editor, typing a new field or relation name in the Inspector palette and then selecting a different field could discard the just-entered name; confirming the edit required pressing Tab or clicking another active object in the Inspector first.

In Client/Server mode, 4D Server could occasionally crash while unzipping a `.4DZ` file right after a packaged project or data file had been swapped in and the server was starting up, apparently due to an issue during archive decompression; restarting a few times usually let the server start successfully.
Switching a listbox's data source from a named selection to the current selection unexpectedly reset some column properties that should have been shared between the two data source types.
[OB Instance of](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-instance-of) failed when checking against `entityClass`, `Dataclass`, or `EntitySelectionClass` in Client/Server mode.

Exporting a 4D Write Pro document to MIME/HTML truncated the beginning of lines whose "wk text indent" standard action used a negative (hanging) indent value; exporting to web-complete HTML was unaffected. Negative indents should simply be ignored during HTML export.

In v18 R5 and later, the popup menu listing field and variable object names sometimes showed names that were concatenations of other object names, an issue specific to the variable name list mode (the object name list mode was unaffected).

Renaming a form object in the Form editor's property list by only changing its letter case (e.g. uppercase to lowercase) was treated as creating a duplicate name, so 4D silently appended a numeric suffix to the new name — a problem specifically affecting objects that had an object method assigned.

Enabling both the Welcome wizard's "don't show at next startup" checkbox and the "Connect to server" dialog's "show this dialog at next startup" checkbox resulted in the Connect dialog not appearing on the next launch, because the `.4DPreferences` file's `automatisms@startup_mode` attribute was set to 0 instead of 3.

Running a client-side data file verification from the MSC failed to produce a viewable report: the downloaded log did not include the required `LogStyleSheet.css`, and in Project mode the button to also download `Verify_Logs.xml` was unresponsive.

In Project mode, setting a listbox column's type to boolean displayed it with the checkbox theme by default but omitted the Title property from the property list; reselecting the checkbox display theme from the popup menu made the Title field appear as expected.
On macOS Big Sur, the Explorer's preview pane did not correctly render a drop-down list preview; the Form editor itself was unaffected.
Valid `#DECLARE` syntax was incorrectly flagged as a syntax error.

Calling [LAUNCH EXTERNAL PROCESS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/launch-external-process) with fewer than four parameters — omitting the error stream (`stdErr`) while still passing `cmd`, `stdIn`, and `stdOut` — caused abnormally high CPU usage and an apparent hang.
Verifying an encrypted data file through the MSC logged error 5 ("table encryption is enabled but data is not encrypted") for a table marked as encryptable that simply had no records yet.

[VP Convert from 4D View](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-from-4d-view) could fail to convert a legacy 4D View document (`.4PV` file); the root cause was a SpreadJS 12 bug where a "duplicate name" exception blocked redraw and left the area unrendered.

Deleting records with [DELETE SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/delete-selection) could corrupt the index on an object-type field, leaving the data file in a state the MSC flagged as corrupted — a cluster index referencing already-deleted records — and requiring repair.

In Project mode, copying and pasting a form object with an assigned object method, then copying that pasted object again into another form, injected extra control characters into the method code of both the copy and the copy-of-copy (the original object's method was unaffected); the bug was specific to copy/paste and did not occur with plain duplication. The root cause was an overlapping byte-order mark (BOM) getting duplicated during the copy.
Under intense processing conditions, an internal array range-check error (`RUNTIME_EXPLORER_HDL`) could occur.
The 4D View Pro formula `COLUMNLETTER`, when called without a parameter, was supposed to return the current column's letter but instead raised an "invalid formula" error.

Converting a 4D View spreadsheet containing a formula parameter that referenced a 4D View area to 4D View Pro dropped the area reference, leaving an empty pair of parentheses instead of preserving it.
Exporting a 4D View Pro spreadsheet to PDF could render a cell's entire text in bold even when only part of it (mixed bold and regular text) should have been bold.

Calling [WA OPEN WEB INSPECTOR](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wa-open-web-inspector) while a CEF web area was displaying a blank page, or on a bare web area, crashed the application (via the embedded engine activation path).

In Client/Server mode only, [Modified record](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/modified-record) returned `True` after successive calls to [SAVE RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/save-record), even though nothing had changed since the last save — a side effect of the fix for ACI0100945.

Pasting text copied or cut from an external application (such as a `.txt` editor) into a 4D View Pro area via right-click or the ribbon interface did not work as expected, though pasting via the Edit menu was fine.

Starting with 18 R2, the Labels editor component (`4D Labels.4dbase`) was missing from the 64-bit 4D Server's `Resources/Internal User Components` folder, preventing [PRINT LABEL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-label) from working server-side; a copy of the component had to be manually added to the project's Components folder as a workaround.

Entering several "contains" conditions joined by "OR" in the Query editor and saving them to disk did not round-trip correctly: reloading the file converted the conditions into "is in list" (strict equality) semantics, and copying the query string to the clipboard showed the wildcard characters had been lost, changing the actual query result.
A method using `#DECLARE` syntax whose return parameter name was omitted returned undefined instead of the actual value — a side effect of the fix for ACI0101458.

Sporadic network disconnections (a "null endpoint" error) could occur when a client resumed a connection after it had been suspended due to an idle timeout. Server-side network request logs showed the exception arising exactly at the moment a suspended process resumed its connection. The root cause was that the two-step reconnection sequence did not correctly anticipate every outcome of a failed first step, an area where the Windows Sockets API's own specification is itself ambiguous.
Exporting a 4D Write Pro document to `.docx` did not preserve `This.xx`-style expressions inserted by an older version of Write Pro as live fields — they were exported as plain static values instead.
In the 4D Mobile Structure section, filtering to show only published tables could trigger a runtime error (#1279) for 4D for iOS.

In a 4D View Pro area using the ribbon toolbar, importing certain spreadsheet files (`.4VP`) suppressed form events such as `On After Edit` or `On Selection Change`; the ribbon interface's own import path was not affected in the same way as importing without the ribbon in use.

In Project mode, running the MSC's "Verify Data" check right after configuring "Data Encryption" returned a misleading error claiming table encryption was not enabled even though the records were encrypted.

Compiling code such as `$fn:=Field name(variable.prop)` or `$fn:=Field name(variable.prop->)` — passing a pointer to a field through an object property or pointer dereference as the parameter to [Field name](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/field-name) — failed with a "missing parameter" compiler error.

On Windows, in a Citrix environment, closing 4D from the taskbar did not shut it down properly: right-clicking the taskbar window in Citrix sends a `WM_CLOSE` message instead of `WM_SYSCOMMAND`/`SC_CLOSE`, which 4D's MDI window did not handle, leaving the application running in the background consuming very high CPU.

In 4D for iOS, configuring a custom formatter on a field in the Labels & Icons section, dragging that field onto the model in the Form section, and then resetting it to the default formatter back in Labels & Icons wrote an invalid format string into `project.4dmobileapp`, crashing the app during data synchronization; removing and re-adding the field to the model worked around it.

Converting an email whose `Content-Type` was `multipart/alternative` with [MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) produced a body with incorrect character encoding.
A hierarchical list's data source ("variable or expression" attribute) did not accept object-style notation such as `Form.var`.

[PRINT LABEL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-label) printed the wrong number of labels per row and left unused margin on the page, wrapping to a new row sooner than the page width actually allowed.
Calling [Compare strings](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/compare-strings) from inside a component crashed the application.
On a 4K or 5K display, the icons in the Write Pro toolbar appeared blurry — an apparent side effect of the fix for ACI0101494.

On macOS, when [ON EVENT CALL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/on-event-call) was used to install an event-handling method, tapping a listbox column header with the trackpad did not fire `On Header Click`, though a regular click did.
Compiling a method could unexpectedly fail with "total size of local variables exceeded 32KB" — a side effect of the fix for ACI0101186.

On macOS, an application folder archived with the [ZIP Create archive](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/zip-create-archive) command could not be expanded using the Finder's built-in Archive Utility, because symbolic links inside the app bundle were not preserved during compression. Expanding the same archive with a 4D command worked correctly.

In 4D View Pro spreadsheets, the `ROUND` function returned an incorrect result when passed an arithmetic expression rather than a direct cell reference or literal value — for example `=ROUND((0.54+0.57)/2;2)` returned 0.56 instead of 0.55. The bug came from the underlying SpreadJS 12 library used in v18 and did not affect later SpreadJS versions; it was fixed by patching the affected rounding code directly.

In 4D View Pro, calling the [VP SET CELL STYLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-set-cell-style) command with a null object failed to clear a cell's applied stylesheet when that style had originally been set through the ribbon interface, because the `parentName` property was not reset. The fix aligns with a SpreadJS API change: resetting a style now requires passing `New object("name"; Null)` rather than `parentName`.

Importing a legacy 4D Write document (.4W7) into 4D Write Pro could crash the application. The crash was traced to an invalid font name (containing a stray `"` sequence) embedded in the source document, which produced malformed XML during conversion.

Calling [SHOW PROCESS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/show-process) unexpectedly brought the target process's window to the very front of the window stack, instead of simply making it visible without forcing it above other windows.

On Windows, running [PRINT SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-selection) on a server started as a service, while printing to PDF through the Microsoft Print to PDF driver, produced a 0 KB empty PDF file instead of the expected content; using [Print form](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-form) instead did not exhibit the problem.
Evaluating a Formula object that returns a time value via `formula.call()` or `formula.apply()` incorrectly returned a Real-type number instead of preserving the Time type.

When converting a legacy 4D Write document to 4D Write Pro, the converter could not determine whether an anchored picture had a fixed size in the source .4W7 file. As a result, pictures that were not fixed-size should have had their width and height converted to `auto`, but this was not being detected correctly.

`WP Get elements` did not return anchored pictures from a 4D Write Pro document in their correct z-order (back-to-front stacking). The fix ensures that pictures returned with the `wk type image anchored` filter are ordered from backmost to frontmost.

In a built 4D Server application, the default HTML Root path shown in the settings dialog referenced a non-existent "Database" subfolder instead of the correct "Server Database" (or "Serveur Database" in the French edition) folder. This was purely a display issue with no functional impact.

The behavior of the star (`*`) parameter for [Is picture file](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/is-picture-file) was reversed relative to its documented spec: omitting the star on a non-picture file with a `.png` extension should return True based on the extension alone but returned False, while passing the star on a picture file with a `.txt` extension should return True based on content analysis but also returned False.

In 4D View Pro, inserting a date value into a cell displayed it using the `mm/dd/yy` format instead of `dd/mm/yy`, even when the spreadsheet's `getCultureInfo()` correctly reported `dd/mm/yy` as the locale date format.

Using [METHOD SET CODE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/method-set-code) to set the code of a table form's method incorrectly tokenized the `On Load` form event constant, replacing it with the name of the table's first field. This only affected methods attached to table forms; other form methods were unaffected.

Running [SET EXTERNAL DATA PATH](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-external-data-path) on a picture field whose storage option was set to store data inside the data file produced orphaned BLOBs, which could subsequently be detected by running a data verification pass in the Maintenance and Security Center (MSC).

In compiled mode, after an application ran for an extended period with many processes active, pointers to form-local variables could become invalid, producing error -20010 ("Bad usage of a pointer on a variable"); on macOS this caused the app to quit, while on Windows it froze. Fixing the issue required recompiling the application.
`MAIL Convert to MIME` could insert an unnecessary underscore character into the `Content-Type` header of the generated email output.

On Windows, calling [Open form window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-form-window) with a Controller form window kind actually displayed a Plain form window instead — the resulting window did not behave as the intended floating window.

In Project mode only, a project converted from a binary database could not be opened if the original database's automatic structure comments contained characters that are not valid under the XML 1.0 specification.

`VP Convert from 4D View` did not correctly convert a legacy 4D View document into 4D View Pro format: the resulting new spreadsheet appeared as an empty, borderless grid with truncated columns, apparently because cells with no value were not handled properly during conversion.
When a virtual structure was configured, opening the Quick Report editor from the User mode Tools menu could return a syntax error instead of opening normally.

In client-server compiled mode only, calling `entitySelection.orderByFormula()` could trigger a "Stack is full" error on the server; the issue was reproducible from an input form but did not occur when the same code was run standalone.

Since v18 R5, launching several processes with the same name in quick succession (via [New process](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/new-process)) could cause the Runtime Explorer to display the same process ID for all of them, even though they were actually distinct processes; this was a display-only issue, but launching identically-named processes concurrently is best avoided for clarity.

Restoring a window from maximized to its normal size changed behavior compared to v17: in v17, un-maximizing resized the window down to the minimum size needed to display its (possibly moved/resized) objects, whereas in v18 the window reverted to its pre-maximize dimensions, which could leave objects that had been resized or moved while maximized rendered outside the visible drawing area.
The Euro currency symbol was not rendered correctly when included in the display format of a drop-down list form object.
An alphanumeric display format applied to a drop-down list or combo box object was not honored — the formatting was simply not rendered.

On Windows in compiled mode, calling a member method that was itself a `Formula` project method through [This](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/this) crashed the application when parameters were passed to it; calling it without parameters worked fine.

In client-server mode, once the 4D Server had itself opened a remote connection to another database, calling member functions on the `ds` object returned information about that remote datastore instead of the server's own local datastore.

Converting a legacy 4D Write document to 4D Write Pro ignored font style information when the font name contained the word "Medium" — for example, "Yu Gothic Medium" was converted to "Yu Gothic Regular" instead of preserving its Medium weight.
On macOS, calling `MAIL Convert from MIME` could crash the application.

In Project mode only, an invisible pop-up/drop-down list object did not correctly render its list items after the form was converted to a project — an exclamation mark ("!") was shown instead of the actual entries.

In Project mode only, enabling the "Not rendered" property on a pop-up menu object failed to hide the "Display format" property, which should not be applicable — and thus should not be shown — in the JSON Property List Editor for a non-rendered pop-up.

In client-server mode, if the client's `inuse.txt` marker file inside its resource/cache folder was not removed for some reason (for instance, an abnormal termination under a Terminal Server/TSE environment), the next connection created a brand-new client cache folder instead of reusing the existing one, even though no process with the recorded PID was actually still running. The fix allows the existing cache folder to be reused in that scenario.
On macOS Big Sur specifically, opening `accounts.google.com` inside a 4D form's embedded web area (with the Embedded Web rendering engine enabled) crashed the application.

Converting a legacy 4D Write document to 4D Write Pro could confuse paragraph styles with character styles, damaging the result. Specifically, some 4D Write documents define "Normal" as a character style rather than a paragraph style, while 4D Write Pro expects "Normal" to be the default paragraph style; the fix ensures the imported "Normal" style is applied at the paragraph level even when the source .4W7 file defined it as a character-level style.

On Windows, with the regional format set to Turkish, displaying a property list in binary mode crashed 4D v18 R5. The crash was a side effect of an internal component having been converted from binary mode to project format, combined with Turkish's special handling of the dotted/dotless "I" characters, which are treated as distinct from the Latin "I".

In the Label editor, applying a display format to a field via the [String](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/string) function had no effect: the format was not reflected when printing or previewing the label.

Text shorter than 112 characters that had been compressed with `COMPRESS BLOB` could not be expanded again with `EXPAND BLOB` — the bug was located in the gzip decompression logic rather than in the compression step itself.

On Windows, concatenating a multi-styled text value produced from a 4D Write Pro document with plain unstyled text, and then displaying the result in a text-entry area, could crash the application. As a side note, the fix does not extend support to the font family "Helvetica Neue LT Std 57 Condensed" on Windows, since its name exceeds GDI's font-name length limit.

A 4D Write Pro document could still display deleted table rows after calling [WP TABLE DELETE ROWS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-table-delete-rows) from within a formula embedded in the document — the rows were not actually removed in that context.
The `lk row is not selectable` list box array attribute did not work correctly on a hierarchical list box that used a row control array.

On Windows, maximizing a form window inside an MDI parent window and then resizing the MDI window caused the form's objects to be resized incorrectly — objects could grow excessively and could not be restored to their original size, and even objects with resize behavior set to "None" were incorrectly resized along with the MDI window.

On Windows, typing Japanese text that included a space into a form text-entry object or list box cell could erase the just-typed text if the space bar was pressed immediately after confirming an IME conversion candidate; the Method Editor was not affected.
On macOS, 3D button objects displayed their title text grayed out whenever their containing window was not the frontmost window.

Calling [BUILD APPLICATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/build-application) from the *On Startup* database method of an uncompiled project did not generate the compiler's error log file, because Design mode is not yet fully set up at the *On Startup* stage.

When the startup mode was set to "Application", structural modifications made through SQL commands such as CREATE TABLE or DROP TABLE were not persisted, since those changes were only saved when the Structure editor itself was opened.

In client-server mode, a local variable stored in a web process did not behave correctly when the "no session" web option was used, because the client-side web server always kept scalable session management enabled regardless of that setting.

When a client began a transaction and then called "Execute on server" (a stored procedure), the transaction state was not immediately propagated to the corresponding server-side twin process; running a database-access command such as `Find in field` on the client first forced the transaction state to synchronize correctly.

On macOS, if a click event on an object placed in a row of a list-form subform opened another window, the subform rows following that object stopped rendering. A related issue where the list-form subform's focus indicator was not displayed was fixed at the same time.
Converting a legacy 4D Write document to 4D Write Pro replaced text set in the Futura font's condensed style with Helvetica's regular style instead of preserving the original font and style.
After a plugin installed on the server was swapped for a different version, the new plugin version was no longer transferred down to connected clients.

Double-clicking a word within text where words were joined by underscore characters no longer selected the full underscore-joined run of text, selecting a single sub-word instead — a side effect of an ICU library update that started treating the underscore as a word-boundary character. The fix restores the pre-v18 R5 behavior, with one deliberate exception: in the Form Editor's property list, double-clicking a dot-notation formula expression still splits the selection at the period so that just the clicked attribute is selected.

The `On Data Change` form event did not fire correctly on a boolean array list box column when its checkboxes were clicked rapidly in succession to toggle several values — some clicks did not generate the event at all, whereas an integer-type array column correctly queued each event.
Inserting a method containing a call to `WP INSERT TABLE` into the Method Editor could crash the application.

On Windows, when static text content was taller than its object's frame, the Form Editor clipped the overflow at the object's bottom edge, but at runtime, for a single line of text that didn't fit the object's height, the text was instead bottom-aligned and rendered above the object's top edge. The runtime behavior for single-line overflow is by design, so the fix instead updates the binary-mode Form Editor's rendering to match the runtime behavior.
The "Search for unused local variables" tool failed to analyze member functions defined inside classes, missing unused local variables in that context.
In client-server mode, `entity.reload()` could not be used on an entity obtained from an entity selection newly created via `dataClass.newSelection()`.

After launching a new process with [New process](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/new-process), aborting it from the Runtime Explorer's execution window worked the first time but failed on a subsequent attempt.

On macOS, when a thermometer/progress bar's format was set to "barber shop" style, setting its data source to a value of 1 (rather than another non-zero value) failed to trigger the animation on Big Sur; Catalina was unaffected.

In client-server mode, if a client locked an entity, locked it a second time, and then cleared the reference by assigning Null to it, the entity's lock could not be released — assigning Null should have freed the locked entity immediately.

Converting a structure to Project mode mishandled fields that used a custom filter format such as `|format1`: the property list displayed the value in red (invalid) because the filter was translated into a malformed JSON pointer like `"numberFormat":{"$ref":"/SOURCES/filters.json#/format1"}` instead of the expected `"numberFormat":"|format1"`.
Converting a structure to Project mode caused inherited form names to be shown in red in the property list, and their value could not be selected/edited.

After changing a picture button's data source from a variable to a file path and then converting the structure to Project mode, the data source name was shown in red in the property list, because the conversion produced an incorrect combination such as `"picture":"var:"` (empty variable name) alongside a stale `"dataSource":"<>vPict"` reference, instead of the expected `"picture":"var:vPict"`.

Pasting text containing invalid control characters such as U+FFFF or U+FFFE — which can occur in content copied from external HTML sources — into a styled text-entry area (including 4D Write Pro areas) failed. The fix also covers assignment to styled-text data sources via `ST` commands, and now such control characters are replaced with a symbol indicating an invalid character rather than causing a failure.
If an application's BackupHistory file became corrupted, the application could no longer launch at all.
Type-ahead suggestions in the Method Editor stopped working across all methods whenever a method named with the pattern "Compiler_xxx" existed in the project.

On macOS with multiple displays connected, calling [Open window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-window) to open a window on the secondary screen (the one without the menu bar) could silently fail to display the window at all.
On Windows, using `WP EXPORT DOCUMENT` to export a 4D Write Pro document to PDF omitted pictures from the output.

With scalable session management enabled, restarting the web server via STOP/START WEB SERVER and then reconnecting from the same client created a brand-new session instead of reusing the existing one; this only affected scalable sessions, not legacy session mode.

Setting a paragraph numbering font family in a 4D Write Pro document via the `wk list font family` constant unexpectedly raised error #205 (invalid constant). The fix renames the constant to `_o_ wk list font family`, giving it the same value as `wk list font`.

Restarting a server published as a Windows service using [RESTART 4D](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/restart-4d) failed when the service name began with a number, because the updater could not stop the service in that case.

In client-server mode, evaluating `OB Entries(cs).length` from the *On Startup* database method returned a count lower than the actual number of entries, because 4D Remote loads data classes asynchronously; waiting and re-evaluating afterward returned the correct count. The fix ensures *On Startup* runs only after data classes have finished loading.

After a field was added to a table that already contained records, existing records had a null value for that field. Calling `max()`, `min()`, or `average()` on an entity selection of such records returned `undefined` instead of properly accounting for the null values; forcing an update of the records with "Map null values to blank values" enabled worked around the issue.

In a 4D Write Pro area, positioning the cursor just before an already-inserted formula reference and clicking the toolbar's "Insert expression" button re-displayed the existing formula's editor in edit mode instead of opening a fresh insertion editor. The fix opens the editor in edit mode only when the selection is empty at that point, and in insert mode when the existing formula is actually selected.

Since 18 R5, calling `Get edited text` inside an `On Before Keystroke` event returned the edited area's content including the very keystroke that triggered the event, rather than only the content as it existed just before that keystroke.
The topmost object in the Import & Export dialog was not adapted for dark mode and remained rendered in white regardless of the active appearance.

In Project mode, if a data file's field index type did not match the type recorded in the project's catalog, the Structure editor displayed the data file's index type rather than the project's, making it impossible to change the index type simply by swapping in a different structure/project. Binary mode correctly used the structure's own index setting.

In 4D View Pro spreadsheets, the `ROUND` function could return an incorrect value — for example `=ROUND(18.205;2)` returned 18.2 instead of 18.21 — due to a bug in the underlying SpreadJS library; the fix backports a SpreadJS 14.0.8 patch into the SpreadJS 12.2.5 build used by this version.
On Windows, clicking a combo box object triggered spurious `On Activate` and `On Deactivate` form events on every click.

Printing a 4D View Pro spreadsheet with `VP PRINT` targeting a PDF file output incorrectly rendered any picture returned by a formula as literal text "_Pict_" instead of the actual image; exporting directly to PDF (rather than printing to a PDF file) worked correctly.
If a component contained an empty folder named with an invalid localization identifier such as "enl.lproj" inside its Resources folder, the host database application would quit unexpectedly.
An email attachment in `application/pdf` format was lost when the message was processed through `MAIL Convert from MIME`, so PDF attachments handled via the IMAP Transporter went missing.
In the French edition of 4D, the function list shown in each category of the 4D View Pro formula editor did not display the correct set of functions.
In Project mode only, combo box objects did not support drag-and-drop (drop) events.

Passing an email consisting only of plain text to `MAIL Convert from MIME` returned a mail object with no body content, specifically when the message lacked a `Content-Type` header at all — a header that RFC 1341 explicitly allows to be omitted.
Using `Choose` as a sort condition inside `ORDER BY FORMULA` could produce a compile error.
Passing a text-type field as a parameter to a compiled component method, at a moment when no current record was loaded, could trigger a runtime error when the field was subsequently accessed.

In the Label editor, dragging a field into the layout or concatenating fields together worked, but editing an already-inserted concatenated expression and confirming the change did not actually save the modification.

The `sk width insensitive` (width-insensitive) constant option of `Compare strings`, used to ignore half-width/full-width differences, did not correctly treat half-width and full-width Katakana characters bearing a dakuten or handakuten diacritic as equivalent.
In Project mode only, on macOS, a form with multiple pages that had a web area on page 1 could end up with that web area invisible after navigating away to another page and then back to page 1.

Running a query on an already-narrowed entity selection using a `NOT IN` condition against an empty collection incorrectly returned all entities in the data class instead of respecting the existing entity selection.

In the Quick Report editor's cross-table tool, clicking a cell's contextual button to show its associated pop-up window caused that pop-up to appear shifted unexpectedly to the left of its correct position.
On macOS, when a tab control's data source used object notation and the control was rendered as a drop-down (due to limited width), individual tab items could not be selected.
On Apple Silicon only, converting a 4D View Pro spreadsheet that contained a floating picture with `VP convert to picture` raised an error; the same operation worked correctly on Intel-based Macs.
Converting a 4D View Pro spreadsheet containing a floating picture to SVG format with `VP Convert to picture` produced a truncated image instead of the complete picture.
Executing a 4D for iOS action whose label name contained a slash character ("/") raised an error.
Exporting a 4D View Pro spreadsheet that contained merged cells to SVG picture format did not render the merged cells correctly.
A REST session could no longer be dropped from the Administration window if that session had executed a REST request that ran a 4D project method.

In Project mode only, after a binary database was converted to a project, connecting a client to the server — even after folder synchronization had finished — could take noticeably longer for the application to actually finish starting up.
`Encrypt data BLOB` and `Decrypt data BLOB` were not actually thread-safe, contradicting the documentation, which claimed they were.
Passing a pointer to a local variable as a parameter to a method used as the formula for `APPLY TO SELECTION` raised a syntax error instead of executing normally.

On Windows, each call to `HTTP Get` created a new handle that was never released, which could be observed accumulating in the Windows Resource Monitor. The leak was in the code that reads proxy settings from the registry, and the fix also benefits web areas and the Design mode Explorer, which share that code path.

In Project mode only, if an application's help tip text, defined via the toolbox, referenced an interprocess variable together with an STR# resource index, hovering over the object showed the raw resource reference instead of the resolved help tip text.

When the legacy network layer was in use, the Remote Debugger could crash; if "Enable Remote Debugger at startup" was also set, the client crashed immediately at startup. As a workaround, the `remote_debugger_auto_attach` key could be removed from the `4DPreferences` file. Note that using the Remote Debugger still requires the new network layer to be enabled even after this fix.

`EXECUTE FORMULA` generated a runtime error even when an error-handling method had already been installed with `ON ERR CALL`, because the error was raised before that handler had a chance to intercept it.

The `CommonCopyright` build XML key was not applied to standalone applications or built server applications (though it worked correctly for built client applications); the `RuntimeVLCopyright` and `ServerCopyright` keys were likewise not applied.

For emails encoded as `us-ascii`, dot-stuffing sequences (a line containing just "CR . CR") caused the remainder of the message body to be truncated; messages using `quoted-printable` encoding were unaffected.

In the Form Editor, the Advanced Properties panel for an Area List Pro (ALP) area no longer displayed its list of columns. Note: for projects exported from binary mode, forms containing plug-in areas need to be re-exported for this fix to take effect.

The `objectGUID` value returned by `LDAP Search` for an LDAP object came back as garbled text, because `LDAP Search` converts binary values to strings assuming numeric data, whereas a GUID is raw binary data that the conversion mangled — a property specific to Microsoft Active Directory (platforms like OpenLDAP on Ubuntu either omit it or store it as a string). The fix returns the GUID as a hexadecimal string instead.
Searching the message body for Japanese text via the IMAP Transporter's search method against a Gmail mailbox incorrectly returned every message in the inbox instead of only the matching ones.

Exporting a 4D Write Pro document that used stylesheets to HTML (whether via direct HTML export or HTML-from-MIME export) could produce excessively tight line spacing, because when a class or text span's style overrode the font size, common browsers did not recompute the inherited line-height (specified as a percentage) to match.
When data-file encryption was enabled, Text, BLOB, Picture, and Object fields whose storage option kept them inside the data file were not actually being encrypted.

Once a date field's display format was modified in the property list or the project was exported, `EXPORT TEXT` permanently reverted to using the shortest date format for that field rather than honoring the configured display format.
Several newer commands — including `WP Find all`, `WP Find next`, `WP Find previous`, and `Compile project` — were missing their tooltip/help description in the Method Editor.
In a list box, when a cell had a choice list applied, its text was vertically aligned slightly too high compared to a normal cell in the same column.

In Project mode, the automatic maximum-length control for alphanumeric field input areas was not enforced; data exceeding the field's defined character limit was silently truncated only once the record was actually saved to the database.

`ORDER BY FORMULA` still evaluated its formula even when the current selection was empty and there were no records to apply it to, so a formula that indexed into an array with an invalid item number returned an out-of-bounds error instead of simply skipping evaluation.
Changing a list box column's data type from Text to Boolean unexpectedly caused 4D to quit.
A server application built with the engine (Engined 4D Server) still displayed menu items for enabling the Remote Debugger, even though these should be absent or disabled for such deployments.

In a list box bound to an entity selection, if a class method opened a dialog and the list box's footer displayed the `Sum` of a related entity's values, closing the dialog left the class method's `This` pointing to an entity rather than back to the class itself.

In a list box bound to an entity selection, using the `unselectable` property returned by a meta-info formula to make a row non-selectable correctly prevented clicking it, but the current item and current item number properties were still updated as if the row had been selected.

The trailing folder separator was unexpectedly stripped from a web root folder path: if `WEB SET ROOT FOLDER` was called without a trailing separator on the path, the path returned by `Get 4D folder` with the `HTML Root folder` selector also lacked one, whereas a trailing separator should be added automatically when omitted.
On Windows, a picture pop-up menu did not visually highlight the currently selected element.
In Project mode only, hyperlinks inside a project method's markup documentation no longer opened when clicked.
Text in the "Database settings" dialog was extremely hard to read when dark mode was active.
Compacting a data file with the "force updating of records" option could crash the application when a record contained a 4D Write Pro document with embedded formulas.
A splitter's line color was not carried over when exporting the structure to Project mode.
Enabling data-file encryption caused the Maintenance and Security Center (MSC) to unexpectedly display a warning (yellow triangle) for a table that had no records at all.

Calling `entitySelection.drop()` to delete every record in a table could deadlock, because the order in which internal semaphores were acquired was not safe against concurrent access to the same table from another thread.
In client-server mode, computing an `INTERSECTION` between a process set and a local set returned the local set's original content unchanged, rather than the correct intersection of the two sets.

Changing a persistent database parameter — specifically the `SQL Engine case sensitivity` value via `SET DATABASE PARAMETER` — more than once from within a `4DSCRIPT` execution context, before running any queries, caused a deadlock that froze the application.
In client-server mode, an object of a user class returned from the server lost its class identity on the client: `OB Class().name` reported "Object" instead of the actual class name.

In Project mode only, opening a v18 project with v19 rewrote the *catalog.4DCatalog* file every time, inserting a line break just before the closing tag of every `<tip>` element (used for field/table help tips) — a change not present up through v18.4 HF3. This had no functional effect but generated large numbers of spurious diffs under version control.
In client-server mode only, calling `entity.reload()` on an entity produced by `entity.clone()` reloaded both the cloned entity and the original source entity, instead of only the clone.

In client-server mode, opening Design mode on a 4D Remote machine separate from the 4D Server and running the Explorer's "Show all data classes" command displayed only user classes, omitting data classes entirely.
Each call to `GET HIGHLIGHT` returned a value one greater than the previous call, incrementing indefinitely instead of returning the actual current highlight state.

In Project mode only, when form objects were grouped, the resulting group information was written into the .4DForm JSON file listed per-page rather than in alphabetical order, making version-control diffs harder to manage; groups should instead be listed independent of page order.
In 4D View Pro, after updating a spreadsheet's print settings with `VP SET PRINT INFO`, a subsequent `VP Print` produced only a blank page instead of printing the actual content.

On macOS, in Project mode, when a tab control was too narrow for its content and rendered as a drop-down pop-up menu instead, that pop-up was stretched to fill the full width of the tab control rather than sizing itself to fit its longest menu item.

On Windows, capturing keystrokes with `ON EVENT CALL` while modifier keys were held returned incorrect character codes: pressing Control+Shift with a character returned the raw key code of the pressed key rather than the actual typed character in the `KEYCODE` system variable, and pressing Control alone with a character returned a control-code value instead of the expected character code.

Importing a .docx document into 4D Write Pro where a table cell's merge field had formatting applied (e.g. `MERGEFIELD pt_FC \# $,#.00`) correctly extracted the merge field name (`«pt_FC»`), but the text value subsequently returned by `WP Get text` had extra line breaks appended after it (`«pt_FC»\r\r`).

On Windows, SVG images created programmatically in a 4D Write Pro document were no longer displayed when the document was exported to PDF; documents printed to PDF via [WP PRINT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-print) were unaffected.
[`JSON Validate`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/json-validate) validated only the first item of an object array in a JSON schema, silently skipping validation of all subsequent array items.

In Client/Server, saving a relation attribute a second time within the same transaction incorrectly failed with a stamp-mismatch error, because the entity's stamp had already been incremented by the first save.

On Windows only, since v19 the TinyMCE HTML editor's spell-check no longer worked when displayed in a CEF-based web area; the fix disables `WinUseBrowserSpellChecker` as Windows CEF migrates toward its own native spell checker instead.
Changing the field entry order on page 0 of a project-mode form had no effect; the setting was silently ignored.
In the Explorer window, selecting a table on the "Home" tab did not populate the field list on the right side of the dialog, unlike the "Tables" page which showed it correctly.

On Windows, after moving the window containing an integrated (embedded-engine) web area, an HTML dropdown menu reopened at the window's previous screen position rather than its new one; clicking the window once after moving it worked around the issue.
Converting a binary structure containing emoji in field comments to Project mode produced an invalid/malformed catalog.4DCatalog XML file.

Formulas (e.g. field references) inserted into a 4D Write Pro document could not be copied and pasted into other applications; the fix corrects the HTML pasteboard data, since Microsoft Word prefers HTML over RTF when both are present and previously failed to paste for that reason.

[`Compare strings`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/compare-strings) with the `sk width insensitive` option failed to treat half-width and full-width dakuten (voiced sound marks) as equivalent when comparing Japanese strings such as ゆーざー and ユーザー, though it worked correctly for characters without dakuten.
On Mac, in Project mode, clicking a popup/dropdown menu taller than 23 points drew the focus highlight ("ghost blue line") at the wrong position; objects of 23 points or less were unaffected.

Displaying a View Pro area on an input form and moving to another record via automatic navigation actions (e.g. [`NEXT RECORD`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/next-record)) left the View Pro area's data-source object empty instead of retaining its value.

Copying a cell's formula from one View Pro area and pasting it into another pasted the computed value instead of the formula when using standard keyboard shortcuts; using the ribbon interface's copy/paste worked as expected.
In Project mode only, calling [`REJECT`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/reject) inside a field's input event no longer prevented the entry from being validated/accepted.
In Client/Server, calling `entitySelection.fromCollection()` from the client side stored date values inside object fields as ISO-formatted strings instead of as native date values.

The IMAP transporter's `getMail` could fail to retrieve attachment file names when the MIME header used an unsupported encoding (e.g. Vietnamese Windows-1258); the fix now returns the encoded string as-is when the header cannot be decoded, rather than mangling it.

Repeatedly calling [`Process activity`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/process-activity) or [`OB Get`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-get) (when reading a text-type property) on 4D Server leaked memory with each call.

In Binary mode, converting a database to Project mode could reset a list box's header/column font color and alignment: properties explicitly set to "Automatic" were omitted from the export and ended up inheriting the list box's overall settings instead of retaining their individual override.
On Mac, attempting to build and install a 4D for iOS app via the "Install" button while no device was connected over cable displayed an error instead of a clearer message.

In the Structure editor, changing a Picture/Object/BLOB field's storage option from "In record" to "In data file" or "Outside data file" set the "Max size intern" value to 2147483647 instead of 0; reopening the Inspector afterward showed the correct value of 0. Text fields were unaffected.

When called from a compiled component, [`METHOD GET PATHS`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/method-get-paths) failed to see the host application's shared methods if the host database was in .4DZ format.

In Client/Server, if a connection attempt to a recently-used server failed after network settings had changed, an `unuse.txt` file was left behind in the client cache; since this file should only exist until a connection succeeds, its presence caused a brand-new local cache folder to be created on every subsequent reconnect attempt, and stale server-side sessions/licenses were never reclaimed.
On Windows, in the 4D Server administration window, the search field's magnifying-glass icon overlapped the text-entry area.

In Client/Server, if a component's folder contained a Resources subfolder alongside archives created by earlier client connections, restarting after swapping the component did not regenerate the cache, so client-side resources were never updated; the fix applies the same cache-refresh logic already used for the host's Resources folder to components as well.
Since v18.4 HF3, disabling a button whose title had a custom color no longer grayed out the title text.

In Client/Server, if the [`On Startup` database method](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/on-startup-database-method) contained code, launching 4D Remote against a database with relations defined between tables produced an unexpected client-side execution error about the relation path.
In Client/Server, when using the Form Editor from a local client, dataclasses no longer appeared as data-source candidates when building an entity-selection list box.

If a server called via [`WEB SERVICE CALL`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-service-call) returned a 500 status with an HTML body, the parser attempted to load external resources such as DTDs, which could freeze the application; the fix skips parsing the body when the `Content-Type` isn't XML, and the raw HTML can still be retrieved via [`WEB SERVICE Get info`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-service-get-info) if needed.

If a client's cached `uuid.txt` file was corrupted, that client connecting to the server caused any stored procedure currently running server-side to be killed; databases still using the legacy network layer were unaffected.
In Project mode, a Line form object's dotted-line style as configured in the property list did not match the style actually rendered on the form.

Setting Write Pro text to subscript or superscript altered the line height/spacing; the fix aligns behavior with the 4D Write plugin and Microsoft Word, though existing documents may see paragraph styling or page-break positions shift as a result.
Editing a time-type cell in a collection-based list box did not save the correct value afterward.
The component method *SVG_Get_version* always returned 0.0; the fix now returns the running 4D version instead of a component-specific version number.

Importing an XML file whose *encoding* attribute was omitted, then exporting it again via a DOM command, wrote out an empty `encoding=""` attribute; since *encoding* is optional, it should be omitted from the output entirely when not set on import.

In Client/Server only, loading an entity with an Object-type field took 2 to 50 times longer ("exec_duration" in the request log) than loading a BLOB of equivalent size — roughly 5x longer in typical cases — even though the issue did not reproduce in standalone mode, indicating the slowdown was not caused by object parsing itself.

On Windows, exporting a Write Pro document containing SVG pictures to PDF rendered all `textArea` element text in black, ignoring the actual text color; printing to PDF via a printer driver was unaffected.

[`VP SET PRINT INFO`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-set-print-info) required the View Pro `printInfo.paperSize.kind` value to be lower-case (e.g. `a4`); upper-case values such as `A4` were rejected.

After setting the paper size as a string with [`VP SET PRINT INFO`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-set-print-info), [`VP Get print info`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-get-print-info) returned the wrong `paperSize.kind` value — an internal SpreadJS constant instead of the paper-size name.

In Client/Server, if a client running a stored procedure was forcibly disconnected (e.g. crash or network loss), the server's user/license count became inconsistent because the client's connection license was not released as it should have been.

On macOS, the [Web Server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-server) could not be started on port 80 bound to a specific IP address (no helper-tool install prompt appeared), whereas binding to "any address" (0.0.0.0/::) worked fine; the fix restores use of the privileged-port helper tool whenever a specific address other than "any" is specified.
Hyperlinks imported into a Write Pro document from HTML sometimes did not display correctly.

In the Method Editor, code completion did not offer property/member-function suggestions after typing dot notation on a plain `Object`-typed variable (`C_OBJECT` or `var : Object`); it worked correctly for `var : 4D.Object`.

When a server returned invalid JSON with a `text/plain` content type, [`HTTP Get`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-get) failed to set [`Null`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) into the object-type variable receiving the response, as it should when the payload can't be parsed as JSON.

For a built (engined) server application, if its *Server Database* folder contained a *Resources* subfolder, the first client connection created a *Caches* folder (with *cache.xml* and *.4darchive* files) inside it — an unwanted modification of the installed application package; the fix makes *Resources*/*Libraries* caching behave the same way it already does for *Components*/*Plugins*.

In Project mode, selecting form objects by drag-rectangle in the Form Editor drew visible borders around elements that should stay invisible — transparent splitters and drop-down list frames — with the drawn rectangle sometimes larger than the actual object.
In compiled mode, an error thrown inside a class member function displayed the wrong line of code in the error dialog — the line following the actual point of failure.

With the legacy network layer, publishing a client-side SOAP server in preemptive mode could freeze the application, because enabling preemptive mode for the [Web Server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-server) in the server-side database settings also forced the client's SOAP server into preemptive mode even though the legacy layer doesn't support it; the fix forces both the Web Server and SOAP server to cooperative mode whenever the legacy network layer is used.
The `--cache-folder-name` command-line argument for customizing an engined (built) server's cache folder location had no effect.
Converting a form created in a much older 4D version to v19 turned enterable checkboxes into non-enterable ones.
Converting a 4D Write document to 4D Write Pro could insert unexpected extra tab characters into the text.
On Mac, in the 64-bit version, starting a drag-and-drop operation from a plugin area with Option+click no longer worked, unlike the 32-bit version where it did.

Inserting an image into a Write Pro document by importing a file set the image's "alt" (alternate text) attribute to the file's full original file-system path instead of just its name — a problem when sharing or exporting the document, since it leaks local path information.
Since v18.2, the Label Editor no longer displayed formatted or expression-based fields (e.g. `[Table_1]Field_2+"bbb"` or `String:C10(...)`) correctly, printing only the plain field value instead.

[`IMAP New transporter`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/imap-new-transporter) could not connect to T-Online (Deutsche Telekom) mail servers, which require an older IMAP syntax — commands sent in uppercase with a period prefix (e.g. `.LOGIN`).
Table cells in a Write Pro document containing bulleted or numbered-list text became empty after the document was saved and reopened.
[`SQL LOGIN`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-login) set the system variable `OK` to 1 even when the user cancelled the connection dialog, instead of leaving it at 0.

Exporting a Write Pro document to MIME/HTML did not correctly convert vertical cell alignment for text in table cells — cells taller than their text always came out centered regardless of the actual setting.
Bringing a form containing an enterable list box back to the front and then pressing the Down arrow key could crash the *com.4d.gui* module.
On Mac, since v19, confirming Japanese IME text conversion in the Method Editor with the Return key inserted an unwanted extra line break.

[`IMAP New transporter`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/imap-new-transporter)'s `searchMails()` method could return error 16 when a mailbox held a very large number of messages (e.g. over 10,000).
Web log files written in ELF (Extended Log File) format were malformed — header names used uppercase letters, which broke some parsing tools, and columns did not align with their headers.

`collection.remove(index; howMany)` ignored the starting `index` and always removed `howMany` elements counted from the end when `howMany` exceeded the number of elements remaining from that index; fixed starting in v19 LTS, while v18 retains the previous behavior for compatibility.

Dragging and dropping fields onto a View Pro pivot table did not work, because the `WA enable URL drop` web-area preference (defaulted to disabled to stop file paths from navigating away the displayed page) also blocked ordinary in-page drag-and-drop; the fix scopes that preference to file/URL drops only.

Exporting an application to Project mode converted "highlight" buttons into invisible buttons but also unexpectedly enabled their *On Mouse Move* object event; the fix only fires that event when the object actually has Help Tips configured, since On Mouse Move is otherwise only needed for showing tips.

On Mac, calling [`SET ABOUT`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-about) no longer customized the "About..." menu item text, a regression caused by a startup-sequence change in 18 R6; the fix ensures the menu updates when the command is called from a project method executed after *On Startup*.

On Mac (Project mode) and Windows, inline-editing a static text object or button title while the Form Editor was zoomed drew the text-entry area at standard (unzoomed) size instead of scaling it with the zoom level.

In interpreted mode, calling a method with a parameter type incompatible with its `#DECLARE` declaration did not raise a type error — the passed value was simply assigned as-is; the fix makes interpreted mode raise error 54, matching compiled-mode behavior, except for `C_@`-declared parameters, which are still cast to a default value of the expected type.
A third-party SOAP client authenticating against the 4D [Web Server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-server)'s web service could be refused when its password digest was hashed with MD5.

In a Write Pro document, if a bookmark's range text included a `¶` (pilcrow), text retrieved via [`WP Get text`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-text) could be missing some of those paragraph marks, because keyboard-based range selection was short one line break; selecting the range instead with [`WP SELECT`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-select) avoided the issue.
Even with the Structure setting "keep only the N most recent backups" configured, the *backupHistory.json* file kept every past backup entry and grew without bound.
On Windows, clicking the down-arrow button of a combo box bound to a zero-element array made the application stop accepting any keyboard input afterward, including Enter/Escape to close the form.
Calling `collection.query()` with the `IN` comparison operator on an empty collection crashed the application.
Executing the (deprecated) `_o_QUERY SUBRECORDS` command while debug log recording was active crashed the application.
In Project mode, fields displayed by [`QUERY BY EXAMPLE`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query-by-example) were not enterable, preventing users from typing search criteria.

Restarting a project or database without quitting the application could make [`Open form window`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-form-window) fail to open a toolbar-type window, returning error -10613 ("window already open") due to a timing conflict with the design-mode toolbar.

Calling [`HTTP Request`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) repeatedly in a loop against the same API could occasionally return error #17 ("unimplemented control instruction"); the real cause was a timeout — no response arrived within the duration configured via [`HTTP SET OPTION`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-set-option) — and the fix corrects the error message to reflect that.
A horizontal (or vertical) line form object's default width (or height) was 1 instead of 0, so setting "line width" greater than 1 could produce a blurry, anti-aliased line instead of a sharp one.
Truncating a table immediately before a subsequent uniqueness (unicity) test could let the test incorrectly pass, since the constraint was not properly re-validated against the truncated data.

In Client/Server, a list box showing an automatic-calculation footer on an entity-selection data source sent a network request to the server on every redraw, even when the entity selection had not changed and no recalculation was needed.

Executing [`SET DATABASE PARAMETER`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-parameter) and [`APPLY TO SELECTION`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/apply-to-selection) at the same time (e.g. from concurrent processes) crashed the application.
Sending an email via SMTP Transporter with an inline (embedded) image attached could result in the attachment not appearing in the iOS Mail app.
On Mac, typing Japanese text into a list box cell and pressing Tab confirmed the IME conversion and moved to the next cell instead of paging through the IME candidate list as it should.

Changing a multi-style text area's background color via `ST SET ATTRIBUTE` sometimes failed to correctly update the `background-color` attribute of the underlying `<span>` tags, particularly when spans were nested and background colors spanned multiple nesting levels.

[`OBJECT SET STYLE SHEET`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-style-sheet) could not be used to clear a password font from an object; the fix makes [`OBJECT SET FONT`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-font) and [`OBJECT SET FONT SIZE`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-font-size) automatically clear the object's style sheet (as documented), and passing an empty string to `OBJECT SET STYLE SHEET` now also clears it.

When the database setting "allow user settings in an external file" was enabled, the "use preemptive processes" setting was incorrectly read from the user's external *settings.4DSettings* file instead of being scoped exclusively to the Structure settings.

When a list box column's background or alternating-row background was set via a CSS class (`fill`/`alternateFill`), the color was correctly shown in the property list but not reflected in the Form Editor preview.
In Binary mode, a list box column displaying a 64-bit integer field could not have a number display format applied.

In the French edition, the Method Editor did not recognize the French command name `WP Insérer formule` (equivalent to [`WP Insert formula`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-insert-formula)); it had to be typed using its English name instead.
In the French edition, the code editor failed to recognize the command `WA Démarrer hors écran`, tokenizing it as a process variable instead, because its official name contains a hyphen.
In the French edition, the method property label "uniquement utilisé dans les projets compilées" had a grammatical error (it should read "projets compilés").

On Mac, changing the target Xcode version could break recompilation of the Apple Silicon target with the error "PCH file uses an older PCH format that is no longer supported," because the C++ precompiled header cache no longer matched; clearing Xcode's cache files resolves the issue.

In Project-mode forms, if a non-enterable/non-focusable object was included in the tab entry order (`entryOrder`), tabbing could land on it and leave nothing focused, instead of skipping to the nearest enterable object; the fix restricts such objects so they can gain focus only via a click, [`GOTO OBJECT`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/goto-object), or by being first in the entry order when the form opens, but never via Tab.

On Mac, typing Japanese text continuously into the Explorer in Design mode (without pressing Return to confirm each IME conversion) inserted characters at the wrong cursor position, scrambling the resulting text.

In the Runtime Explorer, if a watch expression referenced a local variable and the user switched to monitor a process that had already been aborted, the application crashed — more likely to occur with a shorter display refresh interval.

After splitting a statement across multiple lines, type-ahead suggestions on lines after the first incorrectly included the very variable name currently being typed as one of its own completion candidates.
On Mac, typing consecutive Japanese text into a form object without confirming each conversion with Return inserted characters at the wrong cursor position, producing garbled text.
A static text object embedding a real-number process variable with a named format (e.g. `<vTotal;|Montant`) did not display the formatted value correctly.

[`INTEGRATE MIRROR LOG FILE`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/integrate-mirror-log-file) in strict mode returned an error when the server was started in non-interactive (service/headless) mode.
[`OPEN RUNTIME EXPLORER`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-runtime-explorer) had no tooltip/help description shown for it.

Calling *POP3 Transporter*'s `checkConnection()` against certain mail servers hung for tens of seconds before eventually returning an error, because `checkConnection()` first sends a `CAPA` command to discover supported authentication mechanisms, and some POP3 servers reject that command outright; the fix now continues processing immediately when `CAPA` errors instead of waiting for a response.

If [`FORM GOTO PAGE`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-goto-page) was called during the "On Load" [form event](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-event) to jump to another page, the form still briefly flashed page 1 before switching.

In Client/Server, `dataClass.query()` misinterpreted string placeholder values that looked like a date (format `nnnn-nn-nn`), evaluating them as dates instead of literal strings; passing the same value directly as a string literal (not via a placeholder) worked correctly.

In interpreted mode, a list-box row-control array declared as a Longint array was reinitialized as a Boolean array when the form loaded; the fix defaults an undeclared control array to Longint (previously Boolean), retaining Boolean only for arrays already explicitly declared as Boolean, and going forward assigning a boolean value to a control array that only appears in the property list — never declared in code — will raise an error.

When the data language was set to Japanese, [`Compare strings`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/compare-strings) in `sk strict` mode always treated case as insensitive even without the `sk case insensitive` option, unlike the Japanese edition's normal case-sensitive default; separately, `sk kana insensitive` did not work correctly when "use string comparison for text search" mode was enabled unless combined with `sk diacritic insensitive` or `sk case insensitive`.
