The fix switches Japanese case handling from ICU level-3 collation to a dedicated `CaseLevel` option layered on level-2 collation, since level-3 collation cannot be combined with the language-specific text-search "Alternate" setting.

On Windows, [`Print form`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-form) did not render "Calibri Bold Italic" correctly when that font was applied via [`OBJECT SET FONT`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-font) to a text-input object — only the bold attribute was applied, not italic; setting both attributes via [`OBJECT SET FONT STYLE`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-font-style) worked around it.
In the Quick Report editor, a column's header showed the assigned formula's name instead of its generic identifier (e.g. `C1`).

[`OBJECT SET SCROLL POSITION`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-scroll-position) and [`OBJECT GET SCROLL POSITION`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-scroll-position) did not work on subforms (widgets) of the detail-form type; the fix extends both commands to support them, though when the subform's content is set via [`OBJECT SET SUBFORM`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-subform), the scroll position can only be manipulated after the subform has actually finished loading — since loading is asynchronous, this typically requires spreading the logic across two [`CALL FORM`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/call-form) event cycles and may cause a brief visible flicker.
*IMAP Transporter*'s `getMIMEAsBlob` could hang indefinitely on certain mail servers, not reproducible with Gmail accounts; this is a separate issue from ACI0102365.

Passing a real number missing its integer part (e.g. `.5`) to [`EXECUTE FORMULA`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/execute-formula) raised a syntax error, unlike an invalid object-notation expression which did not.

With list box "single-click edit" mode enabled, double-clicking a row, scrolling down, then double-clicking another row could highlight the wrong row — the first click of the second double-click entered cell-edit mode and triggered a scroll, shifting the target out from under the second click before it landed.
An expression like `collection[0]` referencing a collection element could be assigned to from a method but was rejected as non-assignable when used the same way in a form object's expression/formula.

On Windows Server with Volume Shadow Copy (VSS) enabled, successively switching projects via File menu > "Open Recent Project" could crash 4D Server — the crash occurs in the thread managing VSS and is specific to Windows Server 2022, not reproducing on earlier server versions.

A list box configured with automatic row height, when printed via [`Print object`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-object), could have its last row split across a page break or cut off mid-row, depending on the paper margins and list box content.
A View Pro spreadsheet containing merged cells did not convert correctly when exported to SVG.

Calling [`WEB SET HTTP HEADER`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-set-http-header) from inside a class function always returned HTTP status 200 OK regardless of the actual error code set, whereas calling it from a project method worked correctly.
On Mac, hyperlinks and formula references inside styled text used the same color in both light and dark mode, making them invisible against a dark background.
In Project mode, duplicating a class from the Explorer's "Home" tab silently did nothing.

For a table with the "Encryptable" option enabled but containing unencrypted records, compacting the data file via MSC with "force updating the record" enabled returned an error, because 4D incorrectly treated "encryptable" tables as always "encrypted"; standard compacting was unaffected.

In the Method Editor, if a closing bracket appeared inside a comment while its matching opening bracket was in actual code, placing the caret at the opening bracket did not trigger brace-matching highlighting.

Querying a collection of objects for a property equal to `null` incorrectly returned matches when that property held an entity reference — the entity was returned as if it matched `null`; the same incorrect behavior occurred for properties holding a [`File`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/file) or [`Folder`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/folder) reference, unlike properties holding a plain `Object`.
Quitting the application while a compilation was still in progress could crash it.

On Windows, printing a 4D Write document (containing TIFF images across at least two pages) after converting it to 4D Write Pro returned an "unknown error," though exporting via .xps or "Microsoft Print to PDF" worked fine; further testing reproduced the same error with an unrelated form combining TIFF images and static text and [`PAGE BREAK`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/page-break) printed repeatedly in the same job, confirming the root cause was in the physical printer driver / Direct2D print pipeline rather than Write Pro itself.
In a Write Pro area, switching the view mode from "Draft" to "Page" did not immediately show the vertical ruler the first time.
Combining string-subscript syntax (`string[[index]]`) with dot notation, e.g. `$a:=$a[[$b.c]]`, caused a compilation syntax error.
In a component running in a preemptive process, [`RESOLVE POINTER`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/resolve-pointer) could not dereference a pointer to a host database variable.
With the system region/language set to Turkish, [`GRAPH`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/graph) pie charts were rendered incorrectly.
The IMAP transporter's `getMails()` leaked memory — memory used for receiving mail was not released even after the process terminated.

Serializing a class instance with [`JSON Stringify`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/json-stringify) produced slightly different output for computed properties (getter/setter) depending on whether it ran standalone or on the client in Client/Server — the client omitted the `readOnly` property; the fix standardizes ORDA's output across desktop, server, and client to always include `name`, `kind`, `exposed`, `readOnly`, `type`, and `fieldType` (but not `autoFilled`, `indexed`, `keywordIndexed`, `mandatory`, or `unique`).
Running SQL code in a preemptive process that called a method via an `FN` (SQL function) statement could crash 4D Server.
[`MAIL Convert from MIME`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) could crash the application when parsing a malformed/corrupted `.eml` file.

[`WP Get view properties`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-view-properties) incorrectly returned the auto-spellcheck state (equivalent to [`OBJECT Get auto spellcheck`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-auto-spellcheck)) for its `spellEnabled` property instead of the standard "spell/enabled" action state; the fix also changes behavior so that setting `spellEnabled` to true only re-enables auto-spellcheck the first time (for compatibility) when it wasn't already on — afterward it only toggles in-progress spellcheck, and auto-spellcheck must be re-enabled via the menu.

In Project mode, a hierarchical list box could fail to apply bold or italic font styling (underline was unaffected) when the CSS specified a system font, since system font names aren't valid font-family identifiers.
Calling [`RESTORE`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/restore) returned syntax error #607, an apparent side effect of the fix for ACI0102236.

In an engined (built) application — both mono and client — passing a pointer to an Object-type value as a method parameter and receiving it into a Variant (`$1`) parameter crashed the application; the crash did not reproduce with debug logging enabled, nor in non-built compiled mode.

On Windows, right-clicking the title bar of a fixed-size form's window and choosing "Maximize" could make some buttons disappear — the underlying problem being that a fixed-size form should not have been maximizable at all.

Building multiple compiled or Client/Server engined applications with different names into the same output folder caused each new build to delete the previous one, leaving only the most recently built application in the folder.
In upgraded databases, some project methods were inconsistently omitted from the published WSDL, with the set of published methods changing across WSDL reloads.
In the Label Editor's font menu, the smallest selectable font size was 9; sizes 6, 7, and 8 should also have been available.

On Mac, while a window was being resized by dragging, [`GET WINDOW RECT`](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-window-rect) returned a `top` value that fluctuated up and down during the resize instead of tracking smoothly.
If a Narrow No-Break Space character was used as the digit-grouping (thousands) separator, numbers with more than 3 digits were not formatted/displayed correctly.

On Mac only, the label text of object boxes such as check boxes, buttons, and radio buttons no longer shrank in stages as the object was resized down to a minimum height in the Form Editor (design environment only).

When exporting a project whose structure was previously in binary mode, style sheet names that start with a digit were mishandled: the CSS file names and class names got escaped with backslash characters and could no longer be referenced correctly.

On Windows only, using `entity.fromObject()` to update an entity's foreign key incorrectly assigned the primary key value instead of the value of the related "N to 1" relation attribute, corrupting the relation on the "N" side table.
On Mac only, the icons shown in a Tab Control object were badly aligned, drifting progressively further left the further right the tab was positioned.
In the French-localized edition of 4D only, the `WA démarrer hors écran` command was not recognized as a function call and was instead interpreted as a plain variable.

In Client/Server, after a method was run with [Execute on server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/execute-on-server) and a client-side process then locked a record, `LOCKED BY` and `Get lock record info` incorrectly reported the server's user name and machine name instead of the client's.
License activation failed whenever the 4D account's name or company fields contained an accented character.

In Client/Server project mode, starting a transaction in an input form and then closing the form while simultaneously canceling the transaction could, about three minutes later, produce a "broken connection" error; the issue occurs specifically when [ARRAY TO LIST](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/array-to-list) is executed while [In transaction](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/in-transaction), because the underlying query was not released correctly.

In compiled mode only, running [SET DATABASE PARAMETER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-parameter) to turn on debug log recording did not correctly log method parameter values. Since parameter recording is not actually possible in compiled mode, the fix restricts this setting to interpreted mode only.

In the French localization only, some predefined constants were not recognized by the Method Editor because an apostrophe in the translated constant name (e.g. `dossier fichiers d'historique`) caused autocomplete errors; several constant names were renamed to remove the apostrophe.
It was not possible to use a `4DLOOP` tag after a `4DEACH` tag within the same web page document.
In 4D Write Pro, the `wk text color` attribute did not always change the text color of hyperlinks.

In project mode, after a structure that had been converted from binary was opened in v19, a form object's help tip in the property list displayed the literal string "[object Object]" instead of the actual tip text.

Creating a record in an empty table right after a new data file was created, while inside a transaction that was not yet validated, could crash the application if an [ORDER BY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/order-by) or [LISTBOX SORT COLUMNS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-sort-columns) was then performed on an indexed field.
On Mac, when building a compiled application without including related folders, an outdated *lib4d-arm64.dylib* file in the *Libraries* folder was not overwritten by the new one as expected.
Entity selections held on the server were not always released once the corresponding 4D Remote client quit, leading to leaked resources on the server.
In Project mode, component methods could not be exposed as Web Services; this worked fine when the host project was in binary mode.
While typing Japanese text via IME, deleting the entire unvalidated (in-progress) conversion string with the Delete key also incorrectly deleted one already-validated character adjacent to it.

When a Labels layout used a virtual structure with field titles configured, running [PRINT LABEL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-label) printed the field names on the labels instead of the actual field values.
An ORDA query that used the `OR` operator across a one-to-many relation defined on the same dataclass caused 4D to quit unexpectedly.
On Apple Silicon Macs, an application built to target Intel only failed to launch under Rosetta translation.
In the French edition, some 4D Write Pro widget tooltips were displayed in English instead of French, mixing the two localizations.

On Apple Silicon, compiling code that used a literal value directly in an expression (e.g. subtracting a negative constant) triggered an unexpected internal compiler error; using a variable instead of the literal avoided the problem.
On Windows, a list box with automatic row height enabled could have a row cut off when displayed or printed, if a cell used a font that was not installed on the system.

Passing an empty string to [LISTBOX SET PROPERTY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-set-property) with the `lk detail form name` property, intending to reset a list box's detail form, had no effect.

On Apple Silicon, compiling a project failed when a method name used Japanese characters longer than three letters; the underlying cause is that [LAUNCH EXTERNAL PROCESS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/launch-external-process) passed the Japanese file name to `clang` without accounting for UTF-8 requiring more bytes per character than Shift-JIS.

In Client/Server, converting an entity and its related entity into a collection via `.toCollection()` left the underlying entity selections unreleased until the client connection was closed, causing a memory leak.
When the "Allow Web Service Requests" setting was disabled and a browser requested `.../4DWSDL`, the server returned a malformed XML error instead of a proper response.
On Mac, videoconferencing pages displayed in a Web Area could get permission to use the camera, but not the microphone.
A formula built around a pointer dereference and assignment, such as `Formula(gPtr->:=2)`, was misinterpreted because the dereference operator (`->`) was stripped out.
On Mac, `folders()` returned paths prefixed with `///` instead of a single `/`; this happened specifically when the parent folder's path was shorter than 8 characters.
In Client/Server, getter/setter computed attributes bound to list boxes did not work correctly: a value written to the attribute became unset immediately after being set.
In the Toolbox password-change dialog, the new-password field was limited to a maximum of 15 characters, while the confirm-password field had no such limit; both fields should allow unlimited length.
In Client/Server, calling [Create entity selection](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-entity-selection) in a new process to build an entity selection caused a memory leak.

In binary mode, a method published via REST could not be debugged server-side while running in interpreted mode, and in compiled mode such a REST-published method could not be executed in a cooperative process on the server.
Converting a structure to project mode discarded the reference to splash images that had been defined via the picture library on the menu bar.
Creating a new structure in binary mode left the list box header's picture/source property (a variable name) blank in the property list.
Converting a binary structure to project mode did not export the list box header's picture/source property when it was left empty, so the resulting project's list box lacked that property entirely.
Editing a button's title directly in the property list and then closing the form without first confirming the edit discarded the change instead of saving it.

`WP Get position` could return an incorrect `bounds.left` value; the underlying issue is that [WP Text range](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-text-range) returns the end of the paragraph rather than the actual cursor position when the cursor sits on a blank line right after a paragraph.
In the French localization, a help tip in the 4D Write Pro widget toolbar (on the "Insertions et vues" tab, "évaluer les expressions" button) contained a spelling mistake.
In the French localization, some 4D Write Pro toolbar help tips on the Protection tab were left untranslated, showing English text like "Protect table" instead of "Protéger table".
In the French localization, the 4D Write Pro toolbar's spell-check and grammar-check button help tips were left untranslated.
On Apple Silicon Macs, the application could become unresponsive after the system woke from sleep.
On Apple Silicon, compiling code that passed the constant `0xFFFF` as an integer-type plugin command parameter produced a compiler error.

In project mode only, when a form's minimum size was mistakenly configured larger than its maximum size (an inconsistent but reachable state via the .json form file or object properties), objects positioned beyond the maximum width were not fully displayed; in binary mode the larger of the two values was used as the effective maximum instead.

[HTTP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) could occasionally return spurious status codes such as 0 or 1, typically after the application had been running for an extended period; the fix stops processing already-received data when a broken-socket condition (`VE_SOCK_CONNECTION_BROKEN`/`VE_SOCK_PEER_OVER`) is detected mid-read.

In a 4D View Pro spreadsheet, [VP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-export-document) generated an error whenever a column containing values had word-wrap enabled in its cell style.
In compiled mode, parameter names declared with the `#DECLARE` syntax were treated as case-sensitive, distinguishing uppercase from lowercase letters where they should not have been.

In 4D View Pro, part of the area's status bar was not localized: the trailing item, meant to show the zoom level, instead literally displayed the word "undefined" for any localization other than English.

In a 4D Write Pro document, the width of a table's columns could not be changed if a hyperlink was inserted immediately before the table; setting the link with [WP SET LINK](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-set-link) instead of inserting it manually avoided the problem.

After the Structure and Data Analyzer warned "Table is encrypted but some blobs are not" (for BLOB fields stored in the data file), re-running data file encryption or compression from the MSC still failed to encrypt those already-unencrypted BLOB records.

For a private server (not broadcasting its service name), a built remote application that required manually entering the server address on first launch could be prompted to re-enter that address again right after the client's very first automatic update, because the *LastServer.xml* file was not being created or updated at that point.
In Client/Server, enabling the "Remember password" checkbox in the login dialog did not actually persist the password, so it was requested again on the next login.

Running a `SELECT` query via [SQL EXECUTE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-execute) truncated the last character of any returned text longer than 1031 characters; the root cause appears to be a Sybase driver quirk where `SQLGetData` always reports a length of 1032.
In Japanese IME input mode, pressing the space bar inserted a half-width space (`U+0020`) instead of the expected full-width space (`U+3000`).

Switching a form's displayed page via a tab control from the *On Load* form event did not work; using [SELECT LIST ITEMS BY POSITION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/select-list-items-by-position) on the tab control at that point failed to change the visible page.

In 4D Write Pro, inserting a document fragment with `WP INSERT DOCUMENT` into a paragraph that ends with a page, column, or section break corrupted the document's sections and caused [WP Get position](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-position) to subsequently return incorrect values.

The first call to [WP Get position](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-position) could return a different (incorrect) page number than subsequent calls; the value returned from the second call onward is the correct one.

In project mode, switching to form page 0 while the entry-order tool was already selected did not display the entry order of objects on that page; toggling the tool off and back on after switching to page 0 fixed the display.
In 4D View Pro, passing an empty date value (`!00-00-00!`) to `VP SET DATE TIME VALUE` produced the incorrect date 11/30/1899 instead of returning a proper null value.

The *catalog.4DCatalog* file could be rewritten every time a project was opened, because switching data files updates the catalog's index UUIDs to match the data file; the fix instead updates the data file's UUIDs to match the catalog when the two disagree.
On Mac, [WA EXECUTE JAVASCRIPT FUNCTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wa-execute-javascript-function) did not work in a system Web Area (external rendering engine).
On Windows, text in a "printable at variable height" object could be unexpectedly truncated when multiline; this did not happen when the DirectWrite rendering mode was used.

If a project's *Settings* folder was missing, the server administration window failed to load a project-specific log configuration file (*logConfig.json*); the folder and file need to be created manually if required.

Changing the localization language at runtime with [SET DATABASE LOCALIZATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-localization) left the 4D Write Pro area's contextual menu showing a mix of system-language and localized-language items; font style names returned by [FONT STYLE LIST](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/font-style-list) are always shown in the system language by design, but other items such as spell-check options are now correctly shown in the localized language.
Since v19 R4, the popup menus on the Label editor's format page were displayed empty.
Switching between forms that each contained a 4D Write Pro widget could trigger a runtime error.

The web server always decoded incoming GET/POST web form variables as UTF-8, ignoring the character set actually configured in the database settings for the [Web Server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-server).
In interpreted mode, if an application ran for several days while continually creating and destroying processes, pointers to process (local) variables could become invalid/undefined.
In 4D View Pro, using the `HYPERLINK` function to open a local file whose file name or path contained Japanese characters failed to open the link.

On Windows in high-DPI mode, running [DISPLAY RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/display-record) to show an input form rendered the form's contents zoomed several times too large because the DPI setting was not correctly applied.

Converting a 4D View spreadsheet to 4D View Pro mishandled certain named cell references, particularly for cells beyond column Z (e.g. column AB); a reference that should read `Sheet1!$AB$2` was instead converted to something like `Sheet1!$\\$2`.

On Mac, with the Form Editor open in design mode, clicking the toolbar's search field while the cursor was in the property list left the search field without a visible caret, so text could not be typed or selected into it.
Mail bodies encoded in UTF-7 had characters such as the degree sign (°) incorrectly decoded by [MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime).

In project mode, it was not possible to disable journaling; the fix changes the mechanism so that whether a log file is used is now determined by the project file rather than the data file, and the `journal_file_enabled` property in the *.4DCatalog* file is updated a few seconds after changing the database settings or calling [SELECT LOG FILE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/select-log-file)(*).

Converting a 4D View spreadsheet to 4D View Pro and then inspecting a cell's formula in the debugger showed the parameter separator missing from the formula: `=LIBELLE("";A1)` was displayed as `=LIBELLE(""A1)`.

The `idleTimeout` option of [Open datastore](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-datastore) for a remote datastore connection had no effect: the connection was never closed and the license was never released after the specified timeout elapsed.

Since v19 R4, accessing 4D Server's REST API via ORDA when no client was connected returned a "maximum number of sessions reached" error; spare simultaneous-client-connection licenses should be usable for REST session management when no dedicated REST licenses are available.
With debug logging enabled, repeatedly executing [OPEN DATA FILE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-data-file) on the server side eventually caused the server to quit.
Using an ASCII control character such as `Char(2)` as the separator parameter of [Split string](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/split-string) produced an incorrect resulting collection.
In Client/Server, calling a dataclass function under low cache conditions could crash 4D Server, reporting a missing language context error.
On Mac, the application crashed on launch under macOS 12.3 beta 3, because 4D Write Pro was linked against the system's *liblzma.5.dylib* instead of the one bundled with the application.
Passing certain old 4D Write documents to [WP New](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-new) crashed the application.

In the Method Editor, pressing F1 (or Cmd/Ctrl+K) while the [Is table number valid](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/is-table-number-valid) command was selected opened the wrong page of the documentation, due to an incorrect redirect.

Using [EDIT ITEM](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/edit-item) on *On Losing Focus* at the same time as list box single-click editing was starting on a different list box could leave a blinking cursor in one cell while keystrokes actually went to a different cell.

[MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) failed to properly decode mail subjects that used the `unicode-1-1-utf-7` character set (for example, garbling the character "é"); [CONVERT FROM TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/convert-from-text) and [Convert to text](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/convert-to-text) had the same limitation and were fixed alongside it.

[MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) failed to properly decode mail bodies using the `Windows-1258` character set, garbling characters such as "ç"; while true support for that Vietnamese encoding is not added, the fix now falls back to the system's default encoding instead of `US-ASCII` for unsupported charsets.
Repeatedly calling the `VP SET@` command within a single method to update multiple 4D View Pro spreadsheet values made the spreadsheet update very slowly.

In 4D View Pro, passing `Null` to [VP SET CELL STYLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-set-cell-style) to clear a range's background only cleared the background of the first cell in the range, leaving the remaining cells' backgrounds unchanged.

On Windows, the down-arrow indicator shown in a dropdown menu was not vertically centered; setting the dropdown's height to anything other than 20 pushed the arrow toward the bottom instead of the middle.
In the Method Editor, selecting a block of recently pasted text and choosing "Comment" from the context menu could crash the application.

When a query executed against a Sybase stored procedure via `SQL EXECUTE` returned null, the command filled the destination 4D array with one empty element instead of leaving it empty as it should for a null result.

In a 4D Write Pro document, if the cursor was positioned in the header or footer, toggling the visibility of references moved the cursor's position each time; this did not happen when the cursor was in the body text.
In binary mode, loading a blank form on the client side with [FORM LOAD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-load) and then quitting the client caused the application to crash/hang.

After a method was executed on the server, [LOCKED BY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/locked-by) and `Get locked records info` incorrectly returned the server's user name and workstation name instead of the actual client's.

If the debugger was displayed while processing a web request and "step over" was used a few times, the debugger would unexpectedly close and could no longer be reopened afterward; by design, non-context-mode processes abort execution and show an HTML error when the debugger appears, but the fix avoids applying that mechanism to processes where the debugger had never actually been shown.
Passing a large object as the `$1` parameter to [EXECUTE ON CLIENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/execute-on-client) caused a memory leak.
Clicking a tab control to switch a form's page could leave input objects unable to receive focus/input and disable the Edit menu commands.

When the data language was set to Japanese, using `WP Find all` (and likewise `WP Find next`/`WP Find previous`) in strict mode always treated uppercase and lowercase as equivalent even without specifying case-insensitive mode, contrary to the Japanese default of treating case as significant.

On Mac, compiling code that assigned a value to an anonymous interprocess variable (e.g. `<>:=0`) succeeded when targeting Intel but failed with an obscure clang error when targeting Apple Silicon; the fix makes this case correctly report a syntax error on both targets.

An entry filter configured on a text area that was non-enterable but focusable was incorrectly applied to the underlying data source value whenever the object was redrawn (e.g. via scrolling or clicking), even though no text had actually been typed.

Object fields can store instances of a class, but after restoring a data file from a backup with log/journal integration, such stored objects lost their connection to their class and its member functions.
On Windows, when an input form contained a Web Area displaying a PDF, closing that dialog and returning to the output form left part of the input form incorrectly drawn on top of the output form.

Enabling the web server's preemptive mode triggered a compiler error on the `Mobile App Active Session` command of the *4D Mobile App Server* component when it was used in thread-safe methods such as the *On Web Connection* database method; shared component methods default to "cannot be run in preemptive process" because the host caller's threading mode is unknown, so a component method must explicitly be marked "can be run in preemptive process" to be thread-safe.
On Mac, list box headers with a custom height of two or more lines rendered without their top border line.
In project mode, enabling the "automatic width" property (in context/design mode) on a subform that contained a list box, within a project converted from v18, could crash the application.
Calling [DISPLAY RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/display-record) on an input form that contained an object with its resize property set to "enlarge" crashed the application.
Using [GOTO OBJECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/goto-object) on a list box from a background process caused an object in the foreground process to lose keyboard focus.
On Mac, the application crashed on launch under macOS 10.14.6 (Mojave).
In project mode, a button configured with a standard action such as "add subrecord" or "delete subrecord" stopped working once the button was also made focusable.

[Get 4D file](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-4d-file) returned a default file path instead of an empty string for certain nonexistent target files (such as a missing build settings file); to preserve compatibility, other file kinds still return their previous default paths.

Converting a 4D View spreadsheet to 4D View Pro could mis-convert a formula whenever it began with the literal value `-1`. (This bug's fix listing also notes ACI0102771 as a related side-effect entry.)
On Windows, pressing Alt+Down Arrow should toggle open/closed the selection list attached to a combo box or dropdown menu object, but had no effect.
Keyboard shortcuts customized at the structure-settings level were not carried over into the user settings.

In 4D View Pro, after creating a range with `VP All`, clearing the default *backColor* style attribute via [VP SET CELL STYLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-set-cell-style) using [New object](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/new-object)("backColor"; `Null`), a subsequent attempt to set *backColor* on a range built with `VP Cells` cleared every other style attribute but left *backColor* itself unchanged.

If a method ran once during *On Server Startup* and, without that event ever completing (e.g. because a dialog was left open on the server), the same method was later run as a stored procedure via [Execute on server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/execute-on-server) from a remote client, [Current user](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/current-user) incorrectly returned an empty string in that context; ending the *On Server Startup* event avoided the problem, and it is recommended not to leave the startup method running indefinitely.
Switching the Database Settings tab from Client/Server to Backup unexpectedly enabled the OK button, even though nothing had actually been changed and there was nothing to save.
Declaring an object-type class as `4D.System Worker` triggered an incorrect compiler warning 550.2 on calls to methods such as `wait()`.

The `Compile project` command failed to compile an external project that required plugin commands; plugins installed in that project's *Plugins* folder are now loaded passively (definition files only, without their executables/libraries) so compilation can proceed.

Starting multiple HTTP/HTTPS servers via the [Web Server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-server) object should return an error if a requested port is already in use, but under certain conditions the listening port number was silently incremented and the server started anyway instead of raising the expected error.
On Mac, on 4K/5K Retina displays, form objects such as lines, rectangles, and circles were not drawn correctly: their outlines appeared offset from the actual shape.
Retrieving email via the IMAP transporter from a Dovecot mail server could freeze the application; Gmail and Exchange servers were not affected.

In project mode, when there were gaps in user ID numbering, reopening the project caused the order of users and groups within *directory.json* to shuffle, and [GET USER LIST](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-user-list) could no longer match entries against the file properly.
In Client/Server, returning an entity selection object from a class function could cause a memory leak.

On Windows, when a tab control had more tabs than fit the form's width, the scroll arrow buttons for hidden tabs overlapped the vertical scrollbar; on Windows 11 the arrow buttons did not appear at all.

On Windows, if a laptop not connected to power was used to connect to the server and then left to sleep while the client remained running, the client could fail to automatically reconnect to the server after the system woke up.

On Windows, bringing a list form to the front with [BRING TO FRONT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/bring-to-front) while it was previously overlapped by another window did not fully redraw the portion that had been hidden.

If an XML element's value contained a control character such as `Char(29)`, running `DOM EXPORT TO VAR` or [DOM EXPORT TO FILE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dom-export-to-file) crashed the application.
On Mac, setting the `CommonCopyright` key in the build settings file and then running [BUILD APPLICATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/build-application) crashed the application.

On Mac, a child process launched with [LAUNCH EXTERNAL PROCESS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/launch-external-process) unexpectedly inherited the network ports that 4D itself was listening on, apparently due to the `POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT` flag.
The alphanumeric display format applied to a non-enterable field could render incorrectly, cutting off part of the value; this was a side effect introduced by the fix for ACI0102747.

The web server's "No sessions" option was not preserved when "Enable User Settings External File" was set, reproducing specifically in projects upgraded from an earlier version to v19 (new projects created directly in v19 were unaffected); selecting and saving one of the newer session-management options once worked around it.
Importing a query previously saved to disk (as a *.4DF* file) reset any date-type criterion value to zero (`!00-00-00!`).
The "Find" tool in the Structure editor did not work correctly whenever there were gaps in the table numbering.
In the French localization, the 4D View Pro area's Search and Replace interface had localization/UI problems, with some elements left untranslated.
In Client/Server, displaying the server administration window on the client side and then closing it caused the client to freeze when subsequently quitting.

Calling [OPEN DATABASE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-database) from the *On Server Startup* database method while the server administration window was open could block the server from restarting properly until that admin window was closed.

On Windows, compressing a folder whose path exceeded 188 characters with `ZIP Create archive` reported success but omitted the folder's files from the resulting archive; the LTS release line was not affected.

In Apple Silicon compiled mode, calling [Count parameters](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/count-parameters) from a method run in an [Execute on server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/execute-on-server) session did not return the correct parameter count.

On Mac only, using [Dynamic pop up menu](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dynamic-pop-up-menu) in the *On Alternative Click* event of a button linked to a popup menu caused the command's default-selection parameter to be ignored. Separate (unlinked) popup menus were not affected. The item actually was selected, but the Mac system highlight color was incorrectly applied to whatever item happened to be under the mouse pointer instead.

Using [Dynamic pop up menu](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dynamic-pop-up-menu) in the click event of a button that also had a standard action configured caused the command's specified default item to be ignored, and the wrong menu item was selected instead whenever the menu contained hidden standard actions.

Setting a cell's `backColor` with [VP SET CELL STYLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-set-cell-style) in 4D View Pro could incorrectly apply the background color to surrounding ranges as well, not just the specified range.
Calling `SystemWorker.wait()` from a form method failed to actually wait for messages returned by the system worker, so the process would not receive the expected results.

Using [Split string](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/split-string) with a delimiter in the range Char(1) through Char(31) caused the application to crash. Note that even after the fix, Split string still uses the same parsing algorithm as [Position](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/position) (without the `*` option) and is not designed to split strings on control characters.

On Mac only, in Project mode, exporting a form to project mode caused checkboxes or radio buttons in list form (output/subform) rows to be drawn on extra rows that had no corresponding records, even though such rows should not display any field content.

After compacting the data and index files, saving a new record could crash the application when the table had an indexed field. The crash appeared related to calling a thread-unsafe method (e.g. one accessing interprocess variables) in compiled mode from a preemptive thread, such as a Web process.

A date field with an input filter that was initially non-enterable and then switched to enterable via a command, while visible, displayed an incorrect date instead of the correct stored value. This issue only affected nightly builds.
On Mac only, a button configured with the "Page break" (page navigation) standard action could unexpectedly become disabled when another window belonging to the same process was open.

On Windows, if a form was displayed while the monitor resolution was set to 100%, then the application was quit and later reopened after changing the resolution to 125%, static pictures were no longer positioned correctly on screen. The issue did not occur when the resolution was a multiple of 100 (100%, 200%, 300%, etc.), nor if 4D's high-DPI support was disabled.
When a published Web service method used a parameter with a Japanese variable name, the corresponding data value from the SOAP envelope was not correctly assigned to that variable, leaving it blank.
Loading a query that had been saved to a `.4DF` file and contained a date condition initialized the date value to 00.00.00 instead of the value that was actually stored.
Executing TCP socket commands from within a `PHP Execute` call to access a local application's Web server led to excessive CPU consumption and could freeze the application.

In Project mode, when an object's size was defined via CSS, [OBJECT GET BEST SIZE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-best-size) could return an incorrect height value instead of the actual best-fit height.

When a form object had the standard action "Quit" assigned along with an object method, the object method ran first and the confirmation dialog was shown afterward, whereas the dialog should be displayed before the method runs — matching the behavior already used for the *deleteRecord* action. Per 4D's documentation, when both a standard action and a method are assigned to a form object or menu command, the standard action normally executes after the method, with *deleteRecord* being the sole existing exception; this fix effectively adds "Quit" as another exception.
In binary mode, modifying and saving a method that had existing compiled code on the client side in a client/server configuration caused a memory leak during synchronization with the server.

In 4D View Pro, using [VP Convert to picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-to-picture) with a specific range parameter could fail to correctly render the background of that range in the resulting picture.
In the French-localized version, several terms shown in the View Pro ribbon's *Mise en page* (Page Layout) tab — added with SpreadJS v15 — were awkwardly or incorrectly translated.

CSS `@media` (dark/light mode) rules applied to a list box's CSS class were honored in Design mode but ignored at runtime, so the color scheme did not adapt to the system's dark/light setting in the running application.

In Project mode, calling [OBJECT Get format](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-format) on a list box header linked to a picture-type variable returned an empty string instead of the actual format. Note that in Project mode, picture-type variables used for list box headers are referenced with a `var:myVariable` prefix.

In compiled mode, calling collection functions such as `.map()` or `.find()` with a method whose parameter was declared as Pointer raised syntax error #54 ("Expecting a pointer") if [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) was passed for that parameter, instead of the value being accepted normally.

Moving focus to an entity selection list box left a button configured with the "Add subrecord" standard action active/enabled, even though this standard action does not support array-type or entity-selection list boxes; clicking it in this state could cause a crash. The button should instead be disabled in that context.
In the 4D Write Pro Interface widget, displaying a tab other than "Picture" and then command-clicking an image embedded in the document raised a runtime error instead of selecting the image normally.
Starting a backup from a 4D Remote client could cause that client to lose its connection to the server, specifically when the backup took longer than one hour to complete.

Sending more than 8000 bytes of data to a Sybase image field via SQL truncated the data to only 255 bytes; the ODBC Pro plugin was not affected. The fix introduced a new *SQL data chunk size* option for [SQL SET OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-set-option) (default 8000), needed because the Sybase ODBC driver doesn't support fragmented *PutData* calls and must receive binary data in a single send; other database systems like Oracle, MySQL, and Microsoft SQL Server require no configuration change.

In Client/Server mode, saving an instantiated class object to a field, then later retrieving it from the datastore and evaluating one of its computed attributes, could unexpectedly raise a "Missing language context" error instead of returning the computed value.

[MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) failed to locate attachments when the MIME boundary string had a particular format, such as one embedding a date/time string (e.g. `"boundary Wed, 27 Apr 2022 08:46:59 +0200 boundary"`).

In a collection-based list box with a Boolean-type column, cells whose value was undefined or [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) did not display a checkbox, and clicking such a cell assigned the string "true" or "false" to the underlying property instead of an actual boolean value. The fix restores the checkbox display and ensures a real boolean is assigned, and the underlying handling was reviewed across all data types (string, text, number, time, picture), not just boolean.
In binary mode, dragging and dropping a file into the client's Resources window (Design > Toolbox > Resources) caused 4D Client to hang and stop responding.

On Windows in SDI mode, executing [MODIFY SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/modify-selection) to switch from a data-entry (input form) session back to a list view (output form) session left the screen only partially redrawn, with remnants of the input form still visible; resizing the window or clicking the screen forced a full redraw of the list form. This appears to be a side effect of the fixes for ACI0102751 and ACI0102766.
On Windows, in Project mode, Group Box objects were not rendered using DirectWrite, causing their text rendering to look visually inconsistent compared to Static Text objects.

An attachment on an email object created with [MAIL New attachment](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-new-attachment) could not be passed as a parameter to another process, preventing the email object from being handed off across processes.
In 4D Write Pro, deleting the last row of a table also removed the section break that immediately followed that row, when only the row itself should have been deleted.

While editing a list box cell value, holding the command key (Cmd on Mac, Ctrl on Windows) while pressing an alphanumeric key caused the *On Before Keystroke* form event to fire twice instead of once, since a keyboard modifier combination should not be treated as a plain keystroke.
On Mac, the *On VP Ready* form event for a Multi View Pro area did not fire at all, so code relying on it to detect that the View Pro area finished initializing never ran.

In the code editor, type-ahead completion failed to suggest properties and functions matching an object's prototype when the parameter's class was declared via `#DECLARE` using a component-exported class name from that component's namespace. Declaring the same parameter with the `var` keyword worked correctly, so the bug was specific to the newer `#DECLARE` typing syntax combined with component classes.

In Project mode, applying a font to an individual item of a drop-down list object had no effect. The fix only applies to the Mac version; on Windows, setting a font on individual menu items is not supported due to a technical platform limitation.
When a Quick Report was built on a virtual table only, the report displayed field names enclosed in square brackets instead of showing the proper table names in the column headers.

In 4D View Pro, pivot tables in a spreadsheet could become corrupted when the document was exported. This was traced to a bug in the underlying SpreadJS 16.0.x library and was fixed by SpreadJS 16.2.4.

On Windows, if the *On Load* form event set a font on a text input object that had an entry order defined, and a value was then assigned to that object through a pointer, the input area ended up empty. Not calling [OBJECT SET FONT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-font) avoided the issue.
In the Plugin SDK, the `EX_GET_FIELD` entry point failed to retrieve values from BLOB fields, preventing plugins from reading blob-typed field data correctly.
Object-type variables could no longer be used as the data source for a pop-up/drop-down menu object, breaking drop-down lists that were bound to an object.

In Project mode only, converting a database from Binary mode caused users to be dropped from the *Designer* access group; only the *Administrator* group's membership was exported correctly during the conversion.
Calling [DRAG WINDOW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/drag-window) caused the target window to immediately jump off-screen instead of allowing it to be dragged normally.
On Windows, running the obsolete `_O_Gestalt` command in a standalone application (e.g. `$errCode:=_O_Gestalt("sync"; $v)`) could crash the application.

When printing a form with [Print object](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-object), clicking the Cancel button on the printing progress dialog did not stop the print job. The fix allows `Print object` to be interrupted this way, but in a loop calling `Print object` repeatedly, developers must also handle error code -128 via [ON ERR CALL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/on-err-call) to actually break out of the loop.
In a method containing a line such as `return Path is system`, closing and reopening the method in the code editor caused the keyword "return" to unexpectedly disappear from that line.
In the remote debugger, it was not possible to expand an entity selection shown in the variables/expressions view to browse the attributes of its individual entities.
The debugger did not always stop reliably at a [TRACE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/trace) call or at a breakpoint, so execution could continue past a point where it should have paused.

For a text input object placed on a form, the initial text scroll position ended up at the beginning, middle, or end of the content depending on the text's size, when it should always default to a position independent of text size.

When opening a .zip archive containing an empty folder with [ZIP Read archive](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/zip-read-archive), the empty root folder was not returned in the resulting `zip.root.folders` collection.

Emails sent using [SMTP New transporter](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/smtp-new-transporter) could be truncated partway through sending. The issue occurred specifically when the message body happened to contain the sequence `\r\n.\r\n`, which the SMTP protocol uses to signal the end of the message body.

[Compile project](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/compile-project) returned incorrect internal type constants for Text, Pointer, and Picture variables (e.g. Pointer as 40, Picture as 10, Text as 33) instead of the documented language constants (Pointer 23, Picture 3, Text 2). The command had been returning the compiler's internal constants, a legacy of format changes to text/picture in v11 and pointers in v16+; the fix makes it return values consistent with `Is text`, `Is pointer`, and `Is picture`.

Calling [FORM SET INPUT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-set-input) from the *On Load* form event could fail to change the input form used when a list box row was double-clicked, so the table's input form remained unchanged.

Importing a Mac-compiled application build into an engined Windows application to produce a Silicon-Mac-ready client/server build failed with an error stating the folder was "not a correct .4DZ folder", when the build project had been configured with `PackProject=False` so it produced a *Compiled Database* folder instead of a .4DZ file. Embedding a *Compiled Database* folder in place of the .4DZ should have worked without error.

In the Portuguese and Spanish localizations of 4D, the [On REST Authentication database method](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/on-rest-authentication-database-method) was mistakenly labeled "On 4D Mobile Authentication" instead of its correct name.

On Windows, with two monitors connected where the main display's scaling was set to 125%, [SCREEN COORDINATES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/screen-coordinates) returned incorrect values for that screen, while the monitor left at default scaling returned correct values.
An ORDA query on a picture-type field failed when using the keyword search operator (`%`) together with a placeholder value in the query string.
On Mac under macOS 12 Monterey, tab controls rendered smaller than expected on Retina displays, and their icons appeared blurred.
On Mac, running the Structure Consistency Check (MSC/Verify) in dark mode returned an error instead of completing normally.
On Windows Server 2012 R2, the drop-down arrow displayed next to a drop-down list object was positioned lower than the object itself instead of aligning correctly.

The `dataClass.query()` class function returned incorrect results when the query criteria string compared a field against [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) on an attribute that was not indexed.

In a 4D Write Pro table, clearing a cell's content with the Backspace key, typing new content, and then pressing Backspace again unexpectedly deleted the cell itself from the table. Previously Delete only cleared a cell's content while Backspace acted like a cut (removing the cell), but since this distinction was confusing, the behavior was changed so both keys now only clear cell content.

Declaring a method or class function with duplicate parameter names (via `#DECLARE` syntax or in a class member function declaration) only produced a syntax-check warning but still compiled successfully, when it should have raised a compilation error.

On Mac, when the number of PHP processes was limited to 1, running `PHP Execute(""; "quit_4d_php"; *)` took an unexpected 10-second delay to complete, the same being true for the internal `relaunch_4d_php` command.
On Mac, the Print Preview button in the Quick Report editor was unexpectedly grayed out. On Windows this graying is conditional on XPS being installed, but that dependency should not apply on Mac.

[MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) could return an attachment file name containing leftover raw MIME header text appended to it, instead of a clean, correctly decoded file name.

On Mac, opening the Quick Report editor caused CPU usage to spike abnormally, to somewhere between 80% and 100%. The cause appeared to be an internal infinite loop involving [SET TIMER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-timer) and the handling of the *On Bound Variable Change* event.

[SCREEN COORDINATES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/screen-coordinates) returned the working area's origin as an absolute value scaled to the screen's resolution rather than as unscaled logical coordinates, after the system display scale factor for the main screen was set to 125%.
In the French version of 4D, the pop-up menu shown when clicking the export button on the 4D Write Pro toolbar contained incorrectly worded menu text.

When a 4D Write Pro document with an inline picture attachment was exported as MIME (e.g. for an email sent via SMTP Transporter), the picture was displayed duplicated in Apple's Mail client because the exported message did not set the `Content-Disposition` header to `multipart/related`.
On Mac, clicking anywhere in a tab control's body — not just its header row — triggered the tab-switch click event, causing unwanted page changes when users clicked elsewhere inside the control.

In client-server, when an extended entity class function returned an object whose multiple properties referenced the same nested object, the client received independent copies of that object in each property instead of preserving the shared reference; this only worked correctly for On Server methods. Objects with circular/recursive references should be serialized in binary form rather than JSON to preserve such references.

A text-type input field using a numeric-style display format such as `##.##.####` rendered incorrectly depending on the "use period and comma as placeholders" compatibility setting: with it disabled, the first period (meant as a thousands separator) was replaced by a comma and the second by a period, even though such numeric formats should only apply to numeric fields, not text fields.
On Mac, Help Tips containing Japanese text displayed an extra blank line below the tip text.

On Mac in dark mode, switching pages via a tab control caused the text input object being edited to visually lose its active highlight (drawn with the light-mode background color) until the mouse button was released; the same loss of focus occurred when clicking a tab control to bring an inactive window forward.
In a 4D Write Pro document, a second document section could unexpectedly get merged into the first section instead of remaining separate.

On Mac, long-pressing a key to enter an extended/accented character stopped working correctly in combo boxes, the Structure editor, 4D Write Pro, 4D View Pro, list boxes, text input areas, and the property list. After the fix, when the system's press-and-hold accent picker is enabled, it now takes priority over key-repeat (`ApplePressAndHoldEnabled`), except when an IME (e.g. Japanese) is active, in which case key-repeat still takes priority; if the accent picker is disabled in System Preferences, long-press always behaves as key-repeat.

On Mac, opening the Label editor while a custom menu bar was active caused otherwise disabled menu items to lose their grayed-out state; clicking one of these items then produced execution error -10508 because the menu bar itself was not properly locked.

Clicking the 4D Write Pro import/export toolbar button while a Write Pro area did not have focus raised an error stating the pointer to the 4D Write Pro document was `Nil`, apparently because the button was not configured as focusable.

On Windows with display scaling set to 125% or 150%, picture objects rendered with an unwanted 1‑pixel white gap along their bottom edge. The gap itself is now fixed, but at non-integer DPI scale factors, bevel button background images may still show a partial first line of their frame since the image cannot be scaled evenly; designers are advised to leave 1–2px of padding around such images.

On Windows, calling [SET CURRENT PRINTER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-current-printer) with the `PDFCreator` constant failed to make PDFCreator the current printer, because that constant is hardcoded to target PDFCreator's legacy 1.7.x API; newer PDFCreator versions (2.0+) changed their API substantially, so only 1.7.x is supported via the constant going forward — passing the actual printer name instead works with any installed version, but unsupported drivers combined with [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option)'s file destination option will still produce a PostScript file rather than a true PDF, since PDFCreator's conversion API is not compatible in that mode.

Calling `IMAP Transporter.getMails()` to retrieve a large number of messages could make the application appear to freeze before eventually failing with an error, preventing all mail from being downloaded; this occurred specifically when a dovecot or Exchange inbox contained more than 10,000 messages.

On Linux, HTTP requests passing through an Apache reverse proxy could be unexpectedly rejected by the 4D web server with a 400 Bad Request error ("HTTP/1.1 requests must include Host header"); this turned out to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0100450.
In Project mode, a Boolean field configured as non-enterable in the main form could still appear as an editable (clickable) checkbox when placed on a subform.
Converting a 4D View spreadsheet document to 4D View Pro caused cells containing multiple lines of text to collapse into single-line cells, losing the original line breaks.
In a 4D Write Pro document that contained a table, most hyperlinks in the document failed to work correctly.

Inserting a picture produced by [COMBINE PICTURES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/combine-pictures) into an SVG via the `SVG_New_embedded_image` command did not work when the source picture was empty; specifying an image codec such as *.png* in the sixth parameter avoids the problem.

On certain mail servers, `IMAP Transporter`'s `move()` function failed with the error "IMAP MOVE command not supported by server", even though the same operation worked fine from Outlook or Thunderbird, indicating the issue was not on the server side.

On Mac, attempting to open a v19 R6 compiled component built for Apple Silicon in a v19 R5 database caused the application to crash. This has been fixed to fail gracefully, but by design an Apple Silicon component compiled with 19 R6 still cannot be used with 19 R5, nor can a component compiled before 19 R6 be used with 19 R6.
In the Menu editor's toolbox dialog, standard automatic menu actions could be added twice, resulting in duplicate entries; this did not occur in newly created projects.
In the Quick Report editor's field search window, typing text to filter the field list caused related-table (relation) fields to be omitted from the results when two tables were linked by a relation.

On macOS Monterey, using [SET MENU ITEM SHORTCUT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-menu-item-shortcut) to assign the digit "0" as a shortcut displayed the menu label as "⌘à" instead of the expected "⌘0".
Selecting a form name in the Method editor and using the menu or keyboard shortcut to jump to that form in the Form editor stopped working, as a side effect of the fix for ACI0102855.
On Mac, list (output) forms could display extra separator lines between rows that should not be there, a regression caused as a side effect of the fix for ACI0102801.

In Project mode, duplicating a hierarchical pop-up menu object via [OBJECT DUPLICATE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-duplicate) while its variable or expression was a null pointer, then calling [OBJECT SET ENABLED](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-enabled) on the duplicated object, triggered an unexpected execution error.

Declaring a text-type variable with `var` inside a Trigger method could raise a spurious syntax error when the trigger's table had a field literally named "Text", because the `Text` type keyword was mistakenly resolved as a reference to that field (`[Table_1]Text`) instead of the type name.

In Project mode, picture buttons were missing the "Droppable" property in the property list. By design, Project-mode picture buttons do not have a "Draggable" property, so only the drop-target property omission was addressed as a bug.

On Windows with display scaling set to 125%, text shown via [MESSAGE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/message) after positioning the cursor with [GOTO XY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/goto-xy) appeared at the wrong screen location.

After upgrading a project to v19, the database settings still displayed web session management as "legacy", but the actual runtime behavior — and `WEB Server.keepSession` — reported it as disabled (false); re-saving the database settings resolves the mismatch.
When [GRAPH](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/graph) was used to create a chart with Japanese text in its legend, the legend text could be cut off / truncated.
The Method editor incorrectly flagged `4D.HTTPRequest.wait()` with a syntax warning even though the call was valid.

After using [LISTBOX SET PROPERTY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-set-property) with the *lk cell vertical padding* property to change a list box's cell vertical padding, selecting a large range of rows via scrolling and shift-click left visible gaps in the selection highlight instead of a continuous highlighted block.

In the Data File page of User Settings, the OK button became clickable again after switching to the Interface tab and back, even though no setting had actually been changed — a problem similar to ACI0102791.

Calling [Get external data path](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-external-data-path) from within a trigger fired on new record save generated an external data folder with an incorrect name (the table and field numbers used to build the folder name were wrong).

Importing a spreadsheet into 4D View Pro could silently alter numeric values, for example turning `96,07887` into `96,07887000000001`. This was caused by a bug in the underlying SpreadJS library, and was worked around with a patch pending an upstream fix.

Executing [FILTER KEYSTROKE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/filter-keystroke) inside an *On Before Keystroke* form event caused the text cursor to jump to the beginning of the input field's value instead of staying at the current typing position.
In array or entity-selection list boxes, clicking the checkbox displayed on a non-selected row incorrectly updated the value of the last-selected row instead of the row that was actually clicked.

If both HTTP and HTTPS were disabled — one via the database settings and the other via the start parameters — calling WebServer.start() failed to start the server but returned no error, when it should have returned an entry in the `errors[]` array explaining the failure.
Importing certain Excel files into 4D View Pro incorrectly raised an "Incorrect file format" error even though the file was valid.
Quick Reports generated in cross-table (pivot) format failed to output any field values, leaving the cross-table grid empty instead of populated with the underlying data.

On Windows, clicking an uninitialized popup or drop-down menu that displayed an empty array caused text input objects elsewhere on the same form to stop responding to clicks, even though text inside them could still be selected.
On Windows in HiDPI display mode, the Japanese IME's candidate/conversion window could overlap the text input area, obscuring the text being typed and making Japanese input effectively unusable.

When legacy (non-scalable) REST session management was enabled, sessions were not released after the configured timeout of inactivity, unlike with scalable session management. The issue occurred because each refresh of the administration window was incorrectly extending the session's lifetime.

In the Action tab of the 4D Go Mobile project editor, field names were being run through the XLIFF localization lookup and could end up translated according to the system's UI language, even though they should have been displayed as literal, untranslated field names.

Renaming a project method in the Explorer by moving the caret to the end of its name and typing did not enforce the 32-character name length limit, allowing names longer than 32 characters to be saved without warning; the excess characters were only truncated after the project was restarted.

In 4D Go Mobile, viewing the structure section for a project whose data model included sub-tables triggered an unexpected error ("ExposedStructure_fieldType, line 21") instead of displaying the structure normally.

If a server restart was scheduled with a client-side timeout and another client then executed server-side code — such as calling [Current time](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/current-time) — during that timeout window, the client lost its connection with an error. Scheduling the restart with a server-side timeout instead did not exhibit the problem.
In the Client/Server (IP configuration) tab of the Database Settings dialog, clicking the first column of the address list incorrectly enabled the OK button, even when no actual setting had changed.

In Project mode, changing the height property of a line object in the Form Editor was not persisted: after closing and reopening the form, the line reverted to its previous size instead of keeping the newly set coordinates.

On Windows, the field search box in the Structure Editor only considered the first character typed, so searching for a field by name effectively ignored every character entered after the second one and failed to find matches.

In client-server mode, ORDA set operations such as `.and()`, `.or()`, and `.minus()` failed when a primary key value contained special characters like "/" or "?", because those characters were not properly handled when building the ORDA request.

When the native SQL `SELECT` command returned integer values into a text array, the values were not automatically converted to text, unlike the equivalent operation performed through 4D ODBC Pro, which converted them correctly.
On Windows, documents printed through 4D Write Pro did not show a document name in the printer's job queue; the fix makes the queue display the value of the document's *wk title* attribute instead.
In 4D View Pro, applying formatting to a cell could corrupt it so that it could no longer be entered or edited afterward.

In a project that already contained a table named *MyTable*, trying to create a class named *MyTableEntity* raised an error stating the name was reserved, which was misleading; a message indicating that a class with that name already exists would be more accurate.

Using the IMAP Transporter's `.getMails()` method to retrieve a large number of emails in a loop triggered error 200 (reading past the end of a stream) instead of completing the retrieval successfully.

After configuring a Web Folder location in Project mode, the Database Settings dialog displayed the path in red as if the folder didn't exist, even though it did; clicking the associated pop-up menu revealed that the folder hierarchy being checked was actually incorrect.
On Windows, the drop-down list disclosure icon could render incorrectly as three dots when the object was too narrow to display it properly, depending on the control's size.

When a surrogate character was split by the maximum length of an alpha field so that only one half (e.g. `Char(55356)`) was saved in the record, dumping that field's value with a command like [LOG FILE TO JSON](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/log-file-to-json) produced invalid JSON, because the stray surrogate half swallowed a subsequent double-quote as a control character. The fix now truncates incomplete surrogate characters instead of storing them.
The preview pane in the Explorer did not apply the style sheet settings configured for a subform, so subforms appeared unstyled in the preview even though their style sheet was correctly defined.
Calling [MAIL Convert to MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-to-mime) could cause the 4D application to freeze rather than complete the conversion.
The IMAP Transporter's `.getBoxList()` method failed to correctly decode mailbox names containing a plus ("+") sign, causing 4D to report that the mailbox did not exist even though it was present.

In a 4D Write Pro dynamic table, a cell bound to a data source that evaluated to Null displayed the literal text "Null" instead of appearing blank, unlike the equivalent behavior in a list box. The fix makes formulas that return an empty string, undefined, or Null display as a zero-width space instead, since Write Pro formulas cannot be passed a zero-length range.

In 4D Write Pro, running [WP COMPUTE FORMULAS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-compute-formulas), or performing operations such as [WP INSERT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-import-document), [WP New](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-new), or copy/paste, could corrupt internal text ranges, causing the subsequent [WP Text range](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-text-range) command to return incorrect values.

After converting a form to Project mode, if a list box itself had no style sheet but its header, footer, or individual columns did, the conversion generated the corresponding CSS classes but failed to actually assign the class property to those header, footer, and column objects.

A performance regression introduced in v19.3 slowed down SQL pass-through queries to a 4D Server (direct SQL access bypassing ODBC) whenever multiple 4D Server processes were also exposing SQL Server connections.

When printing a Quick Report cross-tab, the left-frame border line printed at only half its expected width, an issue reproduced on certain printers such as the Brother 2710DW and HP Color LaserJet MFP 178nw.
Reloading the same entity twice unexpectedly released the lock that had been placed on it, dropping the lock dependency it should have kept.

When code lines using a backslash line-continuation sequence were followed by a `//` comment or a `/*...*/` block comment nested inside `Case of`/`If` statements, closing and reopening the method could progressively increase the indentation each time, rather than preserving the original formatting.

In Project mode only, form locking in client-server did not behave correctly: after one developer modified and saved a form that was locked because another user had it open, reloading the form on the other user's client unexpectedly cleared the lock indicator, even though the original editor was still working on it.
On Windows, when multiple monitors were connected, the color picker dialog could fail to display at all, blocking further interaction until the hidden dialog was dismissed.

Resizing a PNG image with the picture `*` operator could crop off the trailing pixels: because the resize used floating-point coordinates internally (e.g. scaling to `16.9x16.9` instead of an intended `17x17`), the fractional dimension was truncated when the size was written into the PNG file header, producing a slightly smaller and visibly corrupted image.
After converting a database to Project mode, static text objects that were previously transparent lost that transparency and were rendered with an opaque background instead.
Passing a callback method name in the *methodName* parameter of [QR REPORT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/qr-report) triggered a syntax error instead of being accepted.

On Windows, in SDI mode with a high-resolution (scaled) display, [DRAG WINDOW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/drag-window) did not track the window correctly: the window being dragged no longer stayed under the mouse pointer.

In 4D Write Pro, the type-ahead autocompletion popup for [WP SET ATTRIBUTES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-set-attributes) offered irrelevant constants for a given selector — for example, after the `wk page orientation` constant, the unrelated `wk section index` constant was suggested even though it does not apply.

In the method editor, *Alt*+clicking a token only jumped to the definition of project methods; it did not navigate to the definition of class member functions or variables, contrary to the expected "go to definition" behavior via click-through.

In the Method Editor, Unicode surrogate pairs such as emoji were highlighted incorrectly at the code-point level (high/low) rather than as a single character: selecting via mouse or keyboard could highlight only half of the character, and pressing Delete or Backspace could delete only half of it, corrupting the surrogate pair.

When printing an array-type list box, the column widths progressively narrowed further down each page, so later pages showed increasingly squeezed columns; hiding the vertical scrollbar avoided the problem.
On Windows, starting a print job targeting PDF and then closing it immediately without printing anything still created a blank PDF file on disk.

In 4D Write Pro, when references were hidden and [WP SET DATA CONTEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-set-data-context) was executed before the references were shown again, the computed formula values did not refresh immediately upon re-display.

With the Method Editor option "Highlight variables and fields" set to "selection only," double-clicking a variable was supposed to highlight all occurrences of that name case-insensitively, but the highlighting was incorrectly case-sensitive. The fix keeps property names case-sensitive while making variable-name matching case-insensitive as intended.

Converting a database from Binary to Project mode could cause a list box's alternate-row background color to bleed into other list boxes: when a list box and one of its columns each had their own distinct alternate background color set, the conversion made the column inherit the list box's alternate color instead of preserving its own.

Working in the Structure Editor could trigger an unexpected runtime error, reproducible by double-clicking a table name in the Explorer to jump to the Structure Editor, searching for a string in that table via the search bar, closing the Structure Editor, and repeating the sequence.

After a mailbox that already had an open connection was updated (e.g. by deleting or receiving mail), calling `IMAPTransporter.checkconnection()` incorrectly returned `false` for *success* even though the connection was actually fine.

Passing a formula object as the second parameter to [CALL WORKER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/call-worker), where the formula captured a local variable, failed to clone the captured value properly: an object-type parameter captured by an inner function was not carried over correctly to the worker process.
