In a list box, once the automatic row height property had been enabled, it was no longer possible to switch back to a fixed row height — attempting to set `lk auto row height` back to `lk no` had no effect.

In client-server, 4D commands that manipulate Sets slowed down dramatically while another client was loading records: when one client called [NEXT RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/next-record) while another client or process called [CREATE SET](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-set) on the same table, the operation could take roughly 100 times longer than normal. The regression appeared to be introduced in build 280058.

Sequential searches performed through ORDA on a date attribute were significantly slower — up to 20 times slower — than an equivalent classic [QUERY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query) command search.
4D Server could crash when it had to process a very large number of REST requests.

On Windows, an engined application running in SDI mode sometimes failed to fully quit after all its windows were closed: the icon disappeared from the taskbar, but a background task named "4D Volume Desktop" remained running and visible in Task Manager.

In Binary mode, when [OBJECT SET ENABLED](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-enabled) was used to disable a static text object, the object appeared grayed out (as expected for a disabled control) even if its font color was set to "Automatic," which should not have visually indicated a disabled state in this way.

Calling [OPEN URL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-url) with both a browser name and the `*` option failed to open URLs containing special characters such as `#` that should not have been percent-encoded.

In interpreted mode only, if a method used the new `#DECLARE` syntax without declaring a return type but also used legacy compiler declarations (such as `C_DATE` or `C_LONGINT`) to declare `$0`, 4D could crash — even though mixing the old and new declaration styles this way is not recommended. Compiled mode was unaffected. As a safeguard, the interpreter now creates the `$0` pseudo-variable automatically when `#DECLARE` does not declare a return value, avoiding the crash.
Right-clicking on a comment line in a method did not show the "Go to Definition" or "Search References" context menu items that are normally available.
On macOS, when a form was displayed on a Retina screen and then moved to a non-Retina screen and resized, a rectangle object could disappear entirely. This is the same underlying issue as ACI0103572.
Since v19 R6, the cookie name used for legacy web session management incorrectly embedded the client-server publish name (which could itself be garbled) instead of the structure file name.

In the Quick Report editor, if a formula entered in the first column was very long, its full text was displayed in the column header title with no way to scroll it, making it impossible to see or edit the other report columns.

In the 4D Mobile (4D Go) Data section, selecting a production server's data file made it impossible to confirm a table-name filter — the message "Not validate filter" appeared unexpectedly. Confirming the filter first and only then selecting the production data file worked around the issue.
On macOS 13 (Ventura), a combo box whose height was less than 23 pixels drew its focus ring incorrectly.
On macOS 13 (Ventura), paths to mounted network volumes were not recognized by 4D, and [System info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/system-info) also failed to return network drive paths.
Calling [GRAPH](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/graph) to create a chart without legends could throw an unexpected runtime error — an apparent side effect of the earlier fix for ACI0103151.

On macOS 13 (Ventura), custom or region-specific date formats could render incorrectly: for example, with the system region set to United Kingdom and the language set to Dutch, the *Internal date short* format displayed dates as `DD/MM/YYYY` instead of the correct `DD-MM-YYYY`.

In 4D Write Pro, a project method attached to a document hyperlink did not correctly evaluate expressions referencing fields and tables even when the corresponding records were loaded: fields passed by reference did not receive the current record's value.

Capturing a boolean local variable in a formula did not work: a boolean-type variable passed as a parameter into a [Formula](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/formula) object was not properly captured as a parameter of the resulting function-within-function.

SVG text created with `SVG_New_text` did not support combining underline and strikethrough styles: adding `strikethrough (8)` to `underline (4)` failed to also add the *line-through* value to the *text-decoration* attribute alongside *underline*.
Deleting a method from the Explorer's Home tab via the contextual menu left the deleted method's code still visible in the preview pane instead of clearing it.
Assigning an empty object to an object-type field stored directly in the data file left behind orphaned blob entries in the data file.

In client-server mode, assigning a BLOB attribute accessed via ORDA to a variable could throw an unexpected runtime error, "Try to read beyond end of the stream." This reproduced specifically when a BLOB that was already compressed was compressed again in gzip format.
In the Form Editor, a static line object drawn from right to left or from bottom to top could not be selected and grabbed with the mouse.

On macOS 13 (Ventura), floating palette-type windows (such as controller, palette, or toolbar form windows) created while the application was in the background did not reappear when the application was subsequently brought to the foreground.

Converting a binary database to Project mode incorrectly attached text-specific properties (`stroke`, `fontTheme`, `textDecoration`, `fontWeight`, `fontStyle`, `fontFamily`, `fontSize`) to picture objects, which should not carry text formatting attributes like `fontStyle` or `fontSize`.
When a binary database was converted to Project mode, the title of a picture-datasource object was not rendered with the automatic text stylesheet in the Form Editor as it should be.

Changing a form object's data source type from text to picture failed to reset text-specific properties such as `stroke` and other font attributes, which should be cleared since they no longer apply to a picture object.

With the compiler option "Type the variables" set to fully define all types, parameter indirection symbols (`${2}`) were written to the symbols file typed as `C_VARIANT` rather than their actually declared type. This affected only the symbols file, not the generated code.

In 4D View Pro, the `includeBindingSource` option was ignored when exporting a spreadsheet to Excel via [VP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-export-document): table data was left out of the XLSX export even though the option should make it appear there as well as in the native 4VP format.
On macOS, picture buttons were not displayed correctly in the Form Editor when using Dark Mode.
Exporting a 4D Write Pro document directly to PDF (bypassing the printer driver) degraded the quality of embedded SVG pictures.
On the Portuguese localization of the operating system, the "Compatibility" (Compatibilidade) button label in the database Settings dialog was truncated and not fully displayed.

Queries that mixed indexed and sequential search steps could suffer badly from query-order sensitivity: two logically equivalent queries could run at very different speeds depending on whether the sequential step was run implicitly after an index query or explicitly re-executed with the index flag, with the poorly-ordered version taking roughly twice as long.

Duplicating or pasting a static picture object in the Form Editor could assign it a non-unique object name, which could cause an existing static picture to become effectively "lost" — it still existed in the form but could no longer be displayed.

In Project mode only, calling [OBJECT Get format](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-format) on a list box picture column could return the wrong value, or an empty string, depending on the applied format — reproducible with `Scaled to fit proportional` or `Scaled to fit prop centered`.
On Windows, running 18 or more instances of 4D Server as a Windows service under the same account on the same machine could lead to a deadlock when a 4D Remote client connected.

[IMPORT TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/import-text) failed to correctly recognize field or record separators when one happened to fall exactly at the 255th character of the data, causing records to be misaligned during import.
The automatic client-update confirmation dialog was not displayed when the client to be updated resided in a folder without write permissions, silently skipping a step the user needed to confirm.

In ORDA, a `Not` condition combined with a `null` comparison on an object attribute did not work correctly when run as an indexed query, since `null` — matching no value — should be included in the results of a `Not(attribute = parameter)` query; the equivalent sequential query worked correctly.

On Windows 11 22H2, the print dialog could no longer be controlled by 4D. Because Windows 11 22H2's new print dialog cannot currently be driven via its API, 4D now falls back to displaying the legacy print dialog as a workaround.

In 4D Mobile, if a user logged into an app built with 4D Go via an email address and then updated the app without logging out first, the `device.id` value sent to the server in the session information changed unexpectedly.
Comparing two empty pictures with [Equal pictures](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/equal-pictures) incorrectly returned `False`, even though two empty pictures should be considered equal.
In the Label Editor, importing a label whose text field had its background color set to transparent displayed a gray background instead, contrary to the expected transparent appearance.
On Windows, when using the 4D Write Pro Area + Toolbar widget from the object library, the Write Pro toolbar's tab labels were rendered using a bitmap font, making Japanese text look poor.

When scalable session management and a maximum concurrent web process limit were both configured, the REST server could return an unexpected error 401 after handling a large number of requests. Previously each *On REST Authentication* database event ran in its own dedicated web process; the fix now reuses an already-running process with a language context to run this event when available, avoiding the concurrency limit and also reducing processing time.

In the Quick Report editor embedded in a form, dragging one column to reposition it relative to another caused the break/subtotal to end up attached to the wrong field, because the contextual menu was not refreshed correctly after the drag-and-drop.
On macOS, a component method compiled for the Apple Silicon target ignored its "Execute on server" method property when the component ran in native mode.
Adding a column without a formula to a Quick Report embedded in a form generated an error instead of simply creating an empty column.

The custom *Date* header could not be set on an HTTP request — whether made via the `4D.HTTPRequest` class or the [HTTP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) command — because it was always overwritten internally.
4D Server running as a Windows service could not be restarted from Task Manager. Excluding CEF from the build worked around the problem.

On Spanish or Portuguese Windows, a built desktop application's executable had its product name set to "4D Volume Desktop" instead of the application's actual name, which in turn caused the folder created under Roaming in *AppData* to be named "4D Volume Desktop" rather than after the application.
Assigning [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) to an element of an array of objects triggered an unexpected runtime error.

In 4D Write Pro, after inserting images with [WP Add picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-add-picture) and setting the `wk anchor layout` attribute to `wk in front of text` via [WP SET ATTRIBUTES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-set-attributes), the images were rendered behind the text rather than in front of it as configured.
In Binary mode, changing a highlight button to a 3D button type cleared its assigned keyboard shortcut instead of preserving it.
On macOS, when the database folder was shared over a network and accessed in client-server developer mode while using User mode, picture button icon images failed to display.

Calling [RESTORE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/restore) with a valid archive path and destination folder could sometimes leave the restore dialog open waiting for user input instead of closing automatically once the operation completed.

When the "Scalable sessions" option was enabled, the compiler failed to flag non-thread-safe code in the *On Web Connection* database method, even though this method must be thread-safe in that configuration because the compiler did not check code intended to run in preemptive mode. Temporarily switching to "no session" and back to scalable sessions worked around the issue.

On Windows 11 22H2 only, displaying the legacy print settings dialog via [PRINT SETTINGS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-settings) could randomly cause 4D to quit unexpectedly when the dialog was closed.

On Windows, opening a form on Windows 10 builds earlier than 1703 could crash the application. The crash occurred because such early Windows 10 builds were misidentified internally as Windows 11, triggering calls to high-DPI-support APIs that were not applicable; setting the `WinDPIAwareness` key to `0` in the application's *Info.plist* served as a workaround.

Querying a many-to-one relation attribute (backed by a composite index) via ORDA, then performing a sequential search on the same attribute, could cause the application to freeze or crash during the transformation from an index-based to a sequential search.

On Windows, connecting a local client to a server on the same machine and repeatedly switching between interpreted and compiled mode could eventually cause the client to freeze or crash. Using the legacy network layer avoided the problem.
In the Quick Report editor, if the master table had hidden fields, adding a field through the Quick Report dialog could select the wrong field.
In 4D View Pro, copying and pasting a formula produced the wrong argument separator character.

On Windows, *Alt*+double-clicking a project method or form name written as a string literal did not open that method or form in the editor as expected, though *Control*+K still worked as an alternative.
Clicking the intersection point of ruled lines in a Quick Report embedded in a form returned error `9850` instead of no action.

On macOS, compiling a particular project for both Intel and Apple Silicon targets could produce compilation errors, because unwanted digit-group separators were being applied to numeric constants, which threw off function parameter counts. The underlying cause was an installed plugin changing the global C++ locale without restoring it afterward.
The [LDAP SEARCH ALL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ldap-search-all) command had several memory leaks.

On the Dutch or Spanish localization, [VP REMOVE TABLE COLUMNS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-remove-table-columns) in 4D View Pro did not work correctly; the issue was fixed as part of the SpreadJS 16.2.0 update.

In client-server Binary mode, breakpoints set in Design mode were not saved when [CHANGE CURRENT USER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/change-current-user) was called from the *On Startup* database method.
[LOAD VARIABLES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/load-variables) could crash the application when it read an empty picture variable from disk.

On macOS, [SQL LOGIN](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-login) failed with error 9921 when using the latest (v3.3.1) Devart ODBC Driver for Sybase. 4D correctly follows Microsoft's specification by calling `SQLConnectW` with `SQL_NTS`, but the Apple Silicon build of the Devart driver did not properly implement `SQL_NTS(-3)` handling for the password, failing to read a null-terminated string correctly; 4D was adjusted to pass an explicit character count to work around the third-party driver bug.
Using the ternary operator together with a table field in an expression triggered a syntax error.
Clicking the Restore button in the Maintenance and Security Center while no data file was selected caused the application to crash.
A Quick Report embedded in a form failed to reload the first time the form was reopened after being closed, appearing correctly only every other time.

The Settings > Security panel's label for restricting commands and project methods usable in the formula editor and 4D Write Pro documents also applies to 4D View Pro documents, but the label text did not mention 4D View Pro, leaving that scope unclear.
Setting a list box's alternate background CSS property `alternateFill` to the automatic alternate-color keyword `automaticAlternate` produced a CSS parsing error instead of being accepted.

REST licenses were not always released correctly: on a server with both client-connection licenses and a REST extension license installed, if a client accessed the server both via a regular connection and via REST and the REST session then timed out, some REST licenses remained held instead of being freed.
In client-server mode, the Data Explorer failed to display data because of confusion between the server's webadmin URL and the client's own webadmin URL.
In 4D Write Pro, dragging the vertical scrollbar thumb all the way to the bottom could unexpectedly jump back to the top instead — reproducible specifically on the first such scroll operation.

While compiling for the Apple Silicon target, an unexpected "Internal error while compiling with clang" message could appear — even after clearing compiled code — when a form contained duplicate object names across different pages.

Calling [HTTP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) without specifying keep-alive mode could sometimes return status code 503 with an empty response instead of the expected XML, a behavior difference from v19 that appeared in v19 R.

In the Toolbox's Groups dialog, restarting a project reverted plugin access permissions that had been updated in the Toolbox back to their previous state, so choosing a non-licensed plugin — which makes no sense since this dialog manages access to licensed offerings — was no longer possible to avoid; the dialog now only displays functionality covered by an active license.
On macOS only, the text baseline within a form object's tab control rendered too low.

On Apple Silicon Macs (M1), a compiled application containing a very large number of string literals in the project could crash on startup, apparently because the constants exhausted stack memory during process initialization; Intel Macs were unaffected.

In client-server, opening a project first with a v19 R feature release and later reopening it with a v19.x LTS release triggered a "Failed to synchronize Plugins folder" error, affecting the *Extras*, *Plugins*, and *Components* folder synchronization.

Calling [Pop up menu](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/pop-up-menu) inside an *On Getting Focus* event on a text input, followed by sending a Tab key with [POST KEY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/post-key), left the form stuck in a loop: clicking anywhere on the form would re-focus the same text input and re-fire the event repeatedly. Tracing form events avoided the issue.
Since 19.5 HF1, a multi-criteria query on indexed fields could run up to 400 times slower when all the relevant data was already in cache — an apparent side effect of the earlier fix for ACI0103507.

On Windows only, in client-server mode, using [MESSAGE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/message) right after [GOTO XY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/goto-xy) left the window blank with no message displayed at all.

A form input object whose data source value was [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) refused to accept any data entry; the field worked fine when the data source held an empty string instead, or when "Map Null to empty value" was enabled. The fix ensures that when a form object's data source is an entity attribute holding `Null`, the field type from `entity.getDataClass()[name].fieldType` is now correctly applied to the input control.

Enlarging a large picture using the `Scale` option of [TRANSFORM PICTURE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/transform-picture) and then calling [PICTURE TO BLOB](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/picture-to-blob) could crash the application due to running out of memory; the fix trades a small amount of processing speed for avoiding the crash.

Opening the [IMPORT DATA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/import-data) dialog did not allow choosing the correct table after [SET TABLE TITLES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-table-titles) and [SET FIELD TITLES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-field-titles) had been used to customize titles; launching the dialog from the File menu instead worked correctly.
In 4D Write Pro, the `WParea.modified` flag was set to true every time the cursor was placed in the text area, even when nothing in the document had actually changed.
In the final v19 R7 build, the Stop button (a cross icon next to the progress bar) was missing from the results window while a "Find in Design" search was running.

On Apple Silicon Macs, compiling a project right after restarting the machine could unexpectedly fail with "Couldn't find active developer tools," because the compiler internally runs [LAUNCH EXTERNAL PROCESS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/launch-external-process) with a 2-second timeout that was too short immediately after a system restart; the timeout has been extended to 60 seconds.
In client-server compiled mode, calling a component method configured to run in non-preemptive mode from within a class member function did not raise the expected error.
A built, auto-executable desktop application did not quit cleanly: it crashed right after the sponsored-message dialog was closed on exit.

On Windows, when several instances of 4D Server were run as services under the same local account, [Get license info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/license-info) did not return the correct number of connected clients.

In an entity-selection list box, after selecting a row with [LISTBOX SELECT ROWS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-select-rows), using the arrow keys moved the highlight relative to the row previously selected by a mouse click rather than relative to the row just selected by the command.

On macOS, if the path to Xcode contained a space or other special character, compiling for the Apple Silicon target failed with "Failed to call xcode-select," because the Xcode path was not properly escaped internally.
Displaying a picture in a list box cell caused the image's right edge to overflow past the cell's dividing line.
It was not possible to activate a 4D OEM Desktop license.

It was possible to assign a shared `Signal` object to a property of a non-shared object; attempting to then copy such an object with [OB Copy](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-copy) using the `ck shared` option triggered error -10719. Wrapping access to the `Signal` object in `Use` avoided the problem.
The help tip for [Super](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/super) showed the raw localization key "xliff:desc1705" instead of a translated description.
In client-server, the *On SQL Authentication* database method on 4D Server could not be debugged with [TRACE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/trace).

In compiled mode only, the short-circuit lazy operators (`||` and `&&`) evaluated incorrectly when compared against a negative numeric literal operand: for example, `5 || -1` returned `4` instead of `5`. Adding explicit parentheses (`5 || (-1)`) avoided the miscalculation.
Opening the Maintenance and Security Center without selecting a data file and clicking the encryption or rollback button caused the application to freeze in an endless loop (spinning wheel).
`IMAPTransporter.getBoxList()` did not correctly return special characters such as accented letters (e.g. "é").
In Project mode only, pressing Tab to move between entries in the Form Editor's property list could place the input cursor in the wrong cell.

Launching a project from the command-line interface with the `--dataless` argument (combined with `--headless`) crashed 4D if the project was configured to start its web server automatically; using `--headless` alone worked fine.
The border style set on a picture input object was ignored when the form was actually run, even though it displayed correctly in the Form Editor.
In client-server compiled mode, calling `dataClass.get($key)` where the entity's primary key value contained a comma character crashed the 4D client.

In an entity-selection list box with automatic row height enabled, a row or cell added dynamically without an explicit list box refresh did not display its content correctly; an explicit redraw of the list box was needed to fix the display.

On macOS, the arrow widget on the right side of a combo box was misaligned by 1 pixel relative to the equivalent element in a popup menu. Because combo boxes and popup menus were reworked with different underlying implementations in 19 R8, only v19 was fixed.

On macOS, the width of the focus ring drawn around a combo box differed from that of a popup menu. As with the related alignment issue, only v19 was fixed since 19 R8 uses a different implementation for these controls.

Undo (*Ctrl*+Z) did not work for edits made in a collection-type, entity-selection-type, or record-selection-type list box, unlike an array-type list box or a regular variable, which supported undo correctly. Enabling the "Do not raise event" item property in the Edit menu, or setting the `"4D_execute_without_validating"` item property to [True](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/true) via [SET MENU ITEM PROPERTY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-menu-item-property), worked around the problem.

In an array-based list box with automatic row height enabled, updating a cell's content left the list box incorrectly redrawn; explicitly calling [REDRAW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/redraw) fixed the display.
In an embedded (CEF-based) web area, camera and microphone access permissions were not granted correctly.

In 4D View Pro, using [VP MOVE CELLS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-move-cells), [VP Copy to object](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-copy-to-object), or [VP PASTE FROM OBJECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-paste-from-object) consumed excessive memory and took an unusually long time to complete.

Resizing a window vertically did not fully redraw the list box it contained: the newly visible rows did not trigger an additional *On Display Detail* event, so their content stayed blank until the vertical scrollbar was manipulated to force a redraw.
In the export dialog, changing the field delimiter unexpectedly added all of a table's fields to the preview area.

In Binary mode, opening a method in the editor while another client already had it locked showed the lock icon in the editor's toolbar, but no alert message warned the user that the method was locked by someone else.

In Project mode only, if two form objects of the same data type were selected and then a third object of a different data type was selected, the Explorer's property list display could become blank instead of updating to reflect the mismatched selection.

Changing the *4D Remote mode timeout* option with [SET DATABASE PARAMETER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-parameter) reset the "Web Client IP address to listen" option that had been set via [WEB GET OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-get-option). The root cause was that a listening-port change made in memory was not persisted, but a subsequent update to the settings.4DSettings file via SET DATABASE PARAMETER reloaded the file and overwrote the in-memory setting.
Calling the IMAPTransporter .selectBox() method incorrectly returned error 11 ("IMAP SELECT command failed") even when the mailbox selection should have succeeded, a regression from earlier behavior.
In Client/Server mode, saving a BLOB attribute on an entity using entity.save(dk auto merge) resulted in the BLOB being stored as 0 bytes, silently losing the binary data.

On Windows, typing in a 4D Write Pro document became noticeably laggy when the document contained a high-resolution image (around 300 dpi), because on-screen rendering was not optimized for such images. The fix improves rendering performance, though Windows may now use more memory for image caching.

Using [VP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-export-document) to export a 4D View Pro spreadsheet containing a SpreadJS pivot table to XLSX produced a corrupted file: opening it in Excel triggered a repair dialog.
Choosing "Reveal in explorer" from a method's context menu could freeze the application if the design mode Explorer window had already been closed.
Opening a trigger method in Visual Studio Code with the 4D-Analyzer extension installed could crash the LSP server, leaving the code without syntax/token coloring.

When a field's "map NULL values to blank" property was disabled, typing a value into an attribute of a brand-new entity shown in an entity-selection list box was discarded as soon as focus left the cell (via Tab), similar to the input-area issue in ACI0103657. The fix allows a value matching the field's type to be entered instead of [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null), provided the underlying field for that list box column can be identified from its data source.

With the new network layer, after a server rejected a new client connection and then accepted a subsequent one, the server's application name stopped being broadcast over UDP, and the only way to resume discovery was to restart the server. The legacy network layer was not affected.

The 'Conduit ITC Pro' font's Medium style had to be referenced by a different name on each platform in 4D Write Pro documents ("Conduit ITC Pro Medium" on Windows vs. "ConduitITCPro-Medium" on Mac). The fix normalizes the font's full name (as returned by wk font/wk list font) to be platform-independent, and documents saved on Mac before the fix, which stored a PostScript name, are still correctly recognized; the value returned is now a neutral font name rather than a PostScript or display name.
Converting a 4D View spreadsheet to 4D View Pro did not correctly carry over percentage number formatting, so converted cells lost their percentage display.

On the Japanese version of macOS, setting a combo box's font to "Application font" caused the menu item rows to be rendered too short, cutting off the top 2-3 pixels of the focused item. The application font maps internally to a Western font like Helvetica or San Francisco, but the Japanese system substitutes a different font whose height wasn't accounted for when sizing combo box menu items (unlike regular text input, which adjusts height automatically).

Removing focus from a form object via [GOTO OBJECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/goto-object) at the same time as a standard "next record" action left the visual focus indicator still showing on the object instead of clearing it.

On Windows, at high display scaling (above 100%), changing the font size of styled text via the font picker applied the chosen size multiplied by the scale factor instead of the size itself; conversely, selecting styled text while the font picker was open displayed its size divided by the scale factor. Both cases produced font sizes that didn't match what the user selected or saw.

Exporting a 4D View Pro spreadsheet containing pivot tables to XLSX via [VP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-export-document) while the process was off-screen produced a file that opened in Excel without its sheet-navigation tab bar, leaving Ctrl+Page Up/Down as the only way to switch sheets. Exporting through the normal user interface did not exhibit the problem.

[WP Get sections](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-sections) (and, in a related report, [WP Insert formula](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-insert-formula) as well) leaked memory, which could accumulate over repeated calls and eventually cause the application to hang or crash.

On Windows with an English keyboard layout, key codes captured during [ON EVENT CALL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/on-event-call) did not match the expected character codes in the KEYCODE system variable inside the event-handling method. This is the same underlying issue as ACI0102083, previously fixed for v18 and v19 R3; a French keyboard layout was unaffected.

Compressing a 0-byte BLOB using GZIP fast or GZIP best compression mode made [COMPRESS BLOB](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/compress-blob) return error 100, apparently a side effect of the fix for ACI0103487.

In Project mode, [OBJECT SET LIST BY NAME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-list-by-name) failed to set a choice list on a list box column when that column was linked, through its properties list, to an enumeration defined in the toolbox.

In an entity-selection list box, after deselecting a row with [LISTBOX SELECT ROWS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-select-rows), using the arrow keys to select a row afterward selected the row adjacent to the one that had been deselected, instead of anchoring selection at the first or last row as expected.

Immediately after running a query on an entity selection displayed in a list box, selecting a row with arrow keys or Shift+click anchored the selection to whatever row had been selected before the query ran, rather than the current state; regular selection-based list boxes were not affected.
Variant-type values were not handled correctly in 4D Write Pro tables: once a picture value was displayed in a given column, that column could no longer display other value types such as text.

On Mac, a keyboard shortcut assigned programmatically to a menu item using a symbol such as "cmd #" could display incorrectly in the menu (e.g., showing "⇧⌘3" instead of the intended shortcut), with the exact rendering depending on system localization, keyboard layout, and the character chosen.
On Windows, attempting to print a 4D View Pro spreadsheet to a PDF or XPS printer triggered a system error and crashed the application, apparently a side effect of the fix for ACI0103757.

Displaying an invalid SVG image in a form returned an unexpected error 1 instead of gracefully falling back to an "X" placeholder mark for unrenderable images, for example when the image's link:href attribute contained an invalid data URI.
In the application build screen used when compiling a component, the "Application Name" input field was too narrow to comfortably display or edit longer names.

Using [QR SET SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/qr-set-selection) on a Quick Report editor embedded in a form appeared to select a column internally, but the editor's display did not visually reflect the selected column.
In Client/Server mode, ORDA could not properly access a 4D.Blob whose size was between 1 and 99 bytes: the returned 4D.Blob object had an undefined size property instead of the actual byte count.

Calling [FILTER KEYSTROKE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/filter-keystroke) with an empty string while text was selected in an input field erased the selection, because the empty string was applied as a replacement for the selected characters.

On Windows only, using a Japanese (non-ASCII) local variable name inside a [Begin SQL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/begin-sql)...[End SQL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/end-sql) block caused a compiler error, preventing methods that embed SQL with such variable names from compiling.

In built Client/Server applications on Windows, reaching the maximum number of concurrent users no longer showed the intended "maximum concurrent users has been reached" license message; instead, clients simply got a generic "could not connect, contact your administrator" error.
On macOS Ventura, assigning a button title a font other than the automatic style sheet font caused the title text to be rendered slightly above vertical center instead of centered.

The server Administration window could show multiple updater-related processes at once, one of which could not be aborted, and its type could be mislabeled (e.g., appearing as "Application Server" instead of "Application process") in the type column.

In Client/Server mode, if the server Administration window was open when [RESTART 4D](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/restart-4d) was executed and the window's display was then switched, the actual server restart was blocked until the Administration window was closed.

In a list box with a column set to automatic row height, vertical padding enabled, and a maximum number of lines lower than the number of lines some cells actually contained, those cells' content was displayed truncated.

If a field that is set as non-enterable in the property list is switched to enterable at runtime via [OBJECT SET ENTERABLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-enterable), the drop-down/choice list attached to that field no longer appeared. Doing the same switch from an On Load form event (making the field enterable there, then toggling it later) worked correctly.
In client/server mode, shrinking an existing BLOB (4D.Blob) field to a size smaller than its previous value failed to save when the record was updated using dk auto merge mode.

In the English version of the Settings dialog, clicking the help/documentation link resulted in a "Page not found" error because the generated URL incorrectly included the language identifier segment (/en/), which the English documentation pages omit.

Calling [OBJECT GET BEST SIZE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-best-size) on a bevel button that has a popup menu produced an incorrect result: after resizing, the popup menu icon (linked or separate style) was drawn on top of the button's title instead of alongside it.

When many processes were in a postponed/delayed state during a 4D Server shutdown, the server did not quit promptly. The timeout before forcibly terminating delayed processes had been mistakenly set to 50 seconds instead of 3 seconds, so a "Task Pending" alert appeared before those processes could be killed off; the delay itself posed no risk of data corruption.
On the new ServerNet network layer only, rejecting new incoming client connections from the server administration window also caused already-connected clients to lose their connection to the server.

Using "Go to definition…" from the right-click context menu on a project method name that appeared inside a comment no longer opened that method, even though the equivalent command from the Method menu still worked correctly.
Since 4D v19 R8, type-ahead/autocompletion no longer worked for process and interprocess variable names in the method editor.
On macOS, 4D could no longer connect to Sybase through the freeTDS ODBC driver; the issue appeared after the macOS Ventura 13.3.1 update, which had previously worked fine.
On macOS, compiling for Apple Silicon targets took significantly longer when Xcode 14.3 (build 14E222b) was installed, compared to using Xcode 14.2 or 14.1.

On macOS, calling `collection.orderByMethod()` with a sort callback that set `$1.result` to [True](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/true) even though the comparison `$1.value<$1.value2` evaluated to [False](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/false) could crash the application; on Windows there was no crash, but the sort silently returned an incorrect (False) result instead. An internally inconsistent sort now raises error 917 rather than crashing or misbehaving.

Passing an incorrect value (a `*` in the encoding parameter) as the third argument of [TEXT TO DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/text-to-document) went undetected by the syntax checker and still compiled successfully, but running the compiled code triggered a runtime "unsupported encoding" error instead of failing earlier.
In an array-based list box cell with an associated popup/drop-down menu, selecting a value using the keyboard (rather than the mouse) did not trigger the On Data Change form event.

On Windows in SDI mode, calling [Open form window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-form-window) with the "save window position and size" option enabled failed to actually persist the window's position and size, so the window did not reopen at its previous location after being closed and reopened.
Calling [OBJECT SET VISIBLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-visible) on a 4D Write Pro area/widget raised an error instead of toggling its visibility as expected.
A client application crashed immediately upon connecting to the server when the structure defined two relations between tables that shared the same name.
On macOS, a compiled (built) client could not connect to a compiled server when the QUIC network layer was enabled.
The `certificatesFolder` property passed when creating a 4D.HTTPRequest object was being ignored, so the specified client certificate was not actually used for the request.

In the method editor, typing a period after an object-type variable followed by an underscore and pressing Tab failed to show attribute names starting with an underscore in the type-ahead suggestions. Such attributes are conventionally treated as private and excluded by default, but the behavior was adjusted so that, as in v19, typing the underscore character itself still surfaces them in the completion list.

In the Form Editor's Properties palette, the Help Tips popup menu did not always refresh correctly: after selecting a picture button, opening the toolbox to change its help tip, and then bringing the Form Editor back to the front, the palette kept showing the stale value. Selecting a different object and then reselecting the picture button forced the palette to update properly.
In the Structure Editor, the very first attempt to zoom in returned an error, though subsequent zoom attempts worked fine.
In the Explorer's Table tab, clicking a column header in the fields list on the right side did not sort the list as expected.

In Project mode, opening a database directly from the Maintenance and Security Center (MSC) failed to detect its index file; opening the project first and then launching the MSC from within it avoided the problem.

For certain emails, converting the message to a 4D mail object with [MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) omitted the resulting object's `bodyValues` property.
Picture buttons were created with a default horizontal alignment of "centered" instead of the previous default of "left-aligned," a regression from earlier versions.

On Windows Server 2012 R2 and Windows Server 2016, launching 4D produced an error stating that the entry point `SetThreadDescription` could not be located in Kernel.dll; the application launched normally on Windows Server 2019 and later.

Opening the toolbox from a form via the Properties palette incorrectly marked the current form as modified and caused the .4DForm file to be saved immediately; method and form source files should instead only be saved when the application loses focus, not from within the editor itself.

In an array-based list box, moving a row triggered an unwanted On Clicked event in addition to the expected On Row Moved event. Normally, when row-moving is enabled, the click/drop event should fire only on mouse-button release, whereas without it a click event fires on mouse-button press.

The syntax checker flagged the new `collection.first()` method, added in v20, as an unrecognized member function even though it is a valid method of [New collection](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/new-collection) objects.

On macOS, converting a 4D Write Pro document containing a duplicated SVG picture to PDF via [WP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-export-document) crashed the application; on Windows it did not crash, but the SVG image was rasterized instead of being preserved as vector art.

On Windows in v20, window type 8 behaved differently than in previous versions: it allowed the user to switch focus to its parent window, whereas this window type should remain modal-like and block switching to other windows while displayed.

A syntax error warning displayed in the method editor remained visible even after the underlying issue was fixed, persisting until the method was explicitly saved rather than clearing as soon as the code became valid.

In the method editor, pressing Tab after the `var` keyword to complete an already-declared variable name did not work when the declaration statement was otherwise complete; it only worked correctly mid-declaration, before the colon and variable type had been typed.

In the method editor, typing a numeric literal followed by a period and pressing Tab incorrectly displayed a list of macros as autocompletion suggestions, rather than treating the period as a decimal point in a Real constant.

In the method editor, typing "#dec" and pressing Tab to autocomplete produced the malformed result "##DECLARE" instead of "#DECLARE" when selecting it from the suggestion list; typing "#de" or "#decl" and completing did not exhibit the problem.

In the method editor, pressing Tab to accept a code-completion suggestion for an already-existing variable name no longer corrected the case of the typed characters to match the variable's original casing.
The code editor did not support `//MARK:` style comment tags for organizing and navigating method code into labeled sections.

When a new row was dynamically added to an entitySelection-based list box configured with automatic row height, the new row rendered with a height of 0 instead of sizing to fit its content; the row only displayed correctly after the list box was manually refreshed. The same incorrect zero-height rendering occurred when an existing cell was updated with larger content.

On macOS, in a multi-style text (rich text) object displayed inside a modal form dialog box, choosing "Other…" from the context menu's Color or Background Color option to open the color picker failed to actually change the font color or background color. The custom color could be applied normally when the window was not modal.

Printing an offscreen 4D View Pro area within a print job started via [OPEN PRINTING JOB](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-printing-job) could cause the application to quit unexpectedly; on-screen View Pro areas printed without issue. Note: even after the fix, developers printing offscreen areas must call [SET CURRENT PRINTER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-current-printer) and [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option) before starting the print job, since omitting a path still triggers a file-selection dialog by design, and behavior is undefined when trying to display an offscreen web area in this context.

Enabling client/server communication encryption together with a web server configured to start automatically at launch caused the HTTPS server to use an incorrect (downgraded) certificate chain instead of the proper one.

In a 4D Write Pro document, inserting a formula via [WP Insert formula](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-insert-formula) that referenced [WP Get page count](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-page-count) through a local variable caused [WP PRINT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-print) to crash. Note: the crash is fixed, but a Write Pro area still cannot be assigned to a local variable and self-referenced from within its own formula (it simply returns an empty value); since `WP Get page count` recalculates page layout, embedding it as a formula in the same document creates recursive calls — developers should precompute the page count beforehand or use `This.pageCount` instead.

Repeatedly performing [LDAP LOGIN](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ldap-login) and [LDAP LOGOUT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ldap-logout) in `LDAP password MD5 (0)` mode returned unexpected error -2 on the second login attempt; this appears to be a side effect introduced by the fix for ACI0103594.

Type-ahead completion for table names was broken: pressing Tab after typing only part of a table name inserted whichever table name sorted first alphabetically, ignoring the characters already typed, rather than the matching candidate. The correct table name was only inserted once enough characters had been typed to narrow the match down to a single candidate.

On macOS, when the iODBC framework was not installed, calling [SQL GET DATA SOURCE LIST](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-get-data-source-list) returned an internal error consisting of an array with null size instead of failing gracefully.

Applying a style such as bold repeatedly to styled text — for example right after typing, when no text was actively highlighted/selected — failed to apply the new style, apparently due to nested style spans where one style's range could override another's.

Calling [QR BLOB TO REPORT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/qr-blob-to-report) without first calling [Get current printer](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-current-printer) caused the application to crash unexpectedly.
When multiple web processes concurrently called [WEB SEND TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-send-text), a deadlock could occur while 4D Server was shutting down, freezing the server.
In a 4D Write Pro area placed inside a subform, entering a search string and running a search via the Find widget on the upper toolbar returned unexpected error #108 instead of performing the search.

Importing certain DOCX documents into 4D Write Pro caused some text to be missing from the result (and consequently from any PDF conversion). The issue involved markup tags used for right-to-left language directionality that were not defined in the 2012 OOXML specification. After the fix, the text now displays, but Write Pro still does not support tags that switch text direction mid-paragraph, so content only renders correctly when left-to-right text is inserted within an otherwise right-to-left document (not the reverse).

Changing an array-type list box's row-height behavior via [LISTBOX SET PROPERTY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-set-property) and the `lk auto row height` property, when the list box had zero rows to display, resulted in an incorrectly calculated row height.

In a compiled server build, starting a worker from the *On Server Startup* database method and calling [ds](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ds) inside that worker caused the application to crash unexpectedly.
On Windows, in Project mode, buttons no longer displayed a visible focus highlight ring when they received keyboard focus.

In Project mode, attempting to create a new form using a name that already belonged to an existing form threw a runtime error (reporting that the file already existed) instead of being handled gracefully, e.g. with a proper warning.

In Project mode, setting a button's default-button property to true caused its configured style (when not the regular style) to be ignored, silently reverting the button's appearance to the regular style.

On Windows, exporting a 4D Write Pro document to PDF using [WP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-export-document) failed to render characters from the Wingdings font in the resulting PDF.

When 4D Server ran as a Windows service, [WP PRINT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-print) could fail to print a 4D Write Pro document. This occurred when the selected current printer was a virtual printer that had been renamed to mimic "Microsoft XPS Document Printer" without actually being the genuine driver — 4D has no way to verify authenticity from the name alone, so it assumed an XPS export without a specified file path was intended, and since headless mode disallows showing a file-selection dialog, it returned error 3107 instead of printing.
In an array-type list box with automatic row height enabled, updating a cell's content caused the horizontal grid lines to redraw incorrectly afterward.

Calling `entitySelection.query()` on an existing entity selection when querying a many-to-one relation attribute that was [null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) returned incorrect results instead of properly matching (or excluding) entities with a null related entity.

Passing a ternary (conditional) expression that could yield two different data types as a parameter to a command — such as `CALL WORKER` — caused a compilation error ("Attempting to retype by using a pointer or a variant") in compiled mode, for example `CALL WORKER(Is compiled mode ? 1 : "P2"; Formula(MyMethod))`. This happens because the type of the ternary expression is determined by its second operand, creating a type conflict at compile time.

The [Open form window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-form-window) command incorrectly executed/evaluated arguments that were passed as variables or expressions, when they should have been used as-is without evaluation.

Using [OBJECT SET FORMAT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-format) to hide a button's icon caused its title to become center-aligned instead of preserving the button's configured alignment; if the title was set to left-aligned, hiding the icon should not change its position, unlike in version 19.
On Windows, entering a decimal point in a 4D View Pro area using the numeric keypad always displayed a period (`.`) as the decimal separator, regardless of the system's regional/locale settings.

On macOS, long-pressing a character key to bring up the extended-character picker (e.g. holding "u" to see "u", "û", "ü", "ù", etc.) and selecting a variant using the number keys could insert incorrect text, combining both the accented and unaccented characters. Selecting the variant with arrow keys or a mouse click worked correctly.
On Windows only, exporting a 4D Write Pro document to .4wp format using the upper toolbar's export feature returned an unexpected error if the file extension was not explicitly typed by the user.
When automatic session management was disabled, each REST access caused the internal error stack to keep growing indefinitely instead of being cleared, leading to unbounded memory growth over time.

A Windows 4D Remote client could crash after connecting in compiled mode to a 4D Server project running on macOS that was compiled exclusively for Apple Silicon (no Intel target) and that used an *On Startup* database method; the crash did not occur if no such method existed. Note: 4D previously had no way to detect Apple-Silicon-only compiled projects; the fix adds an internal marker and a new error message, but affected projects must be recompiled to pick up the fix.

When a form's main body contained only a single subform object and no other focusable objects, tabbing through the fields inside the subform could cause focus to be lost entirely at the start or end of the tab order, breaking the ability to cycle through objects with Tab.

On macOS, for a ruler-type form object configured with a negative minimum value, dragging its handle to the left of zero and then back into positive values left the thermometer-style display stuck pointing at zero instead of updating to reflect the current value.

In a list box with multiple rows already selected, clicking on one of the already-selected rows failed to deselect the other rows, so the selection did not collapse to just the clicked row as expected. Clicking an unselected row, or selecting a row programmatically via command, worked correctly.

In a ruler form object, when the minimum value isn't an exact multiple of the step value, the tick marks were computed incorrectly — starting from a multiple of the step instead of from the minimum. For example, with minimum 5, maximum 25, and step 10, the ruler should read 5 10 15 20 but instead showed 10 20 25.
On Mac in Project mode, setting the textAlign property of a text area or input object to "justify" was ignored once the form was run — the field displayed with plain left alignment instead.
On Mac, the copyright information embedded in a built package/file's information still showed "2022" instead of the correct current year.

In the [IMPORT DATA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/import-data) dialog, choosing "Fixed Length Text" from the format popup incorrectly triggered an error claiming a style sheet could not be found.
In the code editor, type-ahead auto-completion for table names stopped working when the leading bracket ("[") was omitted before typing the name.

On Mac, calling [SQL LOGIN](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-login) in an environment where the iODBC Framework isn't installed caused the application to crash instead of failing gracefully.
Attempting to quit 4D Server while the Database Settings dialog was open caused the application to crash.

On Windows, in Project mode, moving keyboard focus to a button styled as a toolbar/Office XP/circular button (appearance unchanged even while focused) meant pressing Enter no longer activated the form's default button, unlike standard buttons.
When tokenizing an object written in literal object syntax, extra whitespace inserted between a property name and its colon (:) was not automatically stripped out during formatting.

When a project was opened from a remote client, or when an already-compiled .4DZ file was opened directly, the Database Settings should be read-only, but the settings dialog still allowed values to be typed into its fields even though the changes could not actually be saved.

After using [LISTBOX SET AUTO ROW HEIGHT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-set-auto-row-height) to set the maximum or minimum row height on an array-type list box with automatic row height enabled, the row heights were not correctly recalculated to reflect the new setting.

On Mac, when the OS appearance setting is "Inherit" and a form's appearance property is set to Dark, a window displayed via the [DIALOG](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dialog) command failed to render in dark mode. Explicitly targeting the form beforehand with [Open form window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-form-window) avoided the issue.

In 4D View Pro, a [Substring](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/substring) formula embedded in a cell of a 4D View spreadsheet was not converted correctly when the spreadsheet was migrated to 4D View Pro, producing wrong results.

In the code editor, type-ahead auto-completion for table names failed when the table name was entered right after a pointer dereference (e.g. `$pTable:=->`), causing the leading bracket to be omitted from the inserted text.

In an array-type list box with the "Single click edit" property enabled, dragging a row to reorder it unexpectedly also fired the On Clicked event in addition to the row-move event — similar to a previously reported issue (ACI0103898).
The IMAP Transporter's searchMails() method failed to find messages whose message ID contained URL-encoded characters.

In a list box, dragging a multi-row selection without holding Alt caused the list to first auto-scroll all the way to the last-clicked row before the drag began, rather than starting the drag immediately. Selections made via command-click or shift-click were unaffected.
On macOS Sonoma, the background of the selected/highlighted tab in a Tab Control was not rendered in Light mode, making its label text effectively invisible.
In 4D Explorer, emptying the trash while it still contained a deleted table and a deleted method could cause the application to quit unexpectedly.
Declaring a class property with an Integer type and then referencing it with a negated pointer-style syntax such as `-This.prop` caused the compiler to return an error.

When a pointer-type parameter was declared with #DECLARE or C_POINTER and a different pointer was assigned directly to that parameter variable inside the method, the caller's original pointer was also unexpectedly updated. A pointer-type parameter should behave like a local variable, not alias the caller's pointer.

Referencing a component's class as the data type in a class's property declaration caused the syntax checker to wrongly warn that the class was undefined, and the code editor's type-ahead failed to list that class's member functions and properties as completion candidates.

On Windows, in SDI mode, quitting an engined single-user application or a client via a standard quit action logged an unexpected error message, including event ID 1000 in the Windows application event log. This appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0103923.

On Windows, switching a form away from (and then back to) a page that contains a hidden web area opened with an empty page via [WA OPEN URL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wa-open-url) left a field on that page unable to accept typed text. Activating a different window and returning to the form restored normal input.

In Project mode, using [SELECTION TO ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/selection-to-array) to copy a Text field into an undefined column of an array-type list box produced an underlying string array (`_o_ARRAY STRING`) instead of the expected [ARRAY TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/array-text), losing the Text type distinction.
When tool4d was used as the Language Server Protocol backend for VS Code, it could occasionally peg the CPU at close to 100% usage.
In Project mode, tri-state checkboxes did not function correctly.

The 4D.SystemWorker.errors property returned undefined instead of an empty collection when no error had occurred, contradicting the documented behavior that it should always contain a (possibly empty) collection.

In a list box using [LISTBOX SET AUTO ROW HEIGHT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-set-auto-row-height) with automatic row height, after changing the maximum row height, scrolling could cause cell contents to be redrawn incorrectly — the problem occurred specifically when a cell's text contained more lines than fit within the configured maximum height.

After changing the maximum row height of an auto-row-height list box with [LISTBOX SET AUTO ROW HEIGHT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-set-auto-row-height), subsequently scrolling it via [OBJECT SET SCROLL POSITION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-scroll-position) landed on the wrong row instead of the intended position.
Querying a calculated attribute reached through a relation, combined with more than one operator such as OR or IN, did not return the expected results.

Launching an application could sometimes fail with an unexpected error stating that an entry point (specifically IsThirdPartyinitialized) could not be found in a Dynamic Link Library, occurring when CEF (Chromium Embedded Framework) libcef.dll was not on the correct path.
In Project mode, using the Form Editor's "Automatic Size" context-menu command on a Radio Button or Check Box object computed the wrong size.

In 4D Write Pro, newly inserted user formulas in a document could no longer have their display switched from reference to computed value — the formula reference was always shown instead of the calculated result.

In 4D Write Pro, inserting a table into a subsection whose horizontal margins differ from those of the following subsection caused a [PAGE BREAK](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/page-break) to be inserted automatically before the table, which was not intended.

On Windows, exporting a 4D Write Pro document to PDF could render some characters overlapping each other compared to a printed copy, depending on the font used — the *Artdeco MN* family was specifically affected. The cause was a low-level kerning issue in the bundled PDF-Writer library; as a workaround, offsets for that font family are now computed via the DirectWrite API instead.
In the French-localized edition of 4D, switching the language preference to French caused the constant `ck count values` to no longer be recognized/tokenized by the method editor.
Using the plugin SDK entry point `PA_ExecuteObjectMethod` to call an entity selection member method with parameters in compiled mode caused the application to crash.
Activating the remote debugger from a 4D client, on a binary (non-project) database, caused the 4D Server to crash.
On macOS, rounded-corner bevel checkboxes/radio buttons with an automatic font color setting displayed their title text in the wrong color instead of white.

The [FORM Event](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-event) command returned an invalid text in its `.description` property — a raw XLIFF reference like `:xliff:PL_event_-4` — whenever the `.code` property was a negative number, notably when a negative form event was sent via [CALL SUBFORM CONTAINER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/call-subform-container).
The method editor's type-ahead/autocomplete failed to accept `entitySelection.length` while typing code.

On macOS, calling [OBJECT GET BEST SIZE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-best-size) after changing a checkbox's title with [OBJECT SET TITLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-title) returned a width of 0 instead of the correct value.

Navigating to a new form page while simultaneously deleting and rebuilding list box columns, combined with applying [LISTBOX SET AUTO ROW HEIGHT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-set-auto-row-height) after [LISTBOX SET PROPERTY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-set-property)(*; ...; lk auto row height; lk yes), caused 4D to crash unexpectedly. The crash did not occur when adding columns to an empty list box or when auto row height was already enabled beforehand.
The help tip shown when hovering over component methods such as `SVG_Export_to_picture` was rendered incorrectly, displaying raw HTML `<span>` markup instead of the intended styled text.
On macOS, the help tip displayed for an entity attribute contained an extra, unwanted blank line.
On Windows, the 4D-Analyzer Visual Studio Code extension could not connect to 4D or 4D Server acting as a Language Server Protocol (LSP) host, producing unexpected errors instead.

On Windows, calling [System info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/system-info) was slow to return when an inaccessible network drive was present, making the application appear to freeze while it waited on the drive.

In 4D Write Pro's side panel, no value was shown in the "Horizontal size" (background width) dropdown after switching the background image display mode to "Contain" or "Cover", leaving the option field appearing blank.
Connecting a built (engined) v19 R8 client to a built v20 server over the QUIC network layer and triggering the automatic client upgrade could return the unexpected error -10091.

[WP SET ATTRIBUTES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-set-attributes) failed to update a 4D Write Pro attribute when the new value was numerically equivalent but expressed in a different unit — for example, changing 20mm to 2cm left the displayed value unchanged.
An ORDA query combining multiple `IN` operators joined with `OR` could crash the application (or return null) whenever one of the `IN` collections was empty.

In binary databases, the "move" dialog shown when dragging and dropping forms or methods between design environments no longer let users sort its list by clicking the column headers — clicking had no effect.
The interpreter raised a syntax error when a collection literal, such as `[1;2]`, was used as one of the results of a ternary expression, e.g. `False ? [1;2] : 3`.

If a client running stored procedures was put to sleep and its user was dropped from the Server Administration window, resuming and reconnecting that client resulted in a duplicate user connection instead of a clean reconnection.
In compiled mode, using an object literal returned from a [Formula](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/formula) object raised an error, whereas the equivalent worked fine in interpreted mode.

Calling the collection-return variant of [FORM GET PROPERTIES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-get-properties) unexpectedly cleared the currently selected row(s) in a list box on the form.

Launching the Quick Report editor from the User mode menu broke print preview: on macOS the job was sent straight to the printer, and on Windows a Save-As dialog appeared instead of a preview. Opening the Quick Report editor programmatically via command did not have this problem.

Single-clicking a formula inserted into a 4D Write Pro document failed to display or allow editing of the formula in the toolbar; double-clicking worked correctly. The behavior was subsequently clarified so the formula toolbar only appears when the selection is non-empty and actually contains a formula, not merely when the cursor is placed just before one.
The offset returned by `filehandle.readText()` after reading up to a stop character was positioned before the stop character instead of after it, as documented.
Calling [Monitored activity](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/monitored-activity) (Get Monitored Activity) simultaneously from several preemptive processes could crash the application.
In binary-mode Picture Libraries on macOS, an image ID of four or more digits had its display truncated with an ellipsis instead of showing the full number.
On macOS, the title text of rounded-corner bevel buttons was not drawn at all.

The value returned by [GET PRINTABLE AREA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-printable-area) — specifically the height — changed between v19.x and v20, producing different layout results. As a workaround pending the fix, calling [SET PRINTABLE MARGIN](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-printable-margin)(-1;-1;-1;-1) before printing restores the expected behavior.

Starting in v20.0, [GET TEXT KEYWORDS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-text-keywords) mis-tokenized text using "@" as a word separator; this was traced to a regression in ICU 72.1 and is fixed by the updated ICU 73.2 library bundled in v20.1. Indexes built before the update are automatically rebuilt.

In binary databases, if the first connected 4D Remote client was joined by a second client that created a new project method outside the "Top level" Explorer folder, the first client could crash — provided it did not itself have the Explorer window open in design mode.
The syntax checker failed on code comparing a pointer to a date field or variable without parentheses on the right-hand operand, such as `If ($ptr=->$date)`, incorrectly reporting a syntax error.

An ORDA query against a calculated attribute reached through a relation, combined with three or more `OR`-joined operators, returned no results instead of the correct matches — a bug similar to ACI0104049.
Rapidly deleting watch expressions in the debugger could crash the application.

When a process variable name began with a digit (e.g. `1ECostBasis`), the `+` or `-` operator immediately following it — and everything after — was unexpectedly absorbed into the variable name during tokenization instead of being parsed as an operator, so the operation never executed and the variable remained undefined. This occurred because `1e` looks like an exponent prefix, even though such names should never have been legal in the first place; older versions had tolerated them.
Passing a value returned from a plugin (e.g. via `AL_GetColumnTextProperty`) to [APPEND TO ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/append-to-array) could crash the application.

Using `copyTo()` to extract a folder (with an extension in its name, e.g. "folder.ext") from inside a `4D.ZipArchive` object dropped the extension from the resulting folder name, unlike extracting the whole archive. Passing `folder.fullName` as the second parameter of `copyTo()` works around the issue.
In binary-mode Picture Libraries, clicking the column headers no longer sorted images by ID or by name.
In binary databases, 3D buttons were not localized correctly: their titles displayed the raw XLIFF identifier instead of the resolved, translated text.
3D buttons displayed their icon slightly misaligned, shifted too far to the right.
On Windows, a group box's title text could be clipped and not fully displayed in some cases, apparently depending on the font, font size, text content, and whether an external monitor was in use.
In some 4D Write Pro dialogs (such as its error dialogs), the Cancel button appeared on the left side instead of the conventional right side.
On macOS, tabbing out of a focusable list box object into a text field did not restore the Japanese input method (IME) mode, forcing users to re-enable it manually.
When the print settings limited the number of pages printed, the final page was handled incorrectly and did not output as expected.
[OBJECT GET BEST SIZE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-best-size) failed to return the correct optimal width for a button that had a popup menu attached to it.

In an array-based list box with automatic row height enabled and driven by a control array, hiding rows via the control array left a blank empty area at the bottom of the list box instead of collapsing properly.

The formula (written in object notation) attached to an anchored image placed in front of text in a 4D Write Pro document could not be edited via the Write Pro tool. Fixing this also extended the syntax of [Formula from string](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/formula-from-string), allowing a component to evaluate a formula in the context of the host database.

In the Export dialog, loading a *.4SI* configuration file left the upper-right tab control showing stale content — for example, the Format tab's dropdown menu remained visible even though the File tab appeared selected.

In 4D Server or standalone (single-user) mode, changing the default user settings from the Project mode Structure Settings did not persist the change to *directory.json*; the equivalent operation from a client worked correctly.

Writing a boolean database field right after a function call combined with a short-circuit operator triggered a syntax error, because the leading part of the field reference was being misinterpreted as a collection rather than a table name.
In 4D NetKit's Microsoft Graph API integration, the `isLastPage` attribute was not set correctly on the final message when retrieving mail, so callers could not reliably detect the end of pagination.

Repeatedly calling [VP PASTE FROM OBJECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-paste-from-object) in a loop caused 4D View Pro to consume excessive amounts of memory; [VP MOVE CELLS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-move-cells) suffered from the same issue. The fix now automatically flushes memory (equivalent to VP FLUSH) every 100 calls to limit the footprint.
[OBJECT SET FORMAT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-format) failed to update the title of a boolean field displayed on a form.
In the 4D NetKit component's Microsoft Graph API integration, retrieving email messages returned incorrect information.

On macOS, the *On Mouse Up* form event did not always fire for input objects on a non-frontmost window of type *Controller form window*; the total number of objects on the form and click speed seemed to influence whether it fired. The *On Clicked* event, by contrast, always fired reliably.
On macOS, using [ERASE WINDOW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/erase-window) turned subsequently drawn text from black to a light gray, appearing greyed-out instead of the correct color.

Updating a 3D button's title via [OBJECT SET FORMAT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-format) when the title was set through an XLIFF resource caused the raw XLIFF resource name to display instead of the resolved localized text.
In Project mode only, the text alignment property configured on an input form object was not reflected in the Form Editor's display, even though it applied correctly at runtime.

In a collection-type list box, selecting a row via [LISTBOX SELECT ROWS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/listbox-select-rows) and then immediately using arrow keys moved the selection relative to whatever row was selected before the command ran, rather than from the newly selected row.
Converting a binary form to Project mode incorrectly changed a boolean field configured to display as a radio button into a checkbox instead.

Setting the `headers` property of an `HTTPRequest` class instance with a collection value did not work correctly for cookie headers: the `Cookie` header's values should be joined with "; " while other headers should be joined with ", ", but this distinction was not honored.
On Windows, printing an XPS or PDF preview showed the generic window/file title "test.xps" instead of the expected "preview.xps".
On macOS, moving a window containing text from a high-resolution Retina display to a standard-resolution display (or vice versa) resulted in the displayed font size becoming incorrect.

Using the [SET ASSERT ENABLED](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-assert-enabled)/[ASSERT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/assert) commands, or enabling the global debug log, could lead to memory corruption.

Sending an email via the SMTP transporter without a "From" address set on the mail object caused `$transporter.send($mail)` to fail with a generic "failed to send message" error rather than a more specific one.
In Project mode, help tips configured for fields in the Structure editor no longer displayed when the field was shown at runtime on a form.

Calling `PA_ExecuteCommandByID()` to invoke the `RESOLVE POINTER` command with a pointer-type `PA_Variable` returned a new `PA_Variable` instance instead of the original one as it did in earlier versions, unexpectedly modifying pointer parameters passed to the plugin.

In a Japanese environment, a runtime error inside the [On Web Connection database method](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/on-web-connection-database-method) generated an error page in the wrong text encoding, producing an XML parse error in the browser and corrupted Japanese characters.
Displaying SVG images in list box cells caused a memory build-up while scrolling, which could eventually crash the application.
In 4D Write Pro's side widget, clicking the "Insert image formula" menu item on the "Pictures and text boxes" tab threw an error instead of inserting the formula.
