Calling [Process activity](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/process-activity) (Get process activity) while a new process was being launched to perform an HTTP request could crash the application.
The Data Explorer's row display became visually broken when field values contained specific characters such as "<" or ">", which were not properly escaped for display.

With "Encrypt Client-Server Communications" enabled, if a TLS connection close was postponed, the 4D Remote client could attempt to close the TLS connection after its underlying socket had already been closed, leading to memory corruption and possible disconnection errors — a side effect of the fix for ACI0103972.

Auto-complete suggestions no longer prioritized table names at the top of the list, as they had in 4D v19.x — for example, when typing parameters for commands like [QUERY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query) or [ORDER BY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/order-by) that expect a table, matching table names should rank first even without a leading "[" bracket.
In 4D Write Pro, selecting text that spanned regions with differing units or settings while the sidebar's background tab was displayed threw an unexpected error.
In 4D Write Pro's sidebar interface, copying and pasting a document's background failed with an error.

In Project mode, calling [WA OPEN WEB INSPECTOR](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wa-open-web-inspector) while a button (rather than the web area itself) had focus on a form with an `entryOrder` set could crash the application.
`4D.FileHandle`'s offset property incorrectly started counting from 1 instead of 0, the expected zero-based position.
Calling `4D.FileHandle.readText()` without specifying an offset started reading from the beginning of the file rather than from the handle's current offset position.
Calling `4D.FileHandle.readBlob()` to read beyond the end of the file returned `undefined` instead of throwing an appropriate error.
Calling `4D.FileHandle.readBlob()` with an invalid offset returned `undefined` instead of a proper error.
Calling `4D.FileHandle.readText()` to read beyond the end of the file returned `undefined` instead of an appropriate error result.
[Application info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/application-info) (Get application info) did not always return the correct remote debugger session ID.
Accessing a picture array through the 4D Plugin SDK entry points could cause a memory access violation, making the application quit unexpectedly.

An input object whose data source was a picture-type attribute could initialize as a plain text input in some cases, meaning it behaved like a text field (with a text-editing mouse cursor) and refused to accept a picture dropped onto it.
Printing a form containing an object bound to a calculated attribute via [Print form](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-form) crashed the application.

Calling [VP IMPORT FROM OBJECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-import-from-object) caused a memory leak in 4D View Pro, with the underlying CefProcessHandler process able to consume more than 15GB of RAM. This was a bug in the bundled SpreadJS 16.0.x library, fixed by upgrading to SpreadJS 16.2.4.
In Project mode, list box columns configured with a default width were not rendered exactly as they would appear at runtime (not WYSIWYG) in the Form Editor.

The confirmation checkbox shown in the design-mode "rename variable" dialog (for non-local variables) displayed the placeholder label "-- set by C code --" instead of the intended text explaining it renames the variable across the whole database.
When a toolbar button's icon and text were large enough to fill the whole button width, the popup-menu indicator arrow attached to that button was drawn truncated/clipped.

Complex ORDA queries combining relation attributes with the `OR` operator suffered from poor query-plan optimization, causing severe and abnormal slowdowns — for example, a query that should complete in 0.001 seconds could take 3 seconds instead.
Reading a string variable through the 4D Plugin SDK could trigger memory corruption, potentially leading to a crash.
Assigning the result of a ternary expression (e.g. `$a:=true ? 1 : 2`) to an undeclared variable caused a compiler error — a side effect introduced by the fix for ACI0103960.

When using the QUIC network layer, the Server Administration window's Application Server page incorrectly displayed TLS as inactive, even though QUIC connections are always encrypted with TLS and should show as active.

Using [HTTP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) with the keep-alive option enabled, a response returning HTTP status 204 (No Content) with an empty body could take nearly 2 minutes to complete, unless an intermediary such as a proxy automatically added a `Content-Length` header.

In a list box (entity selection or collection-based) with "automatic row height" enabled and a large volume of data, scrolling became effectively unusable — a side effect introduced by the fix for ACI0103946.

The code editor's syntax error indicators stopped refreshing correctly: after fixing a syntax problem and re-running the syntax check, the error/warning icon next to the line remained visible instead of disappearing promptly.

A crash could occur when several processes finished handling web requests at the same time that another process called [Process activity](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/process-activity) (Get process activity).
The blue background highlighting the currently selected tab in the Toolbox dialog was not drawn (the User and Group tabs were unaffected).
Calling `SET BLOB CACHE PRIORITY` from a Startup method while indexing was taking place during database launch (e.g. via *On Server Startup*) could crash the application.

In interpreted mode, executing [SET DATABASE PARAMETER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-parameter) with options such as *Max concurrent Web processes* incorrectly forced the web server's processes to run on preemptive threads even in interpreted mode; restarting the web server, or configuring the option via [WEB SET OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-set-option) or database settings instead, avoided the issue.
`FileHandle.readLine()` skipped the file's first line — a side effect introduced when the FileHandle offset convention was changed to start at 0.

If a process running a print job was aborted or stopped from the debugger, 4D failed to clear its internal "open printing job" flag, so a subsequent attempt by any other process to print (opened via [OPEN PRINTING JOB](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-printing-job)) could deadlock the Print Manager.

On Windows, if the Explorer window was left maximized when design mode was restarted, its layout became broken — the window itself remained maximized, but its contents no longer matched the window size.

In client/server applications on macOS using the legacy network layer, setting a breakpoint in the `On Startup` method and then switching a client into design mode could open an empty method editor window and deadlock. Because code-completion and diagnostic logging rely on preemptive processes not supported by the legacy network layer, the fix disables some code-completion features (inter-process variables and undefined object member functions) and diagnostics when that legacy layer is in use.
In 4D View Pro, the `editChange` event/action was not triggered when moving focus between cells by pressing Tab, unlike other ways of committing an edit.
In 4D View Pro, importing a document into a View Pro area was slow when the document contained cell formatters using the "@" character.
In 4D View Pro, the `SUBSTITUTE` spreadsheet formula returned a `#VALUE!` error when its second argument referenced a blank cell instead of handling it gracefully.

Converting an empty journal (log file) with [LOG FILE TO JSON](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/log-file-to-json) produced invalid JSON — the output was the truncated text "[" instead of the empty array "[]".

In the method editor, the help tip shown when hovering over an array whose size was declared using `Size of array` together with an array of a different type displayed the wrong array type in the tip.

On Windows, the default focused/selected button in the [CONFIRM](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/confirm) dialog changed between v19 and v20: the Cancel button received default focus instead of the expected button.
On Windows, text displayed by [CONFIRM](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/confirm) or [ALERT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/alert) could be truncated, a problem related to ACI0104289.

Enabling the *Current process* debug log without also setting bit 4 (value 16) crashed the application whenever a plugin command was subsequently called; enabling debug logging for all processes first avoided the crash.
The `SVG_New_text` command failed to apply the requested text style to the generated SVG text.
`4D.Filehandle.readLine()` returned an empty string instead of reading through to the end of a file that contained no line breaks.

On Apple Silicon, using the Devart ODBC Driver and calling `SQL LOGIN`/`SQL LOGOUT` more than once caused the application to crash. A workaround installs ODBC error handling before certain calls (e.g. division by zero) to catch specific failures, but the root cause — the driver throwing exceptions instead of returning errors — could not be fully resolved for every case.
From build 288506 onward, changing a value in the Shortcuts section of the Preferences dialog produced an unexpected error.
Calling `File.open("write")` returned a `4D.FileHandle` whose `eof` property was set to `True`, when it should have been `False` for a freshly opened file for writing.

Querying with a `context` option through `Open Datastore` from a 4D v20 client against a 4D v19 server could crash the server, since v19 cannot parse the v20 context format. The fix replaces the crash with a proper "query cannot be parsed" error.

[PROCESS 4D TAGS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/process-4d-tags) generated an extra, unexpected ">" character when a space was typed after the condition expression of a `#4DIF` tag — apparently because the length of the `-->` closing sequence was hardcoded.

Defining a computed attribute on the `options` object passed to the `4D.SystemWorker` constructor for a user class caused error -10754 ("Context language missing...") because the required language context was not available when the attribute was evaluated.
On macOS only, a window of type *Movable form dialog box* was missing its close button in the title bar whenever the form had a fixed width and height.
Breakpoints inside a method invoked from a formula embedded in a 4D Write Pro document were ignored during execution; the debugger only opened after the method had already finished running.
In client/server mode, an Administrator could not change a user's group membership — the checkboxes for toggling group membership in the user settings could not be toggled.
Assigning a dereferenced pointer to an array element into an entity attribute raised a "cannot make an assignment with those types" compilation/syntax error instead of succeeding.

`FileHandle.readText()` did not strip the byte order mark (BOM) when reading a UTF-8 text file, which then caused [JSON Parse](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/json-parse) to fail on the resulting string.

On Windows, in the method editor, typing Japanese text containing a half-width katakana dakuten (voiced sound mark) caused the cursor position to become inconsistent, so that deleting a given character actually deleted a different, unrelated character.
The function parameter hint normally shown at the bottom status bar of the code editor was missing when the cursor was placed inside a member function's parameter list.

When iterating a collection with `For each`, a `Null` element immediately following a collection- or object-type member incorrectly reported its [Value type](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/value-type) as `Is collection (42)` or `Is object (38)` (matching the preceding member) instead of `Is null (255)`. The fix requires the iterator variable to be explicitly declared for `Value type` to report correctly in interpreted mode: an undeclared iterator starts untyped and takes on the type of whatever is first assigned to it, and in interpreted mode an assignment tries to preserve the existing type of an already-typed variable, including when the new value is [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null). In compiled mode, undeclared iterators are Variant-typed, and the same type-preserving assignment behavior previously applied even to Variants; after the fix, a variable explicitly declared as Variant now correctly keeps `Null` as `Null`.
Calling ORDA's `entity.clone()` unexpectedly placed a lock on the original entity being cloned.

In compiled mode, an *ak msc* action installed via [SET HELP MENU](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-help-menu) and triggered from the server-side help menu returned a runtime error when executed through [INVOKE ACTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/invoke-action), because the `4D_Server_Interface` worker responsible for it runs on a preemptive process.
For a list box placed in a subform, the "selected elements" property was not refreshed/updated after the list box was reloaded.

Attempting to open a project already open under a Feature Release build simultaneously in an LTS build displayed a "currently being read" message and then crashed the application instead of simply blocking the second open.
In the Czech-localized edition, 4D displayed errors on startup due to malformed JSON in the localization settings.
The label editor did not allow setting a text background color for labels.

Running [Compile project](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/compile-project) (via "path to current file.project" or an external project file) on a project that defined no classes reported `entity.save()` as a syntax error while still returning a compilation success and a misleading message, even though `Compile Project()` itself completed properly.

On Windows in compiled mode, [PRINT LABEL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-label) unexpectedly printed only a single label per page — the problem only occurred on high-resolution (HiDPI) displays.
Sorting by a property path that combined both a relation attribute and an object attribute crashed the application — a side effect introduced by the fix for ACI0097511.

In 4D View Pro, manually assigning a "Currency" format via the format dialog in French or German placed the thousands/decimal separators in the wrong position, e.g. producing "495,00. €" with a stray dot after the last zero; French and German conventions require comma as decimal separator and period as thousands separator.

When two 4D instances were launched on the same machine, WebAdmin automatically increments its port (from the defaults of 7080/7443) to avoid conflicts, but the WebServer property was not updated dynamically, so calling `DataExplorer` from design mode always used the original default port URL instead of the actual incremented one.
On Windows, when the system display scaling option was changed, picture pop-up menus rendered too small on high-DPI monitors, making their contents hard to read or click.

A `4D.WebSocket` server object at a given path could be unexpectedly reset after several reset attempts: if an object at that path already existed and its `terminated` property was not true, 4D returned an error for the new object but still cleared the existing WebSocket object as a side effect, terminating a server that should have kept running.

[Create deployment license](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-deployment-license) incorrectly succeeded and produced a built OEM server deployment license even when the supplied `buildLicense` was a standard (non-OEM) license; the command should instead have rejected the request with an error.

Qodly web pages served by an engined (built) server or a compiled database unexpectedly returned HTTP error #404 instead of rendering; building with `PackProject` set to true and packaging the project folder as a `.4DZ` file avoided the problem.

On Windows, 4D Write Pro could crash when opening HTML content containing a very large number (over roughly 1,000 levels) of nested `<div>` elements. The fix prevents the crash, though nesting beyond 100 levels — already discouraged — is now simply ignored rather than causing instability.

In a list box column bound to a choice list with multi-style formatting, entering and then leaving a cell caused the raw source markup (literal `<span>` tags) to be displayed instead of the styled text.
The method editor raised an unexpected syntax error when an object literal contained a nested collection literal in one of its property values, for example `$test:={addLabelIds: [$toto.id]}`.

Splitting an object literal across multiple lines with the line-continuation backslash caused the leading property name to be mistakenly tokenized as a process variable, triggering a syntax error at the property-name level; this was a side effect of the fix for ACI0103903.

While typing Japanese text with an IME, moving the cursor into the middle of the text and pressing Delete or Backspace to remove the as-yet-unconverted (uncommitted) segment also incorrectly deleted the characters that followed it.

Converting a list form created by the Form Wizard from binary to Project mode could cause a splitter's "Pusher" property (which moves subsequent objects) to be lost, because the invisible button driving splitter behavior was not converted correctly; standard splitter objects were unaffected. The fix applies only to forms converted after the update — already-converted forms are not corrected retroactively.
In a 4D Write Pro document, breaks other than paragraph and line breaks could not be removed when they were located at the very end of the document.
The `4D.HTTPRequest` class leaked object-type memory, causing unexpected memory growth over repeated use.

On Windows, the font list shown in the property list of the Form/Structure editor could display the same font name twice — for example Yu Gothic appeared duplicated. The fix ensures both Yu Gothic Medium and Yu Gothic are listed as distinct, correctly named entries.

4D could freeze when a query using a composite index was executed shortly after [QUIT 4D](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/quit-4d) had already been called, on tables where such an index was defined.

[OBJECT SET ENTERABLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-enterable) no longer properly disabled a check box form object: after calling the command, the check box's appearance did not change to reflect its disabled state and it could still be clicked, unlike in earlier versions.

`dataClass.query()` returned incorrect results when the query string ended with a comparison against [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null); this was a side effect of the fix for ACI0104235, and reordering the criteria so the null comparison was not last avoided the problem.

On Windows, maximizing a window containing a subform whose form had both maximum-width and maximum-height constraints could apply the wrong value: the subform's maximum height was mistakenly used for its maximum width.

Clicking a window's native Maximize button and then calling the [MAXIMIZE WINDOW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/maximize-window) command could produce an incorrect maximized layout instead of properly resizing the window.

In Client/Server, [SET AUTOMATIC RELATIONS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-automatic-relations) and [GET AUTOMATIC RELATIONS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-automatic-relations) did not stay properly synchronized between client and server: a client-side call to set the mode caused the server's internal flag to be updated too, so a subsequent server-side get/set of automatic relations returned unreliable results. Since client-side and server-side twin-process automatic relations are meant to be independent, the fix isolates them again, but requires updating both client and server together — updating only the server has no effect, and updating only the client may cause a modest performance cost on databases with many tables and relations.

On Windows, in a multi-monitor setup, minimizing a maximized SDI-mode window and then restoring it from the taskbar icon could cause the window to reappear on the wrong monitor instead of its original display.
On Windows, when the display scaling was set above 100%, images embedded in SVG graphics appeared distorted, while SVG text rendered correctly.
In compiled mode, the `OT GetPointer` command from the third-party ObjectTools plugin (v5.1r1) returned an incorrect pointer; this was a side effect of the fix for ACI0104030.

[Create deployment license](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-deployment-license) incorrectly succeeded for a built OEM server even when the supplied `buildLicense` was an OEM license bearing a time-bomb expiration, which should have been rejected.
Copying and pasting an empty spreadsheet-style cell could leave an unexpected stray space character in the destination cell instead of leaving it truly empty.

In compiled mode, a pointer to a local array in the host database, when passed to a component method, could lose its reference after the process that created it had been started and killed roughly several hundred million times, eventually producing a runtime pointer-usage error. The fix changes dereferencing so that a pointer to a variable is first resolved in the current process's component language execution context before falling back to another process's context.
On Windows, modal form dialog boxes opened while the 4D application was minimized could appear off-screen instead of within the visible display area.
Join queries built from at least three levels of nested "AND"/"OR" conditions could produce an invalid internal query path, leading to incorrect results.
Assigning a file path value directly to a Picture or BLOB field triggered an unexpected compilation error.

The legacy "Mandatory" field attribute — which has no equivalent in Project mode and was removed from the Structure editor's property list there — was still silently carried over into the `.4DCatalog` file when converting a binary structure to Project mode, without the conversion log producing any warning or error. Afterward, saving the affected field as empty triggered a database error. The fix now logs a clear conversion warning recommending the field instead use "Reject NULL value input" or "Map NULL values to blank values".

On a machine with multiple network cards, if the web server's fixed listening IP address was configured with a domain name, connecting over `https` returned HTTP status 409; connecting over plain `http` worked correctly.

Using 4D Remote, running an ORDA request with `orderBy()` on a relation attribute raised errors 1804 and 1500 when the related entity's primary key value contained a slash (`/`) character; the same issue reproduced against a remote datastore.
On Windows and Intel-based Mac, 4D could crash when displaying a list box whose column properties were computed via a formula referencing a class member function.
Converting a form to Project mode caused button titles that were originally center-aligned to become right-aligned instead.

Calling [FILTER KEYSTROKE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/filter-keystroke) with an empty string (`""`) from the *On Before Keystroke* event of a selection-based list box cell erased the cell's existing content instead of simply filtering new keystrokes.

When multiple local variables and their parameter positions were declared together in one `var` statement, the syntax checker's warning about local variable re-declaration displayed the wrong variable or parameter name.
On macOS, using the `ServerEmbedsProjectDirectoryFile` build key caused the resulting `directory.json` file to be copied into the built application as a hidden file, making it invisible in Finder.

On macOS, renaming a file or folder located on a shared network volume via `File.rename()` or `Folder.rename()` failed with a POSIX "Operation not supported" error, even though the same rename succeeded from the Terminal's `mv` command, ruling out a permissions issue. 4D internally calls `renamex_np`; the fix retries the rename without the exclusive-renaming flag when error 45 (option not supported by network share) is returned.

After using [CREATE INDEX](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-index) to update an index, the change was reflected in the Structure editor but the corresponding SQL system tables were not updated until the project was restarted.

In the 4D Write Pro interface, choosing a font from the font drop-down list did not stick: right after applying the change, the pop-up's displayed selection reverted to showing the previous font name.

Pressing Escape while editing a field title in [QR REPORT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/qr-report) Quick Report output returned an unexpected error 9850, caused by an event-cycle issue when the form was unloaded before a list box cell edit had been validated; standard input areas were unaffected.
In compiled mode, accessing objects or collections through [Storage](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/storage) concurrently from different preemptive web processes could trigger a crash.
On Windows, when a pop-up/drop-down menu was set to be both focusable and tabbable, the arrow keys could select its divider line ("-") item as if it were a normal, selectable entry.

In the Server Administration window's SQL Server tab, the status could show as "Started" even when the "launch on startup" setting was disabled and the SQL server had not actually started, making it appear reachable when it was not.

In a list box, after applying a text style to the first character of a cell's styled content via the contextual menu, selecting the entire cell with Select All extended that style to the whole cell content instead of leaving the rest as-is.

The activity log exported from the Maintenance and Security Center (MSC) used a malformed date format — for example rendering `2023-12-21` as something like `12--0021` — making the date information unusable.
In a 4D Write Pro document containing at least one anchored picture and a text box, programmatically deleting the text box caused the anchored picture's selection to be lost.

In Intel compiled mode, passing a BLOB index exactly equal to the BLOB's size (i.e., one byte past its valid range, as reported by [BLOB size](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/blob-size)) bypassed range checking instead of raising an "out of bounds" error, risking a buffer overflow and application crash; the ARM compiler was unaffected.

On Windows, in an array-type list box column with an associated choice list, clicking a value in the pop-up menu when it was displayed outside the bounds of the form window failed to assign the selected value into the target cell.
In Project mode on Mac, in Dark Mode, the Toolbox dialog's Help tips text appeared as white text on a bright yellow background, making it nearly unreadable.

`NetKit.GoogleMailIdList.getMailIds()` incorrectly returned [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) when calling `google.mail.getMails()` with the `raw` format and only a single matching element; the `minimal` format was unaffected.

In the method editor, double-clicking a class name to highlight/select it and then choosing "Goto Definition" from the menu did not work, whereas placing the caret in the class name without selecting it, or selecting it via mouse drag or keyboard, worked fine.
When a table's entity class defined computed attributes, clicking the List Box Builder button in the Form editor produced an error instead of building the list box.
If a client-side process that was actively communicating with the server was terminated, the entire 4D Remote connection could be disconnected instead of only that process ending.
In Client/Server, 4D could crash in the method editor while typing certain 4D command names and triggering the type-ahead/autocomplete suggestion feature; this did not reproduce in every structure.
[Compile project](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/compile-project) failed for an external (component) project when it contained a method flagged for publication as a Web Service.
Compiling a project with the "Generate syntax file for code completion when compiled" option enabled, on a database containing no classes at all, caused 4D to crash.
On macOS, the [MESSAGE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/message) command's dialog was not adapted for Dark Mode, breaking the visual consistency of the interface.

Record creation performance degraded sharply as the data file grew, due to inefficient free-space lookup: a small data file could sustain roughly 110,000 record creations in 10 seconds, but this dropped to about 42,000 at 100 GB and to only about 6,000 at 1.1 TB.

Chaining a member function call that returns an entity directly with object-notation attribute-path access (without first storing the entity in a local variable) triggered a syntax-check compiler error.

In an entity-selection list box with "Automatic row height" enabled, changing the underlying entity selection did not immediately re-render rows at the correct height; resizing the window forced a redraw that then displayed the correct heights.

[Open datastore](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-datastore) could not authenticate using a 4D Server user name and password, because the *On REST Authentication* database method could not validate the received password hash. This traces back to 4D 19 R3, where `directory.json` began using bcrypt-hashed passwords. The fix sends the password unhashed over the wire (strongly recommending the connection's `tls` option be set to true) so *On REST Authentication* can call [Validate password](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/validate-password); alternatively, setting the connection's `passwordAlgorithm` property to `4d-rest-digest` restores the older MD5-style hash for compatibility with existing *On REST Authentication* code. This `passwordAlgorithm` property should be omitted if REST access is instead managed via Structure Settings' users and groups rather than a custom *On REST Authentication* method.

In the Server Administration window's Processes page, holding Shift while dragging the splitter vertically to move/resize a column triggered an internal error ("MONI_PROCESS_SetInterface line 20: error -10518, Assert failed ...").
The 4D View Pro Formula Editor Panel feature did not work at all, appearing as an empty pane with no functionality.

In the Structure editor's Link inspector (Project mode), after enabling "Automatic wildcard support" on a relation and choosing a Wildcard field, deselecting the relation and reselecting it failed to show the previously chosen field in the inspector, even though the underlying catalog had been updated correctly.
Queries combining `&&`/`||` operators with relation-based search criteria could fail to evaluate the relation conditions at all, returning incorrect results; this worked correctly in 4D v20.1.

[METHOD GET PATHS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/method-get-paths) could crash the application when running in Application mode if certain objects, such as list box headers or footers, had an empty name.
On Windows, a form window containing only a web area required two clicks on its title bar to come to the foreground when the "Use Embedded Web Rendering Engine" option was active.

In a 4D Write Pro area, validating Japanese text typed via IME on a line ending in a soft break (rather than a paragraph break) caused the following styled text to be torn apart into single characters, one per line — reproducible for example by pasting rich text from the method editor, or by creating a soft-break-only empty line and typing Japanese there.

Adding the `//%W-550.10` comment directive to a compiler (project) method did not suppress the "variable redefinition" warning application-wide as expected; the comment had to be added individually to each affected method instead.

A client without the *Client Web Application Expansion* license could not use NetKit's local [WEB Server](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-server) functionality, whereas this worked correctly on 4D 20 LTS.

Using [MAXIMIZE WINDOW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/maximize-window) on a window whose form had both maximum-width and maximum-height constraints left the interface in an inconsistent state after resizing.

Running an indexed query could unexpectedly cause the 4D Server to shut down abruptly. The root cause was in how internal connection worker processes were tracked: if the internal worker list became inconsistent, the theoretical worker limit of 32,767 could be reached, causing new connections to reuse busy workers. If such a worker repeatedly suspended and resumed its database context due to idle timeouts, two connections could end up running queries on the same database context simultaneously, leading to a crash.

In Design mode, searching for unused local variables incorrectly flagged a class function parameter as unused when that parameter was used inline as part of an object literal declaration/initialization on the same line.

On Windows, calling the Plugin API function `PA_GetMainWindowsHWND` from a preemptive thread could crash the application. The crash itself is now avoided, but the API still must not be called from preemptive threads.

With a list box's "Automatic row height" property enabled, meta-info formula expressions were evaluated far more times than the number of visible rows, causing a dramatic performance slowdown, since off-screen rows were also being evaluated unnecessarily.
Calling `entity.save()` failed to accept [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) for a relation attribute's foreign-key field unless that field was also the primary key.
If any installed license had expired, the "Refresh" button in the License Manager became disabled and could not be clicked, preventing the user from refreshing license status at all.
Connecting via Qodly Studio no longer created a REST session, so the connection did not appear in the Administration window's "User" tab; this appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0104503.
Enabling "user authentication by domain server" (SSO) on the new network layer could cause a memory leak and eventually freeze 4D Remote clients; this was a side effect of the fix for ACI0103215.

When sending mail via [SMTP New transporter](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/smtp-new-transporter), setting or modifying standard headers such as `MIME-Version` or `Date` in the email object could result in both the user-supplied and the default header values being duplicated in the resulting MIME message; some mail clients mishandle duplicate headers, whereas only the custom header value should have been sent.

In the French localization, importing a spreadsheet into 4D View Pro caused the `CNUM` function to mishandle the decimal separator (a comma in French formatting); manually re-entering the value in the cell displayed it correctly.
Converting a form containing a Boolean field displayed as a radio button from binary to Project mode could produce a badly sized control whose title text was sometimes cut off and unreadable.

Placing two web areas on a form and calling [WA SET PAGE CONTENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wa-set-page-content) to display an empty page on one of them could crash the application; setting the URL to `about:blank`, or switching either area to the system web area, avoided the crash.

On Windows, printing with Adobe Acrobat Pro set as the current printer could crash 4D. The cause was on the driver side: without an explicit print job name, `PSCRIPT5.DLL` suffered a stack overrun. Managing the print job explicitly with [OPEN PRINTING JOB](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-printing-job), or setting a PDF file name via the Spooler Document Name option of [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option), avoids the crash by ensuring a print session name is set; 4D now recommends always setting a spooler document name when printing to PDF.

Renaming a local variable via the method editor's contextual menu could silently fail to update a multi-line `#DECLARE` statement when a line break was inserted between the parameters and the return type — for example when the closing parenthesis was not immediately followed by the arrow. Inserting the line break after the closing parenthesis instead avoided the problem.

Running [ORDER BY FORMULA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/order-by-formula) against a database that had been compiled as a component via `Compile project(projectFile)` (i.e., specifying another project's path) raised an error; compiling the current project directly with [Compile project](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/compile-project), or using the Design mode compiler, worked correctly.

When a table (row) in a 4D Write Pro document spanned multiple printed pages, text in the final page's row or cell could be truncated in the display or printout — even though copying the full text still worked, indicating a rendering issue. This was most visible with the legacy print layer but also reproduced with the standard layer; note that calling [WP PRINT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-print) after starting a print job under the legacy print layer is unsupported, since Write Pro rendering is designed for the standard print layer (Direct2D on Windows).

Using NetKit's OAuth2 support with Office 365 via JMAP, attempting to mark a message as read or unread failed with an error when the OAuth object was instantiated with the JMAP or MIME mail format; the Microsoft mail format worked correctly, since it is the only format that natively supports updating messages. The fix temporarily converts message formats as needed to support the operation.
On macOS, the "Manage Custom Sizes..." paper-size feature had no effect when printing a 4D Write Pro document; custom paper sizes were not actually applied.

Editing a collection value directly in the debugger pane mishandled certain literals: an empty string (`""`) was deleted entirely, while string values like `"2"` or `"null"` were silently converted into a number `2` or [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null). The fix special-cases empty strings so they are preserved; other similar literal-quoting edge cases are planned to be addressed in a future version.

In Project mode, calling [OBJECT DUPLICATE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-duplicate) on a Boolean-backed form object (such as a radio button or check box using a Boolean field as its data source) had no effect at all, since Project mode has no distinct "Boolean field" form object type.

On Windows, when display scaling was set above 100%, tab control objects on a form stopped responding correctly to clicks. Enabling the compatibility option "Use DirectWrite for text rendering in forms" is recommended for proper high-DPI support; the fix makes tab controls clickable even without that option, at the cost of somewhat reduced text rendering quality.

Opening an updated structure file together with an older data file could cause the data file's "unique key" field setting to silently overwrite the structure catalog's own "unique" (no-duplicates) attribute, effectively discarding the intended structure-level setting even though the field was configured differently in the structure editor.

The `HTTPRequest` class automatically appended a `; encoding=utf8` charset parameter to the Content-Type header of outgoing requests even when none was specified, preventing calls to APIs (such as Claris FileMaker Server) that do not tolerate this extra header information.

On macOS, when the system locale was set to Belgian Dutch (`nl-be`), calling [String](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/string) with the format pattern `dd/MM/yyyy` — for example `String(!2023-11-27!; "dd/MM/yyyy")` — raised an error instead of formatting the date.

On macOS, `BEST OBJECT SIZE` (and the Form editor's "Automatic size" feature) could return an incorrect size for radio buttons and check boxes, because macOS renders these controls in Regular, Small, or Mini variants chosen by control height rather than font height, but the size calculation used the object's height instead of the title's font height to pick the variant — causing the computed width to fall a few pixels short and titles to be clipped.

With the default "Type the variables" compiler pass, compiling a ternary expression whose branches contained a string comparison operator (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `=`, `#`) failed, for example `$b:=False ? False : "cat"#"cat"`.
The server-side ORDA request log file (`ordaRequests_1.json`) omitted the client's IP address (`ipAddress` field) from its logged information.

Calling [OPEN ADMINISTRATION WINDOW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-administration-window) from the object method of a window opened in a [New process](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/new-process) started by the *On Server Startup* database event had no effect at all. The cause was that opening the Administration window depends on a menu command being processed, but a process started this way has no installed menu bar and its form has no associated menu bar either, so the command never reached the menu handler; palette-type windows worked because they fall back to the application process's main menu. The fix ensures the Administration window opens correctly in both cases.

[Create deployment license](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-deployment-license) incorrectly returned an error for legitimate standalone licenses (`4UUD` or `4UOE`); this was a side effect of the fix for ACI0104384.

In the Form editor's property list, setting the associated menu bar to "None" correctly stored an empty `menuBar` value in the `form.4DForm` file, but the property list's own label then displayed as an error (in red text) instead of showing a normal "None" state; this was purely a display glitch in the property list with no functional impact, and existing forms already set to "None" are not automatically corrected.

The Code Live Checker failed to flag a type mismatch when a variable's declaration and initial value assignment were combined on the same line, e.g. `var $val : Integer:="any string"`; splitting the declaration and assignment onto separate lines did trigger the expected error.
On macOS, when a 4D Remote client reconnected to the server after a crash, a new local resource cache folder was created instead of reusing the existing one.

Sending an email through NetKit with a `.bcc` property set silently failed to deliver the message to the BCC recipient; internally NetKit converts JMAP-style mail into MIME, and since mail servers strip BCC headers from MIME anyway, the `.bcc` property should not have been removed before that conversion in the first place.

In Client/Server, `entitySelection.orderByFormula()` raised an unexpected error when passed a project method or class function name as a plain string; first converting the string to a formula object with [Formula from string](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/formula-from-string) avoided the problem.

[Table fragmentation](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/table-fragmentation) returned incorrect values, which in turn also affected the fragmentation figures shown in the Maintenance and Security Center, since it relies on the same underlying command.

Setting the `.certificatesFolder` property to a `4D.Folder` object (rather than a plain path string) before using `4D.HTTPRequest` crashed the application; this was related to the broader memory-leak fix from ACI0104402.
In Client/Server, `EntitySelection.fromCollection()` created brand-new entities instead of updating the corresponding existing entities as expected.

Exporting a 4D Write Pro document containing page numbers to Word (.docx) format corrupted the page numbering: every page ended up displaying as "page 1 of 0" instead of its correct page number and total.

Creating a record with a BLOB field configured to be stored "Outside data file" and with "Map NULL values to blank values" enabled could corrupt the data: the Maintenance and Security Center's data validation detected an invalid field size for the affected field.
The `HTTPRequest` class did not support passing a collection as the body of a request.

In Client/Server, calling [Current user](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/current-user) from within an ORDA data store class function could return incorrect results, often always returning "Designer" as both the current user and alias, because the server-side DB4D process has no real concept of a current user.

On Apple Silicon, compiling code that used the `+=` operator to add a dereferenced pointer value into a field (for example `[Batch]Data1+=($varPtr->)`) caused the Apple Silicon (clang-based) compiler to raise an error; using a variable instead of a field, or replacing `+=` with separate `:=` and `+` operators, avoided the issue.
The Server Administration window's Processes page could return the same internal "MONI_PROCESS_SetInterface" error seen in ACI0104516 when Shift-clicking processes.

In the Quick Report editor, if the underlying saved report file had been deleted (while the report remained available in memory for re-display), closing the editor and clicking "Do Not Save" triggered an unexpected error -43 ("file not found"); the fix restores the report file as needed to avoid the error.

On macOS, the Close button of the 4D Preferences dialog window could stop working entirely, leaving the window impossible to dismiss that way; the fix instead grays out the Close button, requiring Escape or Cancel to close the dialog. This relates to the fix for ACI0104310, which had made fixed-size forms display working Close/Maximize/Minimize buttons even though [Open form window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-form-window)'s "Movable form dialog box (5)" documentation states such forms should not have them; correcting that also unintentionally added a Close button to [Open window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-window)'s equivalent "Movable dialog box (5)" type, which the documentation likewise says should have none. This fix restores [Open window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-window)'s older, documented behavior.
On Windows only, a pop-up window displayed over a web area did not close when the user clicked outside of it, unlike expected pop-up dismissal behavior.

On Apple Silicon only, compiling code that used certain process variable names — such as `param`, `Global`, `local`, `artyp`, `aratt`, `irgule`, or `ariab` — incorrectly triggered a "variable redefinition" error.

4D View Pro's [VP FLUSH COMMANDS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-flush-commands) and [VP SET FORMULA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-set-formula) commands suffered from a performance issue that made repeated or bulk formula updates slower than expected.

In the method editor, collapsing a `Case of` branch, then cutting or deleting a different branch, and undoing the action with Cmd/Ctrl+Z could leave the restored code corrupted instead of correctly reverting to its prior state.
Calling `Collection.equal()` on a collection containing objects with circular references crashed the application instead of returning a comparison result or a controlled error.
Calling `IMAPTransporter.getBoxList()` (e.g. `$boxlist:=$mail.getBoxList($option)`) unexpectedly returned error #13 when the mail account used IMAP.

Setting the CSS `verticalAlign` attribute to control the vertical alignment of a list box column was not reflected in the Form editor's live preview, even though it rendered correctly when the form was actually run.

Starting a database project whose catalog collation locale was Japanese (`ja`) on a system with a non-Japanese language setting, while passing the `--create-data` command-line argument, raised error #126 — caused by the MeCab library not being found; the fix simply ignores this error in that scenario.
On macOS, when the system or application language was not set to Japanese, compiling a database containing a form method with a Japanese name for the Apple Silicon target failed.

Assigning to a BLOB field configured with storage "Outside data file" and a non-zero "Internal storage max size", using a value smaller than that maximum, caused the data not to be saved to the data file at all; this appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0104621.
When a connection to 4D Server was interrupted, an SSL-related error ("DoWrite: failed to write") could be logged repeatedly and indefinitely in the diagnostic log, accompanied by a memory leak.

On macOS, when a pop-up form window was opened from within a Modal form dialog box window, it became impossible to type numbers into a text field on that pop-up. Apple's window model normally disallows giving keyboard focus to an inactive window, but 4D's pop-up windows are designed to accept typed input (and thus focus) even while inactive; the fix works around Apple's restriction, and since the IME appears outside the (inactive) pop-up window while typing to avoid being hidden, using a floating window instead of a pop-up is recommended whenever text entry is required.

`collection.multiSort()` performed noticeably worse than converting the collection to arrays, sorting with array commands, and converting back; the multi-sort implementation was reworked, narrowing the worst-case performance gap between the two approaches to roughly 1.5x-2x.
Renaming a method and then immediately creating a new method reusing that method's previous name caused 4D to lock the newly created method, preventing further edits.
The 4D Helper Tool failed to install into background items because its internal bundle identifier had changed from `com.4D.Helper` to `com.Helper`.

After enabling a field's "no duplicates" (unique) attribute in the Structure editor and then opening an older, previously saved data file, the catalog file could end up out of sync with the Structure editor: the editor continued to display the catalog's setting at startup (unique enabled) while the catalog file itself was silently updated to match the data file's older setting (unique disabled). This is a related but distinct issue from ACI0104582.
In Qodly Studio, after saving a newly created entity, its picture attribute no longer appeared in the bound `image` component.
In a 4D Write Pro document with the decimal tab separator set to "None", numeric values no longer aligned at the position where the decimal point would normally fall.

On macOS, building an application with the "Intel only" target option still produced a Universal Binary executable containing both architectures instead of only Intel, as verified with the `file` or `lipo -archs` commands; the build process should strip unsupported architectures to avoid the risk of launching with the wrong one on the deployment machine.

Assigning a Picture field configured with storage "Outside data file" and a non-zero "Internal storage max size", using a value smaller than that maximum, resulted in a stored size of 0 bytes; although the journal appeared to record the data, it was no longer recognized as a valid `4DPICT` format picture.
[OBJECT SET THREE STATES CHECKBOX](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-three-states-checkbox) failed to actually change a check box's three-state property.
In the Data Explorer, an entity's detail form allowed arbitrary JavaScript to be executed via an injected `<script>` tag while editing, exposing an XSS-style vulnerability.

When a `var` declaration combined with initialization used a lowercase type name such as `4D.folder` or `4D.[File](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/file)` instead of the correctly capitalized `4D.Folder`/`4D.File`, the compiler failed to flag the mismatch, whereas a bare declaration without initialization did correctly warn about an unknown class; this was a side effect of the fix for ACI0104606.

Generating a Quick Report as HTML with a column formatted as a monetary amount (with a euro symbol) caused the total row's cells to be left-aligned instead of right-aligned; printed output was unaffected.

While a stored procedure was running, calling [Count users](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/count-users) returned the actual user count plus one extra user. The specification has since been reviewed and the documentation updated accordingly.
Right-clicking on the monitor graph in the Server Administration window no longer opened the contextual menu, making graph duration no longer adjustable in that graphic area.

Aborting a method with the debugger while running under Qodly Studio reported a network error as the termination reason instead of a normal response; the fix makes it return `{"result":null}` rather than an error.

In client/server mode, restarting the project several times while alternating between compiled and interpreted mode after compiling could cause 4D Remote (the client application) to unexpectedly quit.

Using [VP Convert to picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-to-picture) to convert part of a 4D View Pro spreadsheet to an SVG picture could render text with a different font than the View Pro area itself, because the CEF renderer and the picture engine use different fallback fonts. The fix uses Helvetica Neue as the fallback when Calibri is not installed.

In 4D Write Pro, decimal tab markers failed to align on trailing spaces because those trailing spaces were unexpectedly truncated; the correct behavior, matching Microsoft Word, is to preserve them for alignment purposes.
Calling [HTTP Get](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-get) repeatedly in a loop no longer reset the Content-Length header between requests, leaving a stale value from a previous call.
Pressing the Enter key on the numeric keypad (bottom-right) closed the Data Explorer window instead of being handled as a normal input.
In Qodly Studio/Qodly IDE, the $shared virtual folder was not served through the webAdmin port, a side effect of the ACI0104622 fix. Starting the webAdmin server at launch avoided the problem.
In client/server mode only, calling `SET AUTOMATIC RELATIONS(True; False)` no longer changed the automatic relations setting, an apparent side effect of the ACI0104414 fix.
Editing the catalog in the Qodly Studio model editor could cause permission settings to be lost, requiring a server restart to restore them; this appears to be a side effect of the ACI0104330 fix.

On Windows only, exporting a 4D Write Pro document to PDF could misplace umlauts built from Unicode combining characters, displaying them in the wrong position. Printing to PDF via the printer driver was unaffected. This was traced to a bug in the Hummus PDF-Writer library; the fix outputs precomposed umlaut characters to avoid the rendering issue.
Using [WP Import document](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-import-document) to import certain .docx files into a 4D Write Pro document could crash the application.
In client/server mode only, a checkbox bound to a related field on an input form could crash the application; this appears to be a side effect of the ACI0104414 fix.
In the method editor, right-clicking a class from the 4D ClassStore no longer showed "Show Documentation" in the contextual menu.

In a selection-type list box without a Highlight Set configured, deleting the currently selected records via the "deleteSubrecord" standard action, or via [INVOKE ACTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/invoke-action), silently failed to work.

When converting an email object to MIME with a specified messageId attribute, extra unwanted encoding was applied to the value in the resulting Message-ID header; the fix also stops wrapping the Message-ID header once it exceeds 76 characters.

Double-clicking fields in the sort editor to add them always placed the first and second selected fields on the first and second lines, regardless of the actual order in which they were clicked, producing an unnatural field order.
In client/server mode, an entity's time-type attribute was not sent correctly to 4D Server; the value ended up stored as one-thousandth of the intended number of seconds.
The [VP IMPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-import-document) command did not work correctly: when csvOptions were used, formulas in the imported spreadsheet were not preserved.

On Windows, the print orientation set via [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option) was not applied to pages after the first one when a report generated with [QR RUN](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/qr-run) was printed directly (PDF/XPS output was unaffected). Setting the paper orientation before starting the print job was a workaround; the fix corrects orientation handling when it changes mid-job under Direct2D printing.

Pressing Cmd/Ctrl+F while highlighted text was present in the method editor opened the search tool but left keyboard focus on the highlighted text instead of moving it to the search box; this was intentional behavior, but was changed after developer feedback on the 4D forum.
On Windows, [GET SERIAL PORT MAPPING](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-serial-port-mapping) could not return port numbers higher than COM9.

Entering text into a 4D Write Pro area and then opening and closing another dialog could trigger an error referencing "WP_Toolbar (4D WritePro Interface)" at line 143, apparently tied to closing a dialog containing the Write Pro toolbar.
An ORDA query combining a relation attribute path with a computed attribute failed to run onQuery and returned an empty entity selection instead of the expected results.
In Qodly Studio, the $shared folder could not be reached via the webAdmin port (default 7443) unless the web server was started at launch.

A stand-alone single-user built application could crash at startup when the "Launch Web Server at Startup" database setting was enabled, or when [WEB START SERVER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-start-server) was executed explicitly; build 100332 was unaffected.

While tracing a method that modifies parameter values, the debugger correctly updated the displayed value of named parameters, but sequentially numbered local parameter variables ($1, $2, etc.) kept showing their initial values instead of the updated ones.

In a list box with automatic row height bound to a collection or entity selection, editing a cell or selecting a row caused the scrollbar position to jump unexpectedly; array-type list boxes were unaffected. This appears to be a side effect of the ACI0104541 fix.

Instantiating recursive shared classes that reference each other as properties triggered an error in the constructor. The issue is not limited to shared classes — the same situation can occur with plain shared objects nesting each other via [New shared object](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/new-shared-object); the shared object implementation was revised as part of the fix.
Every time a project was opened, the color and coordinates key order in the catalog_editor.json file was swapped, generating spurious diffs and causing conflicts in version control systems.
An image uploaded via Qodly Studio or the Data Explorer was not displayed after the server was restarted, even though it should still be retrievable when not present in cache.

In client/server mode, if a relation attribute's foreign key value was assigned to a new entity before the related entity actually existed, saving the entity stored an empty value instead of the assigned foreign key.

When a carriage return followed a table in a 4D Write Pro document, text retrieved via [WP Get elements](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-elements) or the wk type table element contained extra unwanted carriage returns; the actual fix was applied to WP INSERT DOCUMENT rather than WP Get elements.
In Qodly Studio, creating a new project did not automatically create the Shared folder, preventing components from being uploaded.
On Windows, a virtual Return key sent by barcode readers that emulate keyboard input did not work as expected.

On Mac only, calling [GOTO OBJECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/goto-object) with an empty object name followed by [CALL FORM](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/call-form) on the Current form window caused a slight but noticeable increase in CPU usage.

When a query executed via [SQL EXECUTE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-execute) was slow, the subsequent call to [SQL LOAD RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-load-record) popped up the record-fetch progress dialog even though [MESSAGES OFF](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/messages-off) had been called.
Projects built in .4DZ format could not have their $shared virtual folder accessed from Qodly Studio.
Form documentation failed to display images referenced by relative paths when the form documentation was opened again in a subsequent session.
A plugin's report-type form variable did not receive any value when used with a binary-format database.
Using [VP Convert to picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-to-picture) to convert part of a 4D View Pro spreadsheet into a picture rendered the text with the wrong font.

Stepping out of an error-handling method installed with [ON ERR CALL](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/on-err-call), back to its caller, left the debugger unable to trace that method again afterward.
In a binary-format database, breakpoints added from the debugger window while tracing were not saved and were effectively ignored.
Tracing a member function of an entity called from a web form (WebForm) could crash the application.
When a 4D Write Pro table had merged cells, the left horizontal ruler markers were displayed at the wrong position.
Inserting a Write Pro table bound to a data source inside a text box, then exporting and re-importing the document as a .4wp file, duplicated the table's data row and break rows.

An input object with "Blank on Null" enabled failed to display [Current time](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/current-time) values on the form when the object was not focused or clicked into; the value should still display even when the object is not in edit state.

In client/server mode only, calling `entitySelection.refresh()` to invalidate a local cache did not correctly cause subsequently accessed deleted entities to be reported as undefined; waiting roughly 30 seconds before accessing the entity selection again produced the expected undefined result.
In a list box column with vertical padding set and row height specified in pixel units, row highlighting was rendered incorrectly; this appears to be a side effect of the ACI0103153 fix.
Calling [OB Copy](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-copy) on a class instance that referenced itself could trigger effectively infinite recursion, potentially crashing the application.
On Mac only, changing 4D's language preference to something different from the OS via the "Language & Region" system panel did not load the corresponding correct .lproj folder stored in the project.

In stand-alone compiled mode only, using [ORDER BY FORMULA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/order-by-formula) with a formula referencing an automatic relation field expression produced an incorrect sort order for the selection; client/server mode and interpreted mode were unaffected.
On Mac with a Retina display, bold checkbox label text used different anti-aliasing rendering in the Form Editor compared to at runtime, making it look different from bold standard text labels.
In Qodly Studio, creating a new entity via a standard action and assigning a related entity to it did not correctly save the relation attribute's key on Save.

Passing a text-type formula expression, such as ($a+$a), as the parameter to [SPELL ADD TO USER DICTIONARY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/spell-add-to-user-dictionary) triggered an unexpected compilation error.
In Qodly Studio, the language server (LSP) did not recognize DataClass member functions, such as .new().
Copying and pasting an Excel table embedded in a Word document into a 4D Write Pro area did not work properly.
On Intel builds in compiled mode only, using a Try expression as a condition inside a Case of statement could crash the application.

If a class source file was saved with incomplete/broken content (e.g. a syntax error mid-edit), reopening the project afterward could crash the application, and recovery required manually deleting the class source file.

A problematic value in the "Redundancy rate" setting of the backup configuration file could cause the application to freeze, with possible crashes occurring during or after a restore depending on the Compression date, Interlacing rate, and Redundancy rate settings.
For OEM-engined 4D Server applications, the license information of a built application showed the standard 4D Mobile Server license, hiding or misrepresenting the actual OEM license details.

When using the Swiss number format (which uses an apostrophe as a thousands separator), decimal tab alignment in a 4D Write Pro document snapped to the apostrophe position instead of the actual decimal point.

On Windows, applying styles such as bold, underline, or italic to items of a [Dynamic pop up menu](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dynamic-pop-up-menu) misaligned the item icons and prevented the popup menu's corners from rendering rounded; the icon positioning was fixed, but square corners on custom popup menus remain a limitation of the Windows API.

In client/server mode, the .4darchive files used to transfer components and plugins from server to client were no longer compressed, since 4D v20, resulting in an unnecessarily low compaction rate for these internal files.
In compiled mode only, dereferencing a pointer to a Boolean variable immediately followed by the `&&` short-circuit operator caused 4D to unexpectedly flip the variable's value from False to True.

When a new request log file was created, the first log entry could get corrupted: information from the "request" column onward repeated the log's own header/session-identifier text instead of the actual request data.

Declaring a typed object variable using an object literal containing a nested ternary expression, such as `var $o : Object:={test: False ? "False" : True ? "True" : "False"}`, triggered an unexpected error.

Activity occurring immediately after startup was sometimes missing from the diagnostic log. The logger keeps a rolling buffer of 1000 entries, and since 4D v20 runs faster than v19, this limit could be reached more easily during startup, causing early entries to be dropped; the buffer limit was reviewed as part of the fix.

In client/server mode with a Designer password set and web processes running in legacy (non-scalable) mode, accessing a set from a web process could raise an unexpected "Bad User Password" error; the issue reproduces specifically under legacy session management, and versions without the ACI0104973 fix might have scalable session management enabled internally even when legacy sessions appear enabled in settings.

The .4DIndx index file size could grow unexpectedly larger than in previous versions when creating records or integrating a journal file into the data file; this appears to be a side effect of the ACI0104510 fix and was seen with certain specific databases.
When a REST server returned a value of 0, 4D failed to display it in the body of the HTTPRequest class, because `4D.HTTPRequest` raised an error caused by the JSON value lacking a byte-order mark.

Launching multiple print jobs simultaneously on the server could raise an unexpected "This method or this function cannot be called when a print job is started" error, because the non-blocking printing setting was being ignored for server-side printing.

In Project mode only, deleting list box columns did not automatically adjust the "Number of locked columns" or "Number of static columns" properties when their values exceeded the new, reduced column count.
The "Query" toolbar button appeared active even when no database/project was open, a regression introduced since version 20 R5.
Calling `SMTPTransporter.send()` with port set to 465 and acceptUnsecureConnection set to True did not work over SSL, and its connectionTimeOut property was not honored either.

Typing [Open form window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-form-window) in the method editor's code completion did not propose the constants "Plain form window no title" and "Movable form dialog box no title" among the smart constants for the window type parameter.

On Windows, if 4D only had en.lproj resources available and the system's regional format was set to a country/locale not managed by 4D, the [Right click](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/right-click) contextual menu in the Structure Editor rendered incomplete XLIFF syntax instead of falling back to the English XLIFF resources by default.
Executing a component method at startup from a method named `Compiler_` triggered an unexpected error.
When "Show toolbar" was disabled in the project settings, reopening the project positioned the Explorer window incorrectly — shifted down by roughly the height of the (hidden) toolbar.
Scrolling did not work in a single-line text input after its "multiline" property was set to 1 programmatically via command, instead of through the form editor.
Setting text alignment to justify on a text input via 4D commands did not actually justify the displayed text.

Choosing "Search references..." from the debugger's contextual menu, then resuming method execution before the Design-mode search completed, and re-triggering the same method in a new process to open its debugger, could crash the application.

After executing `SET AUTOMATIC RELATIONS (True;False)`, [GET FIELD RELATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-field-relation) returned an incorrect status parameter for many-to-one relations; this appears to be a side effect of the ACI0104414 fix.

When the server was too busy to respond to a query before the client's timeout elapsed, the client's network connection could get disconnected; this appears related to the client's idle-connection timeout not keeping pace with a slow-responding server during complex queries.

Sending an instance of a class with a defined computed attribute in an [HTTP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) triggered a syntax error (-10754) about missing language context.
In the Quick Report dialog, changing the display format assigned to Boolean fields was not reflected in the generated report output.

Cross-domain resource sharing in 4D's embedded web areas could still raise a CORS error even with the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header set to "*", because CEF's Access-Control-Request-Headers included "accept-language" (with a hyphen) instead of the correct "accept_language" keyword (with an underscore).

There was an inconsistency between the "legacy sessions" web setting checked in the Settings dialog and `Web Server.scalableSession`, which still returned true: projects with a .4DProject compatibilityVersion of 1860 or higher and no session_mode="3" attribute in settings.4DSettings reported scalable sessions as enabled even when "legacy session management" appeared checked in the settings.
On Mac only, the splash screen did not support Dark Mode: resource picture files with the `_dark` suffix intended for dark-mode display were ignored.

In Design mode, inserting or adding a column to a list box mismanaged the "Number of locked columns" property, causing the "non-scrolling columns" value shown in the Form Editor to become inconsistent with the actual property list value.
Assigning a literal null value to a variable declared with a primitive type produced no compiler error or warning, even after running a compilation pass, and instead resulted in a runtime error.

Running a query via Power Query from Excel or another Office desktop application against 4D returned incorrect numerical values whenever the number exceeded 5 digits; queries via MS Query were unaffected.

When a window lost focus (moved to the background), the text label of checkboxes and radio buttons turned gray along with the control itself; only the button graphic should gray out, while the label text color should remain unchanged.
The 4D Write Pro area's toolbar did not display decimal font size values, even when a font size with a fractional value was actually applied.

After running [QUERY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query) and [ORDER BY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/order-by) following `SET AUTOMATIC RELATIONS (True;False)`, [GET FIELD RELATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-field-relation) still returned an incorrect status parameter for many-to-one relations, indicating the earlier ACI0104959 fix was incomplete.
The [QR REPORT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/qr-report) dialogs incorrectly mixed display names from the real structure and a virtual structure together.
In the Quick Report editor, setting both colors of a background color gradient to the same value was ignored instead of being applied.
On Mac, in binary mode only, the stylesheet's "System font" name got unexpectedly localized based on the system's language when the Windows/Mac system localization changed.

Converting a Binary database to Project mode could produce a CSS file containing a localized (and therefore incorrect) font name, preventing the system font from actually being applied; the fix stops writing the font name to CSS altogether, letting the system font apply automatically when no font-family is specified.
Calling `entity.diff()` on an entity with a picture or blob attribute could incorrectly return null even though that attribute had actually been modified.

Querying an Object field's date property using a 'YYYY-MM-DD' formatted date string via ORDA did not evaluate the date value correctly, whereas querying a native Date-type field with the same format worked correctly.

On Windows, enabling DirectWrite text rendering caused different text alignment than with it disabled, and could truncate the bottom of descender characters (g, j, p, q, y); only buttons and popup/dropdown menus were fixed, since DirectWrite uses different character sizing/spacing than the older GDI renderer (used through 19 R3), meaning text that fit exactly before may now get clipped, requiring layout adjustments or disabling DirectWrite.
In Qodly Studio, related entity data was not returned when accessed through a singleton class function.
Selecting and deleting an empty list box column in the Form Editor could crash the application.
Since 4D v20.x, views could not be renamed in the Form Editor when working with a Binary-format database.
On Mac, calling [Convert to text](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/convert-to-text) with the UTF-7 character set could crash the application.

Combining query conditions on relation attributes with the OR operator produced an incorrect query plan, for instance with code building a query settings object via [New object](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/new-object) and a query string mixing AND/OR across two different relation joins; this appears to be a side effect of the ACI0104799 fix.
Running an ORDA query on a data class using a collection that contains both empty strings and UUID values could return an incorrect result.

On Mac only, various widgets (standard, bevel, rounded bevel, OS X, help, circular, and Office-style buttons, checkboxes, radio buttons, thermometers, sliders, popup menus, combo boxes, and tab controls) displayed as grayed-out when shown in a background (non-frontmost) window, instead of appearing normal like in other applications.

Opening a data file whose index names differed from those recorded in the matching catalog file caused the catalog file to be updated with the data file's index names, when instead the catalog file should have remained unmodified even if reindexing was subsequently required.

The NetKit OAuth2Provider class was not thread-safe in compiled mode, because it internally called [Is license available](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/is-license-available); the fix caches license information at startup so the member function can be made thread-safe.
Selecting multiple form objects via the "Select similar objects" contextual menu left the toolbar's Align and Distribute buttons disabled instead of becoming active.
The "Check syntax" tool did not report a type mismatch when code assigned a value to a computed class attribute.
Setting a method hyperlink (e.g. `method4D:myAlert?parameter='Hello%20World!'`) through the 4D Write Pro area's side widget did not work.
Certain older databases converted from Binary mode to Project mode could crash 4D when opened starting with version 20 R5; opening the data file first in R3 or R4 avoided the crash.

List boxes using an array for managing row heights showed poor scrolling performance, worsening proportionally with the number of columns and becoming very noticeable past around 100 columns; fixed or automatic row heights were unaffected.

Connecting to a server whose computer name contained accented characters via [Open datastore](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-datastore) failed because HTTP headers were sent using UTF-8 instead of US-ASCII; the fix encodes headers like Remote-Hostname using `\uXXXX` escapes and sends them as US-ASCII.

In one specific case, using the method editor's contextual menu to rename a variable could freeze the application; the issue appears related to code containing line continuations via a trailing backslash.

Compiling a method containing a `#DECLARE()` directive placed after an executable statement produced an empty compile error message with a missing red error icon; this appears to be a side effect of the ACI0101345 fix.

Compacting a data file with the "Force updating of the records" option, while the external path to a stored blob/picture file was inaccessible, caused that external file path to be removed from the record entirely.

On Windows in SDI mode with two monitors, opening the DatePicker widget on a form displayed on the secondary monitor showed its popup on the main monitor instead. A companion 4D-Widgets component fix was also applied.
In interpreted mode, applying the unary minus operator to a negative time value did not compute the result correctly.

On Windows, creating a window with [Open form window](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-form-window) and then changing its width with [SET WINDOW RECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-window-rect) could position the window incorrectly in SDI mode. In SDI mode the vertical origin is below the menu bar (not above the title bar); resizing a window narrow enough to wrap the menu bar onto multiple lines shifts the title bar but not the menu bar or client area — this specific case was fixed.
