Processing a REST API authentication method while the Users & Groups page of the toolbox was open could crash the application when [HTTP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) was used with an HTTP POST method.

Running a sequential query with [QUERY WITH ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query-with-array) or [QUERY SELECTION WITH ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query-selection-with-array), after enabling the "map NULL to blank" property on a field with over 300,000 existing records and without using an index, could return a selection with one fewer record than the correct result.
On Windows, pressing the Up or Down arrow key while an empty popup dropdown list was displayed could crash the application.
In Qodly Studio, member functions of a singleton did not return the same metadata (such as filePath, startingLine, endingLine) that member functions of a data model class returned from the server.

Using [COLLECTION TO ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/collection-to-array) to build an [ARRAY TIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/array-time) from a collection of numbers failed to cast the numeric values to time, leaving every array element as 00:00:00; converting to an [ARRAY TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/array-text) worked correctly.
The message shown when trying to activate a 4D license without a network connection was displayed only in English instead of being localized.
On Windows, focusing an empty popup dropdown list and pressing an Up or Down arrow key followed by the Space key could crash the application.

Mounting a Windows shared top-level folder (not a subfolder) over SMB on Mac raised an unexpected error (-43) if the folder name contained special characters such as Japanese characters or an umlaut; Windows-to-Windows shares, and Mac accessing Windows shares in general, were unaffected. This appears to be a side effect of the ACI0104219 fix.

Using the "Rename..." contextual menu in the method editor to rename an inter-process variable showed a dialog message reading 'Rename "..." variable to:' without the leading `<>` diamond symbol that should prefix inter-process variable names; this was purely cosmetic and did not affect the actual rename operation.
[OBJECT SET FORMAT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-format) could not set a list box header icon using a "path:/RESOURCES/" style path; the "#Images/" style path worked correctly.
When a data model class member function was configured with a "promote" privilege action, `Session.hasPrivilege()` failed to report the temporary elevated privilege while that function was executing.

Rendering an SVG image whose `orient` attribute was set to `auto-start-reverse` crashed the application; that attribute isn't actually supported, but the fix ensures the rendering engine no longer errors out on unsupported CSS attributes.

Retrieving mail with the POP3 Transporter caused a memory leak, especially when the connection failed, because the connection object and its buffer were not released; the same underlying issue affects other mail transporters as well.

On Mac, [QR BLOB TO REPORT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/qr-blob-to-report) could crash unexpectedly since version 20 R5, the same underlying issue as ACI0105015, which involves [BLOB to print settings](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/blob-to-print-settings).
The compound assignment operators `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, and `/=` failed to correctly parse expressions combining them with the `[]` collection-literal syntax, such as `$x+=[1; 2; 3].max()`.

Calling `entitySelection.clean()` did not work when used inside a transaction; the fix allows `.clean()` to run during a transaction, and after a transaction is cancelled, calling `.clean()` again now correctly returns the entity selection as it was before the transaction began.

In Qodly Studio, logging out of a session that was in forced-login mode via the standard Logout action failed to clear the session's privileges; logging out with `ds.logout()` worked correctly instead.

On macOS 15 (Sequoia) only, printing to a PDF file from the print preview screen — i.e. combining [SET PRINT PREVIEW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-preview) with a [SET PRINT OPTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-print-option) *Destination option* of `3` (PDF file) — returned an unexpected error #-9630. Using either print preview or PDF output alone worked fine.
In a 4D Dialog window on macOS 15 (Sequoia) only, the focused default button turned white on mouse-over and its title text was invisible until clicked.

On macOS, when the Dock is positioned on the left or right edge of the screen, the toolbar was sized incorrectly: with the Dock on the left, the toolbar's right edge extended off-screen, and with the Dock on the right, a gap appeared at the toolbar's right edge.

An ORDA query involving relation attributes could return an incorrect result set, apparently a side effect of the fix for ACI0104799; a nested `#`/`=` comparison combined with relation attributes across two dataclasses produced an unexpected non-zero count instead of `0`.

On the REST server, calling a singleton class function exposed via the `exposed` attribute that takes no parameters returned an error; sending an explicit empty parameter list (`[""]`) in the HTTP request worked around the issue.

In English localization, forms generated by the Form Wizard could display French words instead of English ones — for example "Vrai"/"Faux" appearing instead of [True](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/true)/[False](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/false) for boolean variables or expressions — caused by an incorrect French translation baked into the *CommonEN.xlf* file of the *en.lproj* resources.

Some entries returned by [Monitored activity](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/monitored-activity) had no `message` property populated, leaving those statistics entries unhelpful for diagnostics.
The `SVG_New_arc` command drew pie-chart sectors incorrectly: instead of rendering a proper pie/disc shape, the sectors overlapped and mixed together.
In the server Administration window, the Maintenance page/tab was not adapted for macOS Dark mode, causing some elements to display incorrectly.
In ORDA, `entitySelection.clean()` (referred to in the fix notes also as `selection.clean()`) did not work correctly once record addresses exceeded the 32-bit (2 GB) range.

On macOS 15 (Sequoia) only, a popup/dropdown-list form object with a small height (under roughly 18–21 pixels) rendered incorrectly — showing a truncated popup menu instead of the compact up/down-arrow-only button style used on macOS Sonoma.

On macOS, repeatedly calling the new `PDF Get attachments` command inside a loop (reproducible after roughly 800 iterations) could crash the application; the fix also ensures `4D.SystemWorker` callback functions are no longer retained by processes other than the one that created them.
In 4D Write Pro, a document's layout rendered incorrectly when it contained subsections with differing numbers of columns alongside paragraphs spanning three or more columns.

Sending an email via `SMTPTransporter` with an OAuth2 token (e.g. through Gmail) exposed the Bcc header to all recipients, a side effect of the fix for ACI0104608; the fix restores the prior behavior where MIME converted from a JMAP message object omits Bcc headers by default, while adding a [MAIL Convert to MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-to-mime) option (`{includeBccHeaders: True}`) for cases like NetKit that require them, and `SMTPTransporter` itself now strips Bcc headers from outgoing messages.

Certain characters, such as a semicolon (";") used inside `//TODO:`, `//MARK:`, or `//FIXME:` tag comments, could corrupt the tags dropdown list shown below the method editor's title bar, because the character was being interpreted as a popup-menu metacharacter.

A 4D Write Pro document failed to load completely when displayed in an embedded web area; the issue relates to the embedded mode always showing a horizontal scrollbar and disabling automatic line-wrap.

An ORDA query on a computed attribute failed to work when using named parameters, because parameter values were not being passed through to the corresponding `Function query` implementation; using placeholders instead worked around the issue.
On Windows, opening the 4D Preferences dialog before ever having opened a project could trigger an unexpected error about an invalid POSIX path, or even crash the application in 20 R7.

In ORDA, calling `entitySelection.clean()` on a sorted entity selection failed to correctly update the selection: entities deleted during a transaction were not removed from the selection, and their positions instead returned [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null).

On Windows 11 24H2 only (not reproducible on 23H2), generating a PDF via a print job could randomly trigger an unexpected error returned from [OPEN PRINTING JOB](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/open-printing-job).
On macOS, using the QUIC network layer specifically, 4D Server could crash after several 4D Remote clients quit or were left idle for a while.

On macOS, when a palette-type window (Controller, Pop up, Toolbar, or Palette form window) had focus, the title text of the default button in the non-focused window matched the button's background color and became invisible; this did not occur in Dark mode.

In the Toolbox dialog, double-clicking (or long-clicking) a user group name to rename it, then confirming the change, did not actually apply the update; using the context menu instead worked correctly.
The list of compiler warnings that can be suppressed incorrectly included some warning numbers that were actually non-suppressible errors.
When a radio button or checkbox label consisted of only a single character, an unwanted colon (":") was automatically inserted before the title text.

On Windows only, using [OBJECT SET HORIZONTAL ALIGNMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-horizontal-alignment) on a static text object failed to change its horizontal alignment whenever the text's orientation differed from the default 0°.

On macOS, attempting to open a project in development mode from a folder shared over SMB/CIFS from Windows could crash the application; sharing the parent folder instead of the project folder itself avoided the problem.

In 4D Write Pro, when a form contained multiple Write Pro standard-action objects, the standard-action information returned by [Action info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/action-info) for a Write Pro area was not always refreshed correctly, leaving the returned values out of sync.

In 4D Write Pro, calling [Action info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/action-info) with a selection spanning multiple paragraphs returned the margin values from only the paragraph where the selection began, and the `status` property was never set to `"mixed"` even though the paragraphs differed; for performance reasons, the fixed behavior only evaluates the first 2000 characters of the range when determining "mixed" status, so larger ranges may still report an incorrect status.

In 4D Write Pro, the *On Selection Change* form event did not always fire — specifically, moving the cursor to the same relative position in a different header while editing and then inserting text failed to trigger it.
Starting a `/*` block comment on a line continued with a backslash (`\`) caused the method editor to treat all subsequent code as commented out, even after a matching `*/` was added.
The application could randomly crash at the moment an entity that had been modified within a transaction was released from memory.
On the Mac client/server platform only, 4D Server could unexpectedly freeze while printing a large report, apparently due to a condition that caused the cooperative-process scheduler to deadlock.
In 4D Write Pro, inserting a table into a document's header and then calling [WP Get position](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-get-position) on that table object crashed the application.

In compiled mode, if a *form.4Dform* description file placed in the `/RESOURCES/` folder had a non-empty `method` property (e.g. `method.4dm`), passing that form's path to [DIALOG](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dialog) or [Print form](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-form) opened the "About" screen instead of the intended form and did not execute the form's method; compiled forms should not attempt to run non-compiled form methods.

In binary mode only, applying a display format to a date column or footer in a list box caused the literal string "todoicu" to be shown instead of the formatted date; setting the format via [OBJECT SET FORMAT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-format) rather than the property list avoided the issue, though existing forms with "todoicu" already registered in the property list need the format reapplied.
Nesting `Try`/`Catch` blocks inside one another triggered an unexpected syntax error (#10756).

[QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query-by-attribute) could fail to return matching records when querying an indexed boolean property of an object (blob) field; affected indexes need to be rebuilt for the fix to take effect.
Chaining a member function call in object notation, such as `entitySelection.toCollection().orderBy()`, incorrectly produced a warning that the function or property `orderBy` was unexpected (550.3).

Importing data with [IMPORT DATA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/import-data) from an XML project file could corrupt Japanese text longer than 170 characters, because UTF-8 strings whose byte length did not divide evenly caused mis-decoding; this problem had been masked previously by the fix for ACI0103521, which instead silently truncated overly long text that exceeded the buffer size without garbling it.
When a radio button or checkbox label consisted of a single Japanese character, it did not render correctly in runtime (execution) mode.
In binary mode only, applying a display format to a time column or footer in a list box caused the value to render incorrectly.

Authenticating a remote datastore connection with `ds.authentify()` prevented the resulting REST session from being detected as active by [Process activity](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/process-activity) or [License info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/license-info); it also went unreported in the Runtime Explorer, the debugger, and the server Administration window.
Connecting to a project in client/server mode while the Structure window was already open triggered an unexpected "A valid platform was expected" error.
On macOS in client/server mode, `entity.fromObject()` could fail to work correctly depending on the order of the dataclass's attributes, apparently a side effect of the fix for ACI0105066.

In a list box bound to a selection or entity selection with the "Hide selection highlight" property enabled, clicking a row no longer triggered the *On Display Detail* [form event](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-event), so meta-info expressions were not re-evaluated; clicking a header or resizing the window forced a redraw. This appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0105065.
In binary mode only, a real (floating-point) field with no display format set was rendered using an hour/time format instead.

In client/server mode, passing a transporter object as a parameter to an "Execute on server" method could lose the attached `File` object from a mail attachment, causing an unexpected error (-10729) when the message reached the server.

Saving an entity inside a transaction once the corresponding data table already held 1024 entities crashed the application; saving the record with classic language commands instead of ORDA avoided the crash.
On Windows, compiling a database could crash the application while generating operation codes, due to an insufficient AST interpreter stack size.

Running a collection or dataclass query on a collection-type property that contained a `null` value positioned before the target value in the collection failed to return matching entities — e.g. a collection of `["Value"; Null]` matched an `attr.col[] in :1` query but `[Null; "Value"]` did not; the fix also corrects a related sequential-query bug so that a boolean field whose value is [Null](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/null) is now correctly matched by `NOT(boolField IS NOT True)`.

In projects originally created before v18 whose structure settings lacked an explicit `automatic_session_management` or `session_mode` entry, the Structure settings showed "Legacy sessions" while User settings showed "Scalable session management" for the same Web Process option — an inconsistency, since User settings should inherit from Structure settings when no override exists in *settings.4DSettings*.

In compiled mode, using the special `//%D` comment (previously used to launch the system debugger) could crash the application; this comment marker has now been removed, and the `%R`/`%T` special comments are likewise ignored when they appear inside `/* */` block comments.

Switching the active localization language with [SET DATABASE LOCALIZATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-localization) while [Time](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/time) or [Date](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/date) commands were in use could crash the application.

On macOS, converting a binary database to a Project one could corrupt the display of a Boolean field represented as a Yes/No radio button on a form: the radio button becomes a mini-size control after conversion (versus a standard-size one in binary mode), and its width was too narrow to fully show the title text.

Passing a certificates folder to [HTTP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) directly (instead of via `HTTPAgent`) returned a 401 error instead of 200, apparently a side effect of the fix for ACI0104923; passing the certificate path to `HTTPAgent` with `keepAlive` set to false instead worked around the issue.

After declaring a variable's data model class with the `var` syntax, typing a path following one of its relation attributes triggered auto-completion suggestions for the variable's own dataclass instead of the related dataclass's properties.
In the WebAdmin settings window, changing port numbers and clicking OK to validate the dialog did not actually save the changes; tabbing out of the input field first worked around the issue.

On Windows, pressing Backspace to delete an unconfirmed (uncommitted) IME input string could incorrectly also delete confirmed Japanese text to the right of it, a side effect of the fix for ACI0104443.

In client/server mode, the client-side toolbar showed the "MSC" button icon instead of the "Administration" button icon, because the flag signaling the toolbar's mode change after connecting to the server was not being updated correctly right after the switch from local mode.
On macOS only, overwriting a read-only `.4wp` document with [WP EXPORT DOCUMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-export-document) caused the file to lose its read-only status.
Clicking the "Database" tab in the database settings window triggered an unexpected runtime error.
Displaying a form with an associated menu bar from a component failed to switch the application's menu bar, leaving the menus that should appear in that context missing.
On macOS with an ARM (Apple Silicon) processor, code could not be compiled when a `While`, `For`, or `For each` loop was placed inside a `Try`/`End try` block.
After modifying a field via a detail form reached by double-clicking a row in a selection-type list box, the list box footer's automatic calculation was not refreshed to reflect the update.
On macOS, scrolling with a trackpad felt sluggish or erratic — a very small two-finger movement could trigger a disproportionately large scroll.

Selecting a journal file with [SELECT LOG FILE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/select-log-file) failed to update the `journal_file_enabled` property in the *catalog.4DCatalog* file; if immediate confirmation of the write is required, inserting a short pause via [DELAY PROCESS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/delay-process) on the [Current process](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/current-process) can help.

Saving an expression in the debugger's expression pane that calls `HTTPRequest.wait()` caused the debugger to enter an infinite loop as soon as a breakpoint was hit, making the debugger window blink and become unusable.

Composite indexes were unexpectedly deprioritized in favor of single-field indexes for query optimization even when a field had a composite index defined; the fix makes 4D prefer composite indexes for comparison operators other than `=` or `#`, but affected indexes must be rebuilt at least once for the fix to take effect.

On macOS, moving a window to a different monitor with [SET WINDOW RECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-window-rect) unexpectedly caused it to lose focus and become inactive, a side effect of the fix for ACI0099153; the same underlying mechanism is shared with [DRAG WINDOW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/drag-window), and the fix also restores the ability to drag windows across monitors.

On macOS, displaying a palette window from a new process could leave both that process's dialog and another process's dialog with keyboard focus set on their input areas simultaneously; typing text in that state crashed the application.

After a 4D client connected to 4D Server, the toolbar's "MSC" button correctly changed to the "Administration" button, but its title text was displayed truncated — a side effect of the fix for ACI0105245.

In Qodly Studio, after debugging a method and running it to a breakpoint, then continuing the trace, attempting to debug that same method a second time in a row could leave the debugger's Play button non-functional.

In client/server mode, certain keyboard shortcut keys — `Escape`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Return`, `Space`, and the arrow keys — could not be assigned as custom keyboard shortcuts from 4D Server's database settings; the cause was traced to an issue in the *ToolBox__.xlf* resource file.

In client/server mode, opening a project via the "Recent projects" File menu entry caused the server Administration window's "Overview & Details" section to show no values, and the application could subsequently freeze on quit; the issue did not occur when the "Recent projects" menu was empty.
Using `4D.WebSocketServer` with HTTPS and the `wss:` protocol limited each connected WebSocket client to processing only a single message.

On a list box, using the *On Outside Call* [command](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/outside-call) to trigger updates from another process caused the list box to unexpectedly scroll upward afterward.

On Windows, the automatic client update process rewrote the *update.win.4darchive* file in a way that broke the client executable's digital signature, apparently a side effect of the fix for ACI0104623.

In client/server mode, the HTTP client's `readwriteTimeout` property was ignored, which risked freezing the application if the telemetry server was busy — compounded by the fact that telemetry's HTTP requests were executed on a cooperative process.
In the French-language splash/welcome screen, the text "Ouvrir ou Créer un projet d'application" incorrectly capitalized the "C" in "Créer", which should be lowercase.

In an application with scalable web sessions and forced-login mode enabled, calling `Session.setPrivileges()` from a web session invoked via a `/4DACTION/` request failed to actually set the session's privileges.

Calling [VP CREATE TABLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-create-table) in 4D View Pro raised an error that the class `cs.TableColumns` was unknown; in 20 R8 the class is actually named `TableColumn` (singular), and in 20 R7 and earlier, options should be passed via [New object](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/new-object) rather than a typed class instance. The documentation examples were corrected accordingly.

In a built (OEM) server application, the "Project Dependencies" menu item incorrectly appeared under the Window menu even though it should be hidden; adding `com.4D.HidePackageManagerMenuItem` to the *Info.plist* file worked around the issue.
In ORDA, declaring `entitySelection.attributeName` as an entity's alias attribute failed to resolve it, so not all of the related attribute's entities were returned.
With the system regional settings set to Turkish, attempting to compile could fail with an unexpected "Can't find form 'Compilation'" error, because the compiler itself could not start.

On macOS in Project mode only, a Boolean field represented as a "Yes/No" radio button — originally created in binary mode — could have its title text clipped after conversion, because the converted radio button's width was insufficient, especially with larger font sizes.

In 4D View Pro, calling [VP PRINT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-print) with the `vk workbook` constant (or `-2`) to print a full spreadsheet stopped working starting in 20 R7, apparently due to a SpreadJS update.
On Windows, launching the debugger from the *On Web Authentication* [database method](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/on-web-authentication-database-method) froze the application.

On macOS, when the system appearance was set to Dark mode while 4D's own appearance was set to Light mode (or vice versa), the "About 4D" and Welcome Wizard dialogs — both implemented as web areas using the CSS `prefers-color-scheme: dark` media query — rendered using the system's appearance instead of 4D's configured appearance; after the fix they follow the application's appearance setting but still won't automatically update if the system appearance changes while the dialog is already open.

On Windows, in client/server mode running a web server on the client side, a network outage while using named sets could crash the application; the underlying network error cannot be avoided, but the fix prevents it from causing a crash.
In the Toolbox dialog, edits made to Lists, Help Tips, or Menu Bars were lost if another application's window was brought to the foreground while editing.

In ORDA, a value assigned to an object (blob) field's property using a mix of classic language and object notation was not reliably saved; using classic language together with [OB SET](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ob-set), or using ORDA together with object notation consistently, saved the value correctly — reproducible with a sequence such as [CREATE RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-record), assigning `obj:={}`, [SAVE RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/save-record), then assigning `obj.Monaco:=True` and saving again.

On Windows, displaying a web application that monitors keystrokes inside a web area using the CEF rendering engine caused performance problems; as a special-case workaround (not recommended generally), calling the unofficial `WA SET PREFERENCES(...;200;False)` to disable `disable-gpu-compositing` can improve performance without relying on the now-ineffective *4DCEFParameters* file, since the underlying CEF version was updated and broke prior patches for older versions.
Right-clicking the function-name dropdown while editing a class file triggered an unexpected runtime error (#-10716).
Editing a method containing a `#DECLARE` directive and triggering auto-completion right after typing `For Each` crashed 4D Mono, apparently a side effect of the fix for ACI0105312.

On Windows only, resizing a form that contains a splitter could leave an object that had been moved by the splitter stuck at its new position instead of settling correctly, most noticeable right after shrinking the window.
When a list box header's height was smaller than its icon's height, the header icon's aspect ratio was not preserved, distorting (squashing) the image.
In binary mode, a checkbox whose label was set to a single space character showed a colon (":") instead when the database was opened, a regression since 20 R6.

In client/server mode, creating a new project from 4D Server did not create the default folders (tables, methods, forms) that normally appear under the "Home" tab in the Explorer; binary mode was unaffected.
Building a single, auto-executable application did not copy the project's components into the built application.

If the startup option "integrate the most recent log file if the database isn't complete" triggered a journal integration when opening the database, the resulting backup journal was created in the *Logs* folder inside the system folder instead of next to the [data file](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/data-file) as expected, apparently a side effect of the fix for ACI0104919 affecting the [log file](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/log-file) location.

Setting a "Goto page" action via [OBJECT SET ACTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-action) on a tab control or button grid that had no automatic action already assigned was silently ignored instead of taking effect.

In client/server mode, quitting the client from the design-mode menu while an [EXECUTE ON CLIENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/execute-on-client) process was in the process of terminating crashed the application.

On Windows, running [PRINT SETTINGS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-settings) on Windows Server 2025 opened that OS's new print settings dialog instead of the classic one that 4D expects, making the dialog unusable.
In ORDA, creating a new record and assigning values to fields configured to "save outside of the data file" did not actually save that data externally when using ORDA syntax.
Using [OBJECT SET LIST BY REFERENCE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-list-by-reference) with a list that had already been deleted crashed the application.
On macOS with an Apple Silicon target, in compiled mode, a failing `Try(expression)` could abort code execution; the runtime itself was fixed, so no recompilation is required.

On Windows, while a popup/dropdown list was open, the Japanese IME remained active and responded to keystrokes, causing an unwanted text-candidate window to appear; the fix disables the Japanese input method while such popups (excluding combo boxes) are displayed, and also adjusts the candidate window's position for dropdown combo boxes.

On Windows with the system regional setting set to English, other-language `.lproj` resource folders (such as French) placed in the Resources folder stopped being resolved — a regression introduced since 20.4 HF1.

When a mail server did not respond to the `CAPA` command with a valid capability list, the `POP3 Transporter` ignored the authentication method specified via its `authenticationMode` property and always used `APOP` instead.

Converting a binary database to Project mode correctly clears a form's binary object (blob) field "mandatory" property as expected, but the affected form object was not recorded in the conversion log as it should have been.
In the Quick Report editor's status editor, a field with a many-to-one relation to another table was listed twice instead of once.

Passing an unassigned Variant variable to certain 4D commands, such as [SET QUERY DESTINATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-query-destination), triggered an unexpected syntax error; assigning a value to the variable first avoided the problem.

Using the QUIC network layer, if a client was forcibly disconnected while its process — deferred after locking records via an SQL query — was still pending, the locked records remained permanently locked.

In a combo box object, changing the horizontal alignment via [OBJECT SET HORIZONTAL ALIGNMENT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-horizontal-alignment) was not applied immediately; the new alignment only took effect once focus moved to another form object.

In a combo box object, changing the display format via [OBJECT SET FORMAT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-format) was not applied immediately; the new format only took effect once focus moved to another form object.

In a combo box object, changing the input filter via [OBJECT SET FILTER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-filter) was not applied immediately; the new filter only took effect once focus moved to another form object.

In 4D Write Pro, running [PRINT RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-record) did not propagate the correct data context to [WP COMPUTE FORMULAS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-compute-formulas), causing computed formulas to be evaluated with the wrong context during printing.
Calling a host-database class function from a compiled component method without using the function's return value crashed the application; assigning the return value to a variable avoided the crash.
Saved user properties for the data-files backup configuration were not reliably remembered — the "User settings" dialog had to be validated (confirmed) twice for the settings to actually persist.
On macOS Monterey, 4D Server could crash when a client process was deferred; disabling process deferral via the client-side database parameter `54` (Idle connections timeout) worked around the issue.

Using the string index operator (`[[]]`) on an object property triggered an unexpected compiler warning, "Assumes that the pointer points to an alphanumeric expression" (533.1); the wording of this warning message was also revised to remove the misleading "pointer" reference.

Using a 4D Write Pro area over Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) caused severe performance problems — typing and adding form items became extremely slow (multi-second delays per keystroke) — after pasting a large block of text, a regression since 4D 20 R6; the cause was that the pasteboard is shared over the network in RDP sessions, and the fix adds database parameter `133`, which when set to `1` restores the prior pasteboard behavior by excluding data-URI-encoded images from copied text.
Using a class instance that contained computed properties as the parameter passed to [throw](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/throw) crashed the application.
On macOS 14.x (Sonoma) only, the default button's title color was incorrect when its window was not focused, appearing white instead of the expected blue.
Displaying a collection-based list box whose contents were swapped out periodically via an *On Timer* event caused a memory leak.
In the server Administration window, closing and reopening the window caused hard-drive information to no longer be displayed on the Monitor page.

On macOS (Intel architecture or Rosetta mode) only, enabling debug logging across multiple preemptive processes simultaneously could crash the application due to a mutual-exclusion issue when accessing a table name from the debug log.

In 4D View Pro, using the toolbar's or ribbon's "no border" borders function failed to actually remove cell borders — a known bug in SpreadJS 16.2.6, worked around by patching the affected JavaScript rather than upgrading SpreadJS.

When a computed attribute was declared to return an object typed with a specific class, the Syntax checker (and the method editor's auto-completion and help tips) failed to recognize that class, showing the attribute only as a generic object type.

4D could unexpectedly stop working (crash) when a record with a Picture and/or Blob field configured to save outside the data file could not actually be saved that way, apparently a side effect of the fix for ACI0105050.

With [SET DATABASE PARAMETER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-database-parameter) selector 34 (debug log) set to "immediate writing" mode, log entries were duplicated when merged into the closing sequence; this was a genuine bug in immediate-writing mode (where command parameters were logged twice), distinct from deferred-writing mode, which intentionally logs the command name both before and after each operation for crash diagnostics rather than for performance benchmarking.

In 4D View Pro, [VP Convert to picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-to-picture) did not respect a cell's foreground color being removed ("no color") via the ribbon: even though the underlying JSON correctly showed `forecolor: ""`, the exported image incorrectly inherited the column's style instead.

In 4D View Pro, [VP Convert to picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-to-picture) did not respect a cell's underline style being removed via the ribbon: even though the underlying JSON correctly showed `textDecoration: null`, the exported image incorrectly inherited the column's style instead.

When a class defined two attributes or member functions whose names differed only in letter case, the method editor's auto-completion (typeahead) offered only one of them as a suggestion instead of both.

With list box column auto-resize enabled, if resizing the list box caused a vertical scrollbar to appear, the last column's content could be partially hidden behind the scrollbar's width instead of adjusting to make room for it.

Using the Licenses Refresh Authentication dialog or the Product auto-activation Authentication dialog without first being signed in on the Welcome screen updated the license correctly, but left the sign-in screen blocking the dialog so it could not be closed afterward.
After refreshing licenses from the license manager window, the displayed license information was not updated immediately; the license manager had to be closed and reopened to see the change.

In the method/class editor, selecting a line containing a member-function declaration or a `/*` block-comment opener, then right-clicking and choosing "Collapse current level," crashed the application.

When more than six new processes simultaneously issued repeated HTTP requests during stress testing, the 4D application could crash after anywhere from a few minutes to several hours. This appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0105495.

In 4D Write Pro, custom (user) properties added to a Write Pro object were not persisted when the document was re-saved a second time; the first save worked correctly, but subsequent re-saves dropped the custom property updates.

In Client/Server, setting a `pattern` in *HTTPHandlers.json* caused the [ds](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/ds) datastore reference to become empty on the 4D Client, apparently because the pattern also matched the REST `/REST/` URL prefix used internally.

The `Accept-Encoding` header passed in the options of `4D.HTTPRequest.new()` was ignored, and the request always sent `gzip, deflate` regardless of what was specified; the older [HTTP Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-request) command allows this header to be customized correctly.

On Windows, a combo box embedded in a list box row displayed unreadable text when that row was hovered and highlighted: the row background rendered as dark blue but the combo box's title text stayed black instead of adapting to the highlight.

Converting a 4D View Pro spreadsheet to a picture with [VP Convert to picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-to-picture) could show a different value for a formula-calculated cell than what appeared on screen. This happens because the underlying SpreadJS `toJSON()` call performs the calculation using JavaScript floating-point arithmetic, so e.g. `40.5895-40.5889` comes out as `0.000599...` instead of the displayed `0.0006`.
Simply viewing a field's documentation in the Explorer, without making any actual change, caused the catalog file to be marked as modified and rewritten on disk.

A bevel button image referenced via the relative path `file:Icons/ICON_ATTACHMENT.png` failed to display at runtime, even though it appeared fine in Design mode; 4D's own file-system notation (e.g. `/RESOURCES/...`) is the recommended way to reference such resources instead of the `file:` prefix.
When a server returned a chunked HTTP response — which happens once the per-connection request limit is reached — `4D.HTTPRequest` could incorrectly return error 23, "Socket Stream is over".

On Windows, maximizing a window using the title bar's maximize button correctly moved/resized form objects such as splitters to fit the larger size, but clicking the restore button to un-maximize the window failed to move those objects back to their original positions and sizes. This regression dates back to 20.6 Hotfix 1.

When a form's input object used a computed entity attribute as its data source, and that attribute's `Function get` referenced another attribute of the same entity, updating the referenced attribute on the form did not trigger re-evaluation of the computed attribute. A note states that computed attributes now share the entity's internal stamp so this dependency is tracked correctly.
Right-clicking a Quick Reports area placed on a form triggered runtime error 10701 ("undefined object") in the component's internal "%Report" form.
Running the Visual Studio Code syntax checker against code that referenced a dataclass whose source file did not actually exist on disk produced an incorrect error.

In the Structure Editor, lines representing a recursive relation (a relation from a table back to itself) were occasionally not drawn at all, apparently because they were rendered behind the table box rather than in front of it.

When a View Pro cell's background color was set to "no color" via the ribbon tool, [VP Convert to picture](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-convert-to-picture) failed to honor that setting and produced an image with the wrong background color; the same problem also affected row and column background colors, and is similar to ACI0105481.

Saving a record a second time while inside `SUSPEND TRANSACTION`, after it had already been saved earlier in the same transaction, could freeze the application and corrupt the data file. A new database engine error 2016 has been added ("a record saved during a transaction cannot be saved again while the transaction is suspended") to prevent this unsafe sequence.

Calling [OBJECT SET ENTERABLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-enterable) on a cell of an array-type list box during the `On Load` form event, or while navigating records with a standard action, could crash the application when the screen was redrawn.
In Client/Server (Remote) mode, `DataClass.getInfo().exposed` always returned True on the client side regardless of the dataclass's actual REST-exposure state.
On macOS only, since 4D v20.x, an image displayed on a bevel button with rounded corners could be unexpectedly truncated and not shown fully within the button.

On Windows, un-maximizing an MDI (main application) window also un-maximized its form windows, but any splitters or other objects that had been moved/resized to fit the maximized layout failed to return to their original positions. The earlier fix for ACI0105507 had not accounted for this MDI-window-restore case.

In Windows Client/Server mode, renaming a table field (for example from the English "ShippingDate" to the Italian "DataSpedizione") could cause the field's `local Function set` to be executed on the server instead of the client.
After the web server was stopped, requests made by Qodly Studio to `/$shared` unexpectedly returned a 404 error. This appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0104786.
In 4D Write Pro, it was no longer possible to reset the background color of text in a Write Pro area back to none/default; this regression was introduced in 20 R3.

Connecting to certain web services with a specific TLS configuration via [HTTP Get](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/http-get) returned the error "Socket stream is over" instead of completing the request.

In single-user built applications, the command-line `--dataless` argument was ignored, so the application kept prompting the user to open or create a data file instead of running without one; note that `--dataless` is meant to take priority over a *Default Data/Default.4DD* file.

While stepping through code in the TRACE window, if a runtime error occurred and displayed its own alert, clicking the "Trace" button afterward left the [TRACE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/trace) debugger window's toolbar buttons visually stuck in an inactive-looking state — a display-only glitch, since the buttons still responded to clicks.
In the Explorer, moving a table into a folder whose name began with a hyphen (`-`) caused that folder to no longer appear in the Structure Editor's folder list.
Duplicating a theme on the Method tab of Preferences added an unnecessary blank space character at the start of the new theme's name.

On macOS, scrolling the mouse wheel over a list box whose "Vertical Scroll Bar" property was set to "No" (hidden) failed to trigger the `On Scroll` form event, since position/movement calculations should not depend on data supplied by the (hidden) scrollbar.
In the method editor, typing code that combined pointer dereferencing with `var` declaration-and-initialization syntax, such as `var vtest:=->`, could crash the application.
Code generated by the Web Services Wizard for proxy methods failed to compile when strict/direct typing mode was enabled.

On Windows, the notification message shown when a server application is shutting down displayed its title in English even when the interface language was set to French, leaving the French localization incomplete.

In the User-mode sort editor ("Order by" dialog), double-clicking a field or using the arrow button to select it no longer actually added the field to the sort criteria; the issue appears related to a broader refactor of hierarchical list handling rather than being confined to the sort editor alone.

When a client/server application's build name differed from its publish name, the client build could not connect to the server even though the publish names matched, because the generated *EnginedServer.4DLink* file stored the internal build application name in `server_database_name` instead of the publish name used with the Build4D component.
Launching an unlicensed single-user built application did not show the correct license dialog, instead of properly indicating that no valid license was installed.
Opening, in 4D v20 R7 or later, a project that had been compiled in 20 R5 caused the `SVG_Define_solidColor` command to return an error.

Connecting to an ODBC data source with [SQL LOGIN](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/sql-login) could return error 9901 while the system variable `OK` was still incorrectly left set to 1, misleadingly suggesting the login succeeded even though no SQL could actually be executed afterward.

When an error was raised via `throw` in `deferred` mode from within a method further down a call chain (not just at the top level of the `Try` block), the corresponding `Catch` block failed to run; errors thrown from member methods should be catchable just as well as those thrown directly in the `Try` block.

A built application that displayed a startup error message (for example, an expired license) could then incorrectly go on to show the license registration dialog as well, when it should not have offered registration in that situation.

Logging into the 4D web server using Digest authentication failed specifically in the Safari browser, while Chrome, Firefox, and Edge worked fine; the root cause was that the server's `WWW-Authenticate` header, which should contain multiple entries separated by `CRLF`, was instead being sent as a single header with escaped line breaks. This appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0105039.

When a dataclass had a read-only computed attribute, merely reading that attribute's value caused it to be added to `entity.touchedAttributes()` and made `entity.touched()` return True, even though the attribute had not actually been modified.

Building a self-executable single-user or evaluation application, without emptying the license list on the build dialog first, could cause the resulting application to show a "4D Volume Desktop license has not been found" message at startup.

[JSON Validate](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/json-validate) mishandled the `items`/`additionalItems` keywords for a JSON-schema property of type `array`: a value that violated the `items` subschema could still be reported as `{success:true}` while an error was also returned at the same time. The fix corrects evaluation so that a single `items` subschema applies to every collection element, multiple `items` subschemas apply positionally, and `additionalItems` is now partially supported (boolean values only, not subschemas).

Using [OBJECT SET SCROLLBAR](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-scrollbar) to attach a vertical scrollbar to a text input object, then duplicating that object with [OBJECT DUPLICATE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-duplicate), produced a duplicate whose scrollbar, focus ring, and border were not drawn correctly.
A subform whose form had an associated form class was not automatically instantiated when displayed as a subform.
On Windows, launching several 4D Server instances via a batch file and the `START` command could cause conflicts over access to the shared diagnostic log file.
`entity.getKey()` returned a real (floating-point) number instead of the expected text or integer type for the entity's primary key.

The `promote` action configured in *roles.json* was not applied in a scenario where a query executed in one class ("Y") was invoked through a function defined on a related class ("X"), and that function processed an attribute of "Y".
Performing a long (press-and-hold) click on the "Open" toolbar button in Design mode triggered runtime errors.
Loading a multi-line query stored in a `.4QF` file (JSON format) into the query editor returned range-check error 53, "the array index is out of bounds".

On Windows, when an HTTPS server had been started using a *cert.pem*/*key.pem* pair located alongside the project folder, the first subsequent call to `4D.CryptoKey.new()` to generate an RSA key returned an internal SSL error 49; later calls worked fine.

After fixing a class's syntax errors and recompiling, the code editor kept showing the previous compilation's error icons at the same locations even though the errors no longer existed. This appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0105580.

On macOS, menu and submenu icons did not adapt correctly to a Retina display's higher resolution or to Dark Mode. The fix ensures icon-file naming conventions for scale factor (e.g. `@2x`) and dark mode (e.g. `_dark@2x`) are now honored correctly.
In some cases, duplicating a list box with the [OBJECT DUPLICATE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-duplicate) command produced a copy whose scrollbars were not displayed.
Building a client application without selecting a 4D Volume Desktop path did not produce any error, even though such a build is not usable without one.
On Windows, when 4D Server was started as a Windows service, the client-side server administration window incorrectly reported that it had not been started as a service.

Querying a collection stored as a property of an object-type field using `[]`/`eval` bracket syntax could return incorrect results when an index existed on that field; the same query worked fine without an index.
Build4D required a license to be specified even when building a server application, though a license should be optional for server builds.
On Windows, in an environment with DPI scaling other than 100%, the `On Display Detail` form event kept firing repeatedly and indefinitely as long as a header input object retained focus.
Passing a malformed *.eml* file to `MAIL Convert from MIME` could freeze the application instead of returning a conversion error.
Retrieving mail using `POP3 Transporter` could leak memory. This appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0105084.
Pasting an image file into the Menu tab's image area of the ToolBox dialog raised an unexpected runtime error 0 inside the internal method "bat_MENUS_SET_BACKGROUND".

On macOS, repeatedly editing blocks that change a member function's indentation level (e.g. adding/removing `case of` or `For each` blocks) in the code editor for a class could corrupt memory and crash the method editor; the same editing pattern in a project method did not trigger the problem.

Changing catalog information such as a relation name while Data Explorer was open in the browser left Data Explorer in a broken state (unexpected errors when inspecting pages), requiring the browser's local storage to be cleared to recover; using Data Explorer in a private/incognito browser window avoided the problem. The *WEBJS/DataBrowser/FormManager.js* file was fixed.

On a new project's settings page, the Web Process setting was displayed as if "No sessions" (legacy single-process sessions) were selected, even though "Scalable sessions" (multi-process sessions) was actually selected internally.
The Progress component's window could no longer be hidden via `Progress window set visible`, whose underlying 4D command is exposed to users as `SET WINDOW VISIBLE(false)`.
Printing a table form omitted the contents of any Date-type fields placed on it.
A particular text-type field placed on a table form displayed only a colon (":") character instead of its actual value.

Declaring and assigning a local variable using the `var` syntax with an explicit Date type — for example `var $date : Date:=This.theDate` — could raise runtime error 54, "Argument types are incompatible", because a date value serialized to ISO format in */PROJECT/DerivedData/CompiledCode/classes.json* was not being cast back from text to Date.

Typing `READ ONLY (*` in the method editor incorrectly triggered an auto-completion suggestion list containing table names, even though [READ ONLY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/read-only) does not take a table-name argument in that position.

The image displayed by a Picture Popup menu was misaligned by several pixels relative to the mouse pointer's actual coordinates, making it hard or impossible to correctly click certain areas of the image.
On macOS, input objects and 4D Write Pro areas whose border style was set to "System" or "Sunken" appeared shifted one pixel to the left or right in the Form Editor.

The help tips for several 4D Write Pro range commands — [WP Paragraph range](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-paragraph-range), [WP Selection range](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-selection-range), [WP Bookmark range](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-bookmark-range), [WP Picture range](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-picture-range), and [WP Text range](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-text-range) — only showed compatibility information rather than actually explaining how each command works.
On Windows, using any three-letter (or longer) sequence followed by parentheses `()` in a project form's name prevented the Design-mode window title from being displayed in full.

Passing an empty string as the default/prefilled text to the [Request](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/request) command left the dialog's "OK" button disabled, preventing the user from confirming an empty value.

In compiled mode, the 4D connection dialog's custom page did not enable its "OK" button after the user typed a server name and network address, even though the values were valid; pressing Tab to move focus out of the field did activate the button.
In a compiled built client application, checkboxes on the connection dialog's custom page were not displayed at the correct position.
Passing an invalid XPath expression to `DOM Find XML element` could crash the application instead of showing a syntax-error alert, apparently due to insufficient null-pointer checking.

Converting a form containing a subform from binary mode to project mode changed the subform's "Selection mode" property from "None" to "Single"; the property's default value in project mode was incorrect.

In Client/Server, when a datastore class constructor was traced on the client, the server-side debugger window remained open until the client's process finished executing entirely, instead of closing as soon as the constructor returned.
On macOS, since 4D v20.x, the form preview image shown in the Explorer in Design mode could be rendered at low resolution, not honoring the system's Retina display scale factor.

A 4D Write Pro document containing a formula (anchor-image or table-embedded) with escaped characters could fail to decode correctly when saved to and reloaded from a BLOB or file; formulas embedded inline were unaffected.
In Client/Server, simply reading a non-null object-type entity attribute (without modifying it) caused `touchedAttributes()` to incorrectly report the attribute as touched.
Connecting a 4D v20.6 client to a v20.7 server (or vice versa) in a cross-version Client/Server setup caused the wrong XLIFF localization file to be loaded.

Calling [OBJECT SET ENTERABLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-enterable) on a list box cell while in-cell editing was active in a dropdown-list-type column could crash the application; the recommended approach is to change the enterable property using the `On After Edit` event rather than a keystroke event during cell editing.
On the server administration window's Maintenance tab, the wording of a button's label and its corresponding help tip were inconsistent with each other.

Displaying a web area in more than one window at once could deadlock the application: the scheduler waited for a window redraw while `WA Evaluate JavaScript` running in that window in turn waited on the scheduler. The fix disables immediate window redraw while JavaScript executes in the web area, avoiding this circular wait.
On Windows, verifying an application with MSC could intermittently raise an error when a form object's "variable or expression" name contained a period (`.`).

Typing a negative time value into a Time-type input field stripped the minus sign and stored a positive value instead; the same problem affected `Time("-1:00:00")`, though assigning a negative integer directly worked correctly.

A range object returned by [VP Get table range](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-get-table-range) could not be passed to [VP RESIZE TABLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/vp-resize-table).
The syntax checker failed to flag an error when a conditional expression expected to evaluate to a boolean instead used object-notation syntax combined with an operator.

In compiled mode, within a Web process context, assigning a value to a project method parameter declared with `#DECLARE` — when the caller had not actually passed that parameter — could raise an error, even though accessing an unpassed parameter is normally supported. The root cause was that, depending on compile order, the syntax checker sometimes failed to detect that a parameter was optional when its type was inferred from how the method was called elsewhere; a recompile is needed after applying the fix.
In binary-mode databases, creating a table form via the wizard — accessible through the "ellipsis" button in the Explorer — did not work.
The documentation preview panel in the Explorer was not available for the form method of a project form.
On Windows, printing raised an error whenever the current printer's name exceeded 30 characters.

[BASE64 ENCODE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/base64-encode) returned inconsistent types for a second-parameter variable that had no explicit type declaration: Text in interpreted mode but BLOB in compiled mode.

For remote entities (including in Client/Server), accessing a non-shared object-type attribute could place that object in the remote cache where it risked being accessed concurrently from several threads, potentially causing application instability.

On Windows, a built application's MDI window title bar showed the application name twice, separated by a dash ("app - app"), because of how the name from the [BUILD APPLICATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/build-application) dialog was combined with the default title.

Building a client application using the `DatabaseToEmbedInClientMacFolder` or `DatabaseToEmbedInClientWinFolder` build settings keys caused the license registration screen for a single-user license to appear after a subsequent [RESTART 4D](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/restart-4d), even though a built client application should not require a license at all, and the registration dialog could not be dismissed.
A MIME header containing an underscore (`_`) character was not encoded correctly by SMTP Transporter.

On Windows, if a print dialog was invoked from a process that had no dialog of its own displayed, the print dialog was no longer treated as modal, so it could be closed simply by clicking on another window — for example, while a tooltip was displayed.

Closing and reopening a method editor window sometimes failed to restore its previous size, causing it to keep an unreasonably large minimum width and/or height even after being resized; this occurred specifically when resizing the window below 964 pixels wide or 399 pixels tall, since that size was then not saved correctly.
When a *LoginImage.png* file was present in the Resources folder to enable a custom login screen, the default 4D icon and window title/message were not hidden as they should have been.
On Japanese-localized systems, some project methods failed to be tokenized properly and were instead misidentified as process variables.

In 4D View Pro, a swipe gesture (left or right) over a View Pro area could cause the browser page to navigate away from the area entirely, making it disappear. A workaround using `WA SET URL FILTERS` to block web-area navigation is documented for reference.

Duplicating a list box column bound to an entitySelection or selection, via the Form Editor's context menu, set a raw token value into the duplicate's "variable or expression" property instead of the correct expression.
On Windows, the same shared object could be released (freed) simultaneously by two different threads, which could crash the application.

With direct typing enabled, calling a 4D command that returns a value through a variable parameter (such as `OBJECT GET COORDINATES`) using previously declared Integer variables produced an unexpected compilation error ("real redefined as longint"), for example when reusing a variable like `y1` declared earlier in the method.
On Windows, if the most recently used project's path pointed to a network volume, attempting to open "Open Recent" for that project crashed the application.

In Client/Server, using `entitySelection.orderByFormula()` with a formula that referenced a local (client-side) entity selection which cannot be streamed to the server (e.g. `This.indexOf(entitySelection)`) produced a misleading error message; the fix clarifies that a client-side entity selection cannot be used inside a query formula.

Using the date picker widget to set a value, in a form reused repeatedly within the same process, could cause the picker to retain and show a previously entered value instead of reflecting the current one.

When mail text contained certain specific characters, [MAIL Convert to MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-to-mime) and [MAIL Convert from MIME](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/mail-convert-from-mime) could fail to convert the body of the message correctly.
Pasting a line of text ending with a backslash (`\`) immediately before a `Begin SQL` statement into a method could instantly freeze the application.
Auto-completion inside a `Begin SQL`...`End SQL` block no longer offered local variables as suggestions in the method editor.
In compiled mode, calling `METHOD Get Path` with a dereferenced pointer to a table produced an error instead of returning the expected path.

Attempting to open a v13 structure file with 4D v20 — even after canceling the conversion dialog — silently updated the internal DB4D version number, leaving the file damaged so that older 4D versions could no longer open it; running MSC to repair the structure restores access.

Since 20.7 HF2, assigning by code a text value too long to fit into a single-line text input object caused the end of the text to be displayed instead of the beginning; enabling multistyle text restored the previous (correct) behavior of showing the beginning. This appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0105769.
The blinking text cursor animation in a list box column being edited did not stop after clicking away to switch to another application.
30-day trial licenses did not grant access to Qodly Studio.

In the method editor, typing a dot (`.`) right after a 4D command name (for example `QUERY`) triggered an auto-completion popup listing irrelevant property names that did not apply to a command in that position.
The [HIGHLIGHT TEXT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/highlight-text) command did not work when used on an object placed inside a subform.

Loading a form with [FORM LOAD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-load) while omitting its second parameter meant that a text form object bound to an expression on the [Form](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form) object could not subsequently have its value set via [OBJECT SET VALUE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-value); passing an object as the second parameter to `FORM LOAD` avoided the problem.

On Windows in GDI mode, scrolling a collection- or entity-selection-type list box that had been defined without a header (via the object passed to the dialog command) rapidly increased the number of GDI objects in use with every scroll; once roughly 10,000 were accumulated, the list box stopped displaying anything at all. Such headerless list boxes normally only occur if the form's definition object is built by code or an externally edited *.4DForm* file.
Downloading a large file with `4D.HTTPRequest` could fail if `wait()` was called on the request object twice.

On Windows, in an environment where the desktop resolution scale was set to something other than 100%, referencing a printer font could deadlock the application, making 4D Remote appear frozen; the fix makes 4D ignore printer fonts altogether, since bitmap fonts are not supported under Direct2D anyway.
On macOS, in Client/Server, the QUIC network layer could crash 4D Server.

On Windows, [SHOW ON DISK](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/show-on-disk) could open and display, in Explorer, the target of a shortcut found inside the passed folder rather than the folder path that was actually passed to the command, if that shortcut happened to be the first item shown.

Since 4D v20, setting an invalid formula with `VP SET FORMULA` no longer displayed the `#NAME?` placeholder text in the cell as it should have. The fix makes the workbook option `allowInvalidFormula` default to true (also configurable via `VP SET WORKBOOK OPTIONS`).
In 4D Write Pro, dragging an image and dropping it after the cursor passed over a header or footer copied the image instead of moving it.

Using the `ngtcp2` QUIC network layer in Client/Server, if a client's system entered sleep mode after the database parameter "Remote connection sleep timeout (98)" was configured, the application could crash; the `lsquic` QUIC layer was not affected.
Assigning a `4D.Signal` object as a property of a shared object raised unexpected error -10721.
Selecting a table in the Explorer did not immediately show its preview; moving the Explorer window to the background and back to the front made the preview appear.
In 4D Write Pro, if a document range or section used with `WP new` did not include its own final character, the new document created could gain an unwanted extra page break, breaking the layout.

In Project mode, enabling "Save password" on a built application's login screen, to auto-connect an engined client to an engined server, did not actually persist the password hash: the login prompt kept reappearing every time. The credentials are stored in a file named "applicationname.mdp" under *AppData/Roaming* (Windows) or Application Support (macOS); holding Shift at startup forces the login dialog to reappear.

The 4D WebSocket server only triggered its worker once per incoming message bundle rather than once per message: if `n+x` messages were queued at once, only `n+1` worker invocations occurred, so the worker could end up processing a stale message from minutes earlier instead of the most recent one.
Hovering over a class property in the method editor showed inconsistent type information in the tooltip when that property was used as an argument to the `Choose` command.
Passing a class property typed as Integer to the `Choose` command produced a compilation error.
[JSON Validate](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/json-validate) could not validate a collection value; the command's syntax was revised to support this.
On Windows only, since 4D 20 R5, dragging and dropping fields onto a View Pro pivot table no longer worked.
On macOS, sorting an entity selection created with `entitySelection.slice()` by an object-type field, without specifying which attribute path to sort on, could crash the application.

In Project mode, if you open a form, change an object's standard action through its context menu, and then close the form without making any other edit, the change to the standard action was silently discarded and never saved.
In the Object Library dialog, filtering by object category and selecting the Progress Indicator category showed no objects at all, even though matching objects exist.

On macOS, the [Folder](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/folder) command mishandled a trailing "/../" appended to a path string: instead of moving up a single directory level, it incorrectly moved up two levels.
In the Explorer window, pressing Return/Enter on a selected form, method, or class failed to open it, requiring a double-click instead.

On Japanese Windows systems, typing long text in the Method Editor caused the text cursor and selection highlight to be drawn at the wrong position; the problem was tied to the Meiryo UI font and grew worse with heavily kerned character pairs (e.g. "/A", "AW"), while monospaced fonts were unaffected.
When using the QUIC network component, 4D Server could crash if many client connections were closed at the same time.

On macOS, the build settings' copyright build keys (CommonCopyright, RuntimeVLCopyright, ServerCopyright, ClientCopyright) were no longer applied in the application build screen or by [BUILD APPLICATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/build-application); the Build4D component was unaffected.
The ORDA request log (as enabled via ds.startRequestLogs()) was not thread-safe, which could lead to an application crash.

On Windows with Japanese localization, the label at the bottom of the "Search in Design" dialog was slightly clipped; the fix replaces the standard tool button (which reserves internal padding that can clip text depending on layout) with a custom button.
The "Connect to 4D Server" screen no longer displayed the list of recently used client/server databases.
In a combo box, the On After Edit form event failed to fire when Japanese text input was validated with the Return key.

Integer overflow behavior was inconsistent across Windows/macOS and interpreted/compiled modes. In interpreted mode, MAXLONG+1 is computed as a float (2147483648) and then converted to an integer via lrint(); on Windows this underlying function returns a 4-byte result (yielding 0 in Visual Studio's implementation) while macOS/Linux return an 8-byte result whose truncation instead produces -2147483648. To unify behavior across platforms and runtime modes, Windows now calls llrint() instead — note this means Windows interpreted mode now also exhibits the sign-flip behavior seen on other platforms.
Compiling an empty (and syntactically invalid) Try() expression triggered memory corruption, detectable via GFLAGS.
Under certain conditions, executing [WEB SEND RAW DATA](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-send-raw-data) could crash the application.
Components configured on the server side via the Project Dependencies dialog were loaded correctly on the server but failed to load on connected clients.

The Form Editor's Object Library showed an invalid "Search area" entry for objects belonging to the 4D Widgets component even when that component wasn't loaded; unused dependencies should be excluded from the library instead.

Frequently calling [License info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/license-info) from a Web process while another process accessed the menu bar could crash the application, because the command's execution updated the menu bar without mutual exclusion, causing simultaneous updates. The fix stops License info from updating the menu bar at all; since it reloads the license folder's contents on every call, it isn't meant to be invoked frequently — use [License usage](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/license-usage) instead for periodic monitoring.

Building an OEM headless server application with tool4d using the Build4D component failed partway through with an error, and no license was installed into the license folder; the fix makes tool4d's [Create deployment license](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-deployment-license) and [BUILD APPLICATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/build-application) usable together.
In a list box with a locked (non-scrolling) column, resizing that locked column caused the horizontal scroll position of the remaining columns to jump unexpectedly.
In the SVG component, ampersand characters (&) within text passed to SVG_New_textArea were not properly encoded, causing XML parsing errors when multiple style attributes were applied.
In the Method Editor, autocomplete no longer suggested a newly typed variable name until the method had been saved (pasting the variable name worked fine), a behavior change from 4D v19.

On Windows, an OS-level feature that smooths button edges with lighter pixels caused visible bleed lines above or below multi-state PNG button images when the states were packed without margins; the fix also improves rendering of bitmap images at Windows desktop scaling above 100% and on Retina displays on macOS (vector images like SVG are unaffected).

A synchronization issue in the list box object could crash the application when data entry in a cell coincided with adding/removing rows and calling [OBJECT SET SCROLL POSITION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-scroll-position) at the same time.
On Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 26.1 (but not 26.0.1), sending simulated keyboard events to a 4D Write Pro area could crash the application.
Cloning a non-shared collection that is part of a shared object graph could trigger a race condition on the client side, potentially crashing the application.
In the HTTP request handler's IncomingMessage object, the urlQuery property incorrectly decoded a literal "%3D" sequence in a URL query value into an "=" character.
In the AST interpreter, dereferencing a null 4D pointer failed to raise an error as it should.

On Apple Silicon Macs, calling [QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query-by-attribute) without the comparison operator argument crashed the application instead of raising a usage error.
In the French edition of 4D, the error message shown when dereferencing a null pointer was missing from the XLIFF localization resources, so it wasn't translated into French.
On macOS, using Quick Report's print dialog to save a PDF and then subsequently opening the preview overwrote that just-exported PDF file.

The [ZIP Create archive](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/zip-create-archive) command reported a successful status (`{"success":true, "statusText":"success"}`) even when it actually failed, for example because the target folder didn't exist.

On macOS 26 (Tahoe), right-clicking 4D's Dock icon and choosing "Show All Windows" displayed a leftover "ghost" of a window that had already been closed, apparently because its NSWindow wasn't being released correctly.

[ARRAY TO LIST](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/array-to-list) and [LIST TO ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/list-to-array) treated list names as case-sensitive in Project mode, inconsistent with Binary mode; after upgrading, any duplicate list names differing only by case in lists.json need to be manually consolidated into one.

Using bracket notation for an object-field reference as a form object's data source (e.g. `[MyTable]MyObjectField["myProp"]`) crashed the application as soon as the form was displayed; dot notation (`[MyTable]MyObjectField.myProp`) worked fine.
A `.query()` call raised error #1112 when its logical connector operator (`|`) was not surrounded by spaces in the query string.
Calling `.getMails()` on the new IMAP transporter to fetch a large batch of emails (e.g. 500) crashed the application, caused by internal use of the unsafe, non-bounds-checked `strstr()` function.
The application could crash if a process being displayed in the Server Administration window terminated right as the window was refreshing its information; closing the window was a workaround.
Sorting an entity selection by a property of an object-type attribute did not apply the standard heterogeneous-type sort rule (objects should sort before collections).
Sorting an entity selection by a numeric property of an object-type attribute could sometimes produce incorrectly ordered results, even without NaN or infinite values, for certain data sets.

NaN values in an object attribute's properties disrupted entity selection sorting via `.orderBy()` or `.query("... order by ...")`; such values should sort the same way as they would for a collection.
In Project mode only, markers on any type of detail (print) form were not shown, and thus could not be managed, in the property list; Binary mode was unaffected.

In a 4D Write Pro document, a carriage return character formatted with a font size different from the preceding character could be omitted when exporting to plain text (or from the end of a paragraph); such a scenario is rare, since a triple-click normally selects a carriage return together with its paragraph, but the fix ensures it's still handled correctly.
On macOS, selecting an option in an HTML dropdown menu shown inside a form's Web area caused the [FORM Event](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/form-event) code On Timer to pause repeatedly.
In a binary-mode database, attempting to build a component crashed the application; this appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0105475.

Passing a numeric value alongside a Boolean expression to the [Choose](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/choose) command (e.g. `Choose($number; True; Not(True))`) triggered a compile error, a side effect of the ACI0105909 fix; keeping the condition/parameters consistently either all values or all expressions (e.g. `Choose($number; True; False)` or `Choose($number=0; True; Not(True))`) avoided the problem.
