In a 4D Write Pro table with multiple sort criteria applied, a bottom break row could be inserted at the wrong position when a top break row for a lower-priority sort criterion was also present; break rows should be inserted immediately before the point where a key field's value changes, per the sort order.
When the Method Editor's coding language was set to French, pressing F1 or Control/Alt+clicking failed to jump to the correct online documentation page, opening a broken URL instead.

Creating a new folder from the Explorer's Home tab (via the "Default Project Method" context menu) created the folder internally but did not refresh the Explorer's display, and the new folder's name wasn't put into edit mode.
In the Query Editor, combining a Date field condition with "is within next" "month" produced incorrect results whenever the current date fell in November.

Passing an object with a Formula-type property into `collection.find()` (e.g. `$col.find($object.findFunction)` where `$object.findFunction` is a Formula) could incorrectly raise a syntax error for otherwise valid code.
Over a 10-gigabit Ethernet interface using the QUIC network layer, a 4D Remote client could hang or disconnect when repeatedly downloading around a megabyte of data at a time from the server.

Displaying a dynamic pop-up menu (via [Dynamic pop up menu](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/dynamic-pop-up-menu)) from the On Clicked event of a picture object inside a widget, invoked through [CALL SUBFORM CONTAINER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/call-subform-container), caused the menu to reappear immediately after being dismissed by a click. This happened because picture objects (unlike buttons) keep focus after On Clicked until the window is deactivated — needed to track mouse state via [Is waiting mouse up](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/is-waiting-mouse-up) — so a click event outside the widget could still be delivered to an object inside it. Using a button object, triggering the menu outside the host form's context, or showing it on On Mouse Up instead of On Clicked avoided the issue.

In Project mode, [OBJECT Get format](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-format) returned an empty string instead of the default format string for objects like thermometers, rulers, steppers, and spinners (among others) that had no explicit display format set.

On macOS, the horizontal text alignment set on drop-down list (pop-up menu) objects was ignored; the fix also corrects custom rendering used for non-system heights above 23 points on pop-up menus and combo boxes.

In client/server mode, if a record saved by a client during a transaction was later rolled back, field updates made by triggers were not reverted, leaving the data inconsistent; saving the record from the server side was unaffected.

On Windows, attempting to print a 4D View Pro spreadsheet froze the user interface, an apparent side effect of the ACI0105828 fix; a workaround using WA SET URL FILTERS on On VP Ready to restrict chrome:// URLs was available before the underlying fix.
[METHOD RESOLVE PATH](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/method-resolve-path) did not support resolving classes.
Searching for methods modified on a specific date in the "Search in Design" dialog returned an error instead of results.
On Windows, when a relation was defined on fields other than the primary key, calling `entity.fromObject()` or `entitySelection.fromCollection()` assigned an incorrect value to the related attribute.
The property list for a form class was missing the Edit button needed to open the associated class in the Method Editor.

In the Explorer's Commands page, selecting Process info under the Processes theme showed a raw XLIFF identifier (`:xliff:desc1843`) in the help tip and preview area instead of the actual descriptive text.

In Project mode on Windows, the Insert key could not be assigned as a keyboard shortcut, though it worked fine in Binary mode; after upgrading, shortcuts already mapped to Insert under Binary mode need to be reassigned.
In an OEM server application, the Quit confirmation dialog's window title showed "4D Server" instead of the custom application name.
Calling PA_GetBlobHandleParameter repeatedly on the same PA_Handle returned an empty value after the first call.

When a Windows client running against a macOS server performed an automatic update, some interface elements showed the generic 4D Volume Desktop icon instead of the custom icon set in the build, apparently because the `.ico` file wasn't copied to the auto-update client.
With ORDA's restrictedByDefault permission setting enabled, entities could not be dropped/deleted.
Referencing a property of an entity-selection-type relation attribute via object notation produced a spurious compiler warning (550.26).
Multiplying a numeric value by a text value (Num*Text) incorrectly caused a compiler error; this was not an issue when explicit typing mode was enabled.
The Design mode Explorer window could not be closed by pressing the Escape key.
In 4D Qodly Pro, a Text component containing text too long to fit failed to show a scrollbar in renderer (runtime) mode.
In 4D Qodly Studio's Page Editor, creating a new state didn't mark the tab as modified, so closing the editor skipped the usual save prompt and the new state was lost on reopening.
Changing the width of a style box nested inside a 4D Qodly Pro matrix component caused an error when the page was subsequently displayed.
In Safari specifically, selecting a date via a 4D Qodly Pro date-picker component showed an invalid date in a linked Text Input component sharing the same Qodly data source.
Nesting 4D Qodly Pro matrix components could intermittently cause data to fail to load correctly.

In client/server mode, if the system woke from sleep after the remote connection's sleep timeout (Remote connection sleep timeout) had already elapsed, the client application crashed instead of displaying an appropriate error message.
For an input object whose expression type was set to Numeric, setting minimum and maximum values caused the property list to incorrectly warn "Expected type: string".

On macOS since 4D 20.8, a non-enterable input object with no fill color and "System" border style, placed in front of a Tab control or Group Box, became almost invisible due to insufficient contrast; the rendering of the "System" border style was fixed.

Evaluating [Call chain](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/call-chain) in a debugger expression incorrectly reported the first formula in the call chain as being the literal text "Call chain" rather than the actual formula.

Passing a parameter with invalid syntax to [QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/query-by-attribute) could crash the application; the fix ensures that when a typo tokenizes a constant into an invalid expression, error 59 (invalid parameter) is returned instead.
Vertically merging two or more cells in a 4D Write Pro table caused the background image in the merged area to be displayed zoomed in.
In the data export dialog, switching the form used to export records could crash the application.
In Binary mode only, changing the Data Source of a "Current Selection" type list box via the property list could crash the application.

Both [TRUNCATE TABLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/truncate-table) and [DELETE SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/delete-selection) took roughly 0.5 seconds to execute even against a table with zero records, an unexpectedly high fixed cost.
On macOS in dark mode, the search field under Settings > Compiler > Warnings rendered with white text on a white background, making typed text unreadable.
Client/server connections using the QUIC network component were very unstable in certain VPN network environments.
In a method without a `#DECLARE` declaration, writing an incompatible-type expression in a `return` statement failed to trigger a syntax error in the code editor as it should.
In the Toolbox, adding a new item to a list inserted it at the end of the list rather than immediately after the currently selected item.
Placing a comment after the `return` keyword on the same line at the end of a function caused the function to return Null instead of the value assigned to `$0` or a named return parameter.
Since 4D v21, the `session.IPAddress` property returned by [License usage](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/license-usage) came back empty.
On macOS, dictating text into a text area using the system's voice-to-text feature caused the previously dictated text to be deleted after about four lines.
Right-clicking with multiple tables selected in the Structure Editor could crash the application, depending on the tables' property settings.
The `session.userName` property returned by [License usage](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/license-usage) came back empty.

Passing the name of a nonexistent callback method to [VERIFY CURRENT DATA FILE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/verify-current-data-file) (or [VERIFY DATA FILE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/verify-data-file)) failed to set the OK system variable to 0. The fix now distinguishes an invalid callback name from an empty string: passing an empty string runs the verification without a callback, while an invalid callback name now returns an error.
In the data export dialog's Form tab, switching between tables didn't refresh the form preview image shown for the newly selected table.
In the data export dialog, selecting a table that had no associated output form made it impossible to subsequently select any other table.

In an engined client, after executing [CHANGE USER](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/change-user), the 4D user selection window could reappear at launch even though a default user was configured — this occurred when a `.4DLink` file registered the server's IP address directly; registering only a port in the URL and relying on server broadcast avoided the problem. The issue appeared related to a `.mdp` password-save file being created during user switching.

On Windows, using Find in the Method Editor caused the search highlight to override the text-selection highlight, making it impossible to distinguish selected text from found matches, due to an incorrect highlight color being applied.
Displaying the Toolbox's "Users & Groups" editor as a non-administrator user resulted in a visually broken layout, with some icon images missing and message text misplaced.
"Goto Definition" did not work when invoked from a project method's `#DECLARE` line or from a class member function's declaration line.

On macOS, the Windows-only "Use DirectWrite" compatibility option was hidden, whereas it should be visible (even if inapplicable) on macOS too, similar to how SDI mode and FluentUI options are shown there.
An application built with the Build4D component was missing its custom icon in several windows, the same underlying issue as ACI0097827.
Subtracting dates using dereferenced pointers triggered an unexpected compiler error claiming a Date could not be cast to Integer.

Launching the application in "Run as administrator" mode on Windows broke the CEF (Chromium Embedded Framework)-based Web area used everywhere web areas appear; this traces to a known CEF issue, worked around by setting the `do-not-de-elevate` switch to True.
On Windows, 4D failed to manage or open new windows correctly once a certain number of windows was open (typically around 80+ Method Editor windows), an apparent side effect of the ACI0106038 fix.
In the English edition, the User Mode entry form's window title was missing a space between "Entry For" and the table name.

The debugger's Step Over behavior was not always correct when a method call had several other method calls as parameters: it no longer stepped in/out in the expected order and level sequence (e.g. for `$a:=Method4(Method1; Method3(Method2))`, the order should be 1→2→3→4).
Double-clicking the Explorer's scrollbar was mistakenly interpreted as an action on the currently selected item, causing the Form Editor or Method Editor to open unexpectedly.

In a 4D Write Pro area, if a style (such as italic or bold) wasn't supported by the selected text's font, the corresponding standard-action checkbox and its context menu entry failed to become disabled as they should.
For an engined server build, the Server Administration window's title showed "4D Server" instead of the custom application name.

Associating a 4D Write Pro standard toggle action with a Boolean-datasource checkbox meant the checkbox no longer automatically reflected the action's on/off state as its value changed; integer-type checkboxes were unaffected.

Setting a button's icon via [OBJECT SET FORMAT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-set-format) with a format string like `";#image.png"` caused [OBJECT GET BEST SIZE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/object-get-best-size) to incorrectly return 0x0 instead of the icon's actual dimensions.
In Binary mode, copying and pasting a group of form objects in the Form Editor could omit some of the objects from the copy.
Inside a component, [GET PROCESS VARIABLE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/get-process-variable) returned no value for an interprocess variable.

Rapidly executing [SAVE RECORD](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/save-record), [FLUSH CACHE](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/flush-cache), [ALL RECORDS](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/all-records), and [DELETE SELECTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/delete-selection) in succession could intermittently return an invalid-index error (#1088).

Using the QUIC network layer, if a client spawned a large number of processes performing database queries, let them finish, and then spawned another large batch of processes, the remote client could stop responding entirely.

On Windows, updates to Microsoft Edge (specifically versions numbered 146.0.3856.59 / .62, released around March 2025) caused the embedded WebView2-based web rendering engine to initialize incorrectly, crashing 4D when a Web area was displayed on affected systems.

On macOS 26 only, modal dialogs (e.g. Save as PDF) and pop-up windows (e.g. printer selection) launched from the [Print Settings](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/print-settings) dialog failed to display, apparently appearing hidden behind the Print Settings window.

On macOS 26 (Tahoe), in the file-save dialog opened by [Create document](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-document), clicking "New Folder" or entering a filename that already existed in the target folder could gray out the dialog with a hidden modal window behind it; the issue cleared with Escape and did not recur once the dialog was reopened.
In the Method Editor, Alt/Option+double-clicking a form name no longer opened that form in the Form Editor.
On Windows, 4D did not make use of address space layout randomization (ASLR), a security hardening measure now enabled for improved protection.

Using pop-up/drop-down objects in a list form from an older database created with 4D 19.x (before 19 R3) could cause crashes; enabling the "Use DirectWrite for text" compatibility option could prevent the issue.

If a 4D Write Pro document's title contained special/URL meta-characters (such as "?" or "/"), images embedded in the document failed to display. Because a `.4WP` file is a zip-compressed HTML package whose subdirectory paths derive from the document title, an improperly encoded title broke the image paths; the fix falls back to a default base name whenever the title contains such characters.
4D Server could crash following an unexpected client disconnection.

On Windows, scrolling a list box left or right using a touchpad's horizontal swipe moved it in the reverse of the expected direction; changing the OS touchpad settings fixed the direction but then reversed scrolling elsewhere in the OS and other form objects.
Setting a breakpoint on a method while the Explorer window was not open could crash the application.

Pressing Ctrl+Shift+W inside a 4D View Pro area turned the screen black and forced the application to quit; Web areas were unaffected. The fix disables several browser-style shortcuts (Ctrl+Shift+W, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+J, F5) within View Pro areas, while others (Ctrl+N/S/P/O, Ctrl+Shift+I) now follow SpreadJS's own behavior rather than CEF's.

The HTTP connection handler consumed excessive CPU, traced to [WEB GET VARIABLES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/web-get-variables) mishandling requests where the HTTP header/body separator `\r\n\r\n` was missing.
If a remote client entered sleep mode while a server request was still in flight and then exceeded the sleep timeout, the server could freeze entirely.

In a 4D Write Pro document, an embedded SVG rendered as empty/white output when a `clipPath` child element itself used a `transform` attribute, unlike standard web browser rendering; avoiding the nested transform (applying the equivalent coordinates directly) worked around the issue.

Entering data into a multi-style list box cell in dark mode saved unwanted style tags that injected a white text color; switching back to light mode (or printing) then made that text unreadable (white on white).
When compacting a database with the "Force update all records" option, pointers stored inside object fields were corrupted, leaving those objects empty after compaction.
On Windows, a remote engined application containing the SDK sometimes failed to restart automatically after being updated.

In Quick Report's crosstab reports, applying a column sort actually reordered the rows instead, and applying a row sort reordered the columns instead — a mislabeled user-interface issue rather than a data problem.

On Windows, the `cpuUsage` value returned for each process by [Process activity](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/process-activity) was unreliable, reporting much higher CPU usage than what Windows Task Manager showed, unlike on macOS.
Using the QUIC network component (but not ServerNet), if multiple processes issued database requests concurrently, 4D Remote frequently returned an unexpected "Cannot read data from stream" error.

Inside a class, code lines following a block comment (/* ... */) with no additional code after them were silently ignored and never executed; adding a blank line after the block comment avoided the problem.
In a list box with automatic column widths, if a selection change caused vertical scroll bars to appear, any manually resized columns were reset back to their minimum widths.
In client/server mode, calling `ds.authentify()` via the REST `$catalog/authentify` endpoint returned an empty string for `Session.info.IPAddress`.
In the Toolbox, editing a user name to match one already in use displayed the expected "user already exists" error, but the edit was still committed despite the error.
Passing a table as a parameter to [REDRAW](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/redraw) incorrectly produced a syntax error.

In 4D Write Pro, passing a table element to [WP New](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-new) cloned the entire source document instead of just that table. The fix ensures only the passed element is copied, and headers/footers are no longer duplicated along with it.
Calling [License info](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/license-info) simultaneously from two processes in compiled mode caused the application to crash.
Compiling a project with tool4D raised errors claiming the `4D.WebSocketServer` and `4D.WebSocketConnection` classes were unknown, blocking compilation even though these classes are legitimate.

A 4D Qodly Pro page bookmarked in a browser's favorites or added to an iOS home screen failed to render, because the URL's query parameters (e.g. `/$lib/renderer/?w=Login`) were not preserved when the start page was requested directly via `http://localhost/$lib/renderer/`.
The keyboard shortcut Control+R for running a method stopped working; Control+Shift+I (restart in compiled mode) reportedly also failed to trigger.

On Windows, forms using the Fluent UI theme could no longer accept a folder dragged and dropped from the desktop into a text area, while dropping onto an MDI window (via the On Drop database method) still worked fine.
Pasting a field name into the Query Editor no longer switched the value-entry box to match the field's data type, so the input area did not adapt appropriately to the pasted field.

Assigning the numeric literal 0 to a UUID-type entity attribute through ORDA was silently accepted instead of raising a syntax error, unlike equivalent code in classic language which correctly flags it as invalid; the inconsistency was specific to ORDA.
In the database Settings dialog, an AI provider's API key was displayed as plain, readable text instead of being masked like a password field.
When using the QUIC network layer, 4D Server could crash on shutdown after running continuously for several days.

On macOS, duplicating a class, renaming it in the Explorer, and then continuing to edit it in the Method Editor left the editor's window title showing the old, pre-rename class name, and eventually caused the application to crash; renaming the file directly in Finder avoided the problem.

A form object property of type Time was not displayed correctly whenever its type was set only through the object's default properties, rather than being explicitly specified via the form object's expression type setting.
Certain 4D commands, such as [COLLECTION TO ARRAY](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/collection-to-array), were not being recorded in the debug log even though they should have been traced.

Running [Create deployment license](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/create-deployment-license) from tool4D in headless mode while building an application with the build4D component caused a crash inside the core licensing routine.
Renaming an input (or output) form caused it to lose its designation as an input/output form entirely, so it no longer functioned as expected once renamed.
On Windows, code-signing a `server.exe` built with the Build4D component from a signed 4D Server failed under SignTool with error `0x800700C1`; the standalone application build was unaffected.

On Windows, after converting a binary database to a project database, checkboxes and radio buttons that had used the "printing" platform style in binary mode did not receive the "flat" style for boolean fields once converted. This relates to Windows Server always using the classic interface theme (since it cannot switch themes), and the classic (Windows XP) theme printing only being supported by the legacy print layer.

Cycling window focus to the Explorer window with a keyboard shortcut let users navigate items with the arrow keys, but pressing Enter no longer opened the editor for the selected item; the mouse pointer's position, not just the window's foreground state, turned out to affect whether Enter was recognized.

On macOS 26 (Tahoe), combo boxes rendered their text at a smaller font size than in previous versions: at a height of 22 points, the classic theme uses the standard font size while the new Liquid Glass theme uses a smaller one. Standard controls like buttons compute their font size from the object's height, but combo boxes were not recalculating font size when their height changed dynamically; pop-up menus were unaffected.
On client/server, calling the plugin API function `PA_ExecuteCommandByID` from an exposed data model class function crashed 4D Server, a regression introduced since 21 R2.
On macOS, pressing the Escape key while the debugger window was open caused the application to crash.

On macOS 26, the [Modified](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/modified) command failed to detect changes made to a field's value, a regression not present on R2/LTS or earlier system versions. The cause was a refactoring of list-form redrawing that now resets the field's modification flag during the redraw cycle.

The `endingDate` and `scheduledDate` values recorded in the `backupHistory.json` file were incorrect because the backup's main duration was not being added in; the backup journal itself was unaffected.
Building an application with tool4D in headless mode together with the build4D component failed because the license could not be registered, causing the build to fail with a missing license file.

On Windows, [DISPLAY NOTIFICATION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/display-notification) could crash the application if the system appearance switched between light and dark mode while the session was running.

Typing a new Case of statement either at the very start of a method, or inside an If statement placed above an existing Case of block, could crash the application shortly afterward, apparently due to a buffer overrun in the method editor.

On Windows client/server, a client could not connect to the server over ServerNet when both client-server encryption and single sign-on (SSO) were enabled simultaneously; disabling either one, or using the QUIC network layer (which is always encrypted), avoided the problem. This appears to be a side effect of the fix for ACI0106296.
On Apple Silicon, in compiled mode, a 4D client failed to run a component method that was supposed to execute on the server.
On client/server using the QUIC network component, quitting a 4D client that was connected to the server could crash the application.
Adding a new item to an existing enumeration list in the toolbox inserted it at the top of the list instead of at the expected position, an apparent side effect of the fix for ACI0106197.
When creating a new list item in the toolbox, the "Modifiable Element" checkbox was left unchecked by default instead of being selected.

In 4D Write Pro, applying bold or italic to text via [INVOKE ACTION](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/invoke-action) or [WP SET ATTRIBUTES](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/wp-set-attributes) could unexpectedly change the font itself rather than just its style — for example, bolding Calibri Light produced Times New Roman Bold instead of Calibri Bold. The problem occurred when a paragraph-level style sheet was applied.
On Windows, the plugin SDK function `PA_CreateNativePictureForPrinting` returned pictures that were incorrectly enlarged and clipped; the related `PA_CreateNativePictureForScreen` was unaffected.
In the Toolbox editor, the right-hand panel of the "List" tab could become hidden or render incorrectly after switching focus away from 4D to another application and back.
In the toolbox's list editor, clicking in the empty area on the left without selecting a list left the right-hand panel showing only two stray horizontal lines instead of the expected empty state.
The right-hand separator line was missing from the enumerations list display in the toolbox editor.

In client/server mode, checking "Remember Password" in the user authentication dialog had no effect — the password was still requested again on the next login. This is the same issue previously reported as ACI0102628.

The QUIC network layer sent fixed-size UDP packets without properly implementing Path MTU Discovery (DPLPMTUD per RFC 8899): inspecting QUIC UDP packets showed the DF (Don't Fragment) bit set to 0 instead of 1. In an IPsec VPN environment with an MTU of 1390, oversized probe packets get fragmented by intermediate devices instead of signaling the correct MTU, causing packet loss and a significant drop in throughput.

On Windows in MDI mode, resizing a maximized window with [SET WINDOW RECT](https://developer.4d.com/docs/commands/set-window-rect) caused the close/minimize/maximize buttons to disappear from the window's top-right corner, sometimes leaving an unexpected extra small window with no such controls.
In compiled mode, arrays of type Time accessed indirectly through pointers reported an incorrect value type.
